nodes.label: Georg Bühler
variants: ゲオルグ・ビューラー
ゲオルク・ビューラー
ヨハン・ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ビューラー
nodes.summary: Georg Bühler worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen (1855–1858), studying under Benfey, Sauppe, Curtius, and Ewald. He held posts at Elphinstone College and Mumbai (~1863–1880) and the University of Vienna (from 1880).

nodes.label: Franz Kielhorn
variants: フランツ・キールホルン
nodes.summary: Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under A. F. Stenzler, Albrecht Weber, and Theodor Benfey at Göttingen, Breslau, and Berlin. He was a professor at Deccan College (1866–1881) before taking the Indology chair at Göttingen in 1881.

nodes.label: Ernst Kuhn
nodes.image: Ernst Kuhn - Aufsätze zur Kultur- und Sprachgeschichte.jpg
nodes.description: German indologist, linguist, philologist and orientalist (1846–1920)
nodes.summary: Ernst Kuhn was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Berlin, Leipzig, Tübingen, and Halle-Wittenberg, working under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Heidelberg and Munich.

nodes.label: Lucian Scherman
nodes.summary: Indologist Lucian Scherman studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and Ernst Kuhn at Munich, where he completed his Promotion and Habilitation. He held multiple professorships at the University of Munich (1893–1916) and led the Museum Fünf Kontinente from 1907.

nodes.label: Ernst Windisch
variants: エルンスト・ヴィルヘルム・オスカー・ヴィンディシュ
エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ヴィンディシュ
nodes.summary: Ernst Windisch specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs at Leipzig, Heidelberg, and Strasbourg, and worked at the India Office Library.

nodes.label: Leipzig University
variants: ライプツィヒ大学インド学・中央アジア学研究所
Department of Indology and Central Asian Studies, University of Leipzig
Institute for the Study of Religions at Leipzig University
Sanskrit-Abteilung des Indogermanischen Forschungsinstituts der Königl. Sächsischen Forschungsinstitute zu Leipzig

nodes.label: Willem Caland
variants: ウィレム・カーランド
nodes.summary: Willem Caland (1859–1932) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Leiden University, studying under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1906–1929) and a post at Leiden.

nodes.label: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg
nodes.image: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg monument in Tranquebar, Tamil Nadu, South India.jpg

nodes.label: August Hermann Francke
nodes.summary: August Hermann Francke worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the Lehrerseminar in Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he became a Privatdozent in 1922.

nodes.id: P:Guillaume-Emmanuel-Joseph Guilhem de Clermont-Lodève, baron de Sainte-Croix
nodes.label: Guillaume-Emmanuel-Joseph Guilhem de Clermont-Lodève, baron de Sainte-Croix
Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres
variants: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles Lettres
Akademie der schönen Wissenschaften zu Paris

nodes.label: Alexander Johnston
nodes.summary: Alexander Johnston was an Indologist and historian who studied law at the University of Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn. He founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland and served as chief justice on the Executive Council of Ceylon.

nodes.label: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron
variants: アンクティル・デュペロン
アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.image: David d'Angers - Portrait d'Abraham-Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731-1805), orientaliste.jpg
nodes.jawiki: アブラアム＝ヤサント・アンクティル＝デュペロン
nodes.summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Sorbonne University, the Old Catholic Seminary of Amersfoort, and under Darab Kumana, later serving as an oriental language interpreter and academy member.

nodes.label: Johann III Bernoulli
nodes.summary: Johann III Bernoulli worked in history/archaeology and related fields. He studied at the University of Neuchâtel and earned a doctorate from the University of Basel (~1757–1758). He was a member of the Prussian, Imperial, and Danzig academies.

nodes.label: Joseph Tiefenthaler
nodes.summary: Joseph Tiefenthaler was an 18th-century scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and was Rector of St. Peter's College, Agra.

nodes.label: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed
nodes.description: Civilian of the British East India Company (1751-1830)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow School and Christ Church, Oxford. He served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

nodes.label: East India Company
variants: イギリス東インド会社

nodes.label: Malabar Mission
variants: Mission an der Küste von Malabar

nodes.label: Paulinus of St. Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Paulinus of St. Bartholomew was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collegio San Pancrazio (~1771–1774). He served at the Malabar Mission (1776–1789) and in 1800 became inspector of studies at the Pontifical Urban University and counsellor to the Congregation of the Index.

nodes.label: University of Oxford
variants: オックスフォード大学
オックスフォード大學
Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Oxford

nodes.label: Charles Wilkins
variants: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・ウィルキンズ
nodes.summary: Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under the traditional teacher Kalinatha. He co-founded The Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company, the India Office Library, and the India Office Records.

nodes.label: Henry Thomas Colebrooke
variants: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・トーマス・コールブルック
nodes.summary: Henry Thomas Colebrooke worked in Indology, studying under Citrapati. He served in the East India Company, Bengal Civil Service, Sadar Diwani Adalat, and Council of India, taught at Fort William College, and presided over the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: William Jones
variants: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジョーンズ (言語学者)
nodes.description: Anglo-Welsh philologist and scholar of ancient India (1746–1794)
nodes.summary: William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harrow, Oxford, Middle Temple, and under teachers including Mirza, Ramachandra, and Ramalocana. He served as Puisne and Chief Justice at Fort William and founded The Asiatic Society (1784).

nodes.id: I:Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
nodes.label: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William
variants: Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William

nodes.label: Robert Chambers
nodes.summary: Robert Chambers (1737–1803) was a legal scholar and Indologist who studied at Lincoln College, Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William (~1789–1798), and Asiatic Society president (~1797–1798).

nodes.label: John Shore
nodes.summary: John Shore was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Succeeding William Jones, he served as President of The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Fort William College
variants: College von Fort William in Kalkutta
College of Fort William in Calcutta

nodes.label: William Carey
variants: ウィリアム・ケアリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ケアリー (宣教師)
nodes.description: English Baptist missionary and Particular Baptist minister (1761-1834)
nodes.summary: William Carey (1761–1834) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma. He was appointed Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College in 1801 and co-founded Serampore College.

nodes.label: Otto von Böhtlingk
variants: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.jawiki: オットー・フォン・ベートリンク
nodes.summary: Otto von Böhtlingk was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Franz Bopp and Christian Lassen. He served as a member and director at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (1842–1868) and taught at the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

nodes.label: Charles Rieu
nodes.summary: Charles Rieu was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies who studied at Geneva and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He served as Curator of Oriental Manuscripts at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

nodes.label: George Thibaut
nodes.summary: George Thibaut was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Principal of Muir Central College (1888–1895) and held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Sanskrit College, Oxford, and the Universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.

nodes.label: Sudhakara Dvivedi
nodes.summary: Sudhakara Dvivedi (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakrishna. He served as librarian and later professor and head of mathematics and astrology at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College and University between 1883 and 1910.

nodes.label: Horace Hayman Wilson
variants: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.jawiki: ホーラス・ヘイマン・ウィルソン
nodes.summary: Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. He held posts with the East India Company, served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint (1816–1833), and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanscrit (1831–1860).

nodes.label: Monier Monier-Williams
variants: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.jawiki: モニエル・モニエル＝ウィリアムズ
nodes.summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at Oxford. He taught at East India Company College and Cheltenham College before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887.

nodes.label: Sanskrit College and University
variants: Postgraduate Training and Research Department of the Sanskrit College
Department of Postgraduate Training and Research, Sanskrit College, Calcutta

nodes.label: Vans Kennedy
nodes.description: Scottish major-general of the British Army
nodes.summary: Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army from 1817 to 1835 and later served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from approximately 1835 to 1846.

nodes.label: James Prinsep
variants: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・プリンセプ
nodes.summary: James Prinsep was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served at the Benares Mint (~1820–1830), the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819, 1830–1838), and led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), where he founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

nodes.label: Arthur Schopenhauer
variants: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
アルトゥール・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.jawiki: アルトゥル・ショーペンハウアー
nodes.summary: Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena (PhD 1813). His teachers included Majer, Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf. He held a lecturing post at the University of Berlin (~1820–1831).

nodes.label: Paul Regnaud
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and linguistics, Paul Regnaud was a student at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and later held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.

nodes.label: École Pratique des Hautes Études
variants: École des Hautes Études in Paris
高等研究実習院第4部門
フランス國立高等研究院
École Pratique des Hautes Études, SHP
École Pratique des Hautes Études (EPHE, PSL University, Paris)

nodes.label: John Muir
nodes.summary: John Muir was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow, East India Company College, and University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853) and was principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1844.

nodes.label: Johannes Klatt
nodes.summary: Johannes Klatt (1852–1903) was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned his doctorate at the University of Halle. Beginning in 1872, he worked at the Prussian State Library, serving as custodian and later as librarian from 1889.

nodes.label: Albrecht Weber
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
アルブレヒト・フリードリヒ・ヴェーバー
nodes.jawiki: アルブレヒト・ヴェーバー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Stenzler, Lassen, Gildemeister, and Kuhn. He served on the faculty of Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 until 1901.

nodes.label: Ignazio Guidi
nodes.summary: Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1860–1864) and later served there as a professor (1876–1919).

nodes.label: Emilio Teza
nodes.description: Italian translator, indo-europeanist, romanist, orientalist and linguist
nodes.summary: Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Anton Boller. He served as professor at the universities of Bologna (1860), Pisa (~1861–1885), and Padua (~1888–1912), and worked at the Laurentian and Marciana libraries.

nodes.label: Ram Mohan Roy
variants: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.image: Portrait of Raja Ram Mohun Roy, 1833.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ラーム・モーハン・ローイ
nodes.description: Indian religious, social, and educational reformer, and humanitarian
nodes.summary: Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Ram Mohan Roy founded several institutions and publications, including Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mirat-ul-Akbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

nodes.label: Alexander Hamilton
nodes.summary: Alexander Hamilton was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature at the East India Company College starting in 1806.

nodes.label: Louis-Mathieu Langlès
variants: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.jawiki: ルイ＝マチュー・ラングレス
nodes.description: French academic, philologist, linguist, translator, author, librarian and orientalist
nodes.summary: Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Indology and Iranian studies, studying at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Chief Keeper of Manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale and founded and directed the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

nodes.label: Henry Pitts Forster
nodes.summary: Henry Pitts Forster was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the Bengal Civil Service and East India Company from 1783 to 1815, and was appointed Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, in 1803.

nodes.label: Joshua Marshman
variants: ジョシュア・マーシュマン
nodes.summary: Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Indology and sinology. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and he founded Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: Friedrich Majer
variants: フリードリヒ・マイヤー
nodes.summary: Friedrich Majer worked in Indology and history, studying at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1798–1803). He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Jena from ~1800 to 1818.

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried von Herder
variants: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・ゴットフリート・ヘルダー
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried von Herder worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg under Immanuel Kant (1762–1764). He held posts at Riga Cathedral School (1764–1769), Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium (~1776–1803), and as General Superintendent at Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach (1776).

nodes.label: Friedrich Schlegel
variants: カール・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・フォン・シュレーゲル
フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, critic and scholar, editor
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, having studied at Göttingen under Heyne, at Leipzig, and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. His academic posts included Jena (1800), École Centrale de Cologne (~1804–1806), and TU Dresden (1828).

nodes.label: Bibliothèque nationale de France

オーギュスト・ウィルヘルム
アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・シュレーゲル
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・ヴィルヘルム・シュレーゲル
nodes.description: German poet, translator, critic, and writer (1767–1845)
nodes.summary: August Wilhelm Schlegel worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Gottfried August Bürger, and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy and Alexander Hamilton, later holding professorships at Jena, Breslau, and Bonn.

nodes.label: William Robertson
nodes.description: British historian, minister of religion, and principal of the University of Edinburgh (1721-1793)
nodes.summary: William Robertson was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh (1733–1741). He later served as the Principal of the University of Edinburgh starting in 1762.

nodes.label: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren
nodes.summary: Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a historian who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (PhD 1784). He spent his career at Göttingen, becoming a professor of philosophy in 1794 and history in 1801.

nodes.label: Peter von Bohlen
nodes.summary: Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist who studied in Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and A. W. Schlegel. He habilitated at Königsberg (~1825–1826) and served there as professor of oriental literature from 1825.

nodes.label: Othmar Frank
nodes.summary: Othmar Frank was an Indologist who studied in Paris and London. He taught at Banz Abbey School, the Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and the University of Bamberg, before holding professorships at the University of Würzburg (from 1821) and the University of Munich (from 1826).

nodes.label: University of Bamberg
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Bamberg

variants: Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institut de Civilisation Indienne of the University of Paris
Institute de Civilisation Indienne of the Sorbonne
Institute of Indian Civilization of the University of Paris

nodes.label: Franz Bopp
nodes.summary: Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under K. J. H. Windischmann, A.-I. Silvestre de Sacy, and A.-L. de Chézy at Paris and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1821 to 1867.

nodes.label: University of London
variants: Institute of Germanic Studies, University of London
Institute of Germanic Studies in London University
Guy's Hospital Medical School, University of London

nodes.label: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann
variants: カール・ヴィンディシュマン
nodes.summary: Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Mainz (1787–1796) and Würzburg (1792–1796). He held posts at Lyceum Hosianum (1803), Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1811), and the University of Bonn (1818).

nodes.label: Friedrich Windischmann
nodes.summary: Scholar of Indology and Iranian studies Friedrich Windischmann studied at Bonn—under Lassen, A. W. Schlegel, and others—and Munich. He held a professorship at Munich (1838–1839) and was General Vicar of the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1839–1861).

nodes.label: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
variants: Antoine Isaac, Baron Silvestre de Sacy
アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝イザーク・シルヴェストル・ド・サシ
nodes.summary: Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, historian, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He taught at INALCO, the Collège de France (1806–1838), and the University of Paris (1815), also serving as president of the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Antoine-Léonard de Chézy
variants: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ＝レオナール・ド・シェジー
nodes.summary: Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

nodes.label: Collège de France
variants: コレージュ・ド・フランス
コレジュ・ド・フランス
Institut de Civilisation Indienne du Collège de France
Centre d'études tibétaines am Collège de France
Institute of Tibetan Studies of the Collège de France

Seminar für Indologie und Buddhismuskunde, Universität Göttingen

nodes.label: Wilhelm von Humboldt
variants: Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Carl Ferdinand von Humboldt
Friedrich Wilhelm Christian Karl Ferdinand von Humboldt
ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
カール・ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・フォン・フンボルト
nodes.description: Prussian philosopher, government official, diplomat, and educator (1767–1835)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt (1767–1835) worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under Campe, Engel, Dohm, Klein, Lichtenberg, Heyne, and Chézy. He founded Humboldt University of Berlin and held a post there around 1809–1810.

nodes.label: Ernst Siecke
nodes.description: born:1846|died:1935|; Siecke, Ernst (Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl), 1846-; Siecke, Ernst Ludwig Albert Karl, 1846-1935

nodes.label: Alexandre Langlois
nodes.summary: Alexandre Langlois was an Indology scholar who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as an inspector for the Académie de Paris, taught at Lycée Charlemagne, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat
variants: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝ピエール・アベル＝レミュザ
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a Sinologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as conservator and president at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

nodes.label: Jean-Louis Burnouf
variants: ジャン＝ルイ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Jean-Louis Burnouf studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served as professor of rhetoric at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, held the chair of Latin eloquence at Collège de France (1816–1844), and was university librarian at the Sorbonne.

nodes.label: Eugène Burnouf
variants: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.jawiki: ウジェーヌ・ビュルヌフ
nodes.summary: Eugène Burnouf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian studies. He studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1822–1832) and held positions at the Société Asiatique (1826, 1829, 1832), Collège de France (1832–1852), and Imprimerie Nationale (~1832–1852).

nodes.label: Christian Gottlob Heyne
nodes.summary: Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who earned a master's at Leipzig University (1748–1752). He was appointed professor at the University of Göttingen (1763) and served as director of Göttingen State and University Library (1764–1812).

nodes.label: Christian Lassen
variants: クリスチャン・ラッセン
nodes.jawiki: クリスチャン・ラッセン (東洋学者)
nodes.summary: Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn (under August Wilhelm Schlegel), he served at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and professor of Old Indian language and literature (1840–1876).

nodes.label: Paul Deussen
variants: パウル・ヤーコプ・ドイセン
nodes.summary: Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, where he studied under Christian Lassen. He taught as a Privatdozent in Geneva and Berlin, and became a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

nodes.label: Otto Strauss
nodes.summary: Otto Strauss was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel University (1920), and the University of Breslau (1928–1935).

nodes.label: Société Asiatique
variants: フランスのアジア協会

variants: アレクサンダー・フォン・フンボルト

nodes.summary: Alexander von Humboldt studied at European University Viadrina, the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena, where he also held an academic post.

ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・フライターク
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フライターク
nodes.summary: Georg Wilhelm Freytag was a linguist who studied at Göttingen (~1807–1811) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1815–1819). He served as a repetent at Göttingen (1811–1813) and as professor of oriental languages at Bonn (1819–1861).

nodes.label: Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg
variants: Centre for Historiography and Intellectual Culture of Kashmir
Institut für Indologie und Südasienwissenschaften, Universität Halle-Wittenberg
Institut für Indologie in Halle an der Saale

nodes.label: University of Königsberg
variants: ケーニヒスベルク大学

nodes.label: Theodor Goldstücker
variants: テオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ゴルトシュテュッカー
nodes.summary: Theodor Goldstücker worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg and Bonn, and under Karl Rosenkranz, Peter von Bohlen, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1851/1852 to 1872.

nodes.label: Friedrich Rückert
variants: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
ヨーハン・ミヒャエル・フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・リュッケルト
nodes.description: German poet, translator, and professor of Oriental languages (1788–1866)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Rückert, an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Hammer-Purgstall and Bopp. He held posts at Jena (1811), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1826), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1849) as professor of Arabic.

nodes.label: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff
nodes.summary: Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff (1774–1835) was a scholar of Indology and other fields. He studied at the Tübinger Stift and University of Tübingen, holding posts at Tartu, Melanchthon-Gymnasium Nürnberg, the University of Würzburg, and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg.

nodes.label: Adolf Holtzmann
nodes.summary: Adolf Holtzmann was an Indologist and linguist. He studied in Berlin, Halle, Munich (under Othmar Frank and Johann Andreas Schmeller), and Paris (under Eugène Burnouf), later serving as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

nodes.label: Johann Andreas Schmeller
nodes.summary: Johann Andreas Schmeller worked in linguistics after studying at the Wilhelmsgymnasium (~1801–1803). He taught at the Bavarian Cadet Corps (~1817–1826), became a Kustos at the Bavarian State Library (1829), and held professorships at the University of Munich (1828, 1846).

nodes.label: Heidelberg University
variants: South Asia Institute of Heidelberg University

nodes.label: Salomon Lefmann
nodes.summary: Salomon Lefmann specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Münster, Heidelberg, Paris, and Berlin (~1861–1864, PhD) under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Heidelberg University as Extraordinariat für Sanskrit (1866), associate professor (1870), and honorary professor (1901).

nodes.label: University of Freiburg
variants: Confucius Institute at the University of Freiburg

nodes.label: Friedrich August Rosen
nodes.summary: Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp, and held professorships at University College London (1828–1831) and the University of London (1834).

nodes.label: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler
variants: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.jawiki: アドルフ・フリードリヒ・シュテンツラー
nodes.summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and others in Berlin, Bonn, and Paris. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and librarian at the University of Breslau from 1833 to 1872.

nodes.label: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Léonard de Chézy. He held the chair of oriental languages at Leipzig from 1836.

nodes.label: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary
nodes.summary: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Halle, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, where he subsequently served as a lecturer of oriental languages and associate professor in theology.

nodes.label: Agathon Benary
nodes.summary: Agathon Benary worked in linguistics. He studied at the universities of Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. Benary served as a gymnasial teacher at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

nodes.label: Köllnisches Gymnasium
variants: ケルン・ギムナジウム

nodes.label: Bernhard Hirzel
nodes.summary: Bernhard Hirzel (1807–1847) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Zurich, Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, Göttingen, and Paris. He subsequently served as a reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich.

nodes.label: Hermann Brockhaus
variants: ヘルマン・ブロックハウス
nodes.summary: Hermann Brockhaus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm Schlegel. He held professorships at the University of Jena and Leipzig University, where he also served as Rektor.

nodes.label: University of Zurich
variants: Völkerkundemuseum of the University of Zurich
Ethnographic Museum of the University of Zurich
Institute for Social Anthropology and Empirical Cultural Studies at the University of Zurich

nodes.label: Georg Martin Dursch
nodes.summary: Georg Martin Dursch was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1818–1823) and under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy at the University of Paris (~1826–1828), becoming professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen in 1829.

nodes.label: Friedrich von Adelung
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology after studying at Leipzig University (1787–1790). He was an honorary professor at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), director at Vienna (1824), and held a post at Utrecht (1825).

nodes.label: Johann Christoph Adelung
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・クリストフ・アーデルング
nodes.summary: Johann Christoph Adelung worked in linguistics. He studied at Kloster Berge school (~1746–1752) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1752). He later served at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and as head librarian at Saxon State Library Dresden (1787).

nodes.label: Colin Mackenzie
nodes.image: Colonel Colin Mackenzie and his Indian pandits by Thomas Hickey.jpg

nodes.label: William Ward
variants: ウィリアム・ウォード
nodes.description: English pioneer Baptist missionary, author, printer and translator
nodes.summary: William Ward was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Ewood Hall Theological Academy under John Fawcett in 1797. He served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission (~1800–1823) and co-founded Serampore College in 1818.

nodes.label: Claude-Auguste Court
nodes.summary: Claude-Auguste Court was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the École polytechnique and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813), and served as an Engineer Officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army (~1827–1843).

nodes.label: École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr
variants: サン・シール陸軍士官学校

nodes.label: George Turnour
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ターナー (歴史家)
nodes.summary: George Turnour worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

nodes.label: John Wilson
nodes.description: Christian missionary, orientalist, and educator in Maharashtra, India (1804-1875)
nodes.summary: John Wilson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He founded Wilson College, served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1842), and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

nodes.label: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
variants: Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Brian Houghton Hodgson
variants: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.image: Brian Houghton Hodgson by Louisa Starr-Canziani.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ホートン・ホジソン
nodes.summary: Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Haileybury and Fort William colleges, he served in Nepal as Assistant Resident starting in 1820 and as British Resident from around 1833 to 1843.

nodes.label: Bhagwanlal Indraji
nodes.summary: Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and a Fellow at Mumbai University.

nodes.label: Charles Masson
nodes.description: British East India Company soldier and explorer (1800–1853)

nodes.label: Edwin Norris
nodes.summary: Edwin Norris (1795–1872) worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology, and taught John Dowson. He held posts as a junior clerk at the East India Company (1818–1837), translator at the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and secretary and librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Edward Upham
nodes.summary: Edward Upham (1776–1834) was a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland and fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

nodes.label: Francis Wilford
nodes.summary: Francis Wilford worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (c. 1784–1822) and served as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1794.

nodes.label: Eugène Jacquet
nodes.summary: Eugène Jacquet was an Indologist and linguist. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from around 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from around 1832 to 1838.

nodes.label: Daniel Wright
nodes.description: Scottish surgeon and physician; resided in Nepal

nodes.label: William Wright
nodes.summary: William Wright was a linguist who studied at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. He taught Arabic at University College London (1855–1856) and Trinity College Dublin (1856–1861), served as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum (1861–1870), and was Adams Professor at Cambridge (1870–1889).

nodes.label: Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern
nodes.summary: Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Utrecht University, Leiden University (doctorate under Antonie Rutgers), and under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865) and Leiden University (1865–1903).

nodes.label: Bunyiu Nanjio
nodes.summary: Bunyiu Nanjio (1849–1927) was an indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist scholar. He studied at Otani University and Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later serving as a lecturer at Tokyo University and long-term director at Otani University.

nodes.label: Edward Byles Cowell
variants: エドワード・バイルズ・コウェル
nodes.image: Portrait of Edward Byles Cowell by Charles Edmund Brock-1905.jpg
nodes.summary: Edward Byles Cowell specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson, became Principal of Sanskrit College (1858-1864), and served as Professor at the University of Cambridge (1867-1903).

nodes.label: Julius Eggeling
nodes.summary: Julius Eggeling (1842–1918) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and as a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

nodes.label: Robert Alexander Neil
nodes.image: R A Neil-R H Lord recto.tif
nodes.summary: Robert Alexander Neil was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at the University of Aberdeen and Peterhouse, studying under mentors including William Duguid Geddes and Edward Byles Cowell. He was appointed University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge in 1884 and Fellow of Pembroke College in 1900.

nodes.label: Alexander Csoma de Kőrös
variants: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.jawiki: ケーレシ・チョマ・シャーンドル
nodes.summary: Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Bethlen Gábor College and the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn. He later served as librarian for The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Isaak Jakob Schmidt
nodes.summary: Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar in Tibetology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies who received a doctorate from Rostock (1825). He served as treasurer for the Russian Bible Society and held memberships at the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire
nodes.description: French philosopher, journalist, statesman, and possible illegitimate son of Napoleon I of France (1805-1895)
nodes.summary: A scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and joined the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques in 1839.

nodes.id: I:Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
nodes.label: Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques
variants: Académie des Sciences morales et politiques
Academy of Moral and Political Science

nodes.label: Jules Mohl
nodes.summary: A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, Mohl studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He was an extraordinary professor at Tübingen (1826–1834) and Professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

nodes.label: Stanislas Julien
variants: エニャン＝スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラス・ジュリアン
nodes.summary: Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and held posts at the Collège de France (Chair of Chinese, 1832–1873), Bibliothèque nationale, and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

nodes.label: Robert Lenz
nodes.summary: Lenz, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Dorpat, Tartu, and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He taught at Tallinn Cathedral School, served in the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and was Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836).

nodes.label: Saint Petersburg State University
variants: Faculty of Oriental Languages at St. Petersburg
Faculty of Oriental languages at St. Petersburg

nodes.label: Gaspare Gorresio
nodes.image: Gaspare Gorresio, post 1869 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0015 B.jpg
nodes.summary: Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held the chair in Sanskrit at Turin (1852) and served as librarian and director of Turin's royal and university libraries.

nodes.label: Émile-Louis Burnouf
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Émile-Louis Burnouf studied at ENS, University of Paris, and École française d'Athènes under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship at University of Nancy (1854–1867) and served as director of École française d'Athènes (1867–1875).

nodes.label: Théodore Pavie
nodes.image: Théodore Pavie (1811–1896), Orientalist, friend of the artist MET 31523.jpg
nodes.summary: Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1845). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew lessons and lectures at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

nodes.label: Adolphe Regnier
nodes.summary: Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, having studied under Eugène Burnouf. His appointments included positions at the Collège de France, École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1855), and Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

nodes.label: Félix Nève
nodes.summary: Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven and under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as a professor at KU Leuven starting in 1841, becoming professor emeritus in 1877.

nodes.label: Abel Bergaigne
variants: アベル・ベルゲーニュ
nodes.summary: Abel Bergaigne worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877), Sorbonne University (1877), and the University of Paris (~1885–1888).

nodes.label: Theodor Benfey
variants: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.jawiki: テーオドール・ベンファイ
nodes.summary: An indologist and linguist, Theodor Benfey studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Munich. He spent his career at the University of Göttingen, serving as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius professor (1862–1881).

nodes.label: Friedrich Max Müller
variants: マックス・ミューラー
フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・マックス・ミュラー
nodes.description: German-born British philologist, orientalist and indologist (1823–1900)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Max Müller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Brockhaus, Bopp, Burnouf, and Wilson. At the University of Oxford, he became Professor of Modern European Languages (1854) and Professor of Comparative Philology (1868; 1883–1900).

nodes.label: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud
nodes.summary: Joseph Toussaint Reinaud specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the École des langues orientales, and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Heinrich Ewald
nodes.description: German orientalist, theologian, and Biblical exegete (1803–1875)
nodes.summary: Ewald worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Thomas Christian Tychsen, he taught at Große Schule (1822–1824), the University of Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867), and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes
variants: Zeitschrift für die Kunde des Morgenlandes

nodes.label: Ernst Trumpp
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・トランプ
nodes.summary: Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the Tübinger Stift, including under Rudolf von Roth. His career included posts at the East India Company, the University of Tübingen, and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: August Schleicher
variants: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・シュライヒャー
nodes.summary: August Schleicher was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald, Christian Lassen, and others, later serving as professor at Charles University (1850–1857) and the University of Jena (1857).

nodes.label: Moritz Abraham Stern
variants: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・アブラハム・シュテルン
nodes.summary: Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Heidelberg and under Karl Otfried Müller at Göttingen. He served as Extraordinarius at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

nodes.label: Rudolf von Roth
variants: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.jawiki: ルドルフ・フォン・ロート
nodes.summary: Rudolf von Roth specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and with Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

nodes.label: William Dwight Whitney
variants: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ドワイト・ホイットニー
nodes.summary: William Dwight Whitney (1827–1894) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Williams College, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Bopp. He held a professorship in Sanskrit at Yale from 1853 to 1894.

nodes.label: James Tod
nodes.description: 1782-1835, English officer of the British East India Company and an Oriental scholar
nodes.summary: James Tod was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, and under Gyanchandra. He served in the East India Company (~1799–1823) and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).

nodes.id: I:Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
variants: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain

nodes.label: Adalbert Kuhn
variants: フランツ・フェーリクス・アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.jawiki: アーダルベルト・クーン
nodes.summary: Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the Köllnisches Gymnasium from 1837 as teacher, professor, and director, and was a member of the Prussian Academy.

nodes.label: Andrzej Gawroński
nodes.summary: Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902–1906) and Leipzig University (~1903–1906). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and the University of Lviv (1917), and founded the Polish Oriental Society and Polish Linguistic Society.

nodes.label: Stamford Raffles
variants: トーマス・スタンフォード・ラッフルズ
nodes.image: George Francis Joseph - Sir Thomas Stamford Bingley Raffles.jpg
nodes.jawiki: トーマス・ラッフルズ
nodes.summary: Stamford Raffles (1781–1826) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was employed by the East India Company (~1795–1824), founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, and served as its president in 1826.

nodes.label: John Crawfurd
nodes.summary: John Crawfurd was an author in history and linguistics who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh from around 1800 to 1803. He served as a physician for the East India Company from 1803 to 1808.

nodes.label: James Fergusson
nodes.summary: James Fergusson was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.

nodes.label: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied under Christoph Theodosius Walther at the University of Königsberg and held posts at the Königsberg Public Library, Königsberg Cathedral, and the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Christoph Theodosius Walther
nodes.summary: Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying theology at the University of Halle in 1720, he served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from circa 1725 to 1740.

nodes.label: Friedrich Bollensen
nodes.summary: Indologist Friedrich Bollensen studied at Göttingen (~1827–1833), including Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1844–1889), the Main Pedagogical Institute (1846), and was professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Geiger
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ルートヴィヒ・ガイガー
ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ガイガー
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Geiger was an Indology, Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg under Friedrich von Spiegel, later serving as professor there (1891) and as professor at the University of Munich (1920-1924).

nodes.label: Friedrich von Spiegel
variants: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
フリードリヒ・（フォン・）シュピーゲル
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュピーゲル
nodes.summary: Friedrich von Spiegel specialized in Iranian and Indological studies. After studying at Erlangen, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena under scholars including Lassen, Brockhaus, and Fleischer, he was a professor of Oriental languages at Erlangen-Nürnberg from 1849 to 1891.

nodes.label: Heinrich Uhle
nodes.summary: Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1863 to 1867. From 1868 to 1911, he served as a classical languages teacher at the Kreuzschule.

nodes.label: Eduard Sachau
nodes.summary: Eduard Sachau specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Brockhaus, Fleischer, and Nöldeke. He held professorial posts at Vienna (1869) and Berlin (1876-1920), directing the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

nodes.label: Hermann Camillo Kellner
nodes.summary: Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from around 1858 to 1863. He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Königliches Gymnasium Zwickau from around 1868 to 1904.

nodes.label: Kreuzschule
variants: Dresden College of the Sacred Cross

nodes.label: Richard Fritzsche
nodes.summary: Richard Fritzsche (b. 1851) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus. He held a post as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.

nodes.label: University of Marburg
variants: マールブルク大学大学院

nodes.label: Niels Ludvig Westergaard
variants: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.image: Niels Ludvig Westergaard by Budtz Müller.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ニルス・ルズヴィ・ヴェスタゴー
nodes.summary: Niels Ludvig Westergaard worked in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, London, and Oxford, later serving as professor and Rektor at the University of Copenhagen.

nodes.label: Albert Hoefer
nodes.summary: Albert Hoefer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin, where he completed his doctorate and Habilitation. He was a professor at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 until his death in 1883.

nodes.label: University of Greifswald
variants: グライフスヴァルト大学

nodes.id: I:Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
nodes.label: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache
variants: Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Greifswald (1808) and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1812). He held professorships at the University of Jena (1817–1824) and Greifswald (1815, 1824–1850).

nodes.label: Siegfried Goldschmidt
nodes.summary: Siegfried Goldschmidt studied Indology and linguistics at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867), under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He taught Heinrich Zimmer and was an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

nodes.label: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca
variants: Anton Edmund Xavier Evarist Wollheim da Fonseca
nodes.image: PPN663949858 Bildnis von Anton Eduard Wollheim Dafonseca.jpg
nodes.summary: Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin circa 1828–1831, later teaching there from 1849 to 1852, and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

nodes.label: Richard Pischel
variants: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.jawiki: リヒャルト・ピシェル
nodes.summary: Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Promotion and Habilitation at Breslau. He held professorships at the University of Kiel, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).

nodes.label: Alfred Hillebrandt
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Hillebrandt studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at Breslau and Martin Haug at Munich. He spent his career at the University of Breslau as a Sanskrit professor (1883) and chair holder (1887–1921).

nodes.label: Adalbert Bezzenberger
nodes.summary: Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and at Munich. After habilitating at Göttingen, he became Professor of Sanskrit at Königsberg in 1879, where he later served as prorector and rector.

nodes.label: Hermann Oldenberg
variants: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オルデンベルク
nodes.summary: Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, Oldenberg studied at Göttingen and Berlin. He held professorial posts at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University (where he was also Rektor), and the University of Göttingen.

nodes.label: Jacob Wackernagel
variants: ヤコブ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ヤーコプ・ヴァッカーナーゲル
nodes.summary: Jacob Wackernagel (1853–1938) was a Swiss linguist and Indologist who studied at Basel, Göttingen (under Theodor Benfey), Leipzig, and Oxford. He served on the faculty at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and held a chair at Göttingen (1902–1915).

nodes.label: Leo Meyer
nodes.summary: Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (1849–1852) under Theodor Benfey and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851–1854). He held posts at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Tartu (1865–1899).

nodes.label: Hermann Collitz
nodes.summary: Hermann Collitz worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen under August Fick, Theodor Benfey, Hermann Sauppe, and Adalbert Bezzenberger, as well as Berlin and Halle. He held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College and Johns Hopkins University.

nodes.label: Friedrich Bechtel
nodes.summary: Friedrich Bechtel was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen, learning under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He served as a Dozent at Göttingen (1884) and later became Ordinarius for comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg (1895).

nodes.label: Berthold Delbrück
variants: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
ベルトルト・グスタフ・ゴットリープ・デルブリュック
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・デルブリュック
nodes.description: German comparative linguist and Sanskrit scholar (1842–1922)
nodes.summary: Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Pott, Weber, Bopp, Steinthal, and Haym, earning degrees at Halle and Berlin. He held posts at Halle and served as professor at Jena from 1870 to 1913.

nodes.label: University of Copenhagen
variants: University of Copenhagen, Department of Asian Studies
Institute of Oriental Studies, University of Copenhagen
Center for Subjectivity Research at the University of Copenhagen

nodes.label: August Leskien
variants: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・レスキーン
nodes.summary: August Leskien was a linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He served as professor at Jena and Göttingen before his long professorship at Leipzig University from 1870 to 1915.

nodes.label: Leopold von Schroeder
nodes.summary: Leopold von Schroeder (1851–1920) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tartu under Leo Meyer and at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu, University of Innsbruck, and University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Anton Schiefner
variants: フランツ・アントン・シーフナー
nodes.summary: Anton Schiefner worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin, later working at the Imperial Academy of Sciences and Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy (1860–1873).

nodes.label: Carl Cappeller
nodes.summary: Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber at Berlin, and also at Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD ~1868), and Jena (Habilitation 1872), where he became professor in 1875.

nodes.label: Karl Rosenkranz
variants: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.jawiki: ヨハン・カール・ローゼンクランツ
nodes.summary: Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Halle, Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, and Heidelberg. He held academic posts at the University of Halle (~1828–1833) and the University of Königsberg (from 1833).

nodes.label: Raymond West
variants: レイモンド・ウェスト
nodes.summary: Sir Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indologist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a judge of the Bombay High Court, Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: University of Tübingen
variants: Seminar für Indologie und Vergleichende Religionswissenschaft, Universität Tübingen

nodes.label: Tübinger Stift
variants: テュービンゲン神学校

nodes.label: Martin Haug
nodes.summary: Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn, under mentors including Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (1859–1866), and the University of Munich (1868).

nodes.label: Karl Friedrich Geldner
variants: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.jawiki: カール・フリードリヒ・ゲルトナー
nodes.summary: Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch. He taught at Tübingen (1876–1887), Halle (1887–1890), Berlin (1890), and Marburg (1907–1921).

nodes.label: Bruno Lindner
nodes.summary: Bruno Lindner was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University and under Rudolf von Roth. From 1878 to 1919, he served as a Privatdozent at Leipzig University.

nodes.label: Richard von Garbe
nodes.summary: Richard von Garbe worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Hermann Günther Grassmann, Rudolf von Roth, and traditional teacher Bhagavata Acharya. After completing degrees at Tübingen and Königsberg, he served as Extraordinarius at Königsberg (1878–1894) and held a chair at Tübingen (1895–1927).

nodes.label: Maurice Bloomfield
variants: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: モーリス・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Chicago, Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

nodes.label: Julius Grill
nodes.summary: Julius Grill (1840–1930) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen under doctoral supervisor Rudolf von Roth and earned a Lic. theol. at Jena (1880), later serving as Professor of Old Testament Exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

nodes.label: Adolf Kaegi
nodes.summary: Adolf Kaegi was a Swiss Indologist and linguist. Educated at Zurich, Tübingen (under Rudolf von Roth), and Leipzig, he spent his career at the University of Zurich, becoming Ordinary Professor of Sanskrit, Indo-European, and Classical Philology (1893–1914).

nodes.label: Heinrich Zimmer
nodes.summary: Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying under Scherer, Goldschmidt, Roth, and Weber. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics (1881), and Berlin's Celtic chair (1901–1910).

nodes.label: Theodor Aufrecht
variants: テーオドール・アウフレヒト
nodes.summary: An indologist and linguist, Aufrecht studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He served as Privatdozent in Berlin (1850), held a post at the Bodleian Library (1852), and became professor at Edinburgh (1861–1875) and Bonn (1875–1889).

nodes.label: Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung
variants: Zeitschrift für Vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete des Deutschen, Griechischen und Lateinischen
Zeitschrift für vergleichende Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiet der indogermanischen Sprachen
ドイツ、ギリシア、ラテン語比較研究誌

nodes.label: Beiträge zur vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete der arischen, celtischen und slawischen Sprachen
variants: Beiträge zur Vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiete der Arischen, Celtischen und Slawischen Sprachen
Beiträge zur vergleichenden Sprachforschung auf dem Gebiet der arischen, keltischen und slawischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Beiträge zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Beiträge zur Kunde der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Wilhelm Schulze
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Schulze was a linguist and Indologist. After studies in Berlin and Greifswald, he held posts at the University of Marburg and the University of Göttingen, before occupying a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1902 to 1932.

nodes.label: Johannes Schmidt
variants: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.jawiki: ヨハネス・シュミット
nodes.summary: Johannes Schmidt (1843–1901) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn and Jena under August Schleicher and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Bonn, the University of Graz, and became professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1876.

nodes.label: Gottfried Hermann
nodes.image: Gottfried Hermann, von Carl Christian Vogel von Vogelstein.jpg
nodes.summary: Gottfried Hermann was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Jena. He spent his career at Leipzig University, serving as professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

nodes.label: Moriz Haupt
nodes.summary: Moriz Haupt was a German linguist who studied under Gottfried Hermann at Leipzig University. He served as professor at Leipzig University from 1841 to 1851 and later held a professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

nodes.label: Anton Westermann
nodes.summary: Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his habilitation at Leipzig University in 1830 and served there as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

nodes.label: Reinhold Klotz
nodes.summary: Reinhold Klotz was a scholar of linguistics who completed his habilitation at Leipzig University (1826–1831). He served at Leipzig University as assistant professor in 1832 and as außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 to 1870, succeeding Gottfried Hermann and teaching Friedrich Max Müller.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling
variants: フリードリヒ・ヴィルヘルム・ヨーゼフ・フォン・シェリング
フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.image: Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling, 1848 daguerreotype - cropped.jpg
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シェリング
nodes.summary: Philosopher Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling studied at Tübingen and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798–1803), Würzburg (1803–1806), Erlangen-Nürnberg (1820–1827), Munich (1827–1841), and Berlin (1841–1845), and served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences (1827–1842).

nodes.label: Hermann Brunnhofer
nodes.summary: Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Humboldt University, and Zurich under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Kuldīga Gymnasium, served as librarian at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek, and lectured at the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Moriz Winternitz
variants: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.jawiki: モーリッツ・ヴィンターニッツ
nodes.summary: Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler in Vienna and Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at Charles University and the German University in Prague, serving there as extraordinary and a. ö. professor, and taught at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: James R. Ballantyne
nodes.summary: James R. Ballantyne was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy (1832–1845), served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1845–1861), and was librarian at the India Office.

nodes.label: Sampurnanand Sanskrit University
variants: ベナレス大学のサンスクリット・カレッジ

nodes.label: Jean-Baptiste Biot
variants: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.jawiki: ジャン＝バティスト・ビオ
nodes.summary: Jean-Baptiste Biot was a scientist and Indologist who studied under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace at École Polytechnique. He held professorships at the École Centrale de Beauvais, the Science Faculty of Paris, and the Collège de France (1800–1862).

nodes.label: Ebenezer Burgess
nodes.description: United States missionary to the Mahrattas, in western India

nodes.label: Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen
variants: Christian Charles Josias, Baron von Bunsen
nodes.summary: Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen (under Christian Gottlob Heyne), Munich, Leiden, and Copenhagen, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in 1816. He founded the German Archaeological Institute (1829).

nodes.label: Ludwig Noiré
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ
nodes.image: Plate 13 Ludwig Noiré, Photograph album of German and Austrian scientists (cropped).png
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ノワレ

nodes.label: Louis Havet
nodes.summary: Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and chair of Latin philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

nodes.label: Kenju Kasahara
nodes.summary: Kenju Kasahara (1851–1883) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, and learned under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell between 1879 and 1882.

nodes.label: Heinrich Wenzel
nodes.summary: Heinrich Wenzel was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, later completing his habilitation at Leipzig in 1887.

nodes.label: Heinrich August Jäschke
variants: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・アウグスト・イェシュケ
nodes.summary: Heinrich August Jäschke was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and as a Moravian Church missionary from 1857 to 1868, later teaching Heinrich Wenzel and Arthur Coke Burnell.

nodes.label: Bruno Liebich
nodes.summary: Bruno Liebich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Breslau, and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He taught as professor at the University of Breslau (attested 1902; 1921–1928) and later held a post at Heidelberg University (~1928–1939).

nodes.label: Archibald Edward Gough
nodes.description: (1845-1915) British educationalist, translator, editor and academic administrator
nodes.summary: Archibald Edward Gough was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He held professorships at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Presidency University, and served as principal of Aliah University between 1878 and 1895.

nodes.label: John Pickford
nodes.summary: John Pickford was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He held a post as Professor at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: University of Madras
variants: Department of Sanskrit, University of Madras
Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras
Radhakrishnan Institute for Advanced Study in Philosophy
Department of Sanskrit in the University of Madras
Centre of Advanced Study in Philosophy, University of Madras

nodes.label: Ralph T. H. Griffith
nodes.summary: Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served in the Indian Education Service (~1853–1885) and was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1861–1876).

nodes.label: Robert Needham Cust
nodes.summary: Cust was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Eton, Trinity College, Cambridge, East India Company College, and Fort William College. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

nodes.label: Aliah University
variants: Madrassa, il Collegio maomettano di Calcutta
カルカッタ・マドラサ・ムスリム・カレッジ
カルカッタ・マドラサ

nodes.label: James Sutherland Cotton
nodes.summary: James Sutherland Cotton was an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College, Oxford (1867–1870). He held posts at The Queen's College, Oxford (1871–1874) and Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874).

nodes.label: William Wilson Hunter
variants: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウィルソン・ハンター
nodes.summary: William Wilson Hunter was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and as vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta in 1886.

nodes.label: University of Edinburgh
variants: Professur für Sanskrit und vergleichende Sprachwissenschaft an der Universität zu Edinburg

nodes.label: Adolf Kirchhoff
nodes.summary: Adolf Kirchhoff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and held professorships at Humboldt University and Frederick William University Berlin.

nodes.label: Hermann Jacobi
variants: ヘルマン・ゲオルク・ヤコービ
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, Jacobi studied under Albrecht Weber in Berlin and Johann Gildemeister in Bonn. He held professorships at the University of Münster, Kiel University, and the University of Bonn (1889–1922).

nodes.label: Jarl Charpentier
nodes.summary: Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, also studying at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He served as Assistant Professor at Uppsala from 1908, succeeding Johansson in 1927.

nodes.label: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
variants: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.image: Young India; an interpretation and a history of the nationalist movement from within (1916) (14781987942).jpg
nodes.jawiki: バール・ガンガーダル・ティラク
nodes.description: Indian nationalist leader, writer and journalist (1856–1920)
nodes.summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai. He co-founded the Deccan Education Society and taught mathematics at the New English School and Fergusson College.

nodes.label: Reinhold Rost
nodes.image: Reinhold Rost, Porträt mit Signatur, um 1890.jpg
nodes.summary: Reinhold Rost was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena. He held posts at St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and served as Headlibrarian of the India Office Library (1869–1893). He also taught Caroline Rhys Davids.

nodes.label: Heinrich Kiepert
nodes.description: German geographer, cartographer and university professor in Berlin (1818–1899)
nodes.summary: Heinrich Kiepert was a historian, archaeologist, and geographer. He studied at Frederick William/Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann and at Jena. He held posts at the Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Deecke
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leipzig (Dr. phil. 1848–1849) and Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as director or administrator at Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Jean Sturm, Gymnasium Buchsweiler, and Lycée de Mulhouse.

nodes.label: Ferdinand von Eckstein
nodes.summary: Ferdinand von Eckstein (1790–1861) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer from circa 1810 to 1812 and was a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1822 to 1861.

nodes.label: Ghent University
variants: Centre for Buddhist Studies, Ghent University

nodes.label: Josef Schick
nodes.summary: Josef Schick was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he earned his PhD in 1889. He held academic posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich, where he was professor (1896–1925).

nodes.label: Michael Viggo Fausbøll
variants: ミケール・ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.jawiki: ヴィゴ・ファウスベル
nodes.description: Danish educator, translator, orientalist and linguist (1821–1908)
nodes.summary: Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847) under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He served at Copenhagen as 副司書 (1861) and Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

nodes.label: Emil Sieg
nodes.summary: Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar. After studying at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Göttingen under Weber, Kuhn, and Kielhorn, he held chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin, Kiel University, and Göttingen.

nodes.label: Walther Schubring
variants: ヴァルター・シュブリング
nodes.summary: Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at Munich and Strasbourg, where he completed a doctorate under Ernst Leumann. He worked at the Prussian State Library (1907) and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

nodes.label: Ernst Leumann
variants: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・ロイマン
nodes.summary: Ernst Leumann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Zurich, Geneva, Leipzig, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Strasbourg. He held posts at Oxford, Frauenfeld, the University of Strasbourg, and the University of Freiburg.

nodes.label: Luigi Suali
nodes.summary: Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi, and he held a post at the University of Pavia from circa 1907 to 1937.

nodes.label: Helmuth von Glasenapp
variants: ヘルムート・フォン・グラーゼナップ
nodes.summary: Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, completing a doctorate under Hermann Jacobi at Bonn. He served as a lecturer at Berlin and Bonn, then held chairs at the universities of Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

nodes.label: Yale University
variants: Yale University's Interdisciplinary Center for Bioethics
Department of East Asian Languages and Literatures at Yale University
Sheffield Scientific School at New Haven

nodes.label: Edward Elbridge Salisbury
nodes.summary: Edward Elbridge Salisbury (1814–1901) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Yale and in Europe under Woolsey, de Sacy, de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen. He served as professor at Yale (1841–1854) and as president of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Charles Rockwell Lanman
nodes.image: Charles Rockwell Lanman Professor of Sanskrit Harvard.jpg
nodes.summary: Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist who earned his B.A. at Yale and studied in Germany. He served as Sanskrit-Dozent at Johns Hopkins (1876–1880) and held a professorship at Harvard University from 1880 to 1926.

nodes.label: John Avery
nodes.summary: John Avery (1837–1887) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Amherst College, Tübingen, and Berlin, he also studied under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College and Bowdoin College.

nodes.label: Ernst Haas
nodes.summary: Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, where he studied under Albrecht Weber. He worked at the British Museum from 1866 and served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1875.

Department of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts in the British Museum
Department of Oriental Antiquities, The British Museum

variants: Wellcome Trust Centre for the History of Medicine at University College London
