Institute of Archaeology, University College London
Wellcome Trust Centre for the study of the History of Medicine at University College London
Institute of Archaeology der Universität London
Institute of Archaeology at the University of London

nodes.label: Wilhelm Pertsch
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Tübingen under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, later serving as head and head librarian at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha.

nodes.label: Fritz Johaentgen
nodes.summary: Fritz Johaentgen worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy, having studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

nodes.label: Hermann Günther Grassmann
variants: ヘルマン・ギュンター・グラスマン
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・グラスマン
nodes.summary: Active in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, Grassmann studied in Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He held teaching posts at the Gewerbeschule Berlin, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Schule Stettin, and Marienstiftsgymnasium, where he was a professor from 1852 to 1877.

nodes.label: Alfred Ludwig
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Ludwig studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and at Vienna. After qualifying at Vienna in 1858, he became a professor of comparative linguistics at Charles University (1860, full professor 1871).

nodes.label: University of Vienna
variants: ウィーン大学インド学研究所
Institut für Indologie der Universität Wien

nodes.label: Friedrich Müller
variants: フリードリヒ・ミューラー
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Friedrich Müller studied at Vienna, Tübingen, and Göttingen, learning under Anton Boller. He served as a Privatdozent (1858–1866) and later Professor (1869) at the University of Vienna, and worked at the Austrian National Library.

nodes.label: Anton Boller
nodes.summary: Anton Boller was an Austrian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a lecturer and extraordinary professor at the University of Vienna, becoming a full professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit there in 1855.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Scherer
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Scherer was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna and in Berlin under Moriz Haupt and Franz Bopp. He held chairs at the University of Vienna, the University of Strasbourg, and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1877).

nodes.label: Kazan Federal University
variants: Oriental department of the Kazan University
Department of Mongolian Studies at Kazan University

nodes.label: University of Cambridge
variants: Mongolia and Inner Asia Studies Unit
Department of East Asian Studies of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Edward Granville Browne
variants: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・グランヴィル・ブラウン
nodes.summary: Edward Granville Browne (1862–1926) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge and St Bartholomew's under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell. He served as lecturer in Persian and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.

nodes.label: Franz Heinrich Trithen
nodes.summary: Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin and Frederick William University Berlin. He held posts at the British Museum (c. 1844–1848) and the University of Oxford (c. 1848–1854).

nodes.label: Friedrich Haag
nodes.description: Swiss classical philologist, linguist and teacher (1846-1914)
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Friedrich Haag studied at Zurich, Göttingen, and Berlin, learning under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler. He taught at the University of Zurich (1873–1884) and served as professor of classical philology at the University of Bern (1887, 1891–1906).

nodes.label: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler
nodes.summary: Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Zurich under Bernhard Hirzel, Johann Caspar von Orelli, and Hermann Sauppe, and later served as ordinary professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Zurich (1841–1889).

nodes.id: I:Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren
nodes.label: Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren
Georg Curtius
variants: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Linguist Georg Curtius studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and Ritschl, and in Berlin under Bopp. He held posts at Berlin (1845–1849), Charles University (1849–1854), Kiel University (1854–1862), and Leipzig University (1862–1885).

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Halle (~1829–1833), Breslau (1834), Bonn (from 1839), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

nodes.label: Friedrich Zarncke
variants: フリードリヒ・ツァルンケ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Zarncke was a linguist who studied at Rostock and Leipzig, where his teachers included Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He held a post at Rostock (~1848–1850) before becoming Rektor (1852) and full professor (1858) at Leipzig University.

nodes.label: Walter Elliot
nodes.summary: Walter Elliot was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St George, later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in the Government of Madras (1837–1842).

nodes.label: Hermann Reich
nodes.description: German writer, literary scholar and classical philologist

nodes.label: Johannes Hertel
nodes.summary: Johannes Hertel (1872–1955) was an Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from Leipzig University. He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln before holding the chair of Indian philology at Leipzig University from 1919 to 1937.

nodes.label: August Friedrich Pott
variants: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フリードリヒ・ポット
nodes.summary: August Friedrich Pott specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Göttingen and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He lectured at Humboldt University of Berlin before becoming professor of general linguistics at the University of Halle from 1833.

nodes.label: Karl Brugmann
variants: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.jawiki: カール・ブルークマン
nodes.summary: Karl Brugmann (1849-1919) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Georg Curtius at Halle and Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Freiburg (1884) and held a chair in Indo-European linguistics at Leipzig University (1887-1919).

nodes.label: Eugen Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Eugen Wilhelm specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under August Schleicher (~1862–1866) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from around 1869 to 1923.

nodes.label: Carl Gaedicke
nodes.summary: Carl Gaedicke is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Jena, completing his PhD by 1877 under the instruction of Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

nodes.label: Ferdinand de Saussure
variants: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.image: Ferdinand de Saussure by Jullien Restored.png
nodes.jawiki: フェルディナン・ド・ソシュール
nodes.summary: Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Leipzig (PhD 1880), Berlin, and Paris. He taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891) and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).

nodes.label: Eduard Sievers
variants: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアルト・ジーファース
nodes.summary: Linguist Eduard Sievers studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Curtius, Leskien, and Zarncke. He founded Beiträge zur Geschichte der deutschen Sprache und Literatur and held professorships at Jena (1871-1883), Tübingen (1883-1887), Halle (1887-1892), and Leipzig (1892-1922).

nodes.label: Ernst Curtius
variants: エルンスト・クルツィウス
nodes.summary: Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Bonn, Göttingen, and Berlin under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, Christian August Brandis, Karl Otfried Müller, and August Boeckh. He held professorships at Berlin and Göttingen, and directed the Altes Museum (circa 1872–1896).

nodes.label: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli
variants: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.image: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli, post 1861 - Accademia delle Scienze di Torino 0066 B.jpg
nodes.jawiki: グラツィアディオ・イザイア・アスコリ
nodes.summary: Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was an Italian linguist and Indologist. He founded the Archivio glottologico italiano in 1873 and served as Professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.

nodes.id: I:Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
nodes.label: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik
variants: Studien zur griechischen und lateinischen Grammatik

nodes.id: I:Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
nodes.label: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen
variants: Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen

nodes.label: Hermann Osthoff
variants: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.jawiki: ヘルマン・オストホフ
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Osthoff studied under Hermann Usener at Bonn and Georg Curtius at Leipzig. He held posts at Friedrichsgymnasium Kassel, Leipzig University, and served as Ordinarius at Heidelberg University from 1877.

nodes.label: University of Geneva
variants: ジュネーブ大学文学部

nodes.label: Pietro Merlo
nodes.summary: Pietro Merlo was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. From 1877 he taught at the University of Pavia, becoming full professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.

nodes.label: Michele Kerbaker
nodes.summary: Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Turin under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri, later teaching Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and literature at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Bardelli
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien, and served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1848).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti
nodes.native: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
variants: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・ガスパロ・メゾファンティ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti (1774–1849) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna (~1789–1797). He served there as professor of Hebrew and later Oriental languages (~1814–1831), and became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

nodes.label: Fausto Gherardo Fumi
nodes.summary: Fausto Gherardo Fumi (1840–1915) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Giuseppe Bardelli at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1858–1862).

nodes.label: Carlo Giussani
nodes.summary: Carlo Giussani was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863), under Giuseppe Bardelli, under Albrecht Weber (1863), and under Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1866).

nodes.label: Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano
variants: Academy of Science and Letters (Italian: Accademia scientifico-letteraria) in Milan
ミラノ科学・文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Francisco García Ayuso
nodes.image: 1897-05-30, La Ilustración Española y Americana, Francisco García Ayuso (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Francisco García Ayuso worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich under Martin Haug between approximately 1870 and 1872.

nodes.label: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev
nodes.summary: Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber. He later served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Garcin de Tassy
variants: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.dewiki: Joseph Héliodore Sagesse Vertu Garcin de Tassy
nodes.summary: Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy and Jean-Daniel Kieffer. He held a chair in Indian languages at INALCO/École des langues orientales (~1828–1878) and directed the Société Asiatique.

nodes.label: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux
variants: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.jawiki: フィリップ・エドゥアール・フーコー
nodes.summary: Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships in Tibetan at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1842, 1854) and in Sanskrit at Collège de France (1857-1894).

nodes.label: Léon Feer
nodes.summary: Léon Feer (1830–1902) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Etienne Marc Quatremère and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, Collège de France, and Bibliothèque nationale de France.

nodes.label: Michel Bréal
nodes.summary: Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, under Bopp, and under Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the EPHE (~1868–1882).

nodes.label: Hermann Wilhelm Ebel
nodes.summary: A linguist who studied under August Boeckh, August Friedrich Pott, and Franz Bopp, Ebel taught at Gymnasium Schneidemühl and succeeded Bopp as chair of comparative philology at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1872.

nodes.label: Ernst Förstemann
variants: エルンスト・ヴィルヘルム・フェルステマン
nodes.jawiki: エルンスト・フェルステマン
nodes.summary: Ernst Förstemann was a linguist and historian who studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp. He served as librarian at the Fürstlich Stolberg-Wernigerödische Bibliothek (1851) and headed the Dresden library (1865–1887).

nodes.label: Otto Blau
nodes.summary: Otto Blau was a scholar of Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle, Leipzig University, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, studying under August Friedrich Pott between ~1848 and 1852.

nodes.label: József Budenz
nodes.summary: József Budenz was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at the University of Marburg. He served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and as professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

nodes.label: August Fick
variants: フリードリヒ・コンラート・アウグスト・フィック
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・フィック
nodes.summary: August Fick was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He later served as professor of comparative linguistics at Göttingen (1876) and as ordinary professor at Breslau (1887–1891).

nodes.label: Ferdinand Justi
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and habilitated at Marburg, where he served as associate professor (1865), full professor (1869), and rector (1887–1888).

nodes.label: Ludwig Lange
nodes.summary: Ludwig Lange studied at Leipzig University and the University of Göttingen, where he studied under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Göttingen, Charles University, the University of Giessen (c. 1859–1871), and Leipzig University (c. 1871–1885).

nodes.label: Theodor Nöldeke
nodes.jawiki: テオドール・ネルデケ
nodes.summary: Theodor Nöldeke specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and Theodor Benfey, as well as Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin. He held professorships at Göttingen, Kiel, and Strasbourg (1872–1906).

nodes.label: John Peile
nodes.summary: John Peile was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey. He served as Fellow and Tutor at Christ's College (~1860–1910) and Reader of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1884–1891).

nodes.label: Émile Senart
variants: エミール・シャルル・マリー・スナール
nodes.summary: Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Émile Senart studied at Munich and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He served as professor at Collège de France and was president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928), having been vice-president in 1890.

nodes.label: Ernst Osiander
nodes.summary: Ernst Osiander was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Repetent at Maulbronn, Blaubeuren, and the Tübinger Stift.

nodes.label: Carl Siegfried
nodes.summary: Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber, Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, and Rudolf von Roth at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Tübingen, later holding posts at Trinity College Dublin, Schulpforta, and Jena (~1875–1903).

nodes.label: Julius Euting
nodes.summary: Julius Euting (1839–1913) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen. He later served as an honorary professor at Strasbourg and as Director of the National and University Library, Strasbourg.

nodes.label: Matthias von Lexer
nodes.summary: Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist who studied at Graz and Erlangen and under Bopp, Haupt, and Weber. He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg (~1864–1868), Würzburg (from 1868), and Munich (1890).

nodes.label: Sophus Bugge
nodes.summary: Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held posts at Uppsala University and at the University of Oslo, where he became professor of comparative philology, comparative Indo-European linguistics, and Old Norse in 1866.

nodes.label: Angelo de Gubernatis
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Angelo de Gubernatis studied at Turin and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Florence (1863–1891) and professor of Sanskrit and Italian literature at Rome (1890).

nodes.label: Henri Gaidoz
nodes.summary: Henri Gaidoz was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865. He taught geography and ethnography at Sciences Po (1872–1908) and served as director of studies for Celtic philology at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).

nodes.label: Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar studied at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen. He served as professor at Deccan College (~1882–1893) and became Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

nodes.label: Heinrich Hübschmann
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hübschmann studied linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Munich under August Schleicher and Martin Haug. He held posts at Leipzig University (1876) and as comparative linguistics professor at Strasbourg (1877).

nodes.label: Julius Jolly
nodes.summary: Julius Jolly (1849–1932) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Leipzig, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug. He served as a professor at the University of Würzburg (1877–1920) and Tagore professor of law at Calcutta (1882–1883).

nodes.label: University of Florence
variants: Istituto dei Studi Superiori in Florenz
Istituto degli studii superiori in Florenz
Istituto di studi superiori di Firenze

nodes.label: Sapienza University of Rome
variants: Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza"

nodes.label: Trinity College Dublin
variants: ダブリン大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Frédéric Baudry
nodes.summary: Frédéric Baudry, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian and administrative posts at the Institut agronomique de Versailles (1849), Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1859), and Bibliothèque Mazarine (1874–1885).

nodes.label: James Burgess
nodes.summary: James Burgess, an Indologist and archaeologist, studied at the Universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as Secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society and held several leadership roles at the Archaeological Survey of India, culminating as Director General from 1886 to 1889.

nodes.label: Robert Caesar Childers
nodes.summary: Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford (~1856–1860) and under Yātrāmullē Dhammārāma (~1863–1864), later serving at the India Office (1872) and as professor at University College London (~1872–1876).

nodes.label: August Rudolf Hoernle
nodes.summary: August Rudolf Hoernle worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as director of Aliah University (1881–1899) and was secretary of The Asiatic Society in 1891.

nodes.label: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
nodes.description: Philosopher, academic, writer, translator, entrepreneur, social reformer and philanthropist (1820-1891)
nodes.summary: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Sanskrit College. He held posts at Fort William College and served as Director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: The Queen's College, Oxford
variants: The Queen's College, University of Oxford

nodes.label: Austrian Academy of Sciences
variants: kaiserl. Akademie der Wissenschaften in Wien
オーストリア科学アカデミー
Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften Institut für Kultur- und Geistesgeschichte Asiens
Austrian Academy of Sciences in Vienna
Institute of Social Anthropology, Austrian Academy of Sciences
Numismatic Commission of the Austrian Academy of Science

nodes.label: Henri Hubert
nodes.summary: Henri Hubert studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure (ca. 1892–1895), working in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held positions at the National Archaeological Museum (ca. 1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (ca. 1901–1927), and École du Louvre (ca. 1906–1927).

nodes.label: Marcel Mauss
nodes.summary: Marcel Mauss was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, and others, and held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1901) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

nodes.label: Wilhelm Grube
variants: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・グルーベ
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Grube worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Leipzig University, where he earned his PhD under Georg von der Gabelentz. He later held posts at the Ethnological Museum and Humboldt University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Karl Florenz
variants: カール・フローレンツ
カール・アドルフ・フローレンツ
nodes.jawiki: カール・フローレンツ
nodes.summary: Karl Florenz worked in Japanology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz and Ernst Windisch, and in Berlin and under Friedrich Max Müller and Tetsujiro Inoue. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) and Hamburg (1914–1935).

nodes.label: University of Tokyo

東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科
東京大学文学部印度哲学科
東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科・文学部
東京大学大学院人文社会系研究科博士課程
東京帝大文学部言語学科

nodes.label: Fitzedward Hall
nodes.summary: Fitzedward Hall (1825–1901) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Sanskrit College, and King's College London, and served as librarian for the India Office (~1862–1869).

nodes.label: Arthur Berriedale Keith
nodes.summary: Arthur Berriedale Keith (1879–1944) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Julius Eggeling and Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later serving in the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) and as professor at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

nodes.label: Junjirō Takakusu
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist
nodes.summary: Junjirō Takakusu (1866–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served as professor and president of the University of Tokyo, and led Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

nodes.label: Otto Stein
nodes.summary: Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at Charles University in Prague, completing his doctorate under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. In 1929, he became a member of the research section at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Joseph Estlin Carpenter
variants: エストリン・カーペンター
nodes.summary: Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion educated at University College School and the University of London. He served as President of Harris Manchester College, Oxford (c. 1876–1915) and taught at the University of Oxford (c. 1889–1915).

nodes.label: Robert Chalmers
nodes.description: British civil servant, and Pali and Buddhist scholar (1858-1938)
nodes.summary: Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse (1924–1931).

nodes.label: Richard Morris
nodes.summary: Richard Morris was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Battersea. He taught at King's College School and Dedham Grammar School, later serving as headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

nodes.label: Edmund Hardy
nodes.summary: Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, founding the Archiv für Religionswissenschaft. He studied at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg under Kuno Fischer, and Freiburg. He was a professor of philosophy at Freiburg (1885-1893) and held a chair at Fribourg (1894-1898).

nodes.label: Dines Andersen
nodes.summary: Dines Andersen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and served there as professor of Indian philology from 1903 to 1927.

nodes.label: W. H. D. Rouse
nodes.summary: W. H. D. Rouse was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cheltenham, Regent's Park, and Cambridge. A fellow at Christ's College, he taught at Bedford, Cheltenham, and Rugby before serving as headmaster of The Perse School (1902–1928).

nodes.label: Sylvain Lévi
nodes.summary: Sylvain Lévi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and occupied the Chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1894 to 1935.

nodes.label: Louis de La Vallée Poussin
variants: ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
L・ドゥ・ラ・ヴァレー・プーサン
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée Poussin
Louis Étienne Joseph Marie de La Vallée-Poussin
nodes.summary: Louis de La Vallée Poussin was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Liège, Leuven, and Leiden under Sylvain Lévi and Hendrik Kern. He served as professor at Ghent University (1893–1929) and the Free University of Brussels (1921–1935).

nodes.label: Godefroy de Blonay
nodes.description: Swiss linguist and member of the International Olympic Committee (1869-1937)

nodes.label: Henry Clarke Warren
nodes.summary: Henry Clarke Warren worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and T. W. Rhys Davids. He founded the Harvard Oriental Series in 1891.

nodes.label: Vincent Arthur Smith
nodes.image: The Early History of India by Vincent Arthur Smith.jpg
nodes.summary: Vincent Arthur Smith, an Indologist and historian/archaeologist, studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1865–1869). He served in the Indian Civil Service as Commissioner of Gorakhpur (1871–1900) and later as Curator at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

nodes.label: Sarat Chandra Das
variants: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.image: Sarat Chandra Das, C.I.E. photo from Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet (page 10 crop).jpg
nodes.jawiki: サラト・チャンドラ・ダス
nodes.description: Indian scholar of Tibetan language and culture (1849-1917)
nodes.summary: Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a scholar in Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Presidency College, Chennai, and University of Calcutta, and under Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Pelden Chophel. He held posts at Bhutia Boarding School and the Government of Bengal.

nodes.label: Cecil Bendall
nodes.summary: Cecil Bendall (1856–1906) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, Oxford, and under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge as Professor of Sanskrit.

nodes.label: Unrai Wogihara
nodes.summary: Unrai Wogihara (1869–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann, completing his degree at Strasbourg. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Shukyo University, Shiba High School, and Taisho University.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Radloff
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ラドロフ
nodes.jawiki: ヴァシーリー・ラドロフ
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Radloff worked in Central Asian studies, linguistics, and archaeology. Educated in Berlin and Jena, he was director of the Asiatic Museum (1885-1890) and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (1894-1918).

nodes.label: Alexander von Staël-Holstein
variants: Alexander Wilhelm Freiherr Staël von Holstein
nodes.summary: Alexander von Staël-Holstein was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate under Richard Pischel at Halle. He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University, Peking University, and the Harvard Sino-Indian Institute.

nodes.label: Rudolf Seydel
nodes.summary: Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig University from 1852 to 1856 and subsequently held a post there from around 1860 to 1892.

nodes.label: Masaharu Anesaki
nodes.summary: Masaharu Anesaki was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University under Friedrich Max Müller, Paul Deussen, and others. He served as professor and library director at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.id: P:Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.label: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
variants: G. A. van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.image: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga.jpg
nodes.enwiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.dewiki: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Adolf van den Bergh van Eysinga was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1893–1901) and later held academic posts at Utrecht University (1924–1957) and the University of Amsterdam (1935–1944).

nodes.label: Richard Fick
nodes.summary: Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who studied at Kiel University. He worked at the Kiel University Library, Prussian State Library, and Göttingen State and University Library, and was an honorary professor at the University of Göttingen from 1923.

nodes.label: Richard Schmidt
nodes.summary: Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught at Halle-Wittenberg and served as ordinary professor at the University of Münster from 1910.

nodes.label: Helmer Smith
nodes.summary: Helmer Smith was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Uppsala University and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He held posts at Lund University (1921) and Uppsala University (1936–1947).

nodes.label: Louis Finot
nodes.summary: Louis Finot, an Indologist and historian educated at the École des Chartes, was the first director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from 1898 and held a chair at the Collège de France (1920–1930).

nodes.label: Édouard Huber
nodes.summary: Édouard Huber, a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studied at Sorbonne, University of Paris, École des langues orientales, and Collège de France, including under Sylvain Lévi. He served as Professeur p. i. de chinois at EFEO (1901–1905).

nodes.label: Kaikyoku Watanabe
nodes.summary: Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (PhD 1900–1907) under Ernst Leumann and held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho Universities, also serving as principal of Shiba High School.

nodes.label: Robert Gauthiot
nodes.summary: Robert Gauthiot (1876–1916) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He was educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and was a member of the Société Asiatique from 1909.

nodes.label: Max Lindenau
nodes.summary: Max Lindenau was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch, finishing in 1913.

nodes.label: Ludwig Heller
nodes.summary: Ludwig Heller specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and completed his Habilitation at Greifswald, where he became an associate professor in 1904, later holding a post at the University of Tartu in 1918.

nodes.label: Theodor Zachariae
nodes.summary: Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist. He studied at Leipzig under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus, and at Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe and Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at the University of Greifswald (1883) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

nodes.label: Hermann Beckh
nodes.summary: Hermann Beckh specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he later served as a Privatdozent from around 1911 to 1921.

nodes.label: Theodor Bloch
nodes.summary: Theodor Bloch was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch around 1888–1892, and later studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler around 1893–1895.

nodes.label: Hermann von Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich from circa 1845 to 1848 and held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1851 to 1854.

nodes.label: Emil Schlagintweit
nodes.summary: Emil Schlagintweit (1835–1904) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who was tutored by Franz Joseph Lauth. In 1864, he became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

nodes.label: Georg Morgenstierne
variants: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.dewiki: Georg Valentin von Munthe af Morgenstierne
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・モルゲンスティールネ
nodes.summary: Georg Morgenstierne was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sten Konow, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Schulze, completing a Promotion in Berlin. He was a professor at the University of Gothenburg (1930) and the University of Oslo (1937–1962).

nodes.label: Sten Konow
nodes.summary: Sten Konow (1867–1948) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Richard Pischel at the University of Halle. He served as Government Epigraphist for India and held professorships at the University of Oslo and the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Frederick William Thomas
nodes.summary: Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, he served at the India Office Library (1898–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

nodes.label: Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu
nodes.summary: Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Halle until 1912. He held an attested post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1920.

nodes.label: Edward Denison Ross
variants: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.image: Edward Denison Ross by John Lavery (1856-1941).jpg
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・デニソン・ロス
nodes.summary: Edward Denison Ross (1871–1940) worked in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UCL and under Theodor Nöldeke at Strasbourg. His posts included UCL, Aliah University, University of Calcutta, the British Museum, and SOAS.

nodes.label: Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan
nodes.summary: Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Presidency University.

nodes.label: Ganganatha Jha
nodes.summary: Ganganatha Jha worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities, he was Sanskrit professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), principal of Sanskrit College (1918), and Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (1923–1932).

nodes.label: Edward Washburn Hopkins
nodes.summary: Edward Washburn Hopkins (1857–1932) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Columbia, Bryn Mawr College, and Yale University, succeeding William Dwight Whitney.

nodes.label: Arthur Coke Burnell
nodes.summary: Arthur Coke Burnell (1840–1882) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London (~1857–1860) under teachers including Fausbøll, Goldstücker, and Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1880).

nodes.label: Peter von Bradke
nodes.summary: Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dorpat, Tübingen, and Jena. He completed his Habilitation at the University of Giessen (~1883–1884), where he served as an associate professor from 1886 to 1896.

nodes.label: Prafulla Chandra Ray
nodes.jawiki: プラフラ・チャンドラ・レイ
nodes.description: Bengali chemist, educationist, poet, historian, industrialist and philanthropist (1861–1944)
nodes.summary: Prafulla Chandra Ray (1861–1944) studied at Vidyasagar College, Presidency College, Chennai, Calcutta, and Edinburgh. Active in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held posts at Presidency College, Chennai, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: George Melville Bolling
variants: ジョージ・M・ボーリング
nodes.summary: George Melville Bolling was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Johns Hopkins. He was a professor at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America in 1931.

nodes.label: Bapudeva Sastri
nodes.description: Indian scholar in Sanskrit and mathematics and translator
nodes.summary: Bapudeva Sastri was a scholar of Indology. He studied at Sehore High School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama, and later taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

nodes.label: S. M. Natesa Sastri
nodes.summary: S. M. Natesa Sastri (1859–1906) worked in Indology and related fields. He was educated at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras, and worked as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1884–1888).

nodes.label: Debendranath Tagore
variants: デヴェンドラナート・タゴール

nodes.label: Rabindranath Tagore
variants: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.jawiki: ラビンドラナート・タゴール
nodes.summary: Rabindranath Tagore was a philosopher and religious studies figure who studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School and University College London. He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

nodes.label: Arthur Anthony Macdonell
variants: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・アンソニー・マクドネル
nodes.summary: Arthur Anthony Macdonell (1854–1930) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888 and held posts at Balliol and Corpus Christi College.

nodes.label: LeRoy Carr Barret
nodes.summary: LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and at Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903), where he was taught by Maurice Bloomfield.

nodes.label: Franklin Edgerton
variants: フランクリン・エジャトン
フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.jawiki: フランクリン・エジャートン
nodes.summary: Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Cornell and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, he was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (1926–1953).

nodes.label: Bernhard Geiger
nodes.summary: Bernhard Geiger (1881–1964) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna, Heidelberg, Bonn, and Göttingen. He taught at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), Asia Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

nodes.label: Willibald Kirfel
nodes.summary: Willibald Kirfel was an Indologist who completed his PhD (1904–1908) under Hermann Jacobi and his Habilitation (~1908–1920) at the University of Bonn. He served as librarian at Bonn's university library (1911–1921) before succeeding Jacobi as Bonn's professor in 1922.

nodes.label: Robert Zimmermann
nodes.summary: Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's Jesuit Spirituality Centre and Humboldt University of Berlin (Promotion, 1908–1913). He served as Professor of Sanskrit and ancient Indian philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and headed the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Leiden University
variants: Leiden University, Department of Indo-European Comparative Linguistics (VIET)
Kern Institute, Leiden University, the Netherlands
Kern Institute of Indology, Leiden University

nodes.label: Friedrich Otto Schrader
nodes.summary: Indologist Friedrich Otto Schrader completed his doctorate at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1902). He served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916) and became Professor of Indology at Kiel University in 1921.

nodes.label: Heinrich Lüders
variants: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.jawiki: ハインリヒ・リューダース
nodes.summary: Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and at Munich. He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and the Humboldt University of Berlin, where he was chair from 1909 to 1935.

nodes.label: Edward Joseph Thomas
nodes.summary: Edward Joseph Thomas (1869–1958) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of St Andrews under John Burnet and at the University of Cambridge, where he served as Dean of the Oriental Languages Department (~1909–1939).

nodes.label: Shwe Zan Aung
nodes.summary: Shwe Zan Aung was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891). In 1895, he studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw.

nodes.label: Pe Maung Tin
nodes.native: ဖေမောင်တင်
nodes.summary: Pe Maung Tin worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford, he served at the University of Rangoon as Professor of Pali (1912) and principal (1937–1946), and later as principal of the University of Adult Education (1947).

nodes.label: Benimadhab Barua
nodes.description: Bengali Writer, Indologist, and pundit of Pali and Buddhism (1888-1948)
nodes.summary: Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied across numerous institutions, earning degrees from Krishnath College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of London. He was a lecturer and later professor at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Hakuju Ui
nodes.image: Recent portrait of Dr. Hakuju Ui.jpg
nodes.summary: Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and abroad at Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Komazawa, and Nagoya universities.

nodes.label: Frank Lee Woodward
nodes.summary: Frank Lee Woodward was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his BA and MA at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, and studied under Caroline Rhys Davids. He served as dean at Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated for the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Fyodor Shcherbatskoy
variants: フョードル・シチェルバツコイ
フョードル・イポリトビッチ・シチェルバツコイ
nodes.jawiki: フョードル・イポリトビッチ・シチェルバツコイ
nodes.summary: Fyodor Shcherbatskoy studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Georg Bühler, Hermann Jacobi, and Ivan Pavlovich Minaev. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1900–1941).

nodes.label: Chimanlal Dahyabhai Dalal
nodes.description: Sanskrit scholar and librarian of the Central Library in Baroda

nodes.label: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar
nodes.summary: Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indian historian and Indologist who studied at Ravenshaw, Brojomohun, Ripon, Surendranath, and Presidency colleges, completing his dissertation at the University of Calcutta. He held professorships and administrative roles at Dhaka, BHU, Nagpur, Chicago, and Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: A. B. Gajendragadkar
nodes.summary: A. B. Gajendragadkar worked in Indology. He served as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College and as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

nodes.label: S. Kuppuswami Sastri
nodes.summary: S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at SPG College and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and later held professorships at Presidency College, Chennai, and Annamalai University.

nodes.label: Richard Jay Kohn
nodes.summary: Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988 under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin-Madison
variants: Buddhist studies department at the University of Wisconsin

nodes.label: Geshe Lhundub Sopa
nodes.death_place: Deer Park Buddhist Center and Monastery
nodes.summary: Geshe Lhundub Sopa was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who earned his Lharampa Geshe at Sera Monastery (1941–1962) under teachers including Geshe Lhundrub Thabkhe. He served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 to 1997.

nodes.label: Dor Bahadur Bista
nodes.summary: Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1978–1990) and served on the board of governors of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.

nodes.label: Tribhuvan University
variants: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies of Tribhuvan University

nodes.label: Bruce McCoy Owens
nodes.summary: Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1988) and Wheaton College, where he is attested in 2019 as associate professor of anthropology.

nodes.label: Columbia University
variants: コロンビア大学大学院
Center for Buddhist Studies, Columbia University

nodes.label: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf
nodes.summary: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf (1909–1995) was an anthropologist working in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Vienna and the LSE, was a professor at Osmania University, and held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (1951–1976).

nodes.label: SOAS University of London
variants: School of Oriental and African Studies in the University of London
School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS) of London University
School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London
School of Oriental and African Studies
School of Oriental and African Studies of the University of London
School of Oriental and African Studies, London
ロンドン大学の東洋アフリカ学院
ロンドン大学東洋アフリカ学院

nodes.label: David Llewellyn Snellgrove
nodes.summary: David Llewellyn Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Southampton and Cambridge, including under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Simon, and served as a professor at SOAS, University of London (1950–1982).

nodes.label: Tadeusz Skorupski
nodes.summary: Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London by 1978. He served at SOAS University of London as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Michael Oppitz
nodes.summary: Michael Oppitz is a Tibetologist and anthropologist. He held a position at the Institute for Advanced Study, Berlin (ca. 1987–1988) and served as director at the University of Zurich from ca. 1990 to 2008.

nodes.label: Mark Tatz
nodes.summary: Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (1978) and served as a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Komazawa University
variants: 駒沢大学仏教学部仏教学科

nodes.label: Kazuo Hyodo
nodes.summary: Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, he served as an associate professor at Otani University (~1986–2014) and director at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute (attested 2005–2007).

nodes.label: Kyoto University
variants: 京都大学文学部哲学科
京都大学人文科学研究所
京都大学大学院文学研究科
京大・大学院文学研究科

大谷大学大学院博士課程

nodes.label: Junsho Kato
nodes.summary: Junsho Kato is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, KU Leuven, and under Étienne Lamotte, Juntaka Kato, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura. He served as professor at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Toyo Bunko

公益財団法人東洋文庫
東洋文庫付属ユネスコ東アジア文化センター

nodes.label: Nobuyoshi Yamabe
nodes.summary: Nobuyoshi Yamabe (born 1960) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Osaka University, Otani University, and Yale University (Ph.D. 1999). He held posts at several junior colleges, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and Waseda University (professor 2015).

nodes.label: Shudo Ishii
nodes.summary: Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (BA ~1961–1965; doctorate 1988) and under Shigeo Kamata. His career was spent at Komazawa University, progressing from assistant (1971) to professor (1984, 2014).

nodes.label: Noriaki Hakamaya
nodes.summary: Noriaki Hakamaya is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Komazawa Junior College, Komazawa University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Stanley Weinstein
variants: スタンリー・ワインスタイン
nodes.jawiki: スタンリー・ワインスタイン
nodes.summary: Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, Kodo Sawaki, and Gyokusen Hosaka, he taught at Komazawa, SOAS (1962–1968), and Yale University (1968).

nodes.label: Jikidō Takasaki
nodes.summary: Jikidō Takasaki was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University under V. V. Gokhale, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo and served as president of Tsurumi University (1992–2004).

nodes.label: Waseda University
variants: 早稲田大学大学院文学研究科
早稲田大学文学学術院

早稲田大学感性文化研究所

nodes.label: Kotatsu Fujita
nodes.summary: Kotatsu Fujita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, he studied under scholars including Hajime Nakamura. He served at Osaka University, as professor at Hokkaido University (~1969–1991), and led Sapporo Otani Junior College.

nodes.label: Esho Mikogami
nodes.summary: Esho Mikogami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University until 2003 and was president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

nodes.label: Ryukoku University
variants: 龍谷大学アジア仏教文化研究センター
龍谷大学仏教文化研究所
龍谷大学大学院文学研究科

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Nasu
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Nasu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes serving as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and holding a post at Kongoju (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Ensho Nasu
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Nasu completed a PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under doctoral supervisor Esho Mikogami and also studied under Kei Mikogami.

nodes.label: Shoryu Katsura
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Shoryu Katsura earned degrees from Kyoto University and the University of Toronto. He served as professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015), alongside visiting appointments at Berkeley and Calgary.

nodes.label: Bradford Lyman Phillips
nodes.summary: Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Naropa University, Harvard University (M.T.S., 1993), and the University of Virginia (B.A. 1989; Ph.D. 2004), where he was supervised by David Germano.

nodes.label: David Germano
nodes.summary: David Germano is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He later served as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Cecil Y. Lang
nodes.summary: Cecil Y. Lang (1920–2003) studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Yale (~1949–1951), the University of Chicago (~1967–1970), and the University of Virginia, where he was Professor of English (~1970–1991).

nodes.label: Michael Aris
nodes.summary: Michael Aris was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Durham University and SOAS (PhD) under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. He held positions at the University of Oxford, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Diana L. Eck
nodes.summary: Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her B.A. at Smith College, M.A. at SOAS, and Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Around 1976, she became a professor at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Hopkins
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Hopkins was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, among others. From 1973 to 2005, he served as Associate Professor and center director at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Noritoshi Aramaki
nodes.summary: Noritoshi Aramaki is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who earned doctorates from Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Osaka University and Otani University, and held posts at Kyoto University and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

nodes.label: Shodo Fujita
nodes.summary: Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

nodes.label: Toru Funayama

nodes.label: Taiken Kimura

nodes.label: Ryugen Tanemura

He held professorships at Koyasan University (~2007–2017) and Komazawa University (~2017).

nodes.label: Toru Tomabechi

nodes.label: Somadeva Vasudeva

nodes.summary: Matthew T. Kapstein (b. 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at UC Berkeley and Brown University. He has held faculty posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Birgit Kellner
nodes.summary: Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She received her doctorate from Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura and has held posts at the University of Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Susanne Mrozik
nodes.summary: Susanne Mrozik is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

nodes.label: Western Michigan University
variants: Department of Art, Western Michigan University, Kalamazoo

nodes.label: A. Charles Muller
variants: アルバート・チャールズ・ミュラー
nodes.jawiki: アルバート・チャールズ・ミュラー
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Muller completed his Ph.D. at Stony Brook University. He held positions at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019).

nodes.label: Jan Nattier
nodes.summary: Jan Nattier (b. 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied at Indiana University and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. She held professorships at Indiana University (1992–2005) and Soka University (2004–2010), among other appointments.

nodes.label: Walter Slaje
nodes.summary: Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2020).

nodes.label: John D. Smith
nodes.summary: John D. Smith is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS in 1975 before moving to the University of Cambridge, where he was Lecturer in Sanskrit in 1984 and Professor from 2001 to 2007.

nodes.label: Roland Steiner
nodes.summary: Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. He is attested as an assistant professor at the University of Marburg in 2002.

nodes.label: Dominik Wujastyk
nodes.summary: Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist educated at the University of London and the University of Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1985–2002), UCL (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2015), and the University of Alberta (2015).

nodes.label: Ute Hüsken
nodes.summary: Ute Hüsken (born 1965) is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at Göttingen and completed her habilitation at Heidelberg, holding professorships at the University of Oslo and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Heinz Bechert
variants: ハインツ・ベッヘルト
nodes.jawiki: ハインツ・ベッヘルト
nodes.summary: Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Erich Frauwallner. He served as an assistant at Saarland, Privatdozent at Mainz, and Chair of Indology at Göttingen from 1965 to 2000.

nodes.label: Museum of Asian Art
variants: Museum für Indische Kunst der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin - Preußischer Kulturbesitz

Museum für Indische Kunst in Berlin
Museum of East Asian Art in Berlin

nodes.label: Jeffrey Samuels
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Jeffrey Samuels earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and studied under W. S. Karunatillake. By 2013, he was Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University.

nodes.label: Karen Christina Lang
nodes.summary: Karen Christina Lang is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, later serving as professor at Virginia.

nodes.label: W. S. Karunatillake
nodes.summary: W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was a Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

nodes.label: Kenyu Mitomo
nodes.summary: Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Rissho University, UC Berkeley, and under teachers including Akira Hirakawa. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015).

nodes.label: Minori Nishimura
nodes.summary: Minori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Taisho University (~1971–1976), studying under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, and held posts at the Sanko Cultural Institute (attested 2002) and Taisho University (attested 2002–2008).

nodes.label: Shunkyo Katsumata
nodes.summary: Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held faculty posts at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1944–1982), where he became an emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Koun Kajiyoshi
nodes.summary: Koun Kajiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1928 to 1931 and held an academic post at Taisho University from ~1949 to 1975.

nodes.label: Shindai Sekiguchi
nodes.summary: Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1928 to 1931. He served as a professor at Taisho University (~1968–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1982).

nodes.label: Seiren Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seiren Matsunami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring. He served as a professor at Kyushu University (circa 1950–1967) and Rissho University (circa 1971–1979).

nodes.label: Yasuhiko Nagano
nodes.summary: Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. ~1976–1983). His posts include the National Museum of Ethnology, Berkeley, NIHU, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

nodes.label: Soshū Nishioka
nodes.summary: Soshū Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at International Buddhist University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

nodes.label: Satoru Harada
nodes.summary: Satoru Harada (born 1947) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning an M.A. from the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

nodes.label: Hajime Kitamura
nodes.summary: A linguist and Tibetologist, Kitamura studied under Tokan Tada at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at NINJAL, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Toyo Bunko, and served as president of Reitaku University (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Tokan Tada
nodes.summary: Tokan Tada (1890–1967) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He attended Akita Prefectural Akita High School and earned a geshe degree at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University, and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.id: I:National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics
nodes.label: National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics
Takeshiro Kuraishi
nodes.summary: Takeshiro Kuraishi (1897–1975) was a Sinology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949), worked at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and served as president of the Chinese Linguistics Research Society (~1957–1968).

nodes.label: Akira Suganuma
nodes.summary: Akira Suganuma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962), where he served as an assistant (~1962–1967) and associate professor (1991–1994). He also taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

nodes.label: Kyoshun Todo
nodes.summary: Kyoshun Todo (1916–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Bukkyo University, where he served as associate professor (attested 1962) and professor (attested 1988–1992).

nodes.label: Narimoto Tamayama
nodes.summary: Narimoto Tamayama (1923–2002) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1974 and 1988.

nodes.label: Kodo Nomura
nodes.summary: Kodo Nomura was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He later served as a researcher at Taisho University.

nodes.label: Xianlin Ji
nodes.description: Chinese academic, linguist, historian, translator and university teacher (1911-2009)
nodes.summary: Xianlin Ji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua University and earned his PhD under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg at Göttingen. He served for decades at Peking University, becoming a professor in 1946 and later Life Professor.

nodes.label: Florin Deleanu
variants: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.jawiki: デレアヌ フロリン
nodes.summary: Florin Deleanu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Bucharest, Waseda, and Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, he held professorships at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Zhongxin Jiang
nodes.summary: Zhongxin Jiang worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960-1965), later holding posts at Peking University (~1968-1978), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978-2002), and Soka University (~1999).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Kanno
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Kanno specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo and served as director of the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2001–2009) and vice director at The Institute of Oriental Philosophy (~2011).

nodes.label: Noriyuki Kudo
nodes.summary: Noriyuki Kudo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He has held teaching posts at Bukkyo University and Soka University's International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

nodes.label: Akira Yuyama
nodes.summary: Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Naoshiro Tsuji, Akira Hirakawa, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and held professorships at Soka University.

nodes.label: Michael Zimmermann
variants: ミヒャエル・ツィンマーマン
nodes.summary: Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, whom he later succeeded in 2007, and held posts at the Nepal Research Centre and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Michihiko Yajima
nodes.summary: Michihiko Yajima (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed graduate work at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

nodes.label: Tsurumi University

鶴見大学仏教文化研究所

nodes.label: Reimon Yuki
nodes.summary: Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa (~1924–1927). He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and became professor emeritus at Tokyo and Ryukoku.

nodes.label: Katsumi Mimaki
nodes.summary: Katsumi Mimaki is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University and a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1972–1975), later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010).

nodes.label: Masaaki Noni
nodes.summary: Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts as assistant professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Osamu Hayashima
nodes.summary: Osamu Hayashima works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and researched at the University of Hamburg in 1992. He held posts at Nagasaki University (attested 1979–2003), Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2003–2013), and Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2015).

nodes.label: Akifumi Naito
nodes.summary: Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Jodo Shinshu Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Yuhiko Katsuzaki
nodes.description: Japanese bhikku and Buddhist studies scholar
nodes.summary: Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from ~1964 to 1974. He later served as the president of Taisho University from ~2010 to 2014.

nodes.label: Yoshihiko Sakurai
nodes.summary: Yoshihiko Sakurai works in Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and held appointments as a part-time lecturer there and as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Center for Kyogaku and Dendo (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Kaji
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He held teaching posts at Koyasan, Tamkang, and Osaka universities, later serving as president of Koshien Junior College and professor at Ritsumeikan University.

nodes.label: Kosho Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kosho Kawamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He worked at Toyo University and later taught at Minobusan and Hamamatsu Universities.

nodes.label: Yukimasa Mizutani
nodes.summary: Yukimasa Mizutani (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University. He served as associate professor (ca. 1960–1974) and president (ca. 1979–1989) at Bukkyo University, later leading Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen and Tokai Gakuen.

nodes.label: Hiroo Kashiwagi
nodes.summary: Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–1998) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College.

nodes.label: Jason Birch
nodes.summary: Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney and completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Gareth Sparham
nodes.summary: Gareth Sparham specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and under Ashok Aklujkar at the University of British Columbia (Ph.D.), later teaching Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

nodes.label: Akira Sadakata
nodes.summary: Akira Sadakata is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959) under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris (1963). He was a professor at Tokai University (~1976–2002).

nodes.label: Étienne Lamotte
variants: エティエンヌ・ラモット
エティエンヌ・ラモート
nodes.summary: Étienne Lamotte specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at KU Leuven, Rome under Carlo Formichi, and under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as chargé de cours at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and president at UCLouvain (1950–1959).

nodes.label: Hubert Durt
nodes.summary: Hubert Durt (1936–2018) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He served as professor and editor-in-chief at the EFEO (~1970–2001), director of the Hōbōgirin Institute (~1981–2001), and professor at the ICPBS (~2001–2010).

nodes.label: Mitsuji Fukunaga
nodes.summary: Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He held professorships at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.

nodes.label: Yoshitaka Iriya
nodes.summary: Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi and served as head of Chinese Literature at Nagoya University (1955–1977) and professor at Kyoto University (1970–1974).

nodes.label: Shinjo Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Shinjo Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Supervised by Hajime Nakamura, he studied at the University of Tokyo, lectured at the University at Buffalo, worked at Toyo Bunko, and was a professor at the University of Tsukuba.

nodes.label: Kangei Okamoto
nodes.summary: Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, attended the University of Paris, and held a non-regular appointment at the Tokyo Imperial Household Museum.

nodes.label: Takamatsu Yoshie
nodes.summary: Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Waseda University and the University of Paris. He founded Waseda University and served there as an English teacher, lecturer, professor (from 1915), and Dean of Letters (1930).

nodes.label: Satoshi Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, working under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, and Luis O. Gómez, and became professor (1996) and president (2014) at Kyoto Bunkyo University.

nodes.label: Kyoto Bunkyo University
variants: 京都文教大学人間学部
京都文教大学総合社会学部

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Honjo
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Sakurabe and held academic posts at Kobe Women's University, Otani University (ca. 2005–2017), and Bukkyo University, where he was appointed professor of Buddhism in 2014.

nodes.label: Shizuka Sasaki
nodes.summary: Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University under Jikidō Takasaki. He served as a lecturer, associate professor, and professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University from 1990.

nodes.label: Stephen Jenkins
nodes.summary: Stephen Jenkins specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, alongside several other teachers, and was attested as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (2010–2013).

nodes.label: Masatoshi Nagatomi
nodes.description: Japanese professor of Buddhist studies at Harvard University
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Nagatomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Nagatomi spent his academic career at Harvard University, becoming an instructor in 1958 and professor in 1969.

nodes.label: Malcolm David Eckel
nodes.summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held faculty posts at Harvard (1980–1991) and Boston University (1990–2024).

nodes.label: Donald S. Lopez Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Virginia (~1970–1982) under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding professorial posts at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan (1990).

nodes.label: Charles Hallisey
nodes.summary: Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Colgate, Harvard, University of Pennsylvania, and University of Chicago. He has held faculty appointments at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

nodes.label: Seiji Kimura
nodes.summary: Seiji Kimura (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He later held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Ernst Steinkellner
variants: エルンスト・シュタインケルナー
nodes.summary: Ernst Steinkellner specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. His career includes posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Vienna, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Helmut Krasser
nodes.summary: Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he taught (~1988–2007), and led the Austrian Academy of Sciences' Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Gerhard Oberhammer
variants: G. オーバーハンマー
nodes.summary: Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Innsbruck and the Sorbonne under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. After working at Utrecht University, he served as professor at the University of Vienna from 1964 to 1997.

nodes.label: Keio University
