慶應義塾大学言語文化研究所

nodes.label: Kisho Masanobu
nodes.summary: Kisho Masanobu (born 1950) specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a master's course at Kyoto University (~1973–1975) and served as a part-time lecturer there around 1987.

nodes.label: Yohei Kawajiri
nodes.summary: Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Kawajiri served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as an extraordinary researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Lilian Silburn
nodes.summary: Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Swami Lakshman Joo, and held a post at the CNRS from ~1948 to 1978.

nodes.label: Swami Lakshman Joo
nodes.summary: Swami Lakshman Joo worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan from 1926 to 1933 and founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991.

nodes.label: André Padoux
nodes.summary: André Padoux was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Paris. Supervised by Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe, he was director of the Institut Français de Francfort (~1959–1964) and a researcher and research director at the CNRS (1959, 1982).

nodes.label: Bettina Bäumer
nodes.summary: Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. She completed her doctorate at Munich and studied under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Vienna, the Alice Boner Institute, and IIAS.

nodes.label: Alexis Sanderson
nodes.summary: Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He held research and teaching posts at Merton, Brasenose, All Souls, and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Dominic Goodall
nodes.summary: Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 1995 and also studied with Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. His career includes posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (2000) and EPHE (2005).

nodes.label: Judit Törzsök
nodes.summary: An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Törzsök completed a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She served as associate professor at Lille 3 University (from 2001) and became professor (directeur d’études) at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2018.

nodes.label: Alex Watson
nodes.summary: Alex Watson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson, and held posts at Harvard University, Wolfson College, Oxford, and Ashoka University.

nodes.label: Isabelle Ratié
nodes.summary: Isabelle Ratié is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Paris 1 and EPHE under Alexis Sanderson and Lyne Bansat-Boudon. Her posts include the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig University, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: University of Lucknow
variants: Abhinavagupta Institute of Aesthetics and Śaiva Philosophy

nodes.label: Kei Kataoka
nodes.summary: Kei Kataoka is an Indologist and philosopher who completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo under Hiroshi Marui. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and became an associate professor at Kyushu University around 2007.

nodes.label: Shigeo Kamata
nodes.summary: Shigeo Kamata was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, and ICPBS.

nodes.label: Edward Winslow Bastian
nodes.summary: Edward Winslow Bastian is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, studied with traditional teachers Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and researched at Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Drepung Monastery. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric Monastery, Principal and Director of CIHTS, President of the Association of Indian Universities, and Chancellor of Sanchi University.

nodes.label: Sera Monastery

nodes.label: Seitatsu Matsunami
nodes.summary: Seitatsu Matsunami was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and was attested as a professor at Taisho University in 1992.

nodes.label: Norio Koyama
nodes.summary: Norio Koyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University.

nodes.label: David P. Jackson
variants: ディヴィッド・ポール・ジャクソン
nodes.summary: David P. Jackson is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He taught at Osaka University (1984–1986) and was a professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

Inner Asia Research Project, University of Washington, Seattle

nodes.label: John E. Cort
nodes.summary: John E. Cort is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned a BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and an AM at Harvard University (~1979–1984), later becoming a professor at Denison University (~1993).

nodes.label: Paul Dundas
nodes.summary: Paul Dundas was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he led Asian studies there (~1976–2017) and later headed the Pali Text Society (~2004–2023).

nodes.label: Christoph Emmrich
nodes.summary: Christoph Emmrich specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University by 2004, held an attested post there in 2001, and has served as an assistant professor at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Karnatak University
variants: Museum of Art and Archaeology, Karnatak University, Dharwad

nodes.label: Shubhachandra
nodes.summary: Shubhachandra is an Indologist. He served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Jayandra Soni
nodes.summary: Jayandra Soni worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning doctorates at Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University. He lectured at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and held posts at the University of Innsbruck and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

nodes.label: Royce Wiles
nodes.summary: Royce Wiles works in the field of Indology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Derek F. Maher
nodes.summary: Derek F. Maher specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia (PhD 2003 under Jeffrey Hopkins), he has taught at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Georges B. J. Dreyfus
nodes.summary: Georges B. J. Dreyfus specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at traditional Tibetan monastic colleges and at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving as Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

nodes.label: William Magee
nodes.summary: William Magee specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held a professorship there (attested 1992), and taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Jules Brooks Levinson
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Levinson earned his PhD at the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins. He served as an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Richard B. Martin
nodes.summary: Richard B. Martin is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He served at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Charles D. Orzech
nodes.summary: Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago. He chaired Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998-2006) and was a fellow at the National Humanities Center.

variants: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
The University of North Carolina at Greensboro

nodes.label: Seizan Yanagida
nodes.summary: Seizan Yanagida was a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, and held posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University, and Chubu University.

nodes.label: Richard Gombrich
variants: リチャード・F・ゴンブリッチ
nodes.summary: Richard Gombrich is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his BA and DPhil at Oxford, studying under Walpola Rahula, Gananath Obeyesekere, and Robert Charles Zaehner. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1965–2004).

nodes.label: Gananath Obeyesekere
nodes.summary: Gananath Obeyesekere specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and University of Washington, and held posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000).

nodes.label: Walpola Rahula
nodes.summary: Walpola Rahula was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied in Ceylon, Calcutta, and Paris under Paul Demiéville. He was a professor at Northwestern University, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, and held a post at Oxford.

nodes.label: Sodo Mori
nodes.summary: Sodo Mori (1934–) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Kogen Mizuno, Hajime Nakamura, and Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera. He held professorships at Josai University and Aichi Gakuin University.

愛知学院大学文学部宗教学科

nodes.label: Kazunari Yamakawa
nodes.summary: Kazunari Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Sophia University and a master's program at Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Norihiko Tanaka
nodes.summary: Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku, Bukkyo, and Visva-Bharati universities. He spent his academic career at Bukkyo University, serving as lecturer, associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Shunzo Onoda
nodes.summary: Shunzo Onoda is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his D.Lit. from Bukkyo University in 1993. He also served on the faculty at Bukkyo University, attested as Associate Professor in 1996 and Professor in 2005.

nodes.label: Mark L. Blum
nodes.summary: Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. His academic posts include serving as assistant professor at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and Associate Professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006).

variants: ニューヨーク州立大学

nodes.label: Mitsunobu Nakasone
nodes.summary: Mitsunobu Nakasone specializes in Buddhist studies. Nakasone has held academic appointments at Bukkyo University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Toshinori Ochiai
nodes.summary: Toshinori Ochiai (born 1948) specializes in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kacho Junior College (~1989–2002), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2002–2019), and directed the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons (~2015).

nodes.label: Daishun Ueyama
nodes.summary: Daishun Ueyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He served at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor around 1970–1976 and became its president in 1983.

nodes.label: Akira Fujieda
nodes.summary: Akira Fujieda specialized in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), he worked at its Institute for Research in Humanities, Northwest Institute, and as professor at Kyoto University (1968).

nodes.label: Paul B. Donnelly
nodes.summary: Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral work under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1997) alongside traditional training with Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

nodes.label: Samdhong Rinpoche
variants: サムドン・リンポチェ5世ロブサン・テンジン
nodes.summary: Samdhong Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery and Gyuto Monastery (Geshe degree, 1970). He served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from 1971 to 2001.

nodes.label: Lobsang Gyatso
nodes.summary: Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (1973), heading it from ~1973 to 1997, and founded the College for Higher Tibetan Studies (1991).

nodes.label: Institute of Buddhist Dialectics
variants: Buddhist Dialectic Institute in Dharmsala, India
Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, Dharamsala, India

nodes.label: Hokei Izumi
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist monk and Sanskrit researcher
nodes.summary: Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and later served there as a professor, attested in 1930.

nodes.label: Shoshin Fukihara
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shoshin Fukihara studied at Otani University under Susumu Yamaguchi and at Hōryūji Kangakuin under Join Saeki. He held teaching posts at Otani University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, Shinshu College, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

nodes.label: Otani University Junior College
variants: 大谷大学短期大学部仏教学科

nodes.label: Hoyo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Hoyo Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961). He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1977–2004) and dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 1984–1985).

nodes.label: Yosho Nomura
nodes.summary: Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1935-1939). He served as a professor at Rissho University (~1961-1987) and as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1977-1988).

nodes.label: Koken Sasaki
nodes.summary: Koken Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He held posts at Rissho University as 助教授 (attested 1972), department chair (attested 1982–1985), and Director/Professor (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Senkyo Sakawa
nodes.summary: Senkyo Sakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University, where he later served as a professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985), as well as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

nodes.label: Enshu Kurumiya
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Kurumiya completed a Ph.D. at the Australian National University by 1974. He held a post as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

nodes.label: K. L. Dhammajoti
nodes.summary: K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya (~1985–2004) and held posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and HKU.

nodes.label: Y. Karunadasa
nodes.summary: Y. Karunadasa, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, earned a BA from the University of Ceylon and a PhD from London under David Friedman. He directed the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and was emeritus professor at Kelaniya (~2000).

nodes.label: Yin Shun
nodes.summary: Yin Shun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Academy, Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and Taisho University. He taught at Minnan, Wuchang, Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute, and directed Fawang Buddhist Institute, later presiding over the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Huifeng
nodes.summary: Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at The University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Daniel M. Veidlinger
nodes.summary: Daniel M. Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University in 1999, and held a post at California State University, Chico (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Steven Collins
nodes.summary: Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and held posts at Bristol (~1980–1991) and the University of Chicago (from 1991) as Chester D. Tripp Professor.

nodes.label: Chiang Mai University
variants: Social Research Institute at Chiang Mai University

nodes.label: Hideo Mineshima
nodes.summary: Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Yamagata High School, Taisho University, and Waseda University. He was a longtime professor at Waseda University (1968–1998) and taught at Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1991–2003).

nodes.label: Zenno Ishigami
nodes.summary: Zenno Ishigami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from Taisho University, later serving there as professor. He was president of Shukutoku Junior College (2002-2014) and professor at Shukutoku University.

nodes.label: Susumu Otake
nodes.summary: Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) under Makio Takemura. He has held part-time lecturer posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University, and Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Dan Arnold
nodes.summary: Dan Arnold works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Carleton College, Columbia University, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago, and later taught at McGill University and the University of Chicago Divinity School (2004–2011).

nodes.label: Barbara Stoler Miller
nodes.summary: Barbara Stoler Miller worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Barnard College, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch, she held professorships at Barnard College and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Robert A. F. Thurman
nodes.summary: Robert A. F. Thurman studied at Harvard University (BA, MA, doctorate) and under Ngawang Wangyal and Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies and held professorships at Amherst College and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Albrecht Wezler
variants: アルブレヒト・ヴェッツラー
nodes.summary: Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and headed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and Nepal Research Centre.

nodes.label: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan (1932–2019) was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Hamburg in 1967. He subsequently served there as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Halbfass
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen, later holding posts at Göttingen, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Pennsylvania (1982-2000).

nodes.label: Satoru Noriyama
nodes.summary: Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and studied under Esho Mikogami (attested 1996). Noriyama held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).

nodes.summary: Silvio Vita studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton, specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1996–2008) and taught at Naples, Rome Sapienza, and Kyoto University of Foreign Studies.

nodes.label: Shoshin Ichishima
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Shoshin Ichishima served at Taisho University, where he was Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2014). He was also a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: David B. Gray
nodes.summary: David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe, later serving at Rice University and Santa Clara University.

nodes.label: Ryuichi Abe
nodes.summary: Ryuichi Abe (born 1954) studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia, learning under teachers including Hakeda and Yampolsky. A scholar of Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies, he held professorships at Columbia (1998–2004) and Harvard University (~2003).

nodes.label: Gary A. Tubb
nodes.summary: Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty and teaching appointments at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Ryushin Uryuzu
nodes.summary: Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1955). He worked at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1972–1997).

nodes.label: Ekyo Ejima
nodes.summary: Ekyo Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Göttingen. He held academic posts at Nagaoka University of Technology and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Fernando Tola
nodes.summary: Fernando Tola (1915–2017) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1933–1945). He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1969) and directed the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2017).

nodes.label: Carmen Dragonetti
nodes.summary: Carmen Dragonetti was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the National University of San Marcos. She held posts at the IIBS (1989), the Nyingma Institute (1996), and the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2018).

nodes.label: Tsugunari Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsugunari Kubo was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He served as president of Reiyukai and of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, which he founded.

nodes.label: Tarthang Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarthang Tulku works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968), and founded the Nyingma Institute, Dharma Publishing, and Dharma College.

nodes.label: Yeshe De Project

nodes.label: Takao Kagawa
nodes.summary: Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

nodes.label: Shoju Inaba
nodes.summary: Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Otani University (~1958–1980) and served as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

nodes.label: Kogi Kudara
nodes.summary: Kogi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held a professorship at Ryukoku University (attested 1979) and worked as an editor for the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Michitoshi Barada
nodes.summary: Michitoshi Barada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997), and held posts at Otani University (1992) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (2000–2003).

nodes.label: V. Raghavan
nodes.summary: V. Raghavan (1908–1979) was an Indian Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras, where he served in the Sanskrit Department from 1934 to 1968, and founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

nodes.label: Juro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Juro Watanabe works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held an attested post at the University of Tsukuba from 1989 to 1990.

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu
nodes.summary: Kiyotaka Yoshimizu (born 1958) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer, later holding posts at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004), Tohoku University (~2004–2023), and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Atsushi Uno
nodes.summary: Atsushi Uno worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under Raghunath Giri, T. R. V. Murti, and others. He held posts at Shuchiin, Tokai, Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (attested 1988–1989) universities.

nodes.label: Raghunath Giri
nodes.summary: Raghunath Giri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He served as a department head at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: Keisho Tsukamoto
nodes.summary: Keisho Tsukamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Tohoku University. He held professorial posts at Rissho University and Tohoku University, and later served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (circa 1992–2002).

東北大学印度学仏教史研究室

nodes.label: Endo Asai
nodes.summary: Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held professorships at Nihon Fukushi University, Minobusan University (serving as president 1998–2001), and Rissho University (1972–1997).

nodes.label: Noriaki Inoue
nodes.summary: Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from around 1949 to 1953 and later served there as a professor.

nodes.label: Ensho Kanakura
nodes.summary: A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Kanakura earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1923–1929) and Rissho University (~1959–1974), and became president of Miyagi University of Education in 1967.

nodes.label: Shuyu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Shuyu Sakurai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943). He later served at Komazawa University from around 1949 to 1987, where he was an emeritus professor.

nodes.label: Takushu Sugimoto
variants: すぎもと・たくしゅう
nodes.summary: Takushu Sugimoto works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, and others, later supervised by Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha. He taught at Kanazawa, Komazawa, and Kinjo Universities.

nodes.label: Yutaka Takagi
nodes.summary: Yutaka Takagi (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1948–1951) and served as a professor at Rissho University (~1968–1999).

Tsuguhito Takeuchi
nodes.summary: Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and Indiana University (PhD 1980–1994), where his doctoral supervisor was Christopher I. Beckwith, and served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).

nodes.label: Hisashi Sato
nodes.summary: Hisashi Sato (1913–2008) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (~1933–1936), he was a professor there (1968), at Komazawa University, and at Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1976–1986).

nodes.label: Tatsuo Nishida
nodes.summary: Tatsuo Nishida was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (1948–1956; doctorate 1962). He spent his career at Kyoto University (1956–1992) and later served at the National Center for Science Information Systems (1992–1994).

nodes.label: Helmut Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin (PhD under Heinrich Lüders) and Marburg. Hoffmann held positions at the Prussian Academy, the Ahnenerbe, Hamburg, the University of Munich, and Indiana University.

nodes.label: Christopher I. Beckwith

nodes.jawiki: クリストファー・ベックウィズ
nodes.summary: Christopher I. Beckwith is a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Ohio State and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, he was appointed professor of Central Eurasian studies at Indiana University in 1982.

nodes.label: Takao Moriyasu
nodes.summary: Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Osaka University, and held professorships at Osaka University (1994–2012) and Kindai University (2012–2015).

nodes.label: Tokio Takata
nodes.summary: Tokio Takata (born 1949) specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences. His career includes posts at Otaru University of Commerce, Kyoto University, and Fudan University.

nodes.label: Nobumichi Kusumoto
nodes.summary: Nobumichi Kusumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

nodes.label: Hideyo Ogawa
nodes.summary: Hideyo Ogawa (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University (~1973–1981), where he later served as an assistant professor (~1989–1998) and professor of Indian Philosophy (~1998–2019).

nodes.label: Yoshihito Muroji
nodes.summary: Yoshihito Muroji (born 1954) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held faculty positions at Koyasan University and Shiga University of Medical Science.

nodes.label: Robert Kritzer
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kritzer completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini by 1995. He was an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

ノートルダム女子大学

nodes.label: Kazufumi Oki
nodes.summary: Kazufumi Oki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

nodes.label: Hiromi Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He taught Nobumichi Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, including lecturer (attested 1987) and an affiliation attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Toshihiko Kimura
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Kimura (born 1940) specializes in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Tohoku University (~1959–1963), he held posts at Tokai Gakuin University (~1978–1988), Tohoku University as a part-time lecturer, and International Buddhist University (~2011).

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Chigusa

nodes.label: Shujun Motegi
nodes.summary: Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and Kyoto University, and later served as a Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University (attested 1998, 2010).

nodes.label: Beatrix Pfleiderer

nodes.label: Tsultrim Kelsang

nodes.label: Kiyotaka Kimura

nodes.label: Eli Franco

nodes.label: Xinchuan Huang

nodes.summary: Stefano Zacchetti (1968–2020) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned his BA and PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice under Alfredo Cadonna. He held professorships at Soka University and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Bunga Fukui
nodes.summary: Bunga Fukui (1934–2017) worked in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Maxime Kaltenmark, and Rolf A. Stein, later serving as professor at Waseda (~1978–2004).

nodes.label: Anthony W. Barber
nodes.summary: Anthony W. Barber specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1984 and held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1998.

nodes.label: Wolfgang Schamoni
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Schamoni is a Japanologist who studied at Waseda University and earned his doctorate at the University of Bonn (~1968–1974). He held posts at the universities of Munich and Marburg before serving as professor at Heidelberg University from 1985 to 2006.

nodes.label: Ryoshu Koda
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Koda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Koda held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Toda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and served as a professor at Tokushima University from circa 1980 to 2000.

nodes.label: Junkichi Imanishi
nodes.summary: Junkichi Imanishi (born 1935) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hokkaido University, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (professor and director), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: University of Minnesota

ミネソタ大学高等研究所

nodes.label: Wei Pachow
nodes.summary: Wei Pachow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Shoyu Hanayama
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shoyu Hanayama studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1950 to 1954. He later served as vice president of Musashino University (~1968–1995) and chairperson of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (~1987–1995).

nodes.label: Chiyong Kim
nodes.summary: Chiyong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at International Buddhist University and Shitennoji Junior College (both attested 1976).

nodes.summary: Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later served on the faculty at Ryukoku University (attested 1956, 1976) and as a professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Eisei Kojima
nodes.summary: Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1976) and as president of Doho University (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Shunpaku Nakao
nodes.summary: Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he was an assistant professor in 1963 and a professor in 1976.

nodes.label: Ryōshō Taira
nodes.summary: Ryōshō Taira (1906-1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Taisho University, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 1976 and further attested in 1984.

nodes.label: Kanchu Onoue
nodes.summary: Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Tetsuei Sato
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Tetsuei Sato studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Keizai University (~1968–1974), and served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1968–1982).

nodes.label: Minoru Hara
nodes.summary: Minoru Hara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Harvard, and Cambridge. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1960–1991) and served as President of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2006).

nodes.label: Keiichi Miyamoto
nodes.summary: Keiichi Miyamoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1966 to 1997 under Minoru Hara. He was a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (1975) and taught at Kokugakuin University (1986–1995).

nodes.label: Karl H. Potter
nodes.summary: Karl H. Potter worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California (~1946–1950) and at Harvard University (1955) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1971) and the University of Washington (~1971–1997).

nodes.label: Hara Prasad Sastri
nodes.summary: Hara Prasad Sastri (1853–1931) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and as Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

nodes.label: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel
nodes.summary: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist. He served as head of the Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1989) and worked in the Oriental Department of the Prussian State Library (attested 1992–1994).

nodes.label: Shobha Rani Dash
variants: ダシュ・ショバ・ラニ
nodes.summary: Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was a researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and is attested as a lecturer at Otani University in 2012.

nodes.label: Makoto Yoshimura
nodes.summary: Makoto Yoshimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1993–2000) and held an assistant professorship at Komazawa University (~2004).

nodes.label: Jien Abe
nodes.summary: Jien Abe was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973) and served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

nodes.label: Ryogon Fukuhara
nodes.summary: Ryogon Fukuhara (1909-2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937-1940), under Shun'ichi Takagi, Ryťjō Yamada, and Ryotai Hatani. He lectured at Berlin and served as professor at Ryukoku (attested 1963-1974).

nodes.label: Meiji University
variants: 明治大学大学院文学研究科博士課程
明治大学大学院文学研究科史学専攻

nodes.label: Noboru Karashima
nodes.summary: Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Taisho University.

nodes.label: Taijun Inokuchi
nodes.summary: Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served at Ryukoku University as a lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987), and led the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Yusen Kashiwahara
nodes.summary: Yusen Kashiwahara (1916–2002) specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University from around 1937 to 1941 and later served there as a professor from circa 1964 to 1987.

nodes.label: Shuyu Kanaoka
nodes.summary: Shuyu Kanaoka specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952) and earning a doctorate from Toyo University in 1962. He served as an associate professor at Toyo University from around 1961 to 1992.

nodes.label: Hiromu Kitanishi
nodes.summary: Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University and later served as a professor there (~1968–1991).

nodes.label: Masahiro Kusunoki
nodes.summary: Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University. He later served as chair professor of religious studies and history of religion at Tohoku University from circa 1974 to 1985.

nodes.label: Encho Tamura
nodes.summary: Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities. He served on the faculty at Kyushu University (1941–1980), as professor at Kumamoto University (~1977–1982), and directed the Kyushu Historical Museum.

nodes.label: Yoshiro Tamura
nodes.summary: Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, later serving as professor at Toyo, Rissho, and the University of Tokyo (chair in Japanese Buddhism, 1972–1982).

nodes.label: Joryu Chiba
nodes.summary: Joryu Chiba was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He held multiple posts there, serving as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor emeritus (1970–1989), alongside leadership roles at the Historical Society of Ryukoku University and other institutions.

nodes.label: Kyosho Hayashima
nodes.summary: Kyosho Hayashima (1920–1987) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested as a lecturer at Yokohama City University and associate professor at Toyo University in 1962, he later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).

nodes.label: Nagaoka University of Technology
variants: 長岡技術科学大学工学部

nodes.label: Yukei Matsunaga
nodes.summary: Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University, and held positions at Koyasan University, serving as director in 1983, and Shuchiin University.

nodes.label: Satoshi Hayashima
nodes.summary: Satoshi Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Nagasaki University
variants: 長崎大学 教育学部

nodes.label: Michihiko Komine
nodes.summary: Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1974). He served at Taisho University as an assistant (~1974–1980) and professor (~1993–2016), and headed the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies in 2015.

nodes.label: Junzo Inagaki
nodes.summary: Junzo Inagaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section head at the Otani University Library.

nodes.label: Giyu Nishi
nodes.summary: Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui, Junjirō Takakusu, Masaharu Anesaki, Makoto Nagai, Taiken Kimura, and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1926) and Toyo University (from 1927).

nodes.label: Seishin Kato
nodes.summary: Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University, Taisho University, and Toyo University, while also teaching at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University.

nodes.label: Yukio Sakamoto
nodes.summary: Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held posts at Toyo University and Rissho University, where he served as dean and president.

nodes.label: Koshiro Tamaki
nodes.summary: Koshiro Tamaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (DLitt 1959). He held posts at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University, and Nihon University (1979–1986).

nodes.label: Takeo Warita
nodes.summary: Takeo Warita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi.

nodes.label: Nobuo Otsuka
nodes.summary: Nobuo Otsuka (born 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

nodes.label: Takayasu Kimura
nodes.summary: Takayasu Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1978) and held posts at Taisho University and the Institute of Contemporary Mission of Shingon Buddhism Buzan-ha.

nodes.label: Masahiro Takano
nodes.summary: Masahiro Takano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University and served there as a librarian (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Keiya Noguchi
nodes.summary: Keiya Noguchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (circa 1978–1984) and held teaching and administrative posts at Shuchiin University (attested 1995–2005) and Taisho University (attested 1995–2017).

nodes.label: Takashi Maeda
nodes.summary: Takashi Maeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He was attested as a lecturer at Taisho University in 1995 and 2006.

nodes.label: Mitsutoshi Moriguchi

nodes.label: Hideomi Yaita
nodes.summary: Hideomi Yaita (born 1953) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (1991–1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (1995).

nodes.label: Shinya Moriyama
nodes.summary: Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2002–2006), later teaching at Shinshu University (~2008).

nodes.label: Shinshu University
variants: 信州大学人文学部心理学科

nodes.label: Hiroshi Marui
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. His posts include lecturer at Musashino Women's Junior College and associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).

nodes.label: Atsushi Kanazawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was a lecturer at the Meteorological College (attested 1986–1989) and an assistant professor and faculty member at Komazawa University (~1996–~2004).

nodes.label: Yoichi Fukuda
nodes.summary: Yoichi Fukuda (born 1955) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a senior researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).

nodes.label: Péter-Dániel Szántó
nodes.summary: Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, he has been a fellow at All Souls College and held posts at Oxford and Eötvös Loránd University.

nodes.label: William M. Gorvine
nodes.summary: William M. Gorvine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Connecticut College (B.A.) and the University of Virginia (M.A., Ph.D.), completing his doctorate under David Germano alongside teachers such as Jeffrey Hopkins.

nodes.label: Sara L. McClintock
nodes.summary: Sara L. McClintock is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD, 2002). Her academic appointments include posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.

nodes.label: John B. Carman
nodes.summary: John B. Carman (born 1930) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He served as director at Harvard University (attested 1999) and director of the Center for the Study of World Religions.

nodes.label: A. K. Ramanujan
nodes.summary: A. K. Ramanujan worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned degrees from Maharaja's College, Mysore and Indiana University, and was a long-serving professor at the University of Chicago (1962–1993).

nodes.label: Elliot Sperling
nodes.summary: Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a Tibetologist and historian. Educated at Queens College, CUNY, and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn Struve, he served on the faculty at Indiana University (1987–2015) and held posts at Harvard and Delhi.

nodes.label: Takashi Ogawa
nodes.summary: Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He became an assistant professor at Komazawa University in 1991.

nodes.label: Kenji Kinugawa
nodes.summary: Kenji Kinugawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1972 to 1980 and under Seizan Yanagida from circa 1976 to 1984.

nodes.label: Kyoko Fujii
nodes.summary: Kyoko Fujii, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo. She held professorships at Yokohama City University (~1989–1995), Hamamatsu University (~1995–1999), Hokkaido University (~1999–2008), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2008).

nodes.label: Kenryo Minowa
nodes.summary: Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toho Kenkyukai, Aichi Gakuin University, University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and became board chairman of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies in 2023.

nodes.label: Shogo Watanabe
nodes.summary: Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1972–1982) and later served there as a faculty member (~1989–1999) and professor (~1999).

nodes.label: Takanori Kimura
nodes.summary: Takanori Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held positions as a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996) and as chief priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Gyoei Takahashi
nodes.summary: Gyoei Takahashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2003–2004) and as a researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Shun'ei Mori
nodes.summary: Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Kaiten Nukariya
nodes.description: Religious scholar and ordained Zen Buddhist monk
nodes.summary: Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Sendan-Rin, Komazawa University, and Keio University. He lectured at Harvard and spent his career at Soto-shu/Komazawa University, serving as its first president from 1925 to 1934.

nodes.label: Kansai University

nodes.label: Nathmal Tatia
nodes.summary: Nathmal Tatia (born 1919) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).

nodes.label: Rita M. Gross

She spent most of her career at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire (~1973–1998) and served as head of Women and Religion at the AAR.

nodes.label: Shunpei Ueyama
nodes.summary: Shunpei Ueyama was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University (1941–1943). He later became a professor and emeritus professor at Kyoto University, director of the Kyoto National Museum, and president of Kyoto City University of Arts.

nodes.label: Gustav Roth
nodes.summary: Gustav Roth was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle, Munich, and Patna under teachers including Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

nodes.label: Reinhold Grünendahl
nodes.summary: Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and at the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Petra Kieffer-Pülz
nodes.summary: Petra Kieffer-Pülz specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Heinz Bechert (~1985–1991) and served as a research fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz (attested 2013, 2016).

nodes.label: Sen Wang
nodes.summary: Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University from circa 1931 to 1935 and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1952 to 1991.

nodes.label: Syed Hasan Askari
nodes.summary: Syed Hasan Askari was a historian and Indologist who studied at Langat Singh College and Patna University. He later served as the Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.

nodes.label: Anantalal Thakur
nodes.summary: Anantalal Thakur was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at the Mithila Sanskrit Research Institute (~1955-1974) and as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968-1971).

nodes.label: Tilmann Vetter

nodes.summary: Tilmann Vetter was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna studying under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel. In 1974, he was appointed professor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Minoru Kiyota
nodes.summary: Minoru Kiyota was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa, and served as Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1966 to 2013.

nodes.label: John P. Keenan
nodes.summary: John P. Keenan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held posts at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and Middlebury College (attested 1989 and 2006).

nodes.label: Paul Loren Swanson
nodes.summary: In Buddhist and religious studies, Paul Loren Swanson studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He served as a professor at Nanzan University from circa 1986 to 2021.

nodes.summary: Kogen Mizuno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who received a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Komazawa University, serving as Komazawa's president in 1976.

nodes.label: Horst Lasic
nodes.summary: Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999, served as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995), and lectured at Vienna in 1999.

nodes.label: Taiken Kyuma
nodes.summary: Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).

nodes.label: Akira Omine
nodes.summary: Akira Omine worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kyoshi Takahama and at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Yumi Nakamoto
nodes.summary: Yumi Nakamoto focuses on Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She held a post as a research fellow (公募研究員) at Ryukoku University in 2012 and also studied there as a researcher (研究生, attested 2014).

nodes.label: Jokai Hiraoka
nodes.summary: Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1948) and Kyoto University (~1948–1953). He served as a professor at Otemae University (~1966–1989) and taught at Shuchiin University (~1989–1999).

nodes.label: Ryosei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Ryosei Fukuda (1937-2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and taught Ryuichi Abe. He served as professor (1973) and professor emeritus (2007) at Taisho University, visiting professor at Shuchiin University (2012), and led several Buddhist institutes.

nodes.label: Ryōjin Soga
nodes.summary: Ryōjin Soga (1875–1971) studied at Otani, Shinshu, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. In Buddhist studies and philosophy, he taught at Toyo and served extensively at Otani University, including as professor, professor emeritus (1951), and 17th president (1961–1967).

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1996) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn in 1930. He held faculty posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

nodes.label: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar
nodes.summary: Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) was an Indologist and philosopher. Formerly the principal of Sir Parashurambhau College, he served as a professor and Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

nodes.label: Hajime Nakamura
nodes.summary: Nakamura studied Indology and Buddhist philosophy at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui, succeeding him in 1943. He taught at Tokyo until 1973, served as a visiting professor at Stanford, and directed the Eastern Institute.

nodes.summary: Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and holds a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.label: Robert H. Sharf
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Sharf earned his B.A. at the University of Toronto, studied at Kyoto University, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez. His career includes posts at McMaster, Michigan, and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Janet Gyatso
nodes.jawiki: ジャネット・ギャツォ
nodes.summary: Janet Gyatso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. After earning her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley, she taught at Amherst College (1987–2001) and Harvard University, where she became Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2001.

nodes.label: Champa Thupten Zongtse
nodes.summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse (born 1934) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he is attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer as attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Hidenori Sakuma
nodes.summary: Hidenori Sakuma specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held positions at International Buddhist University, Taisho University, and the University of Tsukuba.

nodes.label: Huimin
nodes.summary: Huimin (born 1954) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served as a professor at Taipei National University of the Arts, executive director at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and president of DILA (2014–2022).

nodes.label: Erich Heintel
nodes.summary: Heintel was a philosophy scholar who completed his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held posts there as extraordinary professor (1952) and ordinary professor of philosophy (1960–1982).

nodes.label: Tsuyoshi Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Tsuyoshi Yokoyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Kanoko Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kanoko Tanaka specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied under Acharya Tulsi and served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Acharya Tulsi
nodes.description: Indian Jain Guru, author, religious leader, founder of Anuvrat movement (1914–1997)

nodes.label: Takayoshi Namikawa
nodes.summary: Takayoshi Namikawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at Bukkyo University. He was a professor (appointed 1981) and later emeritus professor (2018) at Bukkyo University, also holding posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Hokkaido University.

nodes.label: Geshe Lozang Jamspal
nodes.summary: A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Lozang Jamspal studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. His appointments include the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Delhi, and the Columbia University faculty (attested 1985–1990).

nodes.label: Lisa Grumbach
nodes.summary: Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Stanford University, attested in 1996, and served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Shinya Yasutomi
nodes.summary: Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University, earning a doctorate in literature in 1998. He was a professor at Otani University (~1985–2010, 2014) and directed the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Ryoichi Kondo
nodes.summary: Ryoichi Kondo (1930-2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Geshe Rabten
nodes.description: tibetan Buddhist geshe born in Tibet
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Geshe Rabten studied at Sera Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, earning his Geshe Lharampa degree (~1940–1959). He later taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

nodes.label: Paul Groner
nodes.summary: Paul Groner, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD from Yale University. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–1996, 2009–2010).

nodes.label: Christian Lindtner
nodes.summary: Christian Lindtner (1953–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

nodes.label: Migmar Tsering
nodes.summary: Migmar Tsering (d. 1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Khenpo Appey. He served as Sa skya expert at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1990) and was Head of Sakya College (attested 1991–1997).

nodes.label: Joseph Hackin
nodes.summary: Joseph Hackin was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Sciences Po, INALCO, EPHE, and the University of Paris. He served as conservator at the Musée Guimet (1913–1941) and directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan beginning in 1934.

nodes.label: René Grousset
nodes.summary: René Grousset was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian-Central Asian studies, and sinology who studied at the University of Montpellier. He taught Jeannine Auboyer and held posts at the Louvre, École du Louvre, École Libre des Sciences Politiques, Musée Guimet, and Musée Cernuschi.

nodes.label: Bunzaburo Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Bunzaburo Matsumoto (1869–1944) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Rikkyo University, First Higher School, and Kyoto University (1906–1929), later directing its Institute for Research in Humanities.

nodes.label: Shoson Miyamoto
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Shoson Miyamoto studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa University, Toyo University, and Waseda University.

nodes.label: Giei Honda
nodes.summary: Giei Honda (1888–1953) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (-1914). He served at Kyoto University as lecturer (1929) and assistant professor (1934–1948), and later held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.

nodes.label: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Visva-Bharati University, serving as a collation supervisor and later Principal, and served as the Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Giuseppe Tucci
variants: ジュゼッペ・トゥッチ
nodes.jawiki: ジュゼッペ・トゥッチ
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca, and at Visva-Bharati, Dhaka, and Banaras Hindu universities. He held professorships at Sapienza and led the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

nodes.label: Shuntarō Matsuyama
nodes.summary: Shuntarō Matsuyama, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He held lecturer posts at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, and Tama Art University, and was a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design.

nodes.id: I:Joshibi University of Art and Design
nodes.label: Joshibi University of Art and Design
Rikizan Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1962 to 1973 and later served there as Professor of Buddhist Studies from circa 1975 to 1997.

nodes.label: Shuken Ito
nodes.summary: Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his education, including a doctorate in 2000, at Komazawa University, where he also held appointments from research assistant in 1976 to professor in 1991.

nodes.label: Masashi Nagai
nodes.summary: Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1965–1969, doctorate 1998) and later served there as a lecturer (1984), associate professor (1988, 1994), professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019).

nodes.label: Peter N. Gregory
variants: ビーター・N・グレゴリー
ピーター・N・グレゴリー
nodes.summary: Peter N. Gregory is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD from Harvard (1981). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Kuroda Institute, Komazawa University, and Smith College (attested 2005).

nodes.label: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
variants: Japan House at the University of Illinois

nodes.label: Rosan Ikeda
nodes.summary: Rosan Ikeda (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1960–1969). He held successive academic positions at Komazawa University from 1969 to 2012, including Professor (1983–2012), and became head of the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

nodes.label: Ichiro Katayama
nodes.summary: Ichiro Katayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa and Otani universities under Kogen Mizuno. He held a post at Komazawa University (1975–2013) and served as board chairman of the Society for the Study of Pali and Buddhist Culture.

nodes.label: Tatsugen Sato
nodes.summary: Tatsugen Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University by 1978. He held teaching positions at Komazawa University (attested 1972–1978, 1994), Ryukoku University (attested 1974), and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Morten Schlütter
variants: モルテン・シュルター
nodes.summary: Morten Schlütter specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and earned his PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, later holding academic posts at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, Wisconsin–Madison, and the University of Iowa.

nodes.label: Shigeki Kudo
nodes.summary: Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (~1959–1965) and as an associate professor at International Buddhist University (~1967–1974) and Shuchiin University (~1974–1985).

nodes.label: Makoto Kitada
nodes.summary: Makoto Kitada is an Indologist and linguist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Halle. He held a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

nodes.label: Ven. Dhammapāla
nodes.summary: Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, having also studied under traditional teacher Bhante Dhammasakkaro.
