nodes.label: Yutaka Ochihara
nodes.summary: Yutaka Ochihara (1923–1991) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania, studying under Louis Renou, Atsuuji Ashikaga, W. Norman Brown, and Armand Minard. He held posts at Kyoto University and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Hideaki Nakatani
nodes.summary: Active in Indology and Buddhist studies, Nakatani studied under Gadjin M. Nagao at Kyoto University and completed a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.

nodes.label: Louis Renou
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Louis Renou studied under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch at EPHE and Paris. He held professorships and directorships at the University of Lyon, EPHE, Sorbonne University, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the Institut de civilisation indienne.

nodes.label: Vincent Eltschinger
nodes.summary: Vincent Eltschinger, working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Lausanne (PhD under Tom Tillemans) and Vienna. He served at the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, including as interim director (2014–2015), and joined EPHE around 2015.

nodes.label: Danielle Feller
nodes.summary: Danielle Feller is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2001 under Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.

nodes.label: Yael Bentor
nodes.summary: Yael Bentor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University, where Gregory Schopen was her doctoral supervisor, she held a teaching post in Indian Studies at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
variants: Center for the Study of Christianity der Hebräischen Universität Jerusalem
Franz Rosenzweig Minerva Research Center for German-Jewish Literature and Cultural History

nodes.label: David Dean Shulman
nodes.description: Israeli-American indologist, historian of religion, and poet
nodes.summary: David Dean Shulman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earned his Ph.D. from the University of London under John Ralston Marr. He held multiple editorial and directorial posts at Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Lydia Aran
nodes.description: Professor emerita:Hebrew University of Jerusalem/scholar of Buddhism (1921–2013)

nodes.label: Thubten Jigme Norbu
nodes.image: Thubten Jigme Norbu, The Dalai Lama opens art exhibit in Tokyo, 1967 (cropped) (cropped).jpg
nodes.description: lama, writer, civil rights worker, university and college faculty member
nodes.summary: Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Geshe Ngawang Nyima. He served as director at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1970–1972) and Professor at Indiana University (1965–1992).

nodes.label: Patrick Olivelle
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Indologist and Sanskrit scholar (born 1942)
nodes.summary: Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1969–1972) and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1974) under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin (from 1991).

nodes.label: Gregory Schopen
variants: グレゴリー・ショペン
nodes.summary: Gregory Schopen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Black Hills State, McMaster, Washington, and ANU under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, he held professorships at Indiana, UT Austin, and UCLA.

nodes.label: Dan Martin
nodes.summary: Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University, studying under Elliot Sperling, and held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

nodes.label: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche
nodes.summary: In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Dudjom Rinpoche, Kangyur Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and others. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1960–1970), Kyoto University (1960–1970), and the University of Virginia (~1980).

nodes.label: Shoren Ihara
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Shoren Ihara served as an assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, and attested again in 1977). He was later a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

nodes.label: Ryōshū Matsushita
nodes.summary: Ryōshū Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama. He held a lecturing post at Ryukoku University (attested in 1987).

nodes.label: Fukuoka Human Rights Center
variants: 福岡県人権啓発情報センター

nodes.label: Yutaka Iwamoto
nodes.summary: Yutaka Iwamoto (1910–1988), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga, Toru Haneda, Gyoyu Tokiwai, and Hidenaka Tanaka, and later under Naoshiro Tsuji. He taught at Kyoto, Tokai, Tokyo Science, Kyoto Tachibana, and Soka universities.

nodes.label: Gherardo Gnoli
nodes.description: Italian historian of religions and Iranologist (1937–2012)
nodes.summary: Gherardo Gnoli (1937–2012) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome. He taught at Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and served as president of ISMEO (~1979–1995).

nodes.label: Mauro Maggi
nodes.summary: Mauro Maggi is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", served as a researcher at the University of Hamburg (1990), and held posts at IsMEO and Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Tatsuhiro Saito
nodes.summary: Tatsuhiro Saito is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

nodes.label: Yasuo Sano
nodes.summary: Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996). He founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

nodes.label: Toshio Sako
nodes.summary: Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and Ekyo Ejima, and at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: Anna-Pya Sjödin
nodes.summary: Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University by 2007 under doctoral supervisors Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.

nodes.label: Gunilla Gren-Eklund
nodes.summary: Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Stig Wikander. She held a post at Uppsala University from around 1986 to 2003.

nodes.label: Jonardon Ganeri
nodes.summary: Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford (D.Phil. under Bimal Krishna Matilal). He has held professorships at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, New York University, and the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: K. Venugopalan
variants: K・ヴェーヌゴーパラン

nodes.label: Toshihiro Wada
nodes.summary: Toshihiro Wada (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and held academic appointments at Nagoya University as an associate professor (~1990–2002) and professor (~2002–2020).

nodes.label: Tadashi Tani
nodes.summary: Tadashi Tani is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1970–1977), did domestic study at Kyoto University (1995) under Yuichi Kajiyama, and served as professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (~1988–2006).

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
nodes.label: National Institute of Technology, Kochi College
variants: 高知工業高等専門学校

nodes.label: Ryudo Fujii
nodes.summary: Ryudo Fujii, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kosuke Nakazawa
nodes.summary: Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Rissho University and as a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra, both attested in 2001.

nodes.label: Karl Jettmar
nodes.summary: Karl Jettmar worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, earning his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1936–1941). He held positions at Weltmuseum Wien (~1948–1958), the University of Vienna (1958), Mainz (1961), and Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

nodes.label: Gérard Fussman
nodes.summary: Gérard Fussman was a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1961–1965). Succeeding Jean Filliozat, he served as a professor at the Collège de France beginning in 1984.

nodes.label: Ahmad Hasan Dani
nodes.description: Pakistani intellectual, archaeologist, historian, and linguist (1920–2009)
nodes.summary: Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar in archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Mortimer Wheeler, Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, and A. S. Altekar, holding posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities.

nodes.label: Hideo Murai
nodes.summary: Hideo Murai is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as a professor at Otani University and served as a committee member for the Otani Academic Society.

nodes.label: Klaus Mylius
variants: クラウス・ミューラーダイス
nodes.summary: Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and his habilitation at Leipzig University. He lectured in Sanskrit philology at Leipzig (1970–1991) and taught at Frankfurt, Bayreuth, and Göttingen.

nodes.label: Gessho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He spent his career at Otani University as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925), succeeding Bunyiu Nanjio.

nodes.label: Koichi Hokazono
nodes.summary: Koichi Hokazono is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Bonn and earned his PhD at Kyushu University. He was a professor at The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991, 1997–2000).

nodes.label: Ryuken Sato
nodes.summary: Ryuken Sato (1931–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. Attested in 2014, he served as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Akitoshi Saito
nodes.summary: Akitoshi Saito is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Taisho University as professor (attested 1982) and professor emeritus (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Institute for Zen Studies
variants: Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zen Bunka Kenkyūsho)
Research Institute for Zen Culture (Zenbunka kenkyujo)

nodes.label: Yumi Katayama
nodes.summary: Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Geshe Lobsang Tharchin
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Lobsang Tharchin studied at Gyume Tantric Monastery and earned his Lharampa Geshe degree at Sera Monastery by 1953.

nodes.label: Meiji Yamada
nodes.summary: Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962), where he later served as a professor (attested 1963, 2007).

nodes.label: Frank-Richard Hamm
nodes.summary: Frank-Richard Hamm was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, later lecturing there (1948–1964) and becoming a professor at the University of Bonn in 1965.

nodes.label: Daniel Cozort
nodes.summary: Daniel Cozort is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and served on the faculties of Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988).

nodes.label: Yeshe Thupten
nodes.summary: Yeshe Thupten worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught Daniel Cozort, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and Joe Bransford Wilson, and held appointments as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (1982) and Middlebury College (1982).

nodes.label: Geshe Palden Drakpa
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Geshe Palden Drakpa served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi (attested 1987–1992, 2004) and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987.

nodes.label: Shaoyong Ye
nodes.summary: Shaoyong Ye works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan and served there as an associate professor (attested 2010–2016).

nodes.label: Qing Duan
nodes.description: Chinese scholar of Indian and Iranian languages; Professor of Indo-Iranian Studies and Boya Chair Professor of Peking University
nodes.summary: Qing Duan worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji and Zhongxin Jiang, earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, and was a professor at Peking University.

nodes.label: Zhaohua Yang
nodes.summary: Zhaohua Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang held a post at Stanford University (attested 2007) and served on the faculty at Columbia University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Stanford University
variants: Zentrum für biomedizinische Ethik der Universität Stanford

nodes.label: Shinsho Hanayama
nodes.summary: Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1959) and held professorships at Toyo University and Kokugakuin University.

nodes.label: Naoshiro Tsuji
nodes.summary: Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford under Takakusu, Macdonell, Geldner, and Lévi. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1942–1960).

nodes.label: Paul Hacker
nodes.summary: Indologist and philosopher Paul Hacker studied in Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin. He held a professorship at Mithila Sanskrit Research Institute (1954) and chairs for Indology at the University of Bonn (1955–1963) and University of Münster (1963–1978).

nodes.label: Michael Friedrich
nodes.summary: Michael Friedrich is a Sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1978–1984), where he also worked as an assistant (1983–1986). He served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

nodes.label: Jowita Kramer
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Kramer studied under Lambert Schmithausen at Hamburg (PhD ~2004) and completed her habilitation at Munich. She taught at Munich (2017–2021) before becoming professor and institute head at Leipzig University in 2021.

nodes.label: Masaru Akimoto
nodes.summary: Masaru Akimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University, including as professor of the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002, 2015).

nodes.label: Sergey Oldenburg
variants: セルゲイ・フョードロウィッチ・オルデンブルク
セルゲイ・フョードロヴィチ・オルデンブルク
セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.jawiki: セルゲイ・オルデンブルク
nodes.description: Russian scholar of Sanskrit and Buddhism (1863-1934)
nodes.summary: Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at Saint Petersburg State University. He became a professor there, led the Imperial Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum.

nodes.label: George R. Elder
nodes.summary: George R. Elder is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, attested in 1978.

nodes.label: Ikuhisa Takigawa
nodes.summary: Ikuhisa Takigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University.

nodes.label: Angelika Krebs
nodes.summary: Philosopher Angelika Krebs studied at Freiburg, Oxford, Konstanz, Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt, earning her PhD under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt (1993–2001), and the University of Basel (2001), holding the Lehrstuhl für Praktische Philosophie.

nodes.label: Thomas A. Tweed
nodes.summary: Thomas A. Tweed is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Stanford University, supervised by William R. Hutchison, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill from ~1993 to 2008.

nodes.label: William A. Clebsch
nodes.description: American church historian, developer of religious studies, and university professor (1923-1984)

nodes.label: Robert E. Buswell Jr.
nodes.summary: Robert E. Buswell Jr. (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kusan Sunim and completed his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and others. He was a professor at UCLA (~1994–2022).

nodes.label: Luis O. Gómez
variants: Luis O. GÓMEZ ルイス・ゴメス
nodes.description: Puerto Rican buddhologist, translator and psychologist
nodes.summary: Luis O. Gómez specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler and degrees from Michigan and Puerto Rico. He served as department chair and professor at the University of Michigan and academic director at Mangalam Research Center.

nodes.label: Van Austin Harvey
nodes.image: Van A. Harvey and a dog.jpg
nodes.summary: Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Occidental, Yale, and Princeton Seminary. He chaired programs at Southern Methodist University and the University of Pennsylvania, and was a professor at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Gordon D. Kaufman
nodes.summary: Gordon D. Kaufman worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. Kaufman held positions at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and served as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity at Harvard University beginning in 1963.

nodes.label: Carl Bielefeldt
nodes.summary: Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, earning his PhD at UC Berkeley in 1980. He held an editorial board post at Stanford University (~1980–2017).

nodes.label: William R. Hutchison
nodes.summary: William R. Hutchison was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Oxford and Yale. He held posts at Yale, Hunter College, American University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison before joining Harvard University in 1968.

nodes.label: Kurtis R. Schaeffer
nodes.summary: Kurtis R. Schaeffer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and a PhD from Harvard, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp. He taught at Alabama before joining the University of Virginia in 2005.

nodes.label: Genta Ikeda
nodes.summary: Genta Ikeda was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University and became a professor emeritus at Nara University of Education around 1965.

nodes.label: Chishō Namai
nodes.summary: Chishō Namai (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1996) and president (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Jagdish Kashyap
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Jagdish Kashyap studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and Vidyalankara Pirivena. He taught Pali at Banaras Hindu University, founded Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, and was professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965).

nodes.label: Satkari Mookerjee
variants: サトカリ・ムカージー
サトカーリ・ムケルジー
nodes.summary: Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1944–1955) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

nodes.label: John Brough
nodes.summary: Indologist John Brough studied at Edinburgh under A. B. Keith and at St John's College, Cambridge, under H. W. Bailey. He held posts at SOAS, served as Professor of Sanskrit at London (1948–1967), and was Professor at Cambridge (1967–1984).

nodes.label: Chitai Takenaka
nodes.summary: Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (graduating in 1968) and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and Tokoha Gakuen University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Hideki Kiyoshima
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Kiyoshima studied at the University of Delhi and was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.

nodes.label: Jun Takashima
nodes.summary: Jun Takashima (born 1955) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Minoru Hara at the University of Tokyo. He later held posts at Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (Professor, 2020).

nodes.label: Muneo Tokunaga
variants: Muneo Tokunaga (徳永 宗雄, Tokunaga Muneo)
nodes.summary: Muneo Tokunaga was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD, ~1974–1979). He served as assistant professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology and Kyoto University, later becoming a professor at Kyoto University (~1995–2009).

nodes.label: Yasumasa Sekine
nodes.summary: Yasumasa Sekine specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1969–1975) and SOAS (~1982–1984). He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Nobuyuki Watase
nodes.summary: Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Tokai University and later as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Katsuhiko Kamimura
nodes.summary: Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras (1971–1973) under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He taught as an associate professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (1988–2003).

nodes.label: Michio Yano
nodes.summary: Michio Yano (born 1944) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Kyoto University and Brown University under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and David Pingree, and was a professor in the Faculty of Cultural Studies at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

nodes.label: Issei Suzuki
nodes.summary: Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.

nodes.label: Ryoshu Michihata
nodes.summary: Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1989) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Otani University from circa 1925 to 1928. He later held posts at Otani University (~1949–1969) and Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1970–1979).

nodes.label: Mizumaro Ishida
nodes.summary: Mizumaro Ishida (1917–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Tokai University, an affiliation attested in 1976 and 1987.

nodes.label: Rosemarie Fuchs
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Fuchs (born 1950) is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche
variants: mKhan po Tshul khrims rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: In Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Lama Zolpa Trinlé. He served as principal teacher at Rumtek Monastery's shedra and as spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery in 1992.

nodes.label: Tenzin Dorjee
nodes.summary: Tenzin Dorjee works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Geshes Lobsang Tsephel, Sonam Rinchen, and Dawa. He served as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Allen Wright Thrasher
nodes.summary: An Indologist, Thrasher completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1969–1977) alongside traditional Indian teachers, and later worked at the Library of Congress (~1986).

nodes.label: Daniel H. H. Ingalls
variants: ダニエル・インゴールス
nodes.summary: Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine and Walter Eugene Clark, and under Kalipada Tarkacharya. He held a junior fellowship and later professorships at Harvard (circa 1958–1999).

nodes.id: I:Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute
nodes.label: Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute
variants: Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute
Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute
Deccan College Post-graduate and Research Institute

nodes.label: Stefan Anacker
nodes.summary: Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1964 to 1970 under the direction of Alex Wayman.

nodes.label: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry
nodes.description: Kannada writer, lexicographer, grammar expert, critic and editor
nodes.summary: T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (born 1933) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Mysore, where his supervisors included D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak, and served there as lecturer (1968) and Professor (1984–1994).

nodes.label: University of Mysore
variants: Institute of Kannada Studies, University of Mysore
Department of Jainology and Prakrits, University of Mysore
Kuvempu Institute of Kannada Studies at the university

nodes.label: Jacques May
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Jacques May served as editor-in-chief for Hōbōgirin and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1981). He later served as professor at the University of Lausanne (~1976–1992).

nodes.label: Richard Hugh Robinson
nodes.summary: Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Alberta and the University of London. After teaching at the University of Toronto, he became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1961.

nodes.label: Kyojun Shimizutani
nodes.summary: Kyojun Shimizutani (1891–1979) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He served as professor at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and as abbot of Sensō-ji (~1952–1979).

nodes.label: Manabendu Banerjee
nodes.summary: Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist. He served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society and was the DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: John D. Dunne
nodes.summary: John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and philosophy. After earning his PhD at Harvard under Nagatomi and Eckel, he held posts at Emory University (~2005–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999).

nodes.label: Margaret R. Miles
nodes.summary: Margaret R. Miles studied at San Francisco State University and the Graduate Theological Union. A scholar of religious studies and history, she held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and served as dean at the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

nodes.label: James W. Benson
nodes.summary: James W. Benson is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts as Assistant Professor in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

nodes.label: National Institute of Japanese Literature
variants: 国文学研究資料館文献資料部

nodes.label: Tokyo Woman's Christian University
variants: 東京女子大学文理学部

nodes.label: Leela Aditi Wood
nodes.summary: Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She completed a PhD at the University of Michigan (until 2005) under doctoral supervisors Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College.

nodes.label: Walter M. Spink
nodes.summary: Walter M. Spink was an Indologist and art historian educated at Amherst College and Harvard University (PhD 1954). He taught at Brandeis University before serving as a professor at the University of Michigan from around 1961 to 2000.

nodes.label: Thomas E. Crow
nodes.summary: Crow studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and was appointed Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at NYU in 2007.

nodes.label: Marvin Eisenberg
nodes.summary: Marvin Eisenberg was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954). He served on the faculty at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1993.

nodes.label: Cyrus Stearns
nodes.summary: Cyrus Stearns works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA under Turrell V. Wylie and his PhD under Leonard van der Kuijp at the University of Washington, also studying under several traditional teachers, and became a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

nodes.label: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche
variants: Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che, Ngag dbang legs bshad rgya mtsho
Bco brgyad Khri chen Rin po che
nodes.summary: Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kunga Chophel, Zimwok Rinpoche, and Geshe Tshechok (1929), and later taught Cyrus Stearns, Warren Lee Todd, and David P. Jackson, among others.

nodes.label: Jong-Nam Choi
nodes.summary: Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the International Buddhist University and completed a PhD in 1998 at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying with Albrecht Wezler, David Seyfort Ruegg, and S. A. Srinivasan.

nodes.label: International Buddhist University
variants: 四天王寺国際仏教大学

nodes.label: David Seyfort Ruegg
nodes.summary: David Seyfort Ruegg (1931–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Sorbonne University under Jean Filliozat, Louis Renou, Marcelle Lalou, and Rolf A. Stein. He held chairs and professorships at Leiden, Washington, Hamburg, and SOAS.

nodes.label: Edward Garrett
nodes.summary: Edward Garrett (1971–) is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at UCLA (~1996–2001) under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, with postdoctoral mentoring from Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Carson Schütze
nodes.summary: Carson Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997 and took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

nodes.label: Dominique Sportiche
nodes.summary: Dominique Sportiche (born 1952) is a linguist who completed his studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology around 1979 to 1984. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1987.

nodes.label: Anna Szabolcsi
nodes.summary: Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and earned her Ph.D. at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, where she was a research fellow (~1978–1989). She later served as professor at UCLA (~1990–1998) and New York University (~1999).

nodes.label: Naomi Appleton
nodes.summary: Naomi Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner. She was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University and joined the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Lancaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies in Lancaster
The Institute for Philosophy and Public Policy, Lancaster University

nodes.label: Laurie L. Patton
nodes.summary: Laurie L. Patton (1961–) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (~1986–1991) and held posts at Emory University (~1996–2011), Duke University (~2011–2015), and Middlebury College, serving as president from 2015 to 2024.

nodes.label: Anna Aurelia Esposito
nodes.summary: Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg University and completed an MA at the University of Tübingen (1998). She served as assistant professor to the Chair of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

nodes.label: Jonathan Geen
nodes.summary: Jonathan Geen is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

nodes.label: Phyllis Granoff
nodes.summary: Phyllis Granoff is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Radcliffe College and Harvard University (PhD ~1973), she served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Lex Hixon Professor of World Religions at Yale University (2004).

nodes.label: McMaster University
variants: Department of Religious Studies at McMaster

nodes.label: Shoshin Higuchi
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Shoshin Higuchi served as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 1998) and as a committee member for the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Myoshin Fujitake
nodes.summary: Myoshin Fujitake works in Buddhist studies. He has served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as a committee member at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Ryusei Keira
nodes.summary: Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Keira studied at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans, completing a thesis by 2003.

nodes.label: Koichi Shinohara
nodes.summary: Koichi Shinohara works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as Professor at McMaster University (~1973–2004), coordinator of the Numata Program at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004), and Senior Lecturer at Yale University (~2004).

nodes.id: I:Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture
nodes.label: Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture
Hidetomo Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Hidetomo Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has held several posts at Taisho University, serving as a researcher (1998), research student (2006), lecturer (2008), and chief research fellow (2017).

nodes.label: University of Texas at Austin
variants: The University of Texas at Austin
テキサス大学オースティン校

nodes.label: Hiroko Matsuoka
nodes.summary: Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Sueki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied briefly under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library (~1988–1989). He held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1980–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996, ~2008).

nodes.label: Michael Torsten Much
nodes.summary: Michael Torsten Much is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991). He has held a fellowship at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Helmut Tauscher
nodes.summary: Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held positions as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Zeff Bjerken
nodes.summary: Zeff Bjerken is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held a post at the College of Charleston.

nodes.label: T. Griffith Foulk
nodes.summary: T. Griffith Foulk, specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology, earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1978–1987) under Luis O. Gómez. He taught at Michigan (~1987–1995) and Sarah Lawrence College, where he became Riggs Professor of Religion (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. Trained at Menri and other monasteries, he founded Menri and Triten Norbutse monasteries, serving as lopön at both, and held visiting scholar posts at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

nodes.label: Makoto Nagai
nodes.summary: Nagai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Toyo (~1914–1944), Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon (~1944–1960), and Kamakura Women's University (~1960–1970).

nodes.label: Shun Hidaka
nodes.summary: Shun Hidaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a research post at Otani University's Buddhism and Art Research Center in 2012 and served as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

nodes.id: I:Buddhism and Art Research Center, Otani University
nodes.label: Buddhism and Art Research Center, Otani University
Rajendra Chandra Hazra
nodes.summary: Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka under Sushil Kumar De. He held teaching posts at Jagannath University and the University of Dhaka, and was Associate Professor at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

nodes.label: Sushil Kumar De
nodes.summary: Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist educated at Presidency College, Calcutta, SOAS, and Bonn. He held positions at Presidency College, Calcutta, Dhaka, Sanskrit College, Jadavpur University, and the University of London.

nodes.label: Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar
nodes.summary: Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1939–2001) and as Professor of Sanskrit and Dean of Arts at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Izumi Hoshi
nodes.summary: Izumi Hoshi is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. She has held posts at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, including assistant professor and director.

nodes.label: Michiyo Hoshi
nodes.summary: Michiyo Hoshi is a researcher in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa as a collaborative researcher and at Toyo Bunko as a researcher (attested 2003).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa
nodes.label: Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa
variants: アジア・アフリカ言語文化研究所

nodes.label: Ngawang Thondup
variants: ガワン・トゥンドゥプ

nodes.label: Temba Gyaltsen
variants: テンバ・ギェンツェン

nodes.label: Jitsushyu Oshika
nodes.summary: Jitsushyu Oshika (b. 1919) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and later held a professorship at Toyo University, attested in 1980–1981.

nodes.label: Yasuo Goto
nodes.summary: Yasuo Goto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held lecturing posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Esho Sasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an assistant professorship at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and a professorship at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Ronald Y. Nakasone
nodes.summary: Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies as an assistant professor (~1987) and at the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Hirofumi Isoda
nodes.summary: Hirofumi Isoda (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966), where he served as a lecturer (~1970–1976) and associate professor (~1976–2002).

nodes.label: Werner Abraham
nodes.summary: Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He held positions at the University of Illinois (~1966–1967), Tübingen (1970–1971), and a professorship at the University of Groningen from 1971.

nodes.label: Tarab Tulku
nodes.summary: Tarab Tulku worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen and served as a curator at the Royal Danish Library (~1967–2000).

nodes.label: Hartmut Buescher
nodes.summary: Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Chandrabhāl Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.

nodes.label: Burkhard Quessel
nodes.summary: Burkhard Quessel is a scholar of Tibetology and indology who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member in 1997. Between 2002 and 2012, he was attested as a curator at the British Library.

nodes.label: British Library
variants: British Library’s Oriental and India Office Collections

nodes.label: Kenneth G. Zysk
nodes.summary: Kenneth G. Zysk specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and Australian National University, holding posts at UCLA, Eastern Michigan University, the universities of Wisconsin-Madison and Toronto, and Copenhagen.

nodes.label: Christian K. Wedemeyer
nodes.summary: Christian K. Wedemeyer (born 1969) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his MA and PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, and later taught at the University of Copenhagen (2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (~2003).

nodes.label: Ole Holten Pind
nodes.summary: Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna in 2009 under the supervision of Ernst Steinkellner.

nodes.label: John Newman
nodes.summary: John Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

nodes.id: I:Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Center for Kyogaku and Dendo
nodes.label: Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Center for Kyogaku and Dendo
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派教学伝道研究センター

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Ueno
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He held a post as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Eric David Mortensen
nodes.summary: Mortensen, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under supervisors Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, alongside several other teachers.

nodes.label: Kimberley C. Patton
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies, she completed her dissertation at Harvard University. She was an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and Assistant Professor in the Comparative and Historical Study of Religion at Harvard (~1993).

nodes.label: Christopher S. George
nodes.summary: Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Royal W. Weiler in 1965, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972), and taught at IASWR (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Joe Bransford Wilson
nodes.summary: Joe Bransford Wilson is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 1984). He taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and became Associate Professor of Asian Philosophy and Religion at UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

nodes.label: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin
nodes.summary: Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Moscow State University and under George de Roerich. He held positions at the Institute of Oriental Studies and Moscow State University.

nodes.label: Ryojun Mitomo
nodes.summary: Ryojun Mitomo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Raghu Vira
nodes.summary: Raghu Vira (1902–1963) was an Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned degrees from Punjab, London, and Leiden. He founded the International Academy of Indian Culture and headed the Sanskrit department at Sanatan Dharma College (~1934–1946).

nodes.label: Lokesh Chandra
nodes.jawiki: ローケーシュ・チャンドラ
nodes.summary: Lokesh Chandra is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Raghu Vira, he held long-term leadership posts at the International Academy of Indian Culture, ICCR, and ICHR.

nodes.label: Richard F. Nance
nodes.summary: Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 2004. As attested in 2013, he served as Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University.

nodes.label: Makio Ueno
nodes.summary: Makio Ueno specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Otani University by 2009 and served there as an assistant professor (attested 2010–2012) and staff member (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Toshio Horiuchi
nodes.summary: Toshio Horiuchi (born 1977) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2009) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2011–2017) and Zhejiang University (~2018).

nodes.label: Atsushi Ibuki
nodes.summary: Atsushi Ibuki studied at Waseda University and works in Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies
Tomoyuki Komine

nodes.label: Ruriko Sakuma

nodes.label: Daiju Sasaki
nodes.summary: Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from roughly 1996 to 2007. His attested positions in 2015 include part-time lecturer at Taisho University and full-time lecturer in sectarian studies at Chisan Denpōin.

nodes.label: Fumio Shoji
nodes.summary: Fumio Shoji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University, where he also served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies in 2015.

nodes.label: Kenta Suzuki
nodes.summary: Kenta Suzuki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1994–1998) and Kyoto University (~1999–2007), and was an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College circa 2011.

nodes.label: Nobumasa Miyazaki
nodes.summary: Nobumasa Miyazaki (born 1978) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 2009. He held posts at Toyo University, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Masahide Mori
nodes.summary: Masahide Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Nagoya University and SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, and Kanazawa University.

nodes.label: Tsutomu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Hokkaido University. He held an affiliated researcher post at the Eastern Institute (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Hotta
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Hotta is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and served as an administrator at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Steven Neal Weinberger
nodes.summary: Steven Neal Weinberger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his BA at Amherst and his MA and PhD (2003) at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding an attested post there in 2006.

nodes.label: Ralf Kramer
nodes.summary: Tibetologist Ralf Kramer studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson (~1992–1997). In ~2008, he served as Aris Librarian for Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library.

nodes.label: Achim Bayer
nodes.summary: Achim Bayer is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his MA under David P. Jackson and his PhD from the University of Hamburg (2005) under Lambert Schmithausen. He was a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).

nodes.label: Lore Sander
nodes.summary: Lore Sander specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. She held posts at the Museum of Asian Art, Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and University of Munich.

nodes.summary: Arjo Vanderjagt (born 1948) works in philosophy and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Groningen (1971–1981), he held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

nodes.label: Seiji Kumagai

nodes.label: Takatsugu Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takatsugu Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), Sendai National College of Technology (attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College (attested 2015).

nodes.summary: Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at Kyoto University (1944–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (ca. 1957–1961), and worked as a library-track assistant at Kyoto University from around 1951 to 1984.

nodes.label: Kenji Shimada
nodes.summary: Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) worked in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1941 and later held a researcher post there from circa 1945 to 1981.

nodes.label: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu
nodes.summary: Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Third Higher School and Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Kyoto City University of Arts, and visited Harvard.

nodes.label: Serinity Young
nodes.summary: Serinity Young worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and studied with Vidya Dehejia, later holding posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History in 2000.

nodes.label: Carole McGranahan
nodes.summary: Carole McGranahan is an anthropologist and Tibetologist who studied at Colgate and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. She joined the University of Colorado as Assistant Professor of Anthropology (~2001–2009).

nodes.label: Nicholas Dirks
nodes.summary: Nicholas Dirks (born 1950) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Wesleyan University and the University of Chicago, he held academic posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), the University of Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia University (~1997–2013).

nodes.label: Ann Laura Stoler
nodes.summary: Ann Laura Stoler works in history and archaeology. Educated at Barnard College and Columbia University, she taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and the University of Michigan (1989–2004), becoming chair of anthropology at The New School in 2004.

nodes.label: Dawa Norbu
nodes.summary: Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) was a Tibetology and history scholar. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at San Francisco State University, the University of San Francisco, CIIS, and served as professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2006).

nodes.label: Join Saeki
nodes.summary: Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Sadatomo Chihaya. He held posts at Hōryū-ji, Hōryūji Kangakuin, the Imperial Academy, and the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Shoko Takeuchi
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoko Takeuchi studied at Ryukoku University. He later served as an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University, attested between 1987 and 1995, and was also attested there in 2009.

nodes.label: Yasutoshi Murakami

nodes.label: Guangchang Fang

nodes.label: Michael J. Walsh
nodes.summary: Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town (B.Soc.Sc., ca. 1986–1989) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (M.A., ca. 1991–1994), completing doctoral work under William F. Powell.

nodes.label: Yasuke Ikari

nodes.label: Kiyoshi Okano
nodes.summary: Kiyoshi Okano (born 1957) works in Indology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. At Kyushu University, he served as associate professor (attested 2002) and professor (attested 2013–2024).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Pāsādika

nodes.label: Barbara Nimri Aziz
nodes.summary: Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and a Ph.D. from SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran 1 in 2007.

nodes.label: Aung San Suu Kyi
nodes.native: အောင်ဆန်းစုကြည်
nodes.image: Aung San Suu Kyi at the Enthronement of Naruhito (1).jpg
nodes.description: former State Counsellor of Myanmar and Leader of the National League for Democracy
nodes.summary: Aung San Suu Kyi studied in Tibetology and other fields at Lady Shri Ram College, the University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS. She held a post at the United Nations from 1969 to 1971.

nodes.label: Kojiro Yoshikawa
nodes.summary: Kojiro Yoshikawa was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and as 理事長 of Toho Gakkai (~1973–1980).

nodes.label: Tokuryu Yamauchi
nodes.summary: Tokuryu Yamauchi (1890–1982) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and at the University of Freiburg under Martin Heidegger. He held posts at Kyoto Institute of Technology, Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, Kyoto University of Education, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Ludwig Alsdorf
nodes.summary: Ludwig Alsdorf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studying under Walther Schubring and Heinrich Lüders at Hamburg and Berlin. He taught at the universities of Allahabad, Berlin, and Münster, before holding the chair of Indian history and culture at Hamburg (1950–1972).

nodes.label: Annemarie von Gabain
nodes.summary: Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1930), later holding posts there (~1935–1944) and as a professor at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1966).

nodes.label: Johannes Nobel
nodes.summary: Johannes Nobel (1887–1960) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate under Heinrich Lüders at Berlin, worked at the Prussian State Library and Berlin, and held the Indology chair at Marburg from 1928 to 1955.

nodes.label: Guy Newland
nodes.summary: Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and studied under teachers including Donald S. Lopez Jr., later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University.

nodes.label: Harvey B. Aronson
nodes.summary: Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-director at Dawn Mountain Center (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Shunei Tsuboi
nodes.summary: Shunei Tsuboi was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963 and 1972).

nodes.label: Honsho Ueda
nodes.summary: Honsho Ueda (1937–) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and director of the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Shoku Bando
nodes.summary: A researcher in Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoku Bando studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held appointments at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

nodes.label: Shōdō Yamagami
nodes.summary: Shōdō Yamagami studied at Kyoto University (~1962–1964) and worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from around 1971 to 2005.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Kuroda
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Kuroda specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1976 and served as an associate professor at Osaka Gakuin University (~1983) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (attested 1988).

nodes.label: Osamu Takata
nodes.summary: Osamu Takata was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Baiei Henmi and served as head of the art department at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

nodes.label: Baiei Henmi
nodes.description: Japanese historian of Indian and Buddhist art
nodes.summary: Baiei Henmi was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University and held a post at Tama Art University.

nodes.label: Bimal Krishna Matilal
nodes.summary: Bimal Krishna Matilal (1935–1991) worked in philosophy and Indology. Educated at University of Calcutta and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, he taught at University of Toronto (~1968–1977) before serving as Oxford's Spalding Professor of Eastern Religion and Ethics (1977–1991).

nodes.label: Colette Caillat
nodes.description: French professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar (1921–2007)
nodes.summary: Colette Caillat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at CNRS, University of Lyon, Sorbonne University (1967–1988), and directed the Institut de civilisation indienne (~1980–1993).

nodes.label: Nancy Hock
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Nancy Hock earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1987) under Joanna Gottfried Williams. She held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky
nodes.summary: Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Fergusson College. He founded the Archeology Research Group in 1951 and served as Associate Director (1976–1996) and director emeritus of research (~1974–2005) at the AIIS.

nodes.label: Lewis Lancaster
nodes.jawiki: ルイス・ランカスター
nodes.summary: Lewis Lancaster (born 1932) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson and Edward Conze. He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–1998) and University of the West (1992).

nodes.label: Joanna Gottfried Williams
nodes.summary: Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) was an Indologist and art historian educated at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. She served on the faculty as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1971 to 2007.

nodes.label: Debala Mitra
nodes.summary: Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

nodes.label: Kōichi Kozaka
nodes.summary: Kōichi Kozaka is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University, attested in 1991.

nodes.label: M. N. Srinivas
nodes.summary: M. N. Srinivas (1916–1999) was an Indologist. He studied under M. H. Krishna, G. S. Ghurye, Radcliffe-Brown, and Evans-Pritchard, and held posts at Oxford, Baroda, Delhi, the Institute for Social and Economic Change, and NIAS.

Institute for Social and Economic Change, Bangalore

nodes.label: Govind Sadashiv Ghurye
nodes.summary: Govind Sadashiv Ghurye was an Indologist who studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. He served as Head of Sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

nodes.label: W. H. R. Rivers
nodes.description: English anthropologist, neurologist, ethnologist and psychiatrist (1864-1922)
nodes.summary: W. H. R. Rivers was a British scholar of history and archaeology. After medical studies at St Bartholomew's and the University of London, he worked at several hospitals, taught at Cambridge and UCL, and served as president of the Anthropological Society of London.

nodes.label: Peter Haskel
nodes.summary: Peter Haskel works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

nodes.label: Bruce John Stewart
nodes.summary: Bruce John Stewart studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Sakya College in 1978 and earned a PhD from Columbia University under Alex Wayman, Joel Peter Brereton, and Christopher S. George.

nodes.label: John Gombojab Hangin
nodes.summary: John Gombojab Hangin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana universities, he held posts at Johns Hopkins, UC Berkeley, Georgetown, Columbia, and was a full professor at Indiana University (1965–1989).

nodes.label: Francis Woodman Cleaves
nodes.description: American orientalist historian. mongolist and sinologist (1911-1995)
nodes.summary: Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth, Harvard, and under Paul Pelliot, later serving as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

nodes.label: Brian Gregory Baumann
nodes.summary: Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Indiana University in 2005 under the doctoral supervision of György Kara.

nodes.label: György Kara
nodes.summary: A scholar of linguistics and Central Asian studies, Kara studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh and Lajos Ligeti. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and as Professor at Indiana University (1992–2022).

nodes.label: Stephen R. Bokenkamp
nodes.summary: Stephen R. Bokenkamp is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1978–1986). He taught Classical Chinese at Indiana University (~1986–2007) and later served as Professor of Chinese in Religious Studies at Arizona State University (~2007).

nodes.label: Maho Iuchi
nodes.image: Maho Iuchi in the video 'From teaching networks to reincarnation The transformation of Kadampa monasteries in early Tibet'.png
nodes.summary: Maho Iuchi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University (~2002–2008) and served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2010).

nodes.description: American professor emeritus of medicine and the creator of the Stress Reduction Clinic and the Center for Mindfulness in Medicine
nodes.summary: Jon Kabat-Zinn works in religious studies and medicine, having studied at Haverford College and MIT, alongside meditation training under Philip Kapleau, Thich Nhat Hanh, and Seungsahn Haengwon. He founded UMass Memorial Medical Center and held posts at UMass Chan Medical School.

nodes.label: Philip Kapleau
nodes.summary: Philip Kapleau was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, Soen Nakagawa, and Sogaku Daiun Harada, and founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

nodes.label: Ming-Wood Liu
nodes.summary: Ming-Wood Liu works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned a BA at the University of Hong Kong (1966–1974) and a PhD at UCLA (1974–1979) under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Robert C. Epp, later becoming Professor at HKU (~1979).

nodes.label: Akira Miyaji
nodes.summary: Akira Miyaji specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his degrees at Nagoya University (~1964–1991) and held posts at Hirosaki University, Nagoya University (~1976–2007), Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and Ryukoku University (2013).

nodes.label: Etsuaki Teraishi
nodes.summary: Etsuaki Teraishi works in Indology and philosophy. He held an assistant professorship at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and served as a special researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Dipak Kumar Barua
nodes.summary: Dipak Kumar Barua (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 1987, he served as a postgraduate dean at the University of Calcutta, and from circa 1996 to 2006 he held a post as head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

nodes.label: Saswati Mutsuddy
nodes.summary: Saswati Mutsuddy works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Dipak Kumar Barua and was a member of the teaching staff in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Jacob P. Dalton
nodes.summary: Jacob P. Dalton (born 1969) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1996–2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held posts at Yale (2005), SOAS (~2005–2008), and UC Berkeley (~2008).

nodes.label: Yutaka Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Yutaka Kawasaki specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seio Okuda and held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024).

nodes.label: Patrick McAllister
nodes.summary: Patrick McAllister is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2004–2011) under doctoral supervisor Helmut Krasser and teachers Karin Preisendanz and Ernst Steinkellner.

nodes.label: Mai Mishiro
nodes.summary: Mai Mishiro is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies with posts attested at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2011) and Waseda University (2016).

nodes.label: Junko Matsumura
nodes.summary: Junko Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the Australian National University (MA, 1980) and the University of Göttingen (doctoral dissertation, 1990), and was attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2011.

nodes.label: Henk Bodewitz
nodes.summary: Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who completed his degrees and PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He taught Sanskrit at Utrecht University (assistant professor 1966, chair 1976–1992) and held associate (ca. 1971–1976) and full professorships (1992–2002) at Leiden University.

nodes.label: Yusho Miyasaka
nodes.summary: Yusho Miyasaka (1921–2011) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University under Shoko Watanabe, later holding professorships at Koyasan University and Nagoya University, as well as posts at Chisan Denpōin and Shuchiin University.

nodes.label: John R. McRae
nodes.description: born:1947-04-28|died:2011|; McRae, John R., 1947-2011; McRae, John R.
nodes.summary: John R. McRae was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held teaching posts at Cornell (~1988–1995), Indiana University (~1996–2005), and Komazawa University (~2006–2008).

nodes.label: Ryōshō Tanaka
nodes.summary: Ryōshō Tanaka (1933–2016) studied at Komazawa University and researched Buddhist studies and sinology. He became a professor, dean, museum director, and president (2009) at Komazawa, and held posts at Ryukoku University and the Soto Zen Research Center.

nodes.label: Shinten Sakai
nodes.summary: Shinten Sakai (1913–1968) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He held posts at Koyasan University, where he is attested as a professor in 1970.

nodes.label: Chikyo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1988) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980).

nodes.label: Shinjo Hinonishi
nodes.summary: Shinjo Hinonishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He served at Koyasan University as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Shintaro Kitano
nodes.summary: Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He has held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Akira Mukai
nodes.summary: Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant (~1974–1980), and was later a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Klaus Wille
nodes.summary: Klaus Wille is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. His posts include positions at the University of Göttingen (attested 1996), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009, 2018–2020).

nodes.label: Hironori Tanaka
nodes.summary: Hironori Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and also held a post there.

nodes.label: Yuto Kawamura
nodes.summary: Yuto Kawamura is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University from 2015 to 2018 and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013-2020) and the University of Oxford (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Laura Harrington
nodes.summary: Laura Harrington is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, as well as Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., and several other teachers.

nodes.label: Satoshi Ito
nodes.summary: Satoshi Ito (born 1961) works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1990 and served as a professor at Ibaraki University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Osamu Izumoji
nodes.summary: Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Charles Goodman
nodes.summary: Charles Goodman is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard. He is an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Allan Gibbard
nodes.description: American philosopher and social choice theorist
nodes.summary: A philosopher, Gibbard earned degrees from Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and served as a professor at the University of Michigan (1977–2016).

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Furuta
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Furuta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes serving as editor and publisher at the Otani Academic Society (attested 1991) and as dean at Otani University (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Stephen F. Teiser
nodes.summary: Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religion who earned his degrees at Oberlin College and Princeton University. He has spent his career at Princeton University, where he became D. T. Suzuki Professor in Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Franciscus Verellen
nodes.summary: Franciscus Verellen specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as director of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

She conducted postdoctoral research at Ca' Foscari, the Sorbonne, and Kansai University, and became Associate Professor at Kyoto University in 2003.

nodes.label: François Lachaud
nodes.summary: François Lachaud (born 1965) works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, where he is attested as a professor in 2008 and with an affiliation attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Michael Puett
nodes.summary: Michael Puett is a historian, sinologist, and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (ca. 1987–1994) studying under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu. In ca. 1994, he joined the faculty at Harvard University.

nodes.label: Jean-Noël Robert
nodes.summary: Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied under Bernard Frank. He worked at the CNRS, served as a director of studies at EPHE, and held a professorship at the Collège de France (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Satoshi Kawano
nodes.summary: Satoshi Kawano specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

nodes.label: Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies
Nobukatsu Komai
nodes.summary: Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Paul G. Hackett
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Paul G. Hackett studied at Columbia University. He held positions at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

nodes.label: Masaaki Chikusa
nodes.summary: Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees, including a doctorate, at Kyoto University. He held positions at Kyoto University (1968, 1981–1993) and Otani University (circa 1993–2001).

nodes.label: Lama Thubten Yeshe
nodes.summary: Lama Thubten Yeshe was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar trained at Sera Monastery under teachers including Geshe Rabten. He founded the FPMT, Kopan Monastery, and Tushita Meditation Centre, and taught at the universities of Virginia and California, Santa Cruz.

nodes.label: Jean Filliozat
nodes.summary: Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian who studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He directed EPHE's Indian philology chair, the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977), the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1956–1977), and held a chair at Collège de France.

nodes.label: Thomas Freeman Yarnall
nodes.summary: Yarnall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Washington and Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, he served as Executive Editor in Columbia's Department of Religion (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Wayne Proudfoot
nodes.summary: Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University (PhD ~1972). He held academic posts at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and Columbia University (~1972–2008).

nodes.label: G. Thomas Tanselle
nodes.summary: G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University and taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Columbia University. He also served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation and president of the Bibliographical Society of America.

nodes.label: E. Gene Smith
nodes.summary: E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the universities of Utah, Washington, and Leiden under Turrell V. Wylie and Dezhung Rinpoche, he held positions at the Library of Congress and the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.label: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya
nodes.summary: Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.

nodes.label: Mario D'Amato

nodes.label: Lynn Struve
nodes.summary: Lynn Struve (born 1944) is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan before serving on the faculty at Indiana University from around 1977 to 2012.

nodes.label: Yoshiyuki Kawazoe

nodes.label: Hiromi Habata
nodes.summary: Hiromi Habata specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received a PhD from the University of Freiburg and held a researcher post at the University of Munich (attested 2014).
