nodes.label: Günter Schweiger
nodes.summary: Active in Indology and linguistics, Schweiger studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business under Gert Klingenschmitt. He served as an assistant at Linz (~1966–1972) and as a full professor at WU Vienna (1974–2009).

nodes.label: Gert Klingenschmitt
nodes.summary: Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1962–1968), where he later held posts, before holding the chair for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

nodes.label: Rosemarie Lühr
nodes.summary: Rosemarie Lühr (born 1946) is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nürnberg and habilitated at Regensburg. She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994), Jena (1994–2013), and Humboldt University (2013).

nodes.label: Michael Janda
nodes.summary: Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (PhD, 1988–1996) and habilitated at the University of Zurich. He held an assistant post at Zurich (1995) and a chair at the University of Münster (2002).

nodes.label: Chlodwig H. Werba
nodes.summary: Chlodwig H. Werba is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1997–2006 and 2022).

nodes.label: Toshifumi Goto
nodes.summary: Toshifumi Goto (born 1947) works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (-1982) under Karl Hoffmann and others. He held a professorship at Osaka University and taught at Tohoku University (attested 2003–2012).

nodes.label: Harumi Hirano Ziegler
nodes.summary: Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her MA and PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay
nodes.summary: Samten Gyaltsen Karmay specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Drepung, SOAS, and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove and Rolf A. Stein, later holding posts at SOAS, Collège de France, and CNRS (1980).

nodes.label: Hidetaka Nakatani
nodes.summary: Hidetaka Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under the supervision of Gadjin M. Nagao.

nodes.label: Claus Vogel
nodes.summary: Claus Vogel worked in Indology and Tibetology, completing his PhD and habilitation at the University of Marburg under Friedrich Müller and Wilhelm Rau. He held posts at Marburg, Göttingen, and as Ordinarius at the University of Bonn (1976–1998).

nodes.label: Klemens Karlsson
nodes.summary: Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Uppsala University under the supervision of Peter Schalk in 2000.

nodes.label: Susan L. Huntington
nodes.summary: Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Ohio State University from around 1971 to 2012.

nodes.label: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan
nodes.summary: Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned her PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Theodore Riccardi Jr. She held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

nodes.label: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal
nodes.summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford, and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India.

nodes.label: Rahul Sankrityayan
nodes.description: Indian Buddhist scholar, polyglot and travel writer (1893–1963); 'Father of Hindi travel literature'
nodes.summary: Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a Sanskrit teaching post at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (1937), where he later held a professorship (1945–1947).

nodes.label: Masako Keta
nodes.summary: Masako Keta is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. She studied at Kyoto University (~1971–1975, ~1977–1982) under Yoshinori Takeuchi. Her career includes posts at Hamamatsu University School of Medicine (1975–1977), Kanazawa University (1988, 1998), and Kyoto University (2000–2018).

nodes.label: Keiji Nishitani
nodes.summary: Keiji Nishitani was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Hajime Tanabe, and at the University of Freiburg under Martin Heidegger, he held long-term posts at Otani University and Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Kitaro Nishida
nodes.summary: Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) studied under Tokiyuki Hojo and Karl Florenz at the University of Tokyo. Active in philosophy and religious studies, he taught at the Fourth Higher School and was Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

nodes.label: Om Prakash
nodes.summary: Om Prakash is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma, later teaching there, at Kirori Mal College (attested 1961), and at the Delhi School of Economics (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Dasharatha Sharma
nodes.summary: Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Hindu College, University of Delhi, Jai Narain Vyas University, and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (circa 1970–1973).

nodes.label: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala
nodes.summary: Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He served as Curator of the Government Museum, Mathura, Director of the State Museum, Lucknow, and Head of Indology at BHU.

nodes.label: Leah Zahler
nodes.summary: Leah Zahler (1936–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) as well as Harvey B. Aronson and Ngawang Wangyal.

nodes.label: Lati Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Lati Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Geshe Lharampa degree at Ganden Shartse Monastery and studied at Gyuto. He served as abbot of Ganden and Ganden Shartse monasteries and was a visiting scholar at Virginia.

nodes.label: Geshe Gendun Lodro
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Geshe Gendun Lodro studied under Khensur Ngawang Legden and completed his ge-shay degree at Drepung Monastery by 1961. He held positions at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).

nodes.label: Mikisaburo Mori
nodes.summary: Mikisaburo Mori was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and earned a doctorate from Osaka University in 1962. His posts included Kyoto University (~1935–1950), Osaka High School (1942), Osaka University (1950, 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1984).

nodes.label: Tou-hoi Fok
nodes.summary: Tou-hoi Fok worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Otani University, later lecturing at The Chinese University of Hong Kong from around 1972 to 1982.

nodes.label: Jérôme Ducor
nodes.summary: Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May (around 1984–1992) and held an attested post at the University of Lausanne around 1999.

nodes.label: Egaku Maeda

He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen Women's College, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Fumimaro Watanabe
nodes.summary: Fumimaro Watanabe worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Hammalawa Saddhatissa and Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held posts at Kindai University, Pali Text Society, and Aichi Gakuin University.

nodes.label: Genryu Kagoshima
nodes.summary: Genryu Kagoshima was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1931 to 1937. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1960 to 1983.

nodes.label: Chaeson Kim

nodes.label: Marek Mejor

nodes.label: Ryosei Fuji
nodes.summary: Ryosei Fuji specializes in Buddhist studies and studied at Dongguk University (1986). Posts included lecturer at Daegu University (1988), researcher at the Institute for Religious Culture, and professorial appointments at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and Ryukoku University (attested 2011-2013).

nodes.label: Rupert Gethin
nodes.summary: Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. Since 1987, he has held posts at the University of Bristol, and he became President of the Pali Text Society in 2003.

nodes.label: Shokin Furuta
nodes.summary: Shokin Furuta (1911–2001) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. nodes.label: Taishun Mibu
nodes.summary: Taishun Mibu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Taisho University until 1937 and later served there as director (attested 1972).

nodes.label: Stephan Beyer
nodes.summary: Stephan Beyer is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (attested 1977).

nodes.label: David M. Knipe
nodes.summary: David M. Knipe is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held a long career as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he also served as Chair of Religious Studies (attested between 1975 and 2001).

nodes.label: Robert J. Miller
nodes.summary: Miller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

nodes.label: A. K. Narain
nodes.summary: A. K. Narain was a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and SOAS University of London, later serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

nodes.label: Jun Fujii
nodes.summary: Jun Fujii (born 1976) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who received his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2008 to 2013.

nodes.label: John W. Schroeder
nodes.summary: John W. Schroeder is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon (under Don S. Levi and Hee-Jin Kim), he held posts at Oregon, College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Rau
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Rau was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Leipzig and earned his doctorate at Marburg under Johannes Nobel, later serving as professor at Goethe University Frankfurt (1955) and Ordinarius at the University of Marburg (1958-1987).

nodes.label: Sheng Yen
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist monk, religious scholar, and writer (1931–2009)
nodes.summary: Sheng Yen was a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University. He held posts at Shandao Temple, National Cheng Kung University, and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and founded Dharma Drum Mountain.

nodes.label: Shuntaro Kondo
nodes.summary: Shuntaro Kondo completed his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2011, working in Buddhist studies and religious studies. In 2012, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa
nodes.summary: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998-2006) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Douglas S. Duckworth
nodes.summary: Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He taught at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University.

nodes.label: Sallie B. King
nodes.summary: Sallie B. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1973) under Leon Hurvitz (~1971–1975) and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1991–2017).

nodes.label: Erik Pema Kunsang
nodes.summary: Erik Pema Kunsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director at Rangjung Yeshe Publications around 1980 and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark around 2004.

nodes.label: Gendün Chöphel
nodes.summary: Gendün Chöphel was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung monasteries, training under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso, and was affiliated with the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.

nodes.label: George de Roerich
variants: ユーリイ・リョーリフ
nodes.summary: George de Roerich, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, studied at London, Harvard, the Sorbonne, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi and others. He directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute and later worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

nodes.label: Anagarika Dharmapala

Thomas' College (~1876-1883), Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, St. Benedict's College, and Royal College, Colombo. He founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

nodes.label: Albion Moonlight Butters
nodes.summary: Albion Moonlight Butters is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard, CIHTS, and Columbia University, completing his Ph.D. under Robert Thurman, alongside training under teachers such as Michael Aris, Noel Q. King, and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Samten
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery. A scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–2019) and held visiting posts at Smith College (2004).

nodes.label: Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries and under Dudjom Rinpoche, later chairing the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).

nodes.label: Alexander von Rospatt
nodes.summary: Alexander von Rospatt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Leipzig University and UC Berkeley.

nodes.label: Michihiro Ikeda
nodes.summary: Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts at Setagaya Gakuen Junior and Senior High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and worked as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Yonten Gyatso
nodes.summary: Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) was a Tibetologist and historian. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diploma at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as a research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Per Kværne
nodes.summary: Per Kværne (born 1945) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Oslo (~1965–1973). He lectured at the University of Bergen (1970–1975) and served as professor at the University of Oslo (1975–2007).

nodes.label: Anne-Marie Blondeau
nodes.summary: Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf A. Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Inada
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999), chaired the Numata Center (1996–1999), and chaired the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism until 1999.

nodes.label: Todd Gibson
nodes.summary: Todd Gibson is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned a PhD at Indiana University, attested in 1991.

nodes.label: Jongcheol Lee
nodes.summary: Jongcheol Lee is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo (1994) under Ekyo Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (2001).

nodes.label: Katherine Janiec Jones
nodes.summary: Katherine Janiec Jones specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, also studying under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

nodes.label: Paul Tillich

nodes.summary: Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, University of Tokyo, and University of Vienna (PhD 1994). She held posts at Naritasan Institute, University of Tsukuba, and Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Nemoto
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Nemoto specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned an MA at Hiroshima University and later served as a professor there (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuyoshi Kino
nodes.summary: Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo in 1942 and 1946–1948. He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).

nodes.label: Hōgetsu
nodes.summary: Hōgetsu (1737–1805) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongyuan and Zuihe, and taught Hokai.

nodes.label: Tanso Hirose
nodes.summary: Tanso Hirose was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hodo, later founding Kangien in 1801.

nodes.label: Hokai
nodes.summary: Hokai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.

nodes.label: Masao Abe
variants: Masao Abe (阿部 正雄, Abe Masao)
nodes.description: Japanese Buddhist, professor in religious studies
nodes.summary: Masao Abe was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, Kyoto University, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under scholars including Hajime Tanabe and Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He taught at Nara University and Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Siglinde Dietz
nodes.summary: Siglinde Dietz, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at the University of Bonn in 1980 under Michael Hahn. She taught Ryutaro Tsuchida and Andrey Klebanov, and held a post at the University of Göttingen.

nodes.label: Shripad Krishna Belvalkar
nodes.description: Indian historian and scholar of Sanskrit
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Shripad Krishna Belvalkar studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1904–1927), honorary secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1918–1927), and General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference.

nodes.label: Sojo Hirano
nodes.summary: Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and shika at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann.

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Soto Zen Studies
nodes.label: Research Institute of Soto Zen Studies

nodes.id: I:Setagaya Gakuen Junior and Senior High School
nodes.label: Setagaya Gakuen Junior and Senior High School
Xuesong Zhang
nodes.summary: Xuesong Zhang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hsing Yun
nodes.summary: Hsing Yun was a Buddhist studies and religious studies leader. Trained at Tianning Temple and Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute, he founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as its abbot (~1967–1985), and later held professorial posts at Chinese Culture and Tunghai universities.

nodes.label: Fo Guang Shan
variants: Fo Guang Shan Buddhist monastic order

nodes.label: Taixu
nodes.summary: Taixu (1890–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Jichan, Jingan, and Yang Renshan. He served as a monk at Bilu Temple, led the Minnan Buddhist Academy, and founded several Buddhist institutes, academies, and associations.

nodes.id: I:Tohoku Society for Indology and Study of Religion
nodes.label: Tohoku Society for Indology and Study of Religion
Takao Yamagata
nodes.summary: Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1969–2003) and served as president of the Japanese Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Carlo Formichi
nodes.summary: Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Italian Indologist. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Georg Bühler, Hermann Oldenberg, and Paul Deussen (Kiel University). He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

nodes.label: Alfred Foucher
variants: アルフレッド・フーシェ
アルフレッド・A・フーシェ
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・フーシェ
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Foucher studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE. He directed the EFEO (1905) and held a professorship at the University of Paris (1929–1936).

nodes.label: Marcelle Lalou
nodes.summary: Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her doctorate at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She taught at the EPHE (1938–1963) and edited the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).

nodes.label: Jean Przyluski
nodes.description: French linguist and scholar of religion
nodes.summary: Jean Przyluski was a linguist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at EPHE under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss. He held chairs at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Velcheru Narayana Rao
nodes.description: Indian author, critic, and literary translator
nodes.summary: Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who studied at Sir C.R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and held visiting professorships at Chicago and Emory.

nodes.label: José Ignacio Cabezón
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Cabezón earned his BS at Caltech and his PhD at UW-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and UC Santa Barbara (2001).

nodes.label: Shingo Einoo
nodes.summary: Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1973–1980) under Wilhelm Rau and held a post at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia from circa 1989 to 2013.

nodes.label: Takanobu Takahashi
nodes.summary: Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University (PhD), later serving at International Buddhist University and the University of Tokyo (1996–2016).

nodes.label: Tadashi Toda
nodes.summary: Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

nodes.label: Kevin Alan Vose
nodes.summary: Kevin Alan Vose specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.

nodes.label: Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa
nodes.summary: Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).

nodes.label: Drepung Loseling Monastery
variants: デプン寺ロサーリン学堂

nodes.label: National Taiwan University
variants: Department of Philosophy, National Taiwan University
台灣大學音樂學研究所

nodes.label: Ryosho Onami
nodes.summary: Ryosho Onami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu. Onami served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).

nodes.label: University of Warsaw
variants: Institute of Oriental Studies at the University of Warsaw

nodes.label: Helmut Eimer
nodes.summary: Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm, later serving on Bonn's faculty (~1975–2001).

nodes.label: Esho Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Esho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and later held posts as professor at Osaka University (~1974–1982) and faculty member at Ritsumeikan University (~1982–1989).

nodes.label: Kosaku Hamada
nodes.summary: Kosaku Hamada was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905), later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1909) and Kyoto University (~1909–1938).

nodes.label: Academy of Oriental Culture
variants: 東方文化学院北京出張所
東方文化学院東京研究所

nodes.label: Chandrabhāl Tripathi
nodes.summary: Chandrabhāl Tripathi (1929–1996) was an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Göttingen, Cologne, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the Free University of Berlin as Professor of Indology (~1974–1994).

nodes.label: Romila Thapar
nodes.summary: Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She was a professor of ancient Indian history at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

nodes.label: Arthur Llewellyn Basham
nodes.summary: Arthur Llewellyn Basham (1914–1986) was an Indologist and historian who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held posts at SOAS (1948–1965) and later served as professor at the Australian National University (~1965–1978).

nodes.label: Masatoshi Konishi
nodes.summary: Masatoshi Konishi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

nodes.label: Toshio Yamazaki
nodes.summary: Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. His career included posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1950–1955), the University of Tokyo (~1955–1977), Chuo University (~1977–1987), and Hannan University (~1987–1992).

nodes.label: Myles Dillon
nodes.description: Irish academic, historian, philologist and celticist (1900–1972)
nodes.summary: Myles Dillon was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at University College Dublin and under Rudolf Thurneysen, among others. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as Director of DIAS (1960–1968).

nodes.label: James Kenneth Powell II
nodes.summary: James Kenneth Powell II specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: Chang-geun Hwang
nodes.summary: Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. Hwang studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

nodes.label: Hugh B. Urban
nodes.summary: Hugh B. Urban (born 1968) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993–1998) studying under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and became an associate professor at Ohio State University (~1998).

nodes.label: Bruce Lincoln
nodes.summary: Bruce Lincoln is a scholar of religion, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held faculty posts at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1993).

nodes.label: Jeffrey J. Kripal
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Jeffrey J. Kripal studied at Conception Seminary College and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. Around 2002, he was appointed J. Newton Rayzor Chair and department chair at Rice University.

nodes.label: Tony K. Stewart
nodes.summary: Tony K. Stewart (born 1954) specializes in Indology and religious studies. After studying at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976), he held academic posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

nodes.label: Joachim Prandstetter
nodes.summary: Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned his Magister at the University of Vienna in 1994, where he studied under Gerhard Oberhammer.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Lessing
nodes.image: Professor Ferdinand Deiderich Lessing, Univ. of California, Berkeley. 1952.jpg
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Lessing was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Peking University, China Medical University, Humboldt University, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and UC Berkeley (~1935–1952).

nodes.label: Ronald M. Davidson
nodes.summary: Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earning his PhD from UC Berkeley in 1985. He studied under numerous scholars, including Padmanabh S. Jaini and Lewis Lancaster, and held an attested post at Fairfield University (2002–2005).

nodes.label: Gil Fronsdal
nodes.summary: Gil Fronsdal (born 1954) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Stanford University (attested 1998), studying under teachers including Jan Nattier and Carl Bielefeldt, and was affiliated with the Sati Center and Insight Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Bernard Faure
nodes.jawiki: ベルナール・フォール
nodes.summary: Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned a Doctorat d'État at the University of Paris, studied under Paul Demiéville and Seizan Yanagida, and held professorships at Cornell, Stanford, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: David W. Chappell
nodes.summary: David W. Chappell (1940–2004) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale. He taught as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from ~1972 to 2002 and taught comparative studies at Soka University of America from ~2002 to 2004.

nodes.label: Vesna Wallace
nodes.summary: Vesna Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at the University of Oxford until 2010 and served as a professor at UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: Anthony Kennedy Warder
nodes.summary: Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London under John Brough, taught at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963), and was a professor at the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

nodes.label: Michiyo Demoto
nodes.summary: Michiyo Demoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held an academic post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

nodes.label: Peter Skilling
variants: ピーター・スキリング
nodes.summary: Peter Skilling is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at EPHE under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub. He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and several visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Kunio Harikai
nodes.summary: Kunio Harikai (born 1942) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara, completing his BA and PhD degrees, and served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1993).

nodes.label: Futoshi Omae
nodes.summary: Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Eki Nakayama
nodes.summary: Eki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2020) and held a research fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Hisashi Matsumura
nodes.summary: Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes an attested post at the Australian National University in 1982 and an assistant professorship at Kobe Shinwa University attested in 1996.

nodes.label: Yoshinobu Kimoto
nodes.summary: Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities, and held posts as associate professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College, president of Koshien Junior College, and professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

nodes.label: Yonezawa Women's Junior College
variants: 山形県立米沢女子短期大学

nodes.label: Kazuo Oyamada
nodes.summary: Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Koyo Shimizu
nodes.summary: Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1995.

nodes.label: National Archives of Nepal
variants: ネパール国立古文書館

nodes.id: I:Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
nodes.label: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
variants: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
The Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities

nodes.label: Ernst Waldschmidt
nodes.summary: Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel, Göttingen, and Berlin under scholars including Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, and Heinrich Lüders. He served as professor of Indology at Göttingen (1936–1965).

nodes.label: Kyushu Otani Junior College
variants: 九州大谷短期大学仏教科

nodes.label: Gerald James Larson
nodes.summary: Gerald James Larson was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He served as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and as Rabindranath Tagore Professor at Indiana University beginning in 1995.

nodes.label: Toshiki Osada
nodes.summary: Toshiki Osada (born 1954) works in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Hokkaido University (~1973–1977), he served as a professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2019) and joined Kyoto University of the Arts (~2019).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute for Humanity and Nature
nodes.label: Research Institute for Humanity and Nature
variants: 総合地球環境学研究所
Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (RIHN)
Research Institute for Humans and Nature of Japan
Research Institute for Humanity and Nature in Kyōto

nodes.label: Tomoyasu Oshima
nodes.summary: Tomoyasu Oshima works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012) and served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Naoko Nishimura
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology, Naoko Nishimura completed a PhD at Tohoku University (by 2002) under Toshifumi Goto and later served as a researcher there (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Sumitra Mangesh Katre
nodes.summary: Sumitra Mangesh Katre (1906–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of London. He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, Deccan College (Chair of Indo-European Philology, 1942–1971), and the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Koji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University by 1991. At Bukkyo University, he served as 助教授 (~1969–1999) and 教授 (~1976–1999).

nodes.label: University at Buffalo
variants: ニューヨーク州立大学バッファロー校
University of Buffalo, State University of New York
State University of New York at Buffalo
State University of New York at Buffalo Law School
University at Buffalo, The State University of New York
State University of New York, Buffalo

nodes.label: Sonam Gyatso
nodes.summary: Sonam Gyatso (born 1933) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at the Toyo Bunko (~1960–1968) and as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Chijo Akamatsu
nodes.summary: Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. His posts included Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku University, Hanazono University, Kyoto University, Kyushu University, and Yamaguchi University.

nodes.label: Kazuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Kazuhiko Yoshida studies history, archaeology, Buddhism, and Japanology. He studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Osaka, and Cornell universities—the latter under Jay Jasanoff. He held positions at Nagoya City College for Women (~1989–1997), Kyoto University (~1998–2020), and Nagoya City University (2021–2024).

nodes.label: Tokuno Oda
nodes.summary: Tokuno Oda (1860–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He held posts at Fukui Normal School, Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Mokurai Shimaji
nodes.summary: Mokurai Shimaji (1838–1911) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held leadership posts at Nishi Hongan-ji, Hongan-ji, and Gankyo-ji, and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen.

nodes.label: Enryo Inoue
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Inoue studied at Higashi Hongan-ji and the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University, serving as a lecturer and manager (~1887–1905).

nodes.label: Teun Goudriaan
nodes.summary: Teun Goudriaan was a scholar in indology and religious studies who held a post at Utrecht University (attested 1989), where he later served as Professor Emeritus (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Sanjukta Gupta
variants: サンジェクタ・グプタ
nodes.summary: Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati University (PhD), and Utrecht University (D.Lett. under Jan Gonda). She taught at Jadavpur University, Utrecht University, and the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Kojun Fukui
nodes.summary: Kojun Fukui was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda, he served as 助教授 (1936) and 教授 (1941–1969) at Waseda, and as 学長 of Taisho University (1928–1968, 1972–1975).

nodes.label: Takudo Ishikawa
nodes.summary: Takudo Ishikawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held appointments as a researcher at the Research Institute of Jodo Shu (attested 2005) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kengo Harimoto
nodes.summary: Kengo Harimoto works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999. He held posts at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

nodes.label: Kenji Takahashi
nodes.summary: Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) and under supervisors Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop, as well as Somadeva Vasudeva, Andrey Klebanov, and Masato Fujii. He held a JSPS fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).

nodes.label: Peter Bisschop
nodes.summary: Peter Bisschop specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, later holding posts at the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and Leiden University (attested 2011–2021).

nodes.label: Andrey Klebanov
nodes.summary: Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA (-2010) and PhD (-2016) at the University of Hamburg, studying under Harunaga Isaacson, among others. He was appointed professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: James L. Fitzgerald
nodes.summary: James L. Fitzgerald is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Ryosaburo Sakaki
nodes.summary: Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872-1946) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Atsuuji Ashikaga. Educated at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo (~1892-1895), he held posts at Ryukoku, the Third Higher School, and Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Gikyo Ito
nodes.summary: Gikyo Ito (1909–1996) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Indological studies. Educated at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, he held posts there including professor (1968–1972) and later served as professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

nodes.label: Koji Kamioka
nodes.summary: Koji Kamioka was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1963) and under Yutaka Ochihara, later teaching as a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and 助教授 at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

nodes.label: Norihiko Uchida
nodes.summary: Norihiko Uchida is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies.

nodes.label: Sensho Murakami
nodes.summary: Sensho Murakami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani and Toyo universities. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo and as principal of Etchu Kyoko and Tokyo High School.

nodes.label: Shingo Enomoto
nodes.summary: Shingo Enomoto is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who completed a PhD at the University of Marburg (~1973–1980). He held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology from circa 1983 to 1989.

nodes.label: Takao Hayashi
nodes.summary: Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. After earning a PhD at Brown University under David Pingree, he was a researcher at the Harish-Chandra Research Institute and later an assistant professor (1986–1989) and professor (1995–2015) at Doshisha University.

nodes.label: Mizuho Okita
nodes.summary: Mizuho Okita (born 1977) specializes in Indology and religious studies. Okita completed a BA at Tokai University, studied at Gakushuin University under Atsuhiko Yoshida and Katsuhiko Kamimura, and served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University.

nodes.label: Atsuhiko Yoshida
nodes.summary: Atsuhiko Yoshida studied at Seikei University, University of Tokyo, and under Georges Dumézil. He held research and teaching posts at CNRS (~1961–1969), Seikei University (professor, 1970), and Gakushuin University (professor, 2006).

nodes.label: Gakushuin University
variants: 学習院大学文学部哲学科

nodes.label: Kazuo Matsumura
nodes.summary: Kazuo Matsumura works in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Hitotsubashi University (~1972–1976), he held academic posts at Tenri University (~1990–2006) and Wako University (~2006).

nodes.label: Wako University
variants: 和光大学人文学部芸術学科

nodes.label: Masanori Shono
nodes.summary: Masanori Shono specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. His career includes posts at Osaka University (attested 2012) and the University of Munich (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Michael Radich
variants: マイケル・ラディッチ
nodes.summary: Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Harvard (ca. 2001–2007). He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg University in 2018.

nodes.label: Yumiko Ishihama
nodes.summary: Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at Waseda University from circa 1980 to 1989 and later held a post there around 2003.

nodes.label: Shinkai Sugahara
nodes.summary: Shinkai Sugahara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University (~1947–1951) and Taisho University (Doctor of Letters, 1991). He served on the faculty at Waseda University (~1962–1972), becoming professor emeritus.

nodes.label: Jikai Fujiyoshi
nodes.summary: Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with Kyoto University as a member (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Masao Shizutani
nodes.summary: Masao Shizutani was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He held associate professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

nodes.label: Ryodo Kudo
nodes.summary: Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015-2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Lance E. Nelson
nodes.summary: Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University in 1986 and later served as a professor at the University of San Diego.

nodes.label: Sayaka Sonoda
nodes.summary: Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.

nodes.label: Shinobu Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Shinobu Yamaguchi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She is attested as a professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Puthezhethu Rama Menon
nodes.summary: Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891–1973) was active in Indology and other fields. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and as president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.

nodes.label: Hiroshi Maruyama
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Maruyama was a scholar of Indology who served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 1987) and led the Ayurveda Research Society (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Tsutomu Hatai
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Hatai was an Indology figure who served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society, where he was attested in 1987 having succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama.

nodes.label: Yasuhiro Okazaki
nodes.summary: Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. His career includes posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Kabe Senior, and Takamiya High Schools (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Otoya Tanaka
nodes.summary: Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji from ~1927 to 1930. He later served as a professor at Chuo University from ~1958 to 1974.

nodes.label: Kiyozo Kazama
nodes.summary: Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928) studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held professorial posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

nodes.label: Fujio Taniguchi
nodes.summary: Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and also studied under Yusho Miyasaka, Zuiho Yamaguchi, Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Kaiun Shiradate.

nodes.label: Geshe Sonam Rinchen
variants: Dge bshes bsod nams rin chen
nodes.summary: Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. In 1978, he became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.summary: Kojun Saito was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).

nodes.label: Shinko Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Shinko Mochizuki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928) and Taisho University (1930–1932), where he also held a professorship (~1927–1942).

nodes.label: Junkei Washio
nodes.summary: Junkei Washio (1868–1941) was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Toyo University and founded Sōgenkutsu in 1892. He held professorships at Toyo University and Komazawa University, and also taught at Sendan-Rin School.

nodes.label: Genchi Kato
nodes.summary: Genchi Kato was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied under Tetsujiro Inoue at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships with the Imperial Japanese Army and taught at the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin University, and Taisho University.

nodes.label: Seigai Omura
nodes.summary: Seigai Omura (1868–1927) was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) under Kanō Tomonobu, subsequently serving there as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1898).

nodes.label: Michio Kamikawa
nodes.summary: Michio Kamikawa (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University around 1998.

nodes.label: Yoshitoyo Ohara
nodes.summary: Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held affiliations at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and the Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Akira Shimada
nodes.summary: Akira Shimada is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali. He held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

nodes.label: Michael Willis
nodes.summary: Michael Willis is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Victoria and completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago (1988). He worked as a curator of South Asian Collections at the British Museum (1994–2014).

nodes.label: Kodo Yotsuya
nodes.summary: Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Alexander Wynne
nodes.description: British sanskritist and religious studies scholar, works on the history of Buddishm
nodes.summary: Alexander Wynne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, followed by a DPhil at the University of Oxford supervised by Richard Gombrich.

nodes.label: Paul Williams
nodes.summary: Paul Williams is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his BA at Sussex and DPhil at Oxford. He served as a fellow at Wadham College and held the post of Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at Bristol (~1980–2011).

nodes.label: David Pingree
nodes.summary: David Pingree specialized in Indology and history. He completed his BA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, later holding professorships at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (appointed 1971).

nodes.label: Otto Neugebauer
nodes.jawiki: オットー・ノイゲバウアー
nodes.summary: Otto Neugebauer was an Austrian-American historian of mathematics and science who studied at Graz, Munich, and Göttingen under Boris Turayev. He held professorships at Copenhagen (1933–1939) and Brown University (1939, 1947–1969), and was a permanent member at the Institute for Advanced Study (1980–1990).

nodes.label: Eishun Fushimi
nodes.summary: Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

nodes.label: Hong Luo
nodes.summary: Hong Luo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. A former doctoral student at Peking University, Luo has held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and as a professor at Sichuan University.

nodes.label: Peter Zieme
nodes.summary: Peter Zieme specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies and linguistics. Educated at Humboldt University, he worked at the GDR Academy of Sciences, Institut für Orientforschung, Berlin-Brandenburg Academy, and Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber
nodes.summary: Hu-von Hinüber studied at Peking University under Kemu Jin and Zhongxin Jiang. Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, she held appointments at the University of Vienna (attested 1996) and the University of Freiburg (2010).

nodes.label: Vincent Tournier
nodes.summary: Vincent Tournier, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études by 2012 and studied under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub and Seishi Karashima. He held a post at École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Taiki Mibu
nodes.summary: Taiki Mibu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Harushige Kōzu
nodes.summary: Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and served as professor and dean at Musashi University (1968).

nodes.label: Toru Haneda
nodes.summary: Toru Haneda (1882–1955) worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University, he served in multiple posts at Kyoto University (1909–1948), Toho Gakkai, and the Institute of Eastern Culture.

nodes.label: Shingen Takagi
nodes.summary: Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Gisho Nakano, and Yusho Miyasaka, and served as an assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) of Koyasan University.

nodes.label: Gisho Nakano
nodes.image: 哲學系教授中野義照先生 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and at Kyushu University. He held professorships at Peking University and Koyasan University, serving as president of Koyasan University (1951, 1964).

nodes.label: Ekai Kawaguchi
variants: Ekai Kawaguchi (河口慧海, Kawaguchi Ekai)
nodes.summary: Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College. He held posts as Rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji, Professor at Toyo University, and researcher at Toyo Bunko.

nodes.label: Masakazu Tanaka
nodes.summary: Masakazu Tanaka works in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1980) and earned his Ph.D. at the London School of Economics and University of London (~1980–1986). His career includes positions at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and the Professional Institute of International Fashion (2019).

nodes.label: Renate Syed
nodes.summary: Renate Syed is an Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982). Her doctoral supervisor was Dieter Schlingloff, and she also studied under Friedrich Wilhelm and Gritli von Mitterwallner.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. After studying at Munich under Paul Thieme (~1953–1956), he worked at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences (~1958–1964) and served as Privatdozent (1963) and Professor (1969–1998) at Munich.

nodes.label: Gritli von Mitterwallner
nodes.summary: Gritli von Mitterwallner was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She completed her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.

nodes.summary: William Roxburgh, active in Indology, studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Marischal College. He served as superintendent of Samalkot Garden (1781) and head of the Indian Botanic Garden (1793).

nodes.label: Ryuta Kikutani
nodes.summary: Ryuta Kikutani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Kikutani held posts as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center and Graduate School of Letters (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Ryukai Mano
nodes.summary: Ryukai Mano (born 1929) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who succeeded Yuishin Ito. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1991.

nodes.label: Ryosho Hayashi
nodes.summary: Ryosho Hayashi (1927-2008) studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University, focusing on Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He served at Taisho University as professor (1975), Dean of Letters (1981), and professor emeritus (1990-1994), and headed the Japan-Korea Cultural Exchange Association (1990).

Her posts include Heidelberg University Library, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, a guest professorship at the University of Vienna, and a professorship replacement at the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Karl Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich (1934–1951) under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, and later held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (1955–1983).

nodes.label: Eva Tichy
nodes.summary: Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist. She studied under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1974–1981), completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg (~1981–1989), and held the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

nodes.label: Mahesh A. Deokar
nodes.summary: Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He has served at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021).

nodes.label: Frits Staal
nodes.summary: Frits Staal specialized in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, earning degrees from Amsterdam and Banaras/Madras. He held posts at SOAS (1958–1962), the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967), and the University of California, Berkeley (1968–1991).

nodes.label: Yoshitsugu Sawai
nodes.summary: Yoshitsugu Sawai (born 1951) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned doctorates from Tohoku University and Harvard, where he studied under John B. Carman, and served as professor and Dean of the Faculty of Humanities at Tenri University (1986–2017).

nodes.label: Arindam Chakrabarti

nodes.summary: Liebert was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Gothenburg (~1941–1949). He held positions at Lund University, Uppsala University, and served as professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at Gothenburg (1955–1982).

nodes.label: Keishin Okamura
nodes.summary: Keishin Okamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Kyoto University between 1949 and 1959. He held academic appointments at Koyasan University (1959–1973, 2005–2009) and Kochi University (circa 1970–1995).

nodes.label: Naoji Okuyama
nodes.summary: A specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Naoji Okuyama completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985). He held teaching posts at Tohoku University (~1985–1993) and became a professor at Koyasan University (~1993).

nodes.label: Munenobu Sakurai
nodes.summary: Munenobu Sakurai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral course at Tohoku University around 1986–1991, served as assistant professor at Iwate University (ca. 1994–2002), and became professor at Tohoku University around 2002.

nodes.label: Takanori Unno
nodes.summary: Takanori Unno is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Nagoya University, studying under Yoshifumi Ueda and other scholars. He held posts as an assistant at Nagoya University, lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University, and professor at Meijo University.

nodes.label: Tetsuhiko Shibata
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tetsuhiko Shibata studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

nodes.label: Takeshi Fujii
nodes.summary: Takeshi Fujii is an Indologist and historian who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, advancing from assistant in 1987 to professor and emeritus professor (2021).

nodes.label: Takashi Yamada
nodes.summary: Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He was attested as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto in 2003.

nodes.label: Toru Kumoi

nodes.label: Hidenaka Tanaka

nodes.label: Jeffrey Broughton

nodes.label: Kōzui Ōtani
nodes.summary: Kōzui Ōtani (1876–1948) worked in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology. Educated at Gakushuin and under Keiun Maeda, he served as 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and founded Kojukai in 1919.

nodes.label: Yuko Kamishima

nodes.label: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
nodes.summary: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of London and SOAS, later serving at University College, Colombo and as Dean of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.

nodes.summary: Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (ca. 1936–1940). He held posts at Pravda, the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and the Institute of Oriental Studies (ca. 1960–1998).

nodes.label: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1956–1978) and served as a guest professor at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Haridas Sinharay
nodes.summary: Haridas Sinharay is an Indology scholar who held a post at Central Calcutta College (attested 1970 and 1990).

nodes.label: Central Calcutta College
variants: Department of Sanskrit, Central Calcutta College

nodes.label: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya (1934–2001) worked in the fields of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.

nodes.label: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is an Indologist and philosopher. He taught as a professor at Vidyasagar College and served in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Vidyasagar College
variants: Department of Sanskrit, Vidyasagar College, Calcutta

nodes.label: Suniti Kumar Chatterji
nodes.summary: Suniti Kumar Chatterji (1890–1977) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Scottish Church College, Presidency University, Calcutta, London, Sorbonne, and Paris under Jules Bloch. He held posts at Calcutta, Pennsylvania, Sahitya Akademi, and the Government of India.

nodes.label: Csaba Kiss
nodes.summary: Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held posts as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024).

nodes.label: Édouard Chavannes
variants: エドゥアール・シャヴァンヌ
nodes.jawiki: エドゥアール・シャヴァンヌ
nodes.summary: Sinologist and historian of Buddhism Édouard Chavannes studied at ENS, Collège de France, and INALCO under Marie-Jean-Léon d'Hervey de Saint Denys and Maurice Jametel. He held a professorship at Collège de France (1893–1918) and served at EFEO (~1898–1900).

nodes.label: Bavarian State Library
variants: kgl. bayer. Hof- und Staatsbibliothek in München

nodes.label: Isaline Blew Horner
nodes.summary: Isaline Blew Horner worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Newnham College and Cambridge under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held positions at Newnham College, the University of Cambridge, and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.

nodes.label: Eugen Hultzsch
nodes.summary: Eugen Hultzsch was a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Vienna under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in India and later held the Sanskrit chair at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

nodes.label: Hosakote Krishna Sastri
nodes.summary: Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an epigraphist active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).

nodes.label: Georg von Simson
nodes.summary: Georg von Simson worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Mainz (~1953–1957) and Göttingen (~1957–1974). He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977) and as professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

nodes.label: Thích Minh Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Minh Châu was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (~1957–1961). He served as a Chinese lecturer at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1958–1961) and Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University (~1964–1975).

nodes.label: Ashok Aklujkar
nodes.summary: Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Pune University and completed his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served in the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

nodes.label: Tatiana Oranskaia
nodes.summary: Tatiana Oranskaia specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1974) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (~1987–1988). She taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and served as professor at the University of Hamburg (1998–2016).

nodes.label: Arthur William Ryder
nodes.summary: Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist. He earned his A.B. at Harvard and Ph.D. at Leipzig, also studying at Berlin and under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He was an instructor at Harvard (1902–1906) and Sanskrit professor at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).

nodes.label: Raniero Gnoli
nodes.summary: Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Italian Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz. He served as Professor of Indology at Sapienza University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.

nodes.label: Vempati Kutumba Sastry
nodes.summary: Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist who served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University from 2003 to 2008. He also served as president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies and was a board member of the Wider Association of Vedic Studies.

nodes.label: Mamata Dash
nodes.summary: Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar. She was educated at Ravenshaw Girls' High School and Utkal University.

nodes.label: K. V. Sarma
nodes.summary: K. V. Sarma (1919–2005) was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute, Panjab University, and Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, later directing the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

nodes.label: Mark Singleton
nodes.summary: Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge. He has held a post as Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Elizabeth De Michelis
nodes.summary: Elizabeth De Michelis is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from SOAS and the University of Cambridge (~1998–2002). She held posts at Cambridge as director in 2000 and at the University of Oxford's theology faculty.

nodes.label: Suzanne Newcombe
nodes.summary: Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the Open University and King's College London, where she was honorary director of Inform.

nodes.label: Gangzhun
nodes.summary: Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and earned a master's degree from Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Qinghai Nationalities University
variants: Teachers Training College for Nationalities in Chab-cha

nodes.label: Mysore Hiriyanna
nodes.description: Indian philosopher, Sanskrit scholar and authority on Indian aesthetics
nodes.summary: Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who earned his BA and MA at Madras Christian College. He held posts at Maharaja's College, Mysore (1912–1927), and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

nodes.label: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi
nodes.summary: Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology, serving as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and holding an attested post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, in 1939.

nodes.label: K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar
variants: R. B. Prof. K. V. Rangaswami Iyengar

nodes.label: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka. In 1927, he became Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

nodes.label: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt
nodes.summary: Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who served as a Professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and later as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

nodes.label: Lothar von Falkenhausen
variants: ロータール・アレクサンダー・フォン・ファルケンハウゼン
nodes.jawiki: ロータール・フォン・ファルケンハウゼン
nodes.description: German-American Archaeologist, Sinologist, and Art Historian
nodes.summary: Lothar von Falkenhausen, a specialist in archaeology and Sinology, studied at Bonn, Peking University, and Harvard. Since 1993 he has served as professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was associate director there from 2004 to 2011.

nodes.label: Jinbo Shi
nodes.summary: Jinbo Shi specializes in linguistics, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang. He has held positions at CASS, Minzu University, North Minzu University, and Ningxia University.

nodes.label: Soma Thera
nodes.summary: Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under traditional teacher Jetavana Sayadaw (1936). He was a member of the Servants of the Buddha around 1926.

nodes.label: Dieter George
nodes.summary: Dieter George was an Indologist who held a post at the Prussian State Library from circa 1972 to 1985. In 1985, he was attested as the successor to Wolfgang Voigt.

nodes.label: Michael Schmidt
nodes.summary: Michael Schmidt is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts with the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992) and at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a dictionary editor and contributor.
