nodes.label: Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik
nodes.description: Indian lawyer, writer and social activist
nodes.summary: Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik was an Indology scholar who studied at Elphinstone College (~1847–1851). He served as an examiner in Marathi and Law at the University of Mumbai and as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878).

nodes.label: Steven Heine
nodes.summary: Steven Heine is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University. He held posts at Villanova, La Salle, and Penn State, before becoming a professor at Florida International University in 1997.

nodes.label: Charles S. Prebish
nodes.summary: Charles S. Prebish is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Case Western Reserve University under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007).

nodes.label: Raoul Birnbaum
nodes.summary: Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz, with publications attested in 2003 and 2017.

nodes.label: Christopher S. Queen
nodes.summary: Christopher S. Queen (born 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. His career includes posts at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education (~1989) and Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Manfred Mayrhofer
variants: マンフレート・マイルホーファー
nodes.jawiki: マンフレート・マイルホーファー
nodes.summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein, later holding professorships at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

nodes.label: Ernst Johann Eitel
nodes.summary: Ernst Johann Eitel was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his MA and PhD from the University of Tübingen. He served with the London Missionary Society (circa 1865–1879) and taught German at the University of Adelaide (circa 1897–1908).

nodes.label: Raffaele Torella
nodes.summary: Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He served as a professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1976–1980) and as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome (~1980–2020).

nodes.label: August Fischer
nodes.summary: August Fischer worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1884–1889) and later held posts at Leipzig University (1900–1930) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

nodes.label: Anant Sadashiv Altekar
nodes.description: historian, archaeologist, and numismatist from Maharashtra, India
nodes.summary: Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (~1930-1949) and Patna University (~1949-1957), chaired the Numismatic Society of India (1947), and served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1954-1959).

nodes.label: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington
nodes.image: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, negative, 1927 (Lafayette; NPG x41720).png
nodes.summary: Kenneth de Burgh Codrington (1899–1986) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (circa 1931–1948), University of London (circa 1948–1966), and University of Cincinnati.

nodes.label: Cyril Henry Philips
nodes.summary: Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS University of London. He served as Director of SOAS from 1957 and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London from 1972 to 1976.

nodes.label: Ying-shih Yü
nodes.summary: Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy. Educated at Yenching, New Asia College, CUHK, and Harvard (PhD 1962), he held professorships at Harvard, CUHK, Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton University (1987–2001).

nodes.label: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani
nodes.summary: Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt and studied under M. V. Upadhyay. At Baroda, he was a Sanskrit lecturer and professor (1967–1980), later directing the Oriental Institute (1975–1981).

nodes.label: Parashuram Krishna Gode
nodes.image: Dr. Parshuram Krishna Gode, M.A., D. Litt.jpg

nodes.label: Kenneth Roy Norman
nodes.summary: Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Taunton School and Downing College, Cambridge, he served at the University of Cambridge (1955–1992) and as president of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

nodes.label: Frank Raymond Allchin
nodes.summary: Frank Raymond Allchin was a scholar of Indian archaeology and Indology. He studied at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, subsequently lecturing there (1954–1959) before holding a lectureship and readership in Indian Studies at the University of Cambridge (1959–1989).

nodes.label: D. R. Shackleton Bailey
nodes.summary: D. R. Shackleton Bailey worked in Tibetology, Indology, and classics. Educated at Cambridge, he held fellowships and posts at Cambridge (1944–1968), and was later a professor at the University of Michigan (1968–1976, 1988–2002) and Harvard (1975–1988).

nodes.label: Paul Mus
nodes.summary: A scholar of religion, Buddhism, and history, Paul Mus studied at Oxford, EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He held professorships at the Collège de France (1946) and Yale University (1951).

nodes.label: Kun Chang
nodes.summary: Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua and Yale, where he earned his doctorate under Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Academia Sinica (~1941–1947), the University of Washington (1951), and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

nodes.label: Samuel Beal
nodes.summary: Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1843–1847). He served at Bramham College (1848–1850) and as Professor of Chinese at University College London (1877; ~1877–1889).

nodes.label: Trinity College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学トリニティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Cornelis Petrus Tiele
nodes.jawiki: コルネーリス・ティーレ
nodes.summary: Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) studied at the University of Amsterdam and Remonstrant Seminary. A religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar, he held posts at Rotterdam, Remonstrant Seminary, Leiden University (1877–1901), and the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Teruji Ishizu
nodes.summary: A religious studies and philosophy scholar, Ishizu studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). His posts included president of Tohoku University (1963–1966), president of Miyagi University of Education (1965), and professorships at Keio and Komazawa universities (1966).

nodes.label: Ichiro Hori
nodes.summary: Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1965) and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

nodes.label: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha
nodes.description: Indian archeologist and historian from Bihar
nodes.summary: Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Patna University and the University of London under Lionel David Barnett, later serving as head of department at Patna University and at Patna College.

nodes.label: Patna University
variants: Department of History and Archaeology at Patna University

nodes.label: Thomas Oberlies
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, Oberlies studied under Paul Thieme and Albrecht Wezler, and held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Peter Schreiner
nodes.summary: Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who earned his PhD under Paul Hacker at Münster and completed his Habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen (1974–1982), SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).

nodes.label: Lille 3 University
variants: Charles-de-Gaulle University of Arts and Social Sciences

nodes.label: August Hjalmar Edgren
nodes.summary: August Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Gothenburg, and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

nodes.label: Per Kjeld Sørensen
nodes.summary: Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh, later serving as lecturer there (1982–1989) and as professor at Leipzig University (1994–2017).

nodes.label: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy, he earned his Geshe degree at Menri Monastery's Dialectic School. He served as its director (~1986–1989), held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and founded Ligmincha International.

nodes.label: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima
variants: H. H. Menri Khen Rinpoche Lungdog Denpa Nyima
nodes.summary: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (1927–2017) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and at Kyangtsang Monastery. He lectured at the University of Oslo in 1967 and became abbot of Menri Monastery in 1969.

nodes.label: Anne C. Klein
nodes.summary: Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and a PhD at the University of Virginia (~1974–1981). Around 1990, she became Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University.

nodes.label: Geshe Tshondru Kongpel
nodes.summary: Geshe Tshondru Kongpel was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned Geshe degrees at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Center for Cultural Studies at Rice University

nodes.label: Gergely Hidas
nodes.summary: Gergely Hidas specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, and subsequently held posts as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and as a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum.

nodes.label: Hermann Hirt
nodes.summary: Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Hirt studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University. He taught at Leipzig University from 1891 to 1912 and was a professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Giessen from 1912 to 1936.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Streitberg
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Münster, Berlin, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann. He held professorships at the University of Fribourg, University of Münster, University of Munich, and Leipzig University (1920-1925).

nodes.label: Donald R. Davis Jr.
nodes.summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist. He studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle (attested 2005), and Ludo Rocher.

nodes.label: Richard W. Lariviere
nodes.summary: Indologist Richard W. Lariviere studied at the University of Iowa and completed his Sanskrit doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. His career includes serving as dean at UT Austin, provost at the University of Kansas, and president of both the University of Oregon and the Field Museum.

nodes.label: Timothy Lubin
nodes.summary: Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1994. He was attested as holding a post at Washington and Lee University in 2020.

nodes.label: Louis Dumont
nodes.summary: Louis Dumont specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Alain Froment. He held positions at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, University of Oxford, and the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales.

nodes.label: Anne Casile
nodes.summary: Anne Casile is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. Her posts include AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (attested 2009) and a position at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development.

nodes.label: Virendra Nath Misra
nodes.summary: Virendra Nath Misra was an Indian scholar of Indology and archaeology who studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961). He was Director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1993–2000).

nodes.label: Heidi Pauwels
nodes.summary: Heidi Pauwels (b. 1963) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Washington under Alan W. Entwistle, lectured at SOAS (1994–1996), and became a professor at the University of Washington (1996–2009).

nodes.label: Karl Benedikt Hase
nodes.summary: Karl Benedikt Hase (1780-1864) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the universities of Jena and Helmstedt. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1805-1864), École des langues orientales (1816-1864), and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (1852-1864).

nodes.label: Helga Uebach
nodes.summary: Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich (~1961–1967) and joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1964 as a research associate.

nodes.summary: Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich. From around 1978 to 2004, he worked at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Erich Haenisch

nodes.summary: A scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, Haenisch studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Grube. He held professorships at Leipzig (~1925–1932), Berlin (1932), Munich (1927–1951), and Göttingen (1925).

nodes.label: Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Tatsushi Tamai
nodes.summary: Tatsushi Tamai is a scholar in Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a Visiting Researcher at Soka University (attested 2013) and its International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (attested 2010–2016).

nodes.label: Saraju Rath
nodes.summary: Saraju Rath is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

nodes.label: Christopher Minkowski
nodes.summary: Christopher Minkowski (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Delhi, and held posts at Brown, Cornell (1989–2006), and the University of Oxford as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

nodes.label: Gérard Colas
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, Gérard Colas served as a researcher at the CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Kim Plofker
nodes.summary: In Indology and history/archaeology, she studied at Haverford College and Brown University (PhD 1995 under David Pingree). She held posts at Brown (1989), MIT (2000–2004), Utrecht (2004–2005), and Union College (2007, 2012, 2019).

nodes.description: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma, Dept. of Sanskrit, Aligarh Muslim U., Aligarh-202002
nodes.summary: Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966), he served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.

nodes.label: Jack Goody
nodes.summary: Jack Goody (1919–2015) worked in history and archaeology. Educated at St Albans School and St John's College, Cambridge (~1938–1946), he later held a post as a professor at the University of Cambridge from ~1973 to 1984.

nodes.label: S. N. Savadi
nodes.summary: S. N. Savadi is an Indology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

nodes.label: Sao Htun Hmat Win
nodes.summary: Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

nodes.label: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar
nodes.summary: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist who taught Masaaki Hattori. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Arts & Science College (~1922–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957).

nodes.label: Subhash Kak
nodes.image: Subhash Kak at Single Photon Workshop, Geneva, July 2015.jpg
nodes.summary: Subhash Kak (born 1947) works in Indology and engineering. He earned degrees from NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan, later serving as a professor at Louisiana State University from 1979 and Regents Professor at Oklahoma State University from 2007.

nodes.label: Albert Debrunner
nodes.summary: Albert Debrunner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ferdinand Sommer, Alfred Körte, Friedrich Leo, and Jacob Wackernagel. He held professorships and posts at the universities of Zurich, Greifswald, Bern, Jena, and Basel between 1917 and 1949.

nodes.label: Robert B. Ekvall
nodes.description: missionary, explorer, ethnographer, curator of Asian ethnology (1898-1983)
nodes.summary: Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He was a research associate at the University of Chicago (~1953–1957), a research fellow and chairman at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (~1975–1983).

nodes.label: Csaba Dezső
nodes.summary: Csaba Dezső (b. 1973) is an Indologist who earned master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1998–2004). He became an Assistant Lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2003.

nodes.label: R. Sathyanarayana
nodes.summary: R. Sathyanarayana was an Indologist who earned a master's degree in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

nodes.label: Surendranath Dasgupta
variants: スレンドラナート・ダスグプタ
nodes.description: Bengali scholar of Sanskrit and philosophy (1887-1952)
nodes.summary: Surendranath Dasgupta (1887–1952) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Calcutta and Cambridge under J. M. E. McTaggart and James Ward. His posts included Chittagong College, Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Calcutta.

nodes.label: Christopher Wallis
nodes.summary: Christopher Wallis is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt (PhD 2014). He guest lectured at Naropa University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Robert P. Goldman
nodes.summary: Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, also training under traditional pandits. He became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley circa 1971.

nodes.label: M. Seshagiri Sastri
nodes.summary: M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 1899, he is attested as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Chennai.

nodes.label: K. Kunjunni Raja
nodes.summary: K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned PhDs at the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and at SOAS/University of London under John Brough, later serving as Reader at Madras and honorary director of Adyar Library (~1980–2005).

nodes.label: Harald Hauptmann
nodes.description: German praehistorian and near eastern archaeologist
nodes.summary: Harald Hauptmann (1936–2018) was an archaeologist who studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg (Promotion), and FU Berlin (Habilitation). He held professorships at FU Berlin and Heidelberg (1980–1994), and directed the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (1994–2001).

nodes.label: Shivram Dattatray Joshi
nodes.summary: Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (~1956–1960), Shankara Shastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department.

nodes.label: Peri Sarveswara Sharma
nodes.summary: Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1968–1972) and held a post at the University of Marburg (~1973–1991).

nodes.label: Luca Maria Olivieri
nodes.summary: Luca Maria Olivieri works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin (c. 2006–2010), he served as director of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and joined Ca' Foscari University of Venice c. 2020.

nodes.label: Presidency University
variants: Presidency College of the University of Calcutta
Presidency College der University of Calcutta
Presidency College an der University of Calcutta

nodes.label: Florinda De Simini
nodes.summary: Florinda De Simini (born 1983) is an Indology scholar who held positions at the University of Naples Federico II (~2015–2018) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2019).

nodes.label: Andrea Acri
nodes.summary: Andrea Acri is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (~2006-2011) supervised by Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, and was appointed maître de conférences/assistant professor in tantric studies at the EPHE in 2016.

nodes.label: Nirajan Kafle
nodes.summary: Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University in 2015 under Peter Bisschop, also studying under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyaupane. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Leiden University.

nodes.label: John Myrdhin Reynolds
nodes.summary: John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Namkhai Norbu.

nodes.label: Namkhai Norbu
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Namkhai Norbu studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khams bre bshad grwa. He held posts at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples from the 1960s to 1992.

nodes.label: Triten Norbutse Monastery
variants: Tritan Norbutse Bon Education Centre of Nepal
Khri brtan nor bu rtse Monastery

nodes.label: Megumu Honda
nodes.summary: Megumu Honda was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells, later serving as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Paul Tedesco
nodes.summary: Paul Tedesco worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. After studying philology at the University of Vienna (1916–1921), he held research and faculty posts at Princeton (~1944–1952) and Yale University (1943, 1952, and 1960–1966).

nodes.label: Rulon Wells
nodes.summary: Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Utah (1935–1939) and Harvard University (1939–1942) before serving on the faculty at Yale University from around 1945 to 1989.

nodes.label: Johannes Rahder
nodes.summary: Johannes Rahder (1898–1988) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at Utrecht University, he held posts at Utrecht, Leiden University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and served as professor at Yale University from 1947 to 1965.

nodes.label: Eng Jin Ooi
nodes.summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at Mahidol University (2021). His doctoral supervisors were Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

nodes.label: Walter Clawiter
nodes.description: born:1923|died:1970|; Clawiter, Walter 1923-1970; Clawiter; Clawiter, Walter ....-1970; Clawiter, Walter, m. 1970

nodes.label: Zhihua Yao
nodes.summary: Zhihua Yao works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1996-2002), and held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2003) and The University of Hong Kong (2005).

nodes.label: Dipesh Chakrabarty
variants: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.jawiki: ディペシュ・チャクラバルティ
nodes.summary: Dipesh Chakrabarty (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD), he taught at the University of Melbourne (~1984–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

nodes.label: Christopher Pinney
nodes.image: The President, Shri Pranab Mukherjee presenting the Padma Shri Award to Prof. Christopher Pinney, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 20, 2013.jpg
nodes.summary: Christopher Pinney (born 1959) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (~1993–1994) and University College London (from ~2000), along with positions at Chicago, Cape Town, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Northwestern.

nodes.label: Siniruddha Dash
nodes.summary: Siniruddha Dash is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and held directorships at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library and K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

nodes.label: Godabarish Mishra
nodes.summary: Godabarish Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Ravenshaw University and the University of Calcutta, worked at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya and Chakradharpur High School, and served as Director at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: C. Kunhan Raja
nodes.summary: C. Kunhan Raja (1895–1963) was an indologist who served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras, attested in 1927 and 1946.

nodes.label: N. Veezhinathan
nodes.summary: N. Veezhinathan is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University under A. Sankaran. After research at Deccan College (1960–1963), he became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964, succeeding K. Kunjunni Raja.

nodes.label: Elisa Freschi
nodes.summary: Elisa Freschi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under Raffaele Torella (~2002–2006). She has held posts at Sapienza University of Rome, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna University, and IKGA (~2017–2022).

nodes.label: Nirmal Chandra Sinha
nodes.summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a historian and Tibetologist who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He worked at the National Archives of India and served as the founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987).

nodes.label: John Taber
nodes.summary: John Taber is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg, studying under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (~1982–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989–2021).

nodes.label: K. Srinivasan
nodes.summary: K. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and held a post at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Khammai Dhammasami
nodes.image: ၸဝ်ႈၶူးလူင်ထမ်ႇမသႃႇမိ.jpg
nodes.summary: Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~1999–2004). He served as Oxford Buddhist chaplain, founded Oxford Buddha Vihara and Shan State Buddhist University, and taught at ITBMU.

nodes.label: Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies
variants: Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, University of Oxford

nodes.label: Volker Grabowsky
nodes.summary: Volker Grabowsky is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies. Educated at Kiel, Chiang Mai, and Hamburg, he held posts at Passau, Hamburg, the National University of Laos, and Münster, before becoming chair of Thai language and culture at Hamburg in 2009.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Guthrie
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1994. She served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Peter Gyallay-Pap
nodes.summary: Peter Gyallay-Pap works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics (-1990) and held an adjunct post at Adams State University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Ian Harris
nodes.summary: Ian Harris (1952–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Cambridge and Lancaster. He founded the UKABS and held positions at St Martin's College (~1985–2007) and the University of Cumbria (attested 2000–2014), among others.

nodes.label: University of Cumbria
variants: University College of St. Martin, Lancaster

nodes.label: Peter Koret
nodes.summary: Peter Koret specializes in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: El Colegio de México
variants: Center for Asian and African Studies at El Colegio de México

nodes.label: Juliane Schober
nodes.summary: Juliane Schober is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Hugo David
nodes.summary: Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012, studying with traditional teachers. He held a Newton Fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of EFEO in 2015.

variants: The Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, Madras

nodes.label: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi
nodes.summary: Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, earning PhDs from Central Sanskrit University and National Sanskrit University. He held posts at JRRSU and Karnataka Samskrit University.

nodes.label: N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya
nodes.summary: N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1989–2017).

nodes.label: Vincenzo Vergiani
nodes.summary: Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Raffaele Torella (~1996–2001) and held a post at the University of Cambridge around 2012.

nodes.label: Stewart McFarlane
nodes.summary: Stewart McFarlane is a scholar in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who held an attested post at Lancaster University's Department of Religious Studies in 1991 and 2001.

nodes.label: Turrell V. Wylie
variants: タレル・ヴァール・ワイリー
nodes.summary: Turrell V. Wylie specialized in Tibetology, Sinology, and linguistics, earning a B.A. from the University of Washington, which he founded. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche, later serving as professor at the University of Washington.

nodes.label: Bret W. Davis
nodes.summary: Bret W. Davis is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto universities. He taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin universities and held philosophy professorships at Loyola University Maryland attested in 2007 and 2018.

nodes.label: Jake H. Davis
nodes.summary: Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi, and CUNY, and studied under Sayadaw U Pandita. He held positions at Brown University, New York University, and City College of New York.

nodes.label: City University of New York
variants: the City University of New York
ニューヨーク市立大学

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Pandita
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw, taught meditation at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (from 1955), succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991), and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.

nodes.label: William Edelglass
nodes.summary: William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

nodes.label: Alan Fox
nodes.summary: Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University (attested 1988) and held academic posts in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Delaware.

nodes.label: Brendan S. Gillon
nodes.summary: Brendan S. Gillon specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (c. 1980–1985) and became an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992.

マギル大学イスラーム研究所

nodes.label: Richard P. Hayes
nodes.summary: Richard P. Hayes is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who earned his doctorate from the University of Toronto. He held posts at Toronto, McGill University, Leiden University, and the University of New Mexico.

nodes.label: Fordham University
variants: フォーダム大学のリンカーンセンターキャンパスの人類学研究室

nodes.label: Marc Tiefenauer
nodes.summary: Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist. He studied under Nahid Rouzbeh and completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst.

nodes.label: Christine Chojnacki
nodes.summary: Christine Chojnacki is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and is attested as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 in 2018.

nodes.label: Ingo Strauch
nodes.summary: Ingo Strauch is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He taught Kathrin Holz and was attested as a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2018.

nodes.label: Emi Matsushita
nodes.summary: Emi Matsushita is an archaeology and art history scholar. She studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, holding posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State.

nodes.label: University of East Anglia
variants: イースト・アングリア大学

nodes.label: Bahadur Chand Chhabra
nodes.summary: Bahadur Chand Chhabra was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), as Government Epigraphist, and as professor at Panjab University (~1965).

nodes.label: Nalinaksha Dutt
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nalinaksha Dutt studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (PhD), and SOAS University of London (DLitt). He held posts at Judson College, University of Calcutta, The Asiatic Society, and Maha Bodhi Society.

nodes.label: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist who studied at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, and Sanskrit College and University (1952).

nodes.label: Shaman Hatley
nodes.summary: Shaman Hatley specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania, later teaching at Concordia University (~2007–2015) and becoming chair of Asian studies at the University of Massachusetts Boston in 2015.

nodes.label: Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule
nodes.summary: Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (circa 1955–1968) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (circa 1968–1981).

nodes.label: Natasja Bosma
nodes.summary: Natasja Bosma (born 1981) is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2012 and 2018 under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker.

nodes.label: Dale S. Wright
nodes.summary: Dale S. Wright specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wei Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann, and served as David B. and Mary H. Gamble Professor of Religious Studies and Asian Studies at Occidental College around 1978.

nodes.label: Sarah Lawrence College
variants: サラ・ローレンス大学

nodes.label: Michel Mohr
nodes.summary: Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who completed his PhD at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Mario Poceski
nodes.summary: Mario Poceski earned his PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, his appointments include the University of Iowa (2001) and Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies and Chinese Religions at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

nodes.label: University of Florida
variants: University of Florida College of Medicine
Center for the Study of Hindu Traditions

nodes.label: David E. Riggs
nodes.summary: David E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Los Angeles. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and the University of Hawaiʻi, and held research posts at Nichibunken and Oberlin College.

nodes.label: Albert Welter
nodes.summary: Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2013) and the University of Arizona, beginning in 2013.

nodes.label: Anthony Tribe
nodes.summary: Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and Oxford under Paul Williams, Steven Collins, and Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Montana (1997) and University of Arizona (2020).

nodes.label: University of Arizona
variants: Center for Buddhist Studies at the University of Arizona

nodes.label: Merton College
variants: Merton College an der Universität Oxford

nodes.label: Libbie Mills
nodes.summary: Libbie Mills works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2011 and was attested teaching Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto in 2020.

nodes.label: Nina Mirnig
nodes.summary: Nina Mirnig works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2010 and held a post at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020).

nodes.label: John Nemec
nodes.summary: John Nemec is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Rochester, UC Santa Barbara, Oxford, and Penn, under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. In 2020 he was attested as Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Stephen C. Berkwitz
nodes.summary: Stephen C. Berkwitz is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who conducted Fulbright research at the University of Kelaniya and the University of Colombo. He has served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

nodes.label: Pattaratorn Chirapravati
nodes.native: ภัทรธร จิรประวัติ
nodes.summary: Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Cornell University (~1991–1994) and served on the faculty at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), after positions at Silpakorn University, Tsukuba, and the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

nodes.label: Natasha Heller
nodes.summary: Natasha Heller specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005, held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley, and served as Assistant Professor at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Justin McDaniel
nodes.summary: Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist and religious studies. He has held posts as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

nodes.label: University of California, Riverside
variants: カリフォルニア大学リバーサイド校

nodes.label: Zenno Ikuno
nodes.summary: Zenno Ikuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Tokyo and held an academic post at Asia University (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Elke Rogersdotter
nodes.summary: Elke Rogersdotter specializes in archaeology and Indology. She earned her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), where she was supervised by Thomas B. Larsson and Bozena Werbart, with Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad serving as co-advisors.

nodes.label: Katragadda Paddayya
nodes.summary: Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his doctoral degree from Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1970–2008).

nodes.label: Asko Parpola
nodes.summary: Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968), Academy of Finland, and served as Professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

nodes.label: University of Helsinki
