Institute of Asian and African Studies, University of Helsinki
Helsinki Collegium for Advanced Studies, University of Helsinki

nodes.label: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer
nodes.description: American Archaeologist, worked on the Indus Valley Civilization sites and other places in South Asia
nodes.summary: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. Educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley, he became the George F. Dales Jr. & Barbara A. Dales Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

nodes.label: German Archaeological Institute
variants: Abteilung Istanbul des Deutschen Archäologischen Instituts

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Bodhi
nodes.description: American Theravada Buddhist monk and scholar (born 1944)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University and studied under Nyanaponika Thera. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of BAUS (2013).

nodes.label: Nyanaponika Thera
nodes.summary: Nyanaponika Thera (1901–1994) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Mahasi Sayadaw. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as leader and editor (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).

nodes.label: Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne
nodes.summary: Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne (1928–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London (PhD ~1954–1956), he held academic and dean posts at the University of Ceylon, Peradeniya, and Kelaniya.

nodes.label: University of Ceylon
variants: Department of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon

nodes.label: David Friedman
nodes.summary: David Friedman (1903–1984) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Between circa 1950 and 1970, he served as a professor at the University of London and as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS.

nodes.label: Guang Xing
nodes.summary: Guang Xing is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London (SOAS) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett, and held posts at the University of Hong Kong and the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Jing Yin
nodes.summary: Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He held positions at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2006), where he also served as Director (attested 2009–2010).

nodes.label: Edeltraud Harzer
nodes.summary: Edeltraud Harzer is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Charles University and the University of Washington, and under Shrinarayan Mishra. She has held posts at Stanford, Indiana University, and the University of Texas at Austin (1998).

nodes.label: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi
nodes.summary: Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi (1935–2021) was an Indologist who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University (~1995–2021), Chairman of Kalidasa Akademi, and Advisor at Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Steven Lindquist
nodes.summary: Steven Lindquist is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle. He also studied under traditional teachers and holds a post at Concordia University.

nodes.label: Matthew R. Sayers
nodes.summary: Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle, later holding a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

nodes.label: International Academy of Indian Culture
variants: International Academy of Indian Culture, New Delhi
International Academy of Indian Culture (Saraswati Vihar)

nodes.label: Ram Shankar Tripathi
nodes.summary: Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Ram Shankar Tripathi was Head of the Department of Bauddhadarśana at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1989–1998) and Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Stanley Wolpert
nodes.summary: Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was an Indology and history scholar educated at City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania. He spent his academic career at UCLA, serving as assistant professor (1959), associate professor (1963), and department chair (1967–2002).

nodes.label: Rosalind O'Hanlon
nodes.summary: Rosalind O'Hanlon is an Indology and history scholar who earned her PhD from SOAS (~1978–1983). She was a Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1985–2006), Professor in Indian History and Culture at Oxford (~2006–2020), and a British Academy Fellow (2020).

nodes.label: Wannaporn Rienjang
nodes.summary: Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge. She held positions at the British Museum, the Classical Art Research Centre (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

nodes.label: Peter Stewart
nodes.summary: Peter Stewart is a scholar of Indology, classical art, and archaeology. Educated at Clare College, Cambridge, he held posts at Reading and the Courtauld before becoming Director of the Classical Art Research Centre and Associate Professor at Oxford in 2011.

nodes.label: Quaid-i-Azam University
variants: Taxila Insititute of Asian Civilizations, Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad
Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations at Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad

nodes.label: Juhyung Rhi
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Rhi completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.

nodes.label: Thammasat University
variants: Faculty of Sociology and Anthropology, Thammasat University

nodes.label: Elphinstone College
variants: ボンベイ大学のエルフィンストーン・カレッジ
エルフィンストーン・カレッジ

nodes.label: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales
nodes.summary: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a bachelor's at Queens' College, Cambridge, and a Ph.D. at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden. He served as Field Director for the Greater-India Research Committee (~1934–1941).

nodes.label: John Allan
nodes.summary: John Allan (1884–1955) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist educated at Edinburgh and Leipzig. He served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum and lectured in Sanskrit at University College London, SOAS, and the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Jean Philippe Vogel
nodes.summary: Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under C. C. Uhlenbeck and Hendrik Kern at the University of Amsterdam. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and directed Leiden University and the Kern Institute.

nodes.label: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Cambridge (Ph.D.), Paris, and Berlin. He taught at Calcutta and later served at the Archaeological Survey of India, becoming its Director General from 1948 to 1950.

nodes.id: I:Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz
nodes.label: Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz
variants: Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur, Mainz
Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur zu Mainz
Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz
Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz
Academy of Sciences and Literature in Mainz
Arbeitsstelle für Historiographie und Geisteskultur Kaschmirs der Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur (Mainz)

nodes.label: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti
nodes.summary: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau at the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (professor, 1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad.

nodes.label: Osmania University
variants: Department of Linguistics at Osmania University

nodes.label: Angelika Malinar
nodes.summary: Angelika Malinar works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Mainz and Tübingen (PhD and Habilitation), she taught at the Free University of Berlin (~1999–2000) and SOAS (~2000–2007), becoming extraordinary professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.

nodes.label: Heinrich von Stietencron
nodes.image: Pranab Mukherjee conferring the first ‘Distinguished Indologist’ Award to the Prof. Emeritus Heinrich Freiherr Von Stietencron of the Federal Republic of Germany at the inauguration of the International Conference of.jpg
nodes.summary: Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS, and Heidelberg. He worked as an assistant at Heidelberg in 1965 and served as chairholder at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.

nodes.label: Ryutaro Tsuchida
nodes.summary: Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947), an Indologist, studied at the University of Tokyo and under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg. He served as an assistant at Marburg (~1980–1983) and later as professor and professor emeritus (1995–2012) at Tokyo.

nodes.label: Tej Ram Sharma
nodes.summary: Tej Ram Sharma is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctorate at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University around 1970.

nodes.label: Vishwa Nath Pathak
nodes.summary: Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, where he is attested as a professor in 1987.

nodes.label: Travis L. Smith
nodes.summary: Travis L. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and Columbia University, working under John Stratton Hawley, Vasudha Dalmia, and Robert and Sally Goldman, and held posts at Barnard College and the University of Florida.

nodes.label: Barnard College
variants: バーナード・カレッジ

nodes.label: Vasudha Dalmia
nodes.description: professor of Hindi and Modern South Asian Studies
nodes.summary: Vasudha Dalmia is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Delhi, University of Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg University. Her career includes teaching at the University of Tübingen, UC Berkeley, Free University of Berlin, and Yale University.

nodes.label: Sally J. Sutherland Goldman
nodes.summary: Sally J. Sutherland Goldman specializes in Indology and linguistics. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1979), studied under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and Shrinivasa Shastri, and held a post at UC Berkeley (attested 1996).

nodes.label: Bisheshwar Nath Reu
nodes.summary: Bisheshwar Nath Reu (1890–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He headed the Archaeological Survey of India, Government Museum Jodhpur (~1927–1950), Sumer Public Library (~1923–1950), and Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.

nodes.label: C. S. Srinivasachari
nodes.summary: C. S. Srinivasachari (1890–1951) was an indologist and historian who held professorships at Pachaiyappa's College and Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

nodes.label: Adinath Neminath Upadhye
nodes.summary: Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who earned his BA and D.Litt. from the University of Mumbai. He taught Prakrit at Rajaram College (1930–1962), served as Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University, and chaired Jaina studies at Mysore (1971).

nodes.label: Haridas Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Haridas Bhattacharyya (1891–1956) worked in philosophy and religious studies. After graduating from Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at both institutions, served as Reader at the University of Dhaka (1921), and held a post at BHU (1947).

nodes.label: T. N. Ramachandran
nodes.summary: T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) specialized in Indology and archaeology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1928–1934) and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

nodes.label: Alfred Cooper Woolner
nodes.description: British academic (1878–1936); Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab
nodes.summary: Alfred Cooper Woolner was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Registrar, Principal of the Oriental College, Honorary Librarian, and Vice Chancellor at the University of the Punjab.

nodes.label: Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya
nodes.summary: Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ganganatha Jha and at the universities of Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit. He served at Allahabad (from 1924) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand (~1956–1968).

nodes.label: Sheldon Pollock
nodes.summary: Sheldon Pollock is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his doctorate at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: David N. Lorenzen
nodes.summary: David N. Lorenzen specializes in Indology, history, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and served as a professor at El Colegio de México from 1970 to 2010.

nodes.label: Sonam Kachru
nodes.summary: Sonam Kachru is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He has held appointments at the University of Chicago Divinity School, Forum Transregionale Studien, and MPIWG.

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Mohanty
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Mohanty (1928–2023) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Presidency University (B.A.), Calcutta (M.A.), and Göttingen (Ph.D.). He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, Oklahoma, Emory, and was a professor at Temple University (~1986–2011).

nodes.label: Edward C. Dimock Jr.
nodes.summary: Edward C. Dimock Jr. worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Yale and Harvard (PhD 1959), he was an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972-1986).

nodes.label: Kashinath Trimbak Telang
nodes.description: Indian judge, Indologist, writer and translator (1850–1893)
nodes.summary: Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai under Narayan Mahadev Parmanand. He served at Elphinstone College, as syndic and vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

nodes.id: I:Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
nodes.label: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies
variants: Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies

nodes.label: Johannes Schneider
nodes.summary: Johannes Schneider (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He completed his Magister at the University of Marburg, followed by posts at the Free University of Berlin, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.

nodes.label: David Drewes
nodes.summary: David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia in 2006 under Karen Christina Lang. He held academic posts at Virginia, Indiana University, and the University of Manitoba.

nodes.label: Saroja Bhate
nodes.summary: Saroja Bhate (born 1942) works in Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from around 1992 to 2002 and was attested there as professor in 2011.

nodes.label: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh
nodes.summary: Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Fergusson College under R. D. Ranade, and taught by Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinvijaya, he was a Sanskrit and history professor at Gujarat Vidyapith.

nodes.label: Ramchandra B. Athavale
nodes.summary: Indologist Ramchandra B. Athavale served as Professor of Sanskrit at S. L. D. Arts College (attested 1938) and at Gujarat Vidyapith.

nodes.label: James McHugh
nodes.summary: James McHugh specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), working under Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He has held posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Anne E. Monius
nodes.summary: Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who completed her degrees at Harvard University (~1982–1997). She taught religious studies at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) before becoming professor of South Asian Religions at Harvard in 2002.

nodes.label: Parimal G. Patil
nodes.summary: Parimal G. Patil works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002), and was appointed Professor at Harvard University around 2004.

nodes.label: University of Southern California
variants: USC Shinso Ito Center for Japanese Religions and Culture
南カリフォルニア大学

nodes.label: Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University
variants: Department of Buddhism, Faculty of Buddhism

nodes.label: Pondicherry University
variants: Subramania Bharathi School of Tamil Language and Literature, Pondicherry University

nodes.label: K. A. Subramania Iyer
nodes.summary: K. A. Subramania Iyer (1896–1980) was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He served as a Professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.id: I:Department for the Publication of Oriental Manuscripts, Trivandrum
nodes.label: Department for the Publication of Oriental Manuscripts, Trivandrum
variants: Department for the Publication of Oriental Manuscripts, Trivandrum

nodes.label: Victor Turner
variants: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.jawiki: ヴィクター・ターナー
nodes.summary: Victor Turner was an anthropologist and religious studies scholar educated at UCL and the University of Manchester. He held positions at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, Manchester, Cornell University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Lawrence E. Sullivan
nodes.summary: Lawrence E. Sullivan is a scholar of religious studies. His appointments include Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (attested 2000), Professor at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004), and Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Joseph M. Kitagawa
nodes.summary: Joseph M. Kitagawa worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo University, Church Divinity School of the Pacific, Seabury-Western Theological Seminary, and under Joachim Wach at the University of Chicago (PhD). He served as professor and dean at Chicago.

nodes.id: I:Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies
nodes.label: Shimane Prefectural Junior College of International Studies
variants: 島根県立国際短期大学

nodes.label: Alexandra van der Geer
nodes.summary: Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Leendert van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Y. Sondaar.

nodes.label: Herbert Härtel
nodes.summary: Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Halle and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, Museum of Asian Art, Humboldt University, and Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Oliver Philipp Frey
nodes.summary: Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and held a post there.

nodes.label: Alessandro Graheli
nodes.summary: Alessandro Graheli is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. In 2022, he was attested as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and a principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Yasutaka Muroya
nodes.summary: Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held research associate positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2007), Leipzig University (attested 2015), and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

nodes.label: Philipp André Maas
nodes.summary: Philipp André Maas specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn in 2004 under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Bonn, the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig University.

nodes.label: Heike Oberlin
nodes.summary: Heike Oberlin (b. 1970) is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam, and Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), served as Scholar in Residence at Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and was a guest professor at Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

nodes.label: Elena Mucciarelli
nodes.summary: Elena Mucciarelli is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen. She held positions at the University of Tübingen (2016–2017) and the University of Groningen (2020) as Assistant Professor and Gonda Lecturer.

nodes.label: Annette L. Heitmann
nodes.summary: Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and earned a doctoral degree from the University of Vienna by 2002, studying under David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: Eshin Nishimura
nodes.summary: Eshin Nishimura specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University, Pendle Hill, and Kyoto University, training under Zenkei Shibayama. He served as president and vice-president of Hanazono University and taught at Carleton College.

nodes.label: Paul Pelliot
variants: ポール・ユジェーヌ・ペリオ
nodes.summary: A scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, Paul Pelliot studied in Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EFEO and the Collège de France (1911–1945).

nodes.label: Henri Cordier
nodes.image: Gustave Caillebotte - Henri Cordier - Google Art Project.jpg
nodes.description: French linguist, historian, ethnographer, author, editor and Orientalist (1849–1925)
nodes.summary: Henri Cordier was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from ca. 1881 to 1925 and at Sciences Po from ca. 1886 to 1925.

nodes.label: Noël Péri
nodes.summary: Noël Péri was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Western music at Tokyo Music School before holding posts as resident and secretary-librarian at École Française d'Extrême-Orient. He also founded Mélanges japonais in 1904.

nodes.label: Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises
variants: ベルギー中國學高等研究所
パリ大學中國學高等研究所

nodes.label: Gaston Renondeau
variants: ガストン・ルノンドー
nodes.image: Major Gaston Renondeau - Allied missions at Vladivostock LCCN2014708663 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who completed his education at the École Polytechnique around 1899 to 1901.

nodes.label: Henri Maspero
nodes.image: 201230 camp de Buchenwald dessins de prisonniers par Léon Mazeaud Henri Maspéro Bloc 61 1944 JB (2) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Henri Maspero was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and religion who studied under Édouard Chavannes and at INALCO. He held posts at EFEO, Collège de France (1918–1945), EPHE (ca. 1920–1945), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930), and the University of Paris (ca. 1937–1945).

nodes.label: Marcel Granet
nodes.summary: Marcel Granet was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1922–1940) and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (~1927–1940).

nodes.label: Étienne Balázs
variants: エティエンヌ・バラ―シュ
エティエンヌ・バラーシュ
nodes.summary: Sinologist and historian Étienne Balázs studied under doctoral supervisor Otto Franke (1923–1930). He later served as a senior researcher at CNRS (1949) and as professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).

nodes.label: Otto Franke
nodes.summary: Otto Franke was a sinologist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the chair of Chinese Language and Culture at the University of Hamburg and Hamburg Colonial Institute (1910–1923) and was professor of sinology at Humboldt University (1923–1931).

nodes.label: Jacques Gernet
nodes.summary: A scholar of sinology and history/archaeology, Jacques Gernet studied at the University of Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at the CNRS, EPHE (1955–1976), University of Paris, Paris Diderot University (~1969–1973), and Collège de France (1975–1992).

nodes.label: Paris Diderot University
variants: Lehr- und Forschungseinheit für ostasiatische Sprachen und Kulturen an der Universität Paris VII
Unit of teaching and research of languages and civilizations of East Asia

nodes.label: André Bareau
nodes.summary: André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at the CNRS (1947–1951), EPHE (1956–1973), and Collège de France (1971–1991).

nodes.label: Rolf A. Stein
nodes.summary: Rolf A. Stein was a Tibetologist and sinologist who studied under Paul Pelliot, Marcel Granet, and others. He served as directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).

nodes.label: Bernard Frank
variants: ベルナール・フランク
nodes.summary: Bernard Frank (1927–1996) was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf A. Stein. He headed the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

nodes.label: Michel Soymié
nodes.summary: Michel Soymié was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO (~1948–1952). He served at CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1952–1966), and held the Chair of History and Philosophy of Mediaeval China at EPHE (~1966–1992).

nodes.id: I:Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sezione di Studi Orientali
nodes.label: Istituto Italiano di Cultura, Sezione di Studi Orientali

nodes.id: I:Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe Senior High School
nodes.label: Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe Senior High School
Annette Schmiedchen
nodes.summary: Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian who earned a PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1989–1994) and her Habilitation at MLU Halle-Wittenberg (2008). She held posts at Halle-Wittenberg, the International Association of Sanskrit Studies, and Humboldt University.

nodes.label: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson
nodes.summary: Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson (1840–1890) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1858–1861). He later served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

nodes.label: Atsushi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Atsushi Kiyozawa completed his doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Joseph E. Schwartzberg
nodes.summary: Joseph E. Schwartzberg was an Indologist and geographer educated at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, the Sorbonne, and University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania and was a professor at the University of Minnesota (1964–2000).

nodes.label: Yaroslav Vassilkov
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Vassilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1961–1967). He held posts at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (~1978) and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

nodes.label: Adam Bowles
nodes.summary: Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Greg Bailey and served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

nodes.label: Greg Bailey
nodes.summary: Greg Bailey is an Indologist who studied under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He served as a professor at La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Julia Leslie
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Leslie held a post at SOAS University of London from approximately 1995 to 2004.

nodes.label: Palmira Brummett
nodes.summary: Palmira Brummett is a historian who earned degrees from the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She was a professor at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and a visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak
nodes.image: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak introducing himself for Voice intro project.jpg
nodes.summary: Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as its director in 1988, and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

nodes.label: Central Institute of Indian Languages
variants: Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore

nodes.label: Robin Coningham
nodes.summary: Robin Coningham is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin (PhD, ~1989–1994). He held posts at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).

nodes.label: Ryōō
nodes.summary: Ryōō (1856–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He taught at Tō-ji (東寺総学) and at Kōyasan University.

nodes.label: Friedrich Hirth
nodes.summary: Friedrich Hirth, a sinologist and historian, studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald. He worked for the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) before becoming the Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University (1902).

nodes.label: William Woodville Rockhill
variants: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ウッドヴィル・ロックヒル
nodes.summary: William Woodville Rockhill was a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and under Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1876–1884).

nodes.label: Govind Vishnu Kathavate
nodes.summary: Govind Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist who held the Sanskrit chair at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, succeeding Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar.

nodes.label: Andrew J. Nicholson
nodes.summary: Andrew J. Nicholson is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under traditional teacher Shrinarayan Mishra. He holds a post at Stony Brook University.

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.summary: John Marshall was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College, Cambridge, and under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.

nodes.label: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit
nodes.summary: Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist. He held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1944, succeeding Rakhal Das Banerji.

nodes.label: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917) and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).

nodes.label: George Abraham Grierson
variants: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・エイブラハム・グリアソン
nodes.description: Irish linguistic scholar and civil servant (1851–1941)
nodes.summary: George Abraham Grierson worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1898), was Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and governed SOAS (1917–1925).

nodes.label: M. H. Krishna
nodes.image: Portrait photograph of M. H. Krishna.jpg
nodes.summary: M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner. He held posts at Maharaja's College and the University of Mysore.

nodes.label: Charles Duroiselle
nodes.summary: Charles Duroiselle worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught Pali at the University of Rangoon, collaborated with the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma from 1912 to 1940.

nodes.label: Madeleine Biardeau
nodes.summary: Madeleine Biardeau was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religion who studied at the École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres and the University of Kerala. She served as a teacher at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Samuel
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Samuel is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Cambridge under Edmund Leach, Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, and Peter J. Wilson. He held professorships at Lancaster University, Newcastle, and Cardiff University.

nodes.label: University of Newcastle
variants: University of Newcastle, New South Wales

nodes.label: Sandra Bell
nodes.summary: Sandra Bell is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University in 1991 and also held an academic post there.

nodes.label: Jules Oppert
variants: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.jawiki: ジュール・オッペール
nodes.summary: A linguist and historian who earned his PhD at Kiel University, Oppert served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at INALCO (from 1857) and professor of Assyriology at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

nodes.label: Klaus Röhrborn
nodes.summary: Klaus Röhrborn specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen, working under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain, and served as professor of Turkology at Göttingen (1992–2003).

nodes.label: R. Venkatraman
nodes.summary: R. Venkatraman studied history, archaeology, and Indology at Madurai Kamaraj University, earning a PhD supervised by N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan. He served as a Reader at Madurai Kamaraj University (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Madurai Kamaraj University
variants: Department of Art History, M.K. University, Madurai

nodes.label: Kamil Václav Zvelebil
nodes.summary: Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) specialized in Indology and linguistics. After earning his PhD at Charles University (1946–1952), he held posts at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Charles University, and Utrecht University (~1976–1992).

nodes.label: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat
nodes.summary: Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1967–2004), worked at the EFEO and EHESS, and served as President of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (2010).

nodes.label: Herbert Niel Randle
nodes.summary: Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. He was a professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1908–1927) and served as Librarian at the India Office and the India Office Library (1927–1949).

nodes.label: Minobusan University
variants: 身延山大学東洋文化研究所

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Nichiren Buddhist Studies, Rissho University
nodes.label: Research Institute of Nichiren Buddhist Studies, Rissho University
variants: 立正大学日蓮教学研究所
立正大日蓮教学研究所

nodes.label: Gensho Imanari
nodes.summary: Gensho Imanari was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Waseda University. He was an assistant professor at Kokushikan University before becoming a professor and later professor emeritus at Rissho University.

nodes.label: Gyoshu Chojo
nodes.summary: Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and Minobusan University (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Masumi Mochizuki
nodes.summary: Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held posts at Minobusan University, serving as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhism (attested 2001) and later as a professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yukio Kotani
nodes.summary: Yukio Kotani (1931–) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, studying under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served at Rissho University from ca. 1974 to 2002 as emeritus professor of comparative literature.

nodes.label: Theosophical Society
variants: Kyoto branch of the Theosophical Society

nodes.label: Surama Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Surama Dasgupta (1907–1998) worked in philosophy and Indology. She studied under Surendranath Dasgupta and earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge before serving as a Reader in philosophy at the University of Lucknow.

nodes.label: Elizabeth A. Cecil
nodes.summary: Elizabeth A. Cecil is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at Hastings College, Tennessee, and Brown under James L. Fitzgerald, she held posts at Groningen, Leiden (~2016–2018), and Florida State University (~2018).

nodes.label: Sam van Schaik
nodes.summary: Sam van Schaik is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester (~1996–2000) and held posts at the British Library (from 1999) and SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Lewis Doney
nodes.summary: Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS University of London, completing an MA under Ulrich Pagel and a PhD. He held posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Anna Filigenzi
nodes.summary: Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2021).

nodes.label: Metropolitan Museum of Art
variants: Department of Asian Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art
Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

nodes.label: Jason Neelis
nodes.summary: Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon. He held posts at Washington, Käte Hamburger Kolleg, and Wilfrid Laurier University as Associate Professor and Department Chair.

nodes.label: Richard K. Payne
nodes.summary: Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1996–2019), with later affiliations at GTU and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Rijksmuseum
variants: Museum of Asiatic Art in Amsterdam

nodes.label: Max Deeg
nodes.summary: Max Deeg works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. After earning his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg, he served as Head of the School of Religious and Theological Studies at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021).

nodes.id: I:Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud
nodes.label: Centre d'Études de l'Inde et de l'Asie du Sud
Goethe University Frankfurt
variants: Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main

nodes.label: University of Luxembourg
variants: Department of Philosophy at the University of Luxembourg

nodes.label: Lhagpa Phuntshogs
nodes.summary: Lhagpa Phuntshogs (born 1942) works in Tibetology. He was president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and became Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center in 2000.

nodes.id: I:Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region
nodes.label: Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region
variants: Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region

nodes.label: Dramdul
nodes.summary: Dramdul works in Tibetology and Indology. He served as Director of the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2007) and editor-in-chief of Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
nodes.summary: Prods Oktor Skjærvø (born 1944) specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Oslo and Mainz, later holding academic positions at Mainz, Columbia University, and Harvard University as Aga Khan Professor (c. 1991–2015).

nodes.label: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indologist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1882 and 1914).

nodes.label: Vitus Angermeier
nodes.summary: Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita.

nodes.label: Thomas Edward Colebrooke
nodes.summary: Colebrooke studied at Eton College and East India Company College. Active in Indology, he served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

nodes.label: Pascale Hugon
nodes.summary: Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and its Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

nodes.label: Friedhelm Hardy
nodes.summary: Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral work at the University of Oxford. He served as Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987) and Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004).

nodes.label: A. N. Narasimhia
nodes.summary: A. N. Narasimhia specialized in linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD from SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.

nodes.label: Ralph Lilley Turner
nodes.description: Indic languages philologist and university administrator (1888–1983)
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Ralph Lilley Turner studied at Christ's College (~1907–1910). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and served as Director of SOAS University of London from 1922 to 1957.

nodes.label: Sanne Dokter-Mersch
nodes.summary: Sanne Dokter-Mersch is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

nodes.label: Heinrich Hettrich
nodes.summary: Heinrich Hettrich worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Saarland and Giessen, he completed his habilitation at Munich. He taught at Marburg and Würzburg, where he held the chair of comparative linguistics from 1989.

nodes.label: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis
nodes.summary: Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis (1916–2002) specialized in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Leiden University (ca. 1934–1939) and later held posts at SOAS University of London (ca. 1965–1981) and Leiden University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Nalini Balbir
nodes.summary: An Indologist and linguist, Nalini Balbir studied under Colette Caillat. She held research and academic posts at the CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), INALCO (~1988), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2000).

nodes.label: Sylvain Brocquet
nodes.summary: Sylvain Brocquet is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Marie-Claude Porcher, and he held an academic post at Aix-Marseille University.

nodes.label: Aix-Marseille University
variants: エクス＝マルセイユ大学

nodes.label: Whitney Cox
nodes.summary: Whitney Cox works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago (~1999–2006) under Sheldon Pollock, and held an attested post at the University of Chicago in 2003.

nodes.label: Bard College
variants: Institute of Advanced Theology, Bard College

nodes.label: François Gros
nodes.summary: François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Lyon from 1950 to 1954 and later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1977 to 2002.

nodes.label: Albert Lutz
nodes.description: Swiss art historian, director Museum Rietberg
nodes.summary: Albert Lutz is a scholar in Sinology and archaeology who studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker. He served at the Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art from 1982 and as director from 1998 to 2019.

nodes.label: Michael Jansen
nodes.summary: Michael Jansen was an archaeologist and historian educated at Bonn, Sapienza, Delhi, the Archaeological Survey of India, and RWTH Aachen (PhD ca. 1974–1979). He served as dean at RWTH Aachen, founding rector at GUtech Oman, and president of the Research Centre Indian Ocean.

nodes.label: Christoph Cüppers
nodes.summary: Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (1976–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, later serving as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (circa 1993–2013).

nodes.label: Christopher Key Chapple
nodes.summary: Christopher Key Chapple is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982), Stony Brook University (attested 1983), and Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

nodes.label: Bloomfield College
variants: Bloomfield College of Montclair State University

nodes.label: Ramesh Shankar Gupte
nodes.summary: Ramesh Shankar Gupte was an Indian historian and Indologist. In 1967, he headed the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and was a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest, Salem, and Winston-Salem State.

nodes.label: Radha Krishna Choudhary
nodes.summary: Radha Krishna Choudhary was an Indologist and historian who studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. He headed the history department at Ganesh Dutt College, served as principal of Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and taught at Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University.

nodes.label: Dineschandra Sircar
nodes.summary: Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1961, and held posts at the University of Calcutta as Lecturer (1937) and Carmichael Professor from 1962.

nodes.label: Ram Sharan Sharma
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma earned his PhD at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He headed history departments at Patna University (1958–1973) and the University of Delhi, and served as founding president of the ICHR (1972–1977).

nodes.label: Madhav M. Deshpande
nodes.summary: Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as Professor at the University of Michigan (attested in 1976 and 2006–2009).

nodes.label: Pandurang Vaman Kane
nodes.image: Pandurang Vaman Kane 2022 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai, he served as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and National Professor of Indology for the Government of India (~1959–1972).

nodes.label: Scindia Oriental Research Institute
variants: Scindia Oriental Institute at Vikram University, Ujjain

nodes.label: Amalananda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968), as a UNESCO consultant (1968–1970), and as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
variants: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.image: Photograph of Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan presented to First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy in 1962.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サルヴパッリー・ラーダークリシュナン
nodes.description: 2nd President and 1st Vice President of India, Indian philosopher and politician (1888–1975)
nodes.summary: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied at Voorhees College, Madras Christian College, and University of Madras. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and was Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities.

nodes.label: Edwin Whitfield Fay
nodes.summary: Edwin Whitfield Fay (1865–1920) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins, and Leipzig University. He held positions at the University of Michigan, Washington and Lee University, and the University of Texas at Austin.

nodes.label: Rhodes College
variants: South-Western Presbyterian University of Clarksville, Tennessee

nodes.label: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve
nodes.summary: Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He held professorships in Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

nodes.label: John Henry Wright
nodes.image: John Henry Wright young age photo.jpg
nodes.summary: John Henry Wright was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College and Leipzig University under Georg Curtius, holding posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard (~1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.

nodes.label: Herbert Weir Smyth
nodes.summary: Herbert Weir Smyth worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. His teaching posts included Williams College, Johns Hopkins, Bryn Mawr College, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Minton Warren
nodes.summary: Minton Warren was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). He served as Associate Professor of Latin at Johns Hopkins (1879–1899), directed the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899), and became Professor at Harvard in 1899.

nodes.label: James Wilson Bright
nodes.summary: James Wilson Bright was a linguist who earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882) and taught at Cornell (~1885). He served as the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

nodes.label: Yukio Yamanaka
nodes.summary: Yukio Yamanaka is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

nodes.id: I:Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies
nodes.label: Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies
variants: 知恩院浄土宗学研究所

nodes.label: Eisaku Okada
nodes.summary: Eisaku Okada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). His career includes appointments with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2014), Koyasan University (attested 2014), and Kyoto University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Huanhuan He
nodes.summary: Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University as a professor (attested 2015), and the University of Tokyo as a JSPS postdoctoral fellow (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Hisataka Ishida
nodes.summary: Hisataka Ishida specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Akira Saito, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, Masahiro Inami, and Helmut Krasser, earning a doctorate from the University of Vienna by 2011. He was a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University in 2015.

nodes.label: Chisan Denbo-in
variants: 真言宗智山派智山伝法院

nodes.label: Davadorjiin Pürevdorj
variants: ダワードルジ・プルプドルジ

nodes.label: Jianming Hu
nodes.summary: Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. Hu studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and was attested as a researcher at Komazawa University in 2015.

nodes.label: Shigeki Moro
nodes.summary: Shigeki Moro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai Universities under Ryoshun Okubo and Koyu Tamura. He served as associate professor at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and professor at Waseda University (2025).

nodes.label: Soto Zen Research Center
variants: 曹洞宗総合研究センター

variants: Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts
Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Taiwan

nodes.label: Hideyuki Matsumori
nodes.summary: Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held an assistant post there (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shinran Buddhist Center
variants: 真宗大谷派親鸞仏教センター

nodes.label: Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Gakuin
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派学院

nodes.label: Zijie Li
nodes.summary: Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015) and held a post as a DC research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Siegfried Lienhard
nodes.summary: Siegfried Lienhard studied Indology at Vienna, Paris, and Stockholm. He held posts at Göttingen, Banaras Hindu University, Kiel, Stockholm University, and the Collège de France, and served as Secretary General of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~1979–1994).

nodes.label: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar
nodes.summary: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and became General Editor of the Mahabharata at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 1925.

nodes.label: Paul Fredericq
nodes.description: historian, teacher, professor and rector from Belgium (1850-1920)
nodes.summary: A historian, Paul Fredericq studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège. He served as a professor at the University of Liège (1879–1883) and Ghent University, where he became rector in 1919.

nodes.label: Henri Pirenne
nodes.summary: Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the University of Liège, Ghent University, Berlin, Leipzig, University of Paris, and EPHE. He held posts at the University of Liège (ca. 1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1931 as Professor of History).

nodes.label: Kisari Mohan Ganguli
nodes.summary: Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) worked in the field of Indology. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya was an Indology scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University. He later held teaching posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

nodes.label: Michael Hutt
nodes.description: Professor of Nepali and Himalayan Studies
nodes.summary: Michael Hutt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA (ca. 1976–1980) and a doctorate (ca. 1980–1984) at the University of London. At SOAS, he served as a fellow, department head, and Associate Dean.

nodes.label: Yoshifumi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, where he was a research assistant (1986–1992), and served as associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

nodes.label: Francis Vincent Tiso
nodes.summary: Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary. He taught at Columbia, Sapienza University of Rome, the Archdiocese of San Francisco, and the Pontifical Gregorian University.

nodes.label: Lobsang Shastri
nodes.summary: Lobsang Shastri is a scholar in Tibetology. Shastri served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, attested 2003–2006, and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center, attested in 2018.

nodes.label: Albrecht Hanisch
nodes.summary: Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He has served as Acting Director of the Nepal Research Centre and Local Representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

nodes.label: Nepal Research Centre
variants: Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project und des Nepal Research Centre

nodes.label: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri
nodes.summary: S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri (1893–1942) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

nodes.label: R. Balasubramanian
nodes.summary: R. Balasubramanian was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. From around 1980 to 1989, he served as Director at the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Harold Coward
nodes.summary: Harold Coward (born 1936) is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. After earning a PhD from McMaster University, he served as Professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and as director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

nodes.label: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala
nodes.summary: Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Frank Raymond Allchin, and Harvard University. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).

nodes.label: Department of Archaeology
variants: Archaeological Survey Department of the Government of Sri Lanka

nodes.label: Tse-fu Kuan
nodes.summary: Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2004 under Richard Gombrich. He conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University.

nodes.label: Alexander Yiannopoulos
nodes.summary: Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling, with research supervised by Karin Myers alongside instruction from Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, Jay L. Garfield, and others.

nodes.label: John J. Makransky
nodes.summary: John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under numerous Buddhist teachers. His posts include Boston College (attested 1996–2007), Rangjung Yeshe Institute (attested 2007), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Jay L. Garfield
nodes.summary: Jay L. Garfield is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He has held professorships at Smith College, Hampshire College, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Melbourne, and the National University of Singapore.

nodes.label: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri
variants: シュリーニヴァーサ・シャーストリー
nodes.summary: T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972), where he served as Professor (attested 1984–1992).

nodes.label: Umakant Premanand Shah
nodes.summary: Umakant Premanand Shah worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was appointed deputy director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, in 1954, and became head of its Ramayana Project in 1965.

nodes.label: Yao Wang
nodes.summary: Yao Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He received traditional instruction from Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Tibet Academy of Social Sciences
variants: チベット社会科学アカデミー

nodes.id: I:Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
nodes.label: Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
variants: Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau

nodes.label: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski
nodes.summary: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski studied Indology, philosophy, and religious studies at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Oxford (PhD ~1975–1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), alongside traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Susan J. Rosenfield
nodes.summary: Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, having studied under Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.

nodes.label: Bhagavan Das
nodes.summary: Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who graduated with an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith, serving as headmaster of the latter from ~1921 to 1926.

nodes.label: John W. Spellman
nodes.summary: John W. Spellman was an Indologist and historian. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Windsor (~1967–1999).

nodes.label: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi
nodes.summary: Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi (1921–1994) worked in history, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University under Mohammad Habib, he held positions at the University of Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).

nodes.label: Thomas R. Trautmann
nodes.summary: Trautmann is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and held a post as professor for history and anthropology at the University of Michigan (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Bala Sahai Shastri
nodes.summary: Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist. He held posts at Panjab University, where he served as an Assistant (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Morgenroth
nodes.summary: Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena. He held academic posts at the universities of Greifswald and Jena, and was Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).

nodes.label: Richard Hauschild
nodes.summary: Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena, training under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. He served as Lektor at the University of Jena and joined the Saxon Academy of Sciences.

variants: Institute of Tibetan Cultural Heritage, Palace Museum, Beijing

variants: ヴィクトリア&アルバート博物館

nodes.label: Zhejiang Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology
Jinhua Jia
nodes.summary: Jinhua Jia is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Colorado under Paul W. Kroll. She held posts at Colorado, City University of Hong Kong, and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

nodes.label: International Christian University

国際基督教大学教養学部人文学科

variants: Needham Institute for the History of Science and Technology in East Asia

nodes.label: Mary Shepherd Slusser
nodes.description: American anthropologist, archaeologist and art historian (1918 - 2017)
nodes.summary: Mary Shepherd Slusser was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Michigan, Harvard, NYU, and Columbia University. She served at the US Department of State (1951–1958) and the National Museum of African Art (1971–1978).

nodes.label: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, Narmada Tarkatirtha, Panchanana Sastri, and Narayana Chandra Gosvami Nyāyācārya, as well as Gopinath Bhattacharya and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, holding a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Dipak Ranjan Das
nodes.summary: Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was attested in 1994 as a faculty member in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: Ram Karan Sharma
nodes.summary: Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

nodes.label: Arvind Sharma
nodes.summary: Arvind Sharma works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Allahabad, Syracuse, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Queensland (1976–1980), University of Sydney (1980), Harvard, and McGill University (Birks Chair in Comparative Religion, 1994).

nodes.label: Gyatsho Tshering
nodes.summary: Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. He served as Acting Director (1972) and Director (1974–1998) of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

nodes.label: Hans Harder
nodes.summary: Hans Harder is an Indology scholar who completed his Magister at Heidelberg University and his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das and Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he served as Assistent (1995–2007).

nodes.label: Ellen M. Raven
nodes.summary: Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She was affiliated with Leiden University, where her posts are attested in 2003 and in 2018 as a member of the Editorial Board.

nodes.label: Corrado Pensa
nodes.summary: Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome.

nodes.label: Sarva Daman Singh
nodes.summary: Sarva Daman Singh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

nodes.label: University of Queensland
variants: University of Queensland's School of Historical and Philosophical Inquiry
クイーンズランド大学

nodes.label: Govind Chandra Pande
nodes.image: The Vice President Shri Bhairon Singh Shekhawat presenting 13th "Saraswati Samman" award to Prof. G.C. Pande on his book 'Bhagirathi' at a function organised by K.K. Birla foundation in New Delhi on September 6, 2004.jpg
nodes.summary: Govind Chandra Pande was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan, professor at the University of Allahabad, and chairman of the Allahabad Museum.

nodes.label: K. V. Ramesh
nodes.summary: K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987) and Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Panjab University
variants: Visvesvaranand Institute of Sanskrit and Indological Studies der University of the Punjab

nodes.label: Oriental College
variants: Oriental College der University of the Punjab in Lahore

nodes.label: Gudrun Melzer
nodes.summary: Gudrun Melzer is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She completed her Doktorgrad der Philosophie and PhD at the University of Munich, studying under doctoral supervisor Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

nodes.label: Bruce B. Lawrence
nodes.summary: Bruce B. Lawrence, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at Princeton University, the Fay School, and the Episcopal Divinity School. He served as a professor at Duke University from approximately 1971 to 2014.

nodes.label: Annemarie Schimmel
nodes.summary: Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) was a religious studies scholar who earned doctorates from Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Marburg. She held professorships at Marburg (1946; 1953–1954), Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

nodes.label: B. N. K. Sharma
nodes.summary: B. N. K. Sharma was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Madras, Presidency College Chennai, and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. He held posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, Poornaprajna Sanskrit College, and Ramnarain Ruia College.

nodes.label: Arinde L. Jonker
nodes.summary: Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under Jonathan A. Silk and MA supervisor Peter Bisschop.

nodes.label: Hermann Goetz
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, Goetz studied at the University of Munich and under mentor Jean Philippe Vogel. He held posts at Leiden University, Baroda Museum, the National Gallery of Modern Art, and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery
variants: Museum des Maharadscha Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III von Baroda

nodes.label: Haraprasad Shastri
nodes.summary: Haraprasad Shastri (1853–1931) studied at Presidency College and Sanskrit College. In Indology and Buddhist studies, he was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1900–1908), head of Bengali and Sanskrit at University of Dhaka (1921–1924), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1919–1921).

nodes.label: Ibrahim Shah
nodes.summary: Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned a PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Farid Khan and Ihsan Ali. He served as Associate Professor and Chairman at Hazara University.

nodes.label: Ihsan Ali
nodes.summary: Ihsan Ali is a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin. His career includes serving as Professor at Peshawar, Director of Archaeology and Museums in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University.

nodes.label: Pratapaditya Pal
nodes.summary: Pratapaditya Pal (born 1935) specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Tibetology, earning degrees at Calcutta and Cambridge. He held curatorial and leadership posts at the Boston MFA, LACMA, the Art Institute of Chicago, and Norton Simon Museum.

nodes.id: I:Los Angeles County Museum of Art
nodes.label: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
variants: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

nodes.label: Adam Hardy
nodes.summary: Adam Hardy works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, he served as Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University (~2005) and directed PRASADA.

nodes.label: Joe Cribb
nodes.summary: Joe Cribb (b. 1947) is a scholar of numismatics, archaeology, and Indology educated at Queen Mary University of London. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and held leadership roles in the Royal and Oriental Numismatic Societies.

nodes.label: Hari Damodar Velankar
nodes.summary: Hari Damodar Velankar (1898–1967) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).

nodes.label: Charles Burnett
nodes.summary: Charles Burnett is a historian and philosopher who earned his BA and doctorate at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and notably the Warburg Institute, where he became professor in 1999.

nodes.label: Jan Pieter Hogendijk
nodes.description: Dutch mathematician and historian of science (born 1955)
nodes.summary: Jan Pieter Hogendijk (b. 1955) works in the history of mathematics. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under G. J. Toomer and held professorships in the history of mathematics at Leiden University (2004–2009) and Utrecht University (appointed 2005).

nodes.label: Warburg Institute
variants: ヴァールブルク研究所

nodes.label: Edwin Gerow
nodes.summary: Edwin Gerow (1931–2018) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–1997) and was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1985–1997).

nodes.id: I:Journal of the American Oriental Society
nodes.label: Journal of the American Oriental Society
variants: Journal of the American Oriental Society

nodes.label: Shlomo Pines
nodes.description: Israeli scholar of Jewish and Islamic philosophy (1908–1990)
nodes.summary: Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) specialized in philosophy and Indology, studying at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a lecturer at the University of Paris (1937) and was a philosophy professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

nodes.label: Rosane Rocher
nodes.summary: Rosane Rocher (born 1937) is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970), became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970), and headed the Rocher Foundation (~2013).

nodes.label: Sang-Kyun Sun
nodes.summary: Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Sanghasen Singh. In 1995, he held a post as a lecturer at Jingak Sangha University.

nodes.description: Buddhist scholar and professor of Indo Tibetan studies

nodes.label: Nicolas Morrissey
nodes.summary: Nicolas Morrissey specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen and holds a post at the University of Georgia.

nodes.id: I:State University of New York at New Paltz
nodes.label: State University of New York at New Paltz
Jinah Kim
nodes.summary: Jinah Kim works in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams and others. She held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Kurt A. Behrendt
nodes.summary: Kurt A. Behrendt (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1997) and became an assistant curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (~2006).

nodes.label: Drexel University
variants: Hahnemann University of the Health Sciences

nodes.label: Lionel David Barnett
nodes.summary: Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool (~1888–1892) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1892–1896). He served at the British Museum (1899–1948), University College London (1906–1917), and SOAS (1917–1948).

nodes.label: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch
nodes.summary: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under David P. Jackson and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held posts at the Universities of Hamburg, Munich, and Copenhagen, and worked on the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.

nodes.label: Gustaaf Houtman
nodes.summary: Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell, later serving there as a Senior Teaching Fellow (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Pyi Phyo Kyaw
nodes.summary: Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at King's College London in 2014 and was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow there in 2017.

nodes.label: Asatoshi Kamiya
nodes.summary: Asatoshi Kamiya studied Buddhist studies as a graduate student at Komazawa University (attested 1973). He later worked as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School (attested 1978).

nodes.label: Gail Hinich Sutherland
nodes.summary: Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Carol Bolon, Wendy Doniger, and Virendra Singh.

nodes.label: Narayan Hemandas Samtani
nodes.summary: Narayan Hemandas Samtani (born 1924) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Delhi, where he was also a research fellow, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1963–1984).

nodes.label: Prahlad Pradhan
nodes.summary: Prahlad Pradhan (1910–1982) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Patna and Visva-Bharati. He held posts at Visva-Bharati, Ravenshaw College, Utkal University, Gangadhar Meher University as principal, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

nodes.label: Mithila Sanskrit Research Institute
variants: Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research

nodes.label: N. Aiyaswami Sastri
nodes.summary: N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

nodes.label: Vidya Niwas Mishra
nodes.image: Dr. Vidhyanivas Mishra with Dr. Archana Dwivedi.jpg
nodes.summary: Vidya Niwas Mishra specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Allahabad under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya and at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University. He served as Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1986–1989).

nodes.label: Richard Peter Hottelet
nodes.summary: Richard Peter Hottelet is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, attested in 1971.

nodes.label: Marie G. Wanek
nodes.summary: Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and was taught by Sengaku Mayeda.

nodes.label: Giacomella Orofino
nodes.summary: Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981) and Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985) under Raniero Gnoli, and later taught at Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2000–2007).

nodes.label: Roger R. Jackson
nodes.summary: Roger R. Jackson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Carleton College from ~1989 to 2016.

nodes.label: John S. Strong
nodes.summary: John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He served as a professor of religious studies at Bates College from ~1978 to 2017.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden
