nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Yeshe Tobden studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Lodrö Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Kelsang Gyatso
variants: dGe bshes sKal bzang rgya mtsho
nodes.summary: Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sera Monastery and other monasteries under Trijang Rinpoche. He taught at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977 and founded the New Kadampa Tradition in 1991.

nodes.label: Thubten Zopa Rinpoche
variants: Thub bstan bzod pa rin po che
nodes.image: Kyabje Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche December 2008 Kopan monastery Nepal.jpg
nodes.summary: Thubten Zopa Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, studying at Dungkar Monastery and under Lama Thubten Yeshe, Geshe Rabten, and Tenzin Gyatso, among others. He founded the FPMT, serving as its spiritual director in 1984.

nodes.summary: Kurt Andrew Johnson is an Indology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

nodes.label: Martin Baumann
nodes.description: German university teacher in religious studies at university of Lucerne (Switzerland)
nodes.summary: Martin Baumann is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover and his Habilitation at Leipzig University, becoming Professor of Religious Studies and seminar head at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

nodes.label: J. Gordon Melton
nodes.summary: J. Gordon Melton (born 1942) works in religious studies. He studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1968) and held posts at UCSB (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).

nodes.label: George D. Bond
nodes.summary: George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Northwestern University and studied at the University of Sri Lanka. He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University from circa 1974 to 2012.

nodes.label: Richard Kieckhefer
nodes.summary: Richard Kieckhefer is a historian and religious studies scholar educated at Saint Louis University and the University of Texas at Austin (PhD 1972). He held posts at Monumenta Germaniae Historica and joined Northwestern University in 1975.

nodes.label: Gavin Flood
nodes.summary: Gavin Flood is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held professorships at the University of Stirling and the University of Oxford, where he also directed the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

nodes.label: Carola Roloff
nodes.summary: Carola Roloff is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang. She held posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, CIHTS, and the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).

nodes.label: Erling von Mende
nodes.summary: Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied at the universities of Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, completing his PhD and habilitation at Cologne. He served as a professor of sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.

nodes.label: Lutz Bieg
nodes.summary: Lutz Bieg (born 1943) is a Sinologist who earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University and completed his habilitation at the Free University of Berlin. From 1989 to 2008, he served as a professor at the University of Cologne.

nodes.label: Monika Zin
nodes.summary: Monika Zin specializes in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Jagiellonian University and the University of Munich, she taught at Munich and FU Berlin before becoming a project head at the Saxon Academy and honorary professor at Leipzig University.

nodes.summary: Dalsukh D. Malvania worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies after studying under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He held an attested post at Banaras Hindu University in 1951 and served as Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1965–1971).

nodes.label: Douglas Osto
nodes.summary: Douglas Osto, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned a Master's from the University of Washington and a PhD from SOAS under Ulrich Pagel (~2000–2004). In 2005 he joined Massey University, becoming Senior Lecturer around 2007.

nodes.label: Dan Lusthaus
nodes.summary: Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning a Ph.D. from Temple University under scholars including Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Bimal Krishna Matilal. He taught at institutions including Grinnell, Florida State, Georgia, and Harvard.

nodes.label: Gunapala Dharmasiri
nodes.summary: Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who held an academic post at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991 and 2008).

nodes.label: Ulrich Pagel
nodes.summary: Ulrich Pagel works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip T. Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Carola S. Carstens
nodes.summary: Carola S. Carstens is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2005 and held a post at Rice University (1998–1999).

nodes.label: Michael Balk
nodes.summary: Michael Balk is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Richard Carnac Temple
nodes.summary: Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who attended Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served in the Bengal Staff Corps and Indian Army, owned the Indian Antiquary (~1884–1931), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.

nodes.label: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff
nodes.summary: Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed PhDs at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours, and was a professor at Indiana University (1964–1982) and Hamburg (1982–1993).

nodes.label: William C. Kirby
nodes.summary: William C. Kirby (b. 1950) is a Sinologist and historian. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He was professor and dean at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) before becoming a dean at Harvard (~1992).

nodes.label: Philip A. Kuhn
nodes.summary: Philip A. Kuhn was a scholar of Sinology and history. Educated at Harvard, Georgetown, SOAS, and the Defense Language Institute, he served as associate professor at the University of Chicago (1963-1978) and center director at Harvard (1980-1986).

nodes.label: Nicola Di Cosmo
nodes.summary: Nicola Di Cosmo works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history. After earning his PhD from Indiana University (~1985–1991), he held posts at Harvard, Columbia, the University of Canterbury, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

nodes.label: Arthur Waley
variants: アーサー・デイヴィッド・ウェイリー
nodes.jawiki: アーサー・ウェイリー
nodes.summary: Arthur Waley (1889–1966) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at King's College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and held an honorary lectureship at SOAS in 1948.

nodes.label: Wm. Theodore de Bary
variants: ウィリアム・セオドア・ド・バリー
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・セオドア・ド・バリー
nodes.description: American sinologist and scholar of East Asian philosophy (1919–2017)
nodes.summary: Wm. Theodore de Bary was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. Educated primarily at Columbia University, he spent his career there as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies from 1953 to 2017 and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies (1969–1970).

nodes.label: Charles Alexander Moore
nodes.summary: Charles Alexander Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who studied at Yale (A.B., Ph.D.). He taught at Yale (~1933–1936), served as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1936–1967), and founded and edited Philosophy East and West.

nodes.label: William James
variants: ウィリアム・ジェームズ
nodes.image: William James by Alice M. Boughton, c. 1907, platinum print, from the National Portrait Gallery - NPG-NPG 87 37James-000001 (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ジェームズ
nodes.summary: William James was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Plymouth College, Harvard University, and Harvard Medical School, he held posts at Harvard as lecturer (1872), assistant professor (1876, 1880), and professor (1885).

nodes.label: Maurice O'Connell Walshe
nodes.summary: Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the University of London from around 1955 to 1979.

nodes.label: Ann Heirman
nodes.summary: Ann Heirman specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012), where she became a professor of Chinese language and culture and head of Buddhist studies (~2000).

nodes.label: Lisa N. Owen
nodes.summary: Lisa N. Owen specializes in Indology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995 and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Janice Leoshko.

nodes.label: Josiah Dwight Whitney
nodes.summary: Josiah Dwight Whitney studied at Yale University (~1836–1839) after attending Round Hill School and Phillips Academy. He held academic posts at the University of Iowa (~1855–1858) and as professor at Harvard University (1865–1896).

Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA)

nodes.label: Mattia Salvini
nodes.summary: Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski. He has held positions at Mahidol University and the International Buddhist College.

nodes.label: Daud Ali
nodes.summary: Daud Ali is a historian and Indologist. He earned his BA at William & Mary and his MA and PhD at the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught at SOAS (circa 1994–2008) before joining the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

nodes.label: Harold Hargreaves
nodes.description: British archaeologist; active in British India
nodes.summary: Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) was an Indologist and archaeologist. After heading Government Senior Secondary School, Amritsar (~1908–1914), he served in the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent (1914) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931), succeeding John Marshall in 1928.

nodes.label: Frederick M. Asher
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his academic career at the University of Minnesota from around 1971 to 2021, serving as a professor from around 1982 to 2021.

nodes.label: Shailendra Bhandare
nodes.summary: Shailendra Bhandare specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He has held positions as curator at the British Museum, a fellowship at the Fitzwilliam Museum, fellow at St Cross College (attested 2022), and assistant keeper in numismatics at the Ashmolean Museum.

nodes.label: Dilip K. Chakrabarti
nodes.summary: Dilip K. Chakrabarti is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta. He taught archaeology at Calcutta (1965-1977) and Delhi (1977-1990), and was later Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Cambridge (1990-2008).

nodes.label: Library of Congress
variants: Library of Congress Field Office in India
Library of Congress Middle Eastern Office
United States Library of Congress Field Office
John W. Kluge Center, Library of Congress
Library of Congress office in Delhi
Library of Congress New Delhi Field Office

nodes.label: Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute
variants: 長谷川仏教文化研究所

nodes.label: Krishna Kanta Handiqui
nodes.image: Krishna Kanta Handique 1983 stamp of India.jpg
nodes.summary: Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist who studied at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jagannath Barooah College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957), and founded the Hemalata Handique Memorial Institute.

nodes.label: Surya Kumar Bhuyan
nodes.summary: Surya Kumar Bhuyan (1894–1964) worked in Indology and history, studying at Cotton University, Presidency University, Calcutta, and SOAS. His career included roles at Cotton University, Jorhat Mission School, Nowgong College, and serving as Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1957–1958).

nodes.label: Banikanta Kakati
nodes.summary: Banikanta Kakati was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and later as Dean and department head at Gauhati University (1948).

nodes.label: Cathy Cantwell
nodes.summary: Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Kent (~1983–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

nodes.label: Robert Mayer
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Mayer studied at the University of Bristol and Leiden University under Alexis Sanderson, Tilmann Vetter, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. In 2002, he joined the Oriental Studies faculty at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Esho Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director of Bukkyo Bunka Kenkyujo (attested 1999) and president of the Kyushu Ryukoku Academic Society (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Fang-Kuei Li
nodes.summary: Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago, working under Edward Sapir. His career included posts at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Hellmut Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke after studies at Frankfurt, Kiel, and Grenoble. He held posts at Peking University (~1933–1948) and the University of Washington (1948–1971), and co-edited Monumenta Serica.

nodes.label: Joseph Rock
variants: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フランシス・チャールズ・ロック
nodes.summary: Joseph Rock worked in sinology and Tibetology. He held positions at the Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), the University of Hawaiʻi as botanist and curator (1908; 1911–1920), the United States Department of Agriculture (~1920–1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).

nodes.label: Peter M. Scharf
nodes.summary: Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist. He completed his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, also studying with Shrinarayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.

nodes.label: Qian Lin
nodes.summary: Qian Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Lin studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and earned a PhD from the University of Washington under Collett Cox, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and others.

nodes.label: Fudan University
variants: National Institute for Advanced Humanistic Studies at Fudan University

nodes.label: Amy Snyder Ohta
nodes.summary: Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of Washington around 1995.

nodes.label: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami
nodes.summary: Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She later held a post at the University of Washington, where she taught Qian Lin.

nodes.label: Itsuko Nishikawa
nodes.summary: Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, and held a post at the University of Washington.

nodes.label: University of Rangoon
variants: Pāli and Abhidhamma Department of the University of Yangon

nodes.label: Chi-chiang Huang
nodes.summary: Chi-chiang Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Arizona in 1986 under Jing-shen Tao, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: John Alexander Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Alexander Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. Supervised by Kenneth Herbert Joseph Gardiner, he earned his MA at the Australian National University, where he later held posts, and was senior lecturer at Griffith University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Miriam Levering
nodes.summary: Miriam Levering (born 1943) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

nodes.label: Whalen Lai
nodes.summary: Whalen Lai (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. After earning his BA at International Christian University and PhD at Harvard (~1968–1975), he taught at UIUC (~1976–1977) and the University of California, Davis (~1977–2003).

nodes.label: Taigen Dan Leighton
nodes.summary: Taigen Dan Leighton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned a BA from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from Graduate Theological Union. He taught as an adjunct professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Shohaku Okumura
nodes.summary: Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1970–1975). He founded Sanshin Zen Community and served as director of the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).

nodes.label: Ruth Fuller Sasaki
variants: ルース・フラー・エヴェレット
nodes.summary: Ruth Fuller Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at the University of Chicago and under D.T. Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She directed the Buddhist Society of America and served as abbess of Ryosen-an.

nodes.label: Ashin Nandamālābhivaṃsa
nodes.native: နန္ဒမာလာဘိဝံသ

nodes.label: University of Mandalay
variants: Department of Oriental Studies, Art and Sciences University, Mandalay

nodes.label: Harogadde Manappa Nayak
nodes.summary: Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

nodes.label: Ryosho Nakamura
nodes.summary: Ryosho Nakamura (1927-2013) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura (~1949-1953), and Rissho University (DLitt, 1977), later serving as professor at The International University of Kagoshima (~1968-1998).

nodes.label: Masanori Nakagawa
nodes.summary: Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and associate professor of literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

nodes.label: M. Shinoda
nodes.image: Linkin Park - From Zero Lead Press Photo - James Minchin III (Mike Shinoda).jpg
nodes.description: American musician, rapper, singer and songwriter
nodes.summary: M. Shinoda (born 1977) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami and attended Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design.

nodes.label: Mun-keat Choong
nodes.summary: Mun-keat Choong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland (MA and PhD), where he was supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell.

nodes.label: Roderick S. Bucknell
nodes.summary: Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Queensland, where he served starting around 1976 and later as Associate Professor from around 1995 to 2002.

nodes.label: Asim Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.description: indologist; writer; taught at Dept. of Ancient Hist. and Culture, Calcutta U., India
nodes.summary: Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta by 1967, where he was a Senior Research Fellow (attested 1970). He also lectured at Jangipur College.

nodes.label: Lobsang Dargyay
nodes.summary: Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and the University of Munich (~1969–1974), where he earned his Dr.phil.

nodes.label: K. V. Raman
nodes.summary: K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras, he served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1957–1976) and was Professor and Head at Madras (1976–1995).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson
nodes.image: Jeffrey Masson appearing on "After Dark", 23 September 1989.jpg
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard, earning his PhD in 1970. A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he taught at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and UC Berkeley as Professor of Sanskrit (1981–1992).

nodes.label: Anukul Chandra Banerjee
nodes.summary: Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, later teaching Pali there (attested 1943) and directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

nodes.label: Richard D. Mann
nodes.summary: Richard D. Mann works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at McMaster University (attested 2003) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Errington
nodes.description: specialist on the archaeology of Gandhara and the collections of Charles Masson, and a numismatist specialising in Asian coins
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Errington is a historian and archaeologist specializing in Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and held posts at the Fitzwilliam Museum, the British Institute of Persian Studies, Oxford, and the British Museum (1993).

nodes.label: Dorji Banzarov
nodes.summary: Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Imperial University (~1842–1846) under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski, as well as the école militaire russo-mongole.

nodes.label: Galsang Gomboev
nodes.summary: Galsang Gomboev worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855 to 1863.

nodes.label: Gombojab Tsybikov
nodes.summary: Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, and served as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).

nodes.label: Jamsrangiin Tseveen
nodes.summary: Jamsrangiin Tseveen (1881–1942) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences (~1921–1930), and worked at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Oriental Studies (1932–1937).

nodes.label: Mongolian Academy of Sciences
variants: Scientific Committee of the Mongolian People's Republic
Akademie der Wissenschaften der Mongolischen Volksrepublik

nodes.label: Scientific Committee of the Buryat-Mongolian ASSR
variants: Scientific Committee of the Buriat Mongolian ASSR

nodes.label: Sachindra Kumar Maity
nodes.summary: Sachindra Kumar Maity is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1953–1957) and held a post at Jadavpur University around 1958.

nodes.label: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar
nodes.summary: Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held positions at the Central Institute of Hindi and Kendriya Hindi Shikshan Mandal.

nodes.label: Anil Vidyalankar
nodes.summary: Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi (Ph.D.). He founded Sandhaan in 1988 and served as its director (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Iwao Nakajima
nodes.summary: Iwao Nakajima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hitotsubashi University under Nikki Kimura. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and is attested at Sandhaan in 1999.

nodes.label: Hitotsubashi University
variants: 一橋大学大学院社会学研究科

nodes.label: Ernst Fürlinger
nodes.summary: Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who habilitated at the University of Vienna. He held positions at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), the University of Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems (from 2007).

nodes.label: Robert M. Gimello
nodes.summary: Gimello specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. from Columbia University (~1969–1976). He was department head at the University of Arizona (~1981–2006) and a professor at Harvard University (~2001–2006).

nodes.label: Bruce Matthews
nodes.summary: Bruce Matthews, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, completed graduate studies at McMaster University. He was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Peradeniya and served as professor of comparative religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

nodes.label: Mathieu Boisvert
nodes.summary: Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at the Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992 and founded the GRIMER research group.

nodes.id: I:Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux
nodes.label: Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux
variants: Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux

nodes.label: Victor Chan
nodes.image: The Dalai Lama @ The Vancouver Peace Summit.jpg
nodes.summary: Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago. In 2005, he founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education and served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Larry DeVries
nodes.summary: Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He held teaching or research posts at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, Washington, Chicago, and Langara College.

nodes.label: Mavis L. Fenn
nodes.summary: Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at the University of Winnipeg, University of Calgary, and McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen, she held posts at St. Paul's University College (attested 2005–2006) and the University of Waterloo (attested 2016).

nodes.label: St. Paul's University College
variants: St Paul's College, University of Waterloo

nodes.label: James G. Mullens
nodes.summary: James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

nodes.label: Robert Florida
nodes.summary: Robert Florida works in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

nodes.label: University of Victoria
variants: Centre for the Study of Religion and Society at the University of Victoria
University of Victoria's Centre for Studies in Religion and Society

nodes.label: Baihui Wu
nodes.summary: Baihui Wu was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1945–1951), served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University, and worked at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and its Institute of Philosophy (~1978).

nodes.label: Robert Gardner
nodes.summary: Robert Gardner (1925–2014) earned his BA at Harvard University (~1943–1947), worked at the Fogg Museum (~1947–1949), and taught at the University of Puget Sound before serving as a professor at Harvard University (1956–1997).

nodes.label: R. Gordon Wasson
variants: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.jawiki: ロバート・ゴードン・ワッソン
nodes.summary: R. Gordon Wasson studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics. Active in religious studies and Indology, he held posts at journalism outlets, the Guaranty Trust Company of New York, J.P. Morgan & Co., and the American Council of Learned Societies.

nodes.label: Ernest Bender
nodes.summary: Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry M. Hoenigswald. He held faculty posts at the University of Pennsylvania from 1950 to 1989.

nodes.label: Paul Thieme
nodes.summary: Paul Thieme worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD and habilitation at Göttingen and also studied at Berlin and Allahabad. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973; emeritus 1975).

nodes.label: David Webster
nodes.summary: David Webster works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

nodes.label: University of Gloucestershire
variants: Cheltenham and Gloucester College of Higher Education

nodes.label: Kanai Lal Hazra
nodes.summary: Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed a PhD under Sirima Kiribamune at the University of Ceylon (~1964–1968), later lecturing in Pali at Calcutta (attested 1982).

nodes.label: Paul Fuller
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Paul Fuller completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Rupert Gethin, having also studied under Paul Dundas.

nodes.label: John Dowson
nodes.summary: John Dowson was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Edwin Norris. He held positions at the East India Company College (~1840–1858), the Royal Asiatic Society, Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877), and University College London (1855–1877).

nodes.label: Krishna Mohan Banerjee
nodes.summary: Krishna Mohan Banerjee was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics who studied at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College under Alexander Duff. He taught at Hare School and became Second Professor at Bishop's College in 1852.

nodes.label: Edward Backhouse Eastwick
nodes.summary: Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charterhouse and Oxford. He served as Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and worked at the Foreign Office (~1860-1863).

nodes.label: Christ's College
variants: ケンブリッジ大学クライスツ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
variants: ルートヴィヒ・ヨーゼフ・ヨーハン・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.jawiki: ルートヴィヒ・ウィトゲンシュタイン
nodes.summary: Philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein studied at Technische Hochschule Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge, where he earned his Ph.D. He taught as a lecturer, fellow, and professor of philosophy at Cambridge and Trinity College between 1929 and 1947.

nodes.label: Simo Parpola
nodes.summary: Simo Parpola is a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968) while also studying at the Pontifical Biblical Institute and British Museum. He held posts at Helsinki, Heidelberg, and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Pentti Aalto
nodes.summary: Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Gustaf John Ramstedt at the University of Helsinki (~1935–1939), where he served as Docent of Comparative Linguistics (1958–1980).

nodes.label: Kimmo Koskenniemi
nodes.summary: In linguistics, he studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and director of the BAULT research community (~2008–2013).

nodes.label: Eric Grinstead
nodes.summary: Specializing in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, Grinstead studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1945–1950). He held posts at the British Library (~1957–1970) and the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1969).

nodes.label: Frank Ernest Keay
nodes.birth_place: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames

nodes.label: Thomas Zehnder
nodes.summary: Zehnder works in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

nodes.label: Alexander Lubotsky
nodes.summary: Alexander Lubotsky is a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, later becoming full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.

nodes.label: Jan Gonda
nodes.summary: Jan Gonda (1905–1991) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Utrecht University under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff and at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and was Professor of Indology (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

nodes.label: Mirle Srinivasa Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: Mirle Srinivasa Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) specialized in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Mysore and Savitribai Phule Pune universities, he held posts at Karnatak University, the Karnataka archaeology department, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.id: I:Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage, Karnataka
nodes.label: Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage, Karnataka
Govind Swamirao Gai
nodes.summary: Govind Swamirao Gai was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India and Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), succeeding Dineschandra Sircar.

nodes.id: I:Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland
nodes.label: Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland
Weijen Teng
nodes.summary: Weijen Teng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University under supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and joined the faculty at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

nodes.label: Dylan Esler
nodes.summary: Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at SOAS University of London, completed a PhD at UCLouvain (until 2018), and served as a research scholar at UCLouvain.

Institut Orientaliste of the University of Louvain

nodes.label: University of Zagreb
variants: Faculty of Law at the University of Zagreb

nodes.label: Chen-kuo Lin
nodes.summary: Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at Temple University in 1991. He served as Professor (attested 1997–1999) and Distinguished Professor (attested 2014–2018) at National Chengchi University.

nodes.label: Andrea Schlosser
nodes.summary: Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed both a master's degree (by 2008) and a PhD (by 2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

nodes.label: Yao-ming Tsai
nodes.summary: Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Cristina Pecchia
nodes.summary: Cristina Pecchia works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (PhD ~1999–2003) and the University of Vienna, under Raniero Gnoli, Raffaele Torella, Corrado Pensa, and Ernst Steinkellner, later researching at IKGA.

nodes.label: K. Meenakshi
nodes.summary: K. Meenakshi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under M. A. Mehendale. She held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

nodes.label: M. A. Mehendale
nodes.summary: M. A. Mehendale (1918–2020) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983).

nodes.label: Jiryo Masuda
nodes.summary: Jiryo Masuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara (attested 1930). He later served as a professor at the University of Calcutta and taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

nodes.label: Adyar Library and Research Centre
variants: The Adyar Library and Research Centre
Adyar Library of Theosophical Society Adyar

nodes.label: James Haughton Woods
nodes.summary: James Haughton Woods worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard, the University of Strasbourg under Paul Deussen, and under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Arthur Venis, and Mukunda Shastri Adkar, later holding a post at Harvard in 1914.

nodes.label: Arthur Venis
nodes.summary: Arthur Venis (1857–1918) was an Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor and principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1881–1888) and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1888–1914).

ユニバーシティ・カレッジ

オックスフォード大学のコーパス・クリスティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Charles Henry Tawney
nodes.summary: Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as professor and principal at Presidency College, Chennai, headed Presidency University, and later served as librarian of the India Office Library from 1892 to 1903.

nodes.label: Robert Ford Campany
nodes.summary: Robert Ford Campany (born 1959) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He was a professor at Indiana University (~1989–2004) and later joined Vanderbilt University (~2010).

nodes.label: D. N. Shukla
nodes.summary: D. N. Shukla was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer and held an attested post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

nodes.label: Jitendra Nath Banerjea
nodes.summary: Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri around 1916–1918, taught Sarasi Kumar Saraswati, and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

nodes.label: Tiziana Pontillo
nodes.summary: Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.

nodes.label: David Burton
nodes.summary: David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). In 2010, he was attested as Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University.

nodes.label: Kodo Akino
nodes.summary: Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University, including president in 1909, and lectured at the University of Tokyo.

nodes.label: Nyoten Jinbo
nodes.summary: Nyoten Jinbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Baisen Azegami and held a professorship at Komazawa University.

nodes.label: Kōdō Yamada
nodes.summary: Kōdō Yamada (1868–1947) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Komazawa University and Keio University.

nodes.label: Totsudo Kato
nodes.summary: Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) studied Buddhist and religious studies under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Banne Shimada, attending Oriental Hall, Kyoto Legal School, and Chuo University. He held teaching posts at Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

nodes.label: Seiran Ouchi
nodes.summary: Seiran Ouchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (jiko) at Nishi Hongan-ji and as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

nodes.label: Tokugen Sakai
nodes.summary: Tokugen Sakai (1912–1996) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at Komazawa University from 1949 to 1987 and as a lecturer at Eihei-ji from 1977 to 1987.

nodes.label: Sokuo Eto
nodes.summary: Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo in 1937 and served as a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

nodes.label: Joseph Dalton Hooker
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・ダルトン・フッカー
nodes.summary: Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow from around 1832 to 1839. He worked at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847) and served as Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, from 1847 to 1885.

nodes.label: George Watt
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ワット (植物学者)
nodes.summary: George Watt studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. He held positions at the University of Glasgow, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Moodeen Sheriff
nodes.description: Indian surgeon and practitioner of native medicine
nodes.summary: Moodeen Sheriff was an Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College. He served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

nodes.label: Govind Vinayak Devasthali
nodes.summary: Govind Vinayak Devasthali was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. His career included posts as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts and RYK Science College and Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

nodes.label: Ram Niwas Pandey
nodes.summary: Ram Niwas Pandey, active in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and completed doctoral studies under Hit Narayan Jha.

nodes.id: I:Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology
nodes.label: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology
variants: School of Archaeology at New Delhi

nodes.label: Francis X. Clooney
nodes.summary: Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he was a professor at Boston College (1984–2005) and has held professorial and directorship roles at Harvard University since 2005.

nodes.label: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst
nodes.summary: Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who completed doctoral research under Julius Lipner (attested 2005). She held an academic post at the University of Manchester, attested in 2005.

nodes.label: Julius Lipner
nodes.summary: Julius Lipner (born 1946) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Hywel David Lewis at King's College London. He taught at Birmingham and was Professor of Hinduism and Comparative Religion at Cambridge (1975–2013).

nodes.label: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar
nodes.summary: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

nodes.id: I:Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet
nodes.label: Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet
variants: Administrative Commission of Museum and Archaeological Data, Tibet

nodes.label: Elliot M. Stern
nodes.summary: Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a PhD candidate until 1988 and earned his PhD in 1998.

nodes.label: Peter Gaeffke
nodes.summary: Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist who studied at Regensburg, Mainz (PhD 1952), and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003; visiting professor 1972).

nodes.label: James Morison
nodes.summary: James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as a librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

nodes.label: Kenneth Somerled Macdonald
nodes.image: Kenneth S. Macdonald, M.A., D.D. (page 8 crop).jpg

nodes.label: Erik Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik Zürcher was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University, studying under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Édouard Chavannes. He served as director at Leiden University (1961–1993).

nodes.label: John Powers
nodes.summary: John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his doctorate from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His appointments include the Australian National University (1995) and Deakin University (2016–2022).

nodes.label: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi
nodes.summary: Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was an Indologist and historian who earned his BA at Deccan College and a PhD from the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Mahavidyalaya, and later held chairmanships and professorships at Nagpur University.

nodes.label: Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University
variants: College of Indology of Nagpur University

nodes.label: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz
nodes.summary: Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Central Asian studies. She studied and completed her PhD and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, and became a professor (1999) and faculty dean (2007–2010) at the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Youru Wang
nodes.summary: Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, later serving at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.

nodes.label: Charles Wei-hsun Fu
nodes.summary: Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and the University of Illinois System (~1963–1969), and held an academic post at Ohio University (~1968–1972).

nodes.label: Marc Aurel Stein
variants: マーク・オーレル・スタイン
nodes.summary: Marc Aurel Stein was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology studies. He completed his PhD under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen and held posts at the University of the Punjab and Archaeological Survey of India.

nodes.label: Jinhua Chen
nodes.summary: Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University and Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held appointments at the University of Virginia and as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Pradyot Kumar Mukhopadhyay
nodes.summary: Pradyot Kumar Mukhopadhyay (born 1938) works in philosophy and Indology. He was a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University and served as a National Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research around 2007–2010.

nodes.label: Ana Agud
nodes.summary: Ana Agud is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Salamanca and the University of Tübingen. Around 1984, she became a professor in the Department of Classical and Indo-European Philology at the University of Salamanca.

nodes.label: Andrew Glass
nodes.summary: Andrew Glass is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed an MA (-2000) and PhD (-2006) at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon, and also studied at Bukkyo University (2003).

nodes.label: Embar Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held positions as a Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library and Research Institute, at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937), and at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1939).

nodes.label: Noémie Verdon
nodes.summary: Noémie Verdon is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand. She held a post attested at Kyoto University in 2019.

nodes.label: John Faithfull Fleet
nodes.summary: John Faithfull Fleet was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Merchant Taylors' School and University College London (~1865–1867), served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), was an Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886), and was a Fellow at the University of Mumbai.

nodes.label: Robert Sewell
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Sewell served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1868 to 1894 and as Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives from circa 1888 to 1894.

nodes.label: C. S. Sundaram
nodes.summary: C. S. Sundaram was an indologist who held posts at Madras Sanskrit College and the University of Madras, where he was appointed Reader in Sanskrit in 1951.

nodes.label: Masato Kobayashi
nodes.summary: Masato Kobayashi specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and completed his Ph.D. under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000). He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2005).

nodes.label: Junglan Bang
nodes.summary: Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seung-suk Jung, Sungdoo Ahn, and doctoral supervisor Harunaga Isaacson, earning a PhD from Hamburg in 2012. She also served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

nodes.label: Karma Lekshe Tsomo
nodes.description: Buddhist nun, scholar and social activist
nodes.summary: Karma Lekshe Tsomo works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied under Tenzin Gyatso and earned a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi. She held posts at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and the University of Hawaiʻi (2023).

nodes.id: I:Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
nodes.label: Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women
variants: Sakyadhita: International Association of Buddhist Women
Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women

nodes.label: Michael Alram
nodes.summary: Michael Alram is a specialist in numismatics, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer, holding major posts at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Kunsthistorisches Museum
variants: Münzkabinett des Kunsthistorischen Museums in Wien
Vienna Coin Cabinet at the Kunsthistorisches Museum

nodes.label: Deborah Klimburg-Salter
nodes.description: Austrian art historian and professor for non-European art history
nodes.summary: Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian of Asia working in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and completed her Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where she held the Chair of Asian Art History from 1994 to 2015.

nodes.label: Durga Prasad Dikshit
nodes.summary: Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He pursued his studies under R. K. Dikshit, Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.

nodes.label: Baij Nath Puri
nodes.summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist and historian. He earned his M. Lit. and D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (~1949–1951). He later served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971–1976).

nodes.label: Satya Swarup Misra
nodes.summary: Satya Swarup Misra (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

nodes.label: Reiner Wiehl
nodes.summary: Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt (Ph.D.). He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977), and taught John Taber.

nodes.label: University of Lille
variants: Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III

nodes.label: R. N. Gadre
nodes.summary: R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

nodes.label: R. P. Paranjpye
nodes.summary: R. P. Paranjpye studied under Vaman Shivram Apte and served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

nodes.label: Volker Caumanns
nodes.summary: Volker Caumanns specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson at the University of Hamburg and Franz-Karl Ehrhard at the University of Munich, where he was a research assistant (2006–2012) before posts at LIRI and the University of Bern.

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wackernagel
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wackernagel was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He served as professor and Ordinarius at the University of Basel from 1833 until 1869.

nodes.label: Haruka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1980–1990) and the University of Tokyo (~1990–2007).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Yamashita
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).

nodes.label: Nobuhiro Ota
nodes.summary: Nobuhiro Ota (born 1969) is an Indologist and historian who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. After research fellowships there, he joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, advancing from assistant in 2002 to professor in 2021.

nodes.label: Akio Tanabe
nodes.summary: Akio Tanabe works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor in 2015).

nodes.label: Nicolas Tournadre
variants: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.jawiki: ニコラ・トゥルナドル
nodes.summary: Nicolas Tournadre works in linguistics and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle under Claude Hagège and held positions at INALCO, Paris 8, the University of Provence, and Aix-Marseille University.

nodes.label: Khenpo Appey
nodes.summary: Khenpo Appey was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Drakgyab Lodrö, and served as director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985.

nodes.label: Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (~1984–2004) and Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel.

nodes.label: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under numerous teachers, including the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse. He founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute (1981) and became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (1976).

nodes.label: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Samten Gyatso, Dilgo Khyentse, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery and taught numerous disciples.

nodes.label: John Clifford Holt
nodes.summary: John Clifford Holt is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He served as Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (~1978–2014) and held the Numata Chair at Calgary in 2006.

nodes.label: Pahalawattage Don Premasiri
nodes.summary: Pahalawattage Don Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Peradeniya, University of Cambridge, University of Canterbury, and University of Hawaiʻi, later serving as professor and Pali and Buddhist Studies department head at Peradeniya.

nodes.label: Asanga Tilakaratne
nodes.summary: Asanga Tilakaratne works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. At the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, he served as Head of Buddhist Thought (attested 1993), Professor (~2003–2006), and Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Kelaniya.

nodes.label: Alvappillai Veluppillai
nodes.summary: Alvappillai Veluppillai was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under K. Kanapathypillai at the University of Peradeniya and Thomas Burrow at the University of Oxford. He taught at Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Mahinda Deegalle
nodes.image: Mahinda Deegalle in the video 'Imagine a Buddhist AI...'.png
nodes.summary: Mahinda Deegalle works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago, working with Reynolds, Doniger, and Eck. His posts include lecturer at Bath Spa (~2002) and visiting appointments at McGill, Harvard, and Colgate.

nodes.label: Abdur Rehman
nodes.summary: Abdur Rehman is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who completed a PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. By 1988, he held an assistant professorship at the University of Peshawar.

nodes.label: Luise Hercus
nodes.summary: Luise Hercus (1926–2018) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. She held positions at St Anne's College, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University.

nodes.label: Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw
nodes.summary: Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw (1919–1983) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Leiden and under Jan Gonda at Utrecht, later teaching at Groningen and Cambridge before directing the Institute of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Pamela Gutman
nodes.summary: Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She pursued studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University.

nodes.label: Phramaha Sakda Hemthep
nodes.summary: Phramaha Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MPhil at Cardiff University by 2014, supervised by Max Deeg.

nodes.label: Radhika Herzberger
nodes.summary: Radhika Herzberger is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Toronto in 1982 under the supervision of Bimal Krishna Matilal. Around 1982, she became Director of the Rishi Valley School.

nodes.label: Alois Anton Führer
nodes.summary: An Indologist and archaeologist, Führer earned a PhD from Würzburg and studied under Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, the Lucknow State Museum, the Archaeological Survey of India, and later the Christian Catholic Church.

nodes.label: Jean Dantinne
nodes.summary: Jean Dantinne was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte and served as a librarian at the University of Liège.

nodes.id: I:Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
nodes.label: Royal Academy of Science, Letters and Fine Arts of Belgium
variants: Académie royale des Sciences, des Lettres et des Beaux-Arts de Belgique
Königliche Akademie der Wissenschaften, Literatur und Schönen Künste Belgiens

nodes.label: Michael Carrithers
nodes.summary: Michael Carrithers is an anthropologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford, and held academic posts at Oxford, the London School of Economics, and Durham University (1982–present).

nodes.label: Caroline Humphrey
nodes.summary: Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, religious, and Indic studies who earned degrees from Cambridge and Leeds, studying under Edmund Leach. She taught at the University of Cambridge (1971–2010) and held fellowships at Girton and King's Colleges.

nodes.label: Klaus Bruhn
nodes.summary: Klaus Bruhn (1928–2016) was an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring. He served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991.

nodes.label: Mary Jaksch
nodes.summary: Mary Jaksch works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and trained under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

nodes.label: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez
nodes.summary: Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Peter Harvey and completed an MA at the University of Sunderland.

nodes.label: Patricia Berger
nodes.summary: Patricia Berger works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley, served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, and joined the History of Art faculty at UC Berkeley in 1996.

nodes.label: Vanderbilt University
variants: ヴァンダービルト大学

nodes.label: Sanjay Subrahmanyam
nodes.summary: Historian Sanjay Subrahmanyam studied at Sardar Patel Vidyalaya, St. Stephen's College, and the University of Delhi's Delhi School of Economics. His academic posts include positions at Oxford, the EHESS, the Collège de France, and the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Calambur Sivaramamurti
nodes.summary: Calambur Sivaramamurti (1910–1983) was an indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency College, Chennai under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held curatorial posts at the Government Museum Chennai, Indian Museum, Archaeological Survey of India, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

nodes.label: A. Aiyappan
nodes.summary: A. Aiyappan worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Madras (~1925–1927), served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1972).

nodes.label: Mortimer Wheeler
nodes.summary: Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at University College London. He directed the National Museum Wales and the London Museum, and served as Director-General of Archæology in India for the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948).

nodes.label: Hermann Beythan
nodes.summary: Hermann Beythan worked in the fields of linguistics and Indology. His education included studying under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

nodes.label: Kodo Kawamura
nodes.summary: Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1963 to 1999.

nodes.label: Sibani Dasgupta
nodes.summary: Sibani Dasgupta was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate degree at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

nodes.label: Ram Chandra Kak
nodes.summary: Indologist and archaeologist Ram Chandra Kak studied at Sri Pratap College and trained under John Marshall (1914–1919). He served as Director of the Department of Archaeology and Research for Jammu and Kashmir State (1919–1929) and as an ASI superintendent.

nodes.label: John Collinson Nesfield
nodes.summary: John Collinson Nesfield was an Indologist and linguist educated at Merton College. He taught at Highgate School before holding professorships at Presidency College and Krishnagar Government College, becoming principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1878.

nodes.label: Lodrö Sangpo
nodes.summary: Lodrö Sangpo, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Ernst Steinkellner and taught Geshe Yeshe Tobden. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Thupten Jinpa
nodes.image: HH the Dalai Lama enlightened translator, Dr. Thupten Jinpa.jpg
nodes.summary: Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned a Geshe Lharam at Ganden Monastery and a B.A. from Cambridge. He held posts at Girton College, Cambridge, Stanford University, and the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

nodes.label: Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: Tashi Tsering works in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans and under many teachers, including Tenzin Gyatso. He was Research Officer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979) and founded Amnye Machen Institute.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Napper
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Virginia under supervisor Paul Groner. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Rory Mackenzie
nodes.summary: Rory Mackenzie is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He held a teaching post at the International Christian College.

nodes.label: Timothy Lenz
nodes.summary: Timothy Lenz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed graduate studies at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox. He held posts at the University of Washington, where he was attested as professor in 2017.

nodes.label: Kurunegoda Piyatissa
nodes.summary: Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1928–2015) was a Buddhist studies figure who served as head of the New York Buddhist Vihara, where his affiliation is attested in 1998 and 2009.

nodes.label: Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra
nodes.summary: Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra is an Indology scholar who studied under Rambhadracharya. He headed the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, served as Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and was a visiting professor at the University of Indonesia.

nodes.label: Pascale Haag
nodes.summary: Pascale Haag specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and at Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay, holding a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences around 2005.

nodes.label: David L. Haberman
nodes.description: American indologist and historian of religion
nodes.summary: David L. Haberman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado from around 1970 to 1974. He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (circa 1993).

variants: Oriental Research Institute der University of Kerala

nodes.label: Norvin J. Hein
nodes.summary: Norvin J. Hein was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as an associate professor of comparative religion at Yale Divinity School.

nodes.label: John James Jones
nodes.summary: John James Jones worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Aberystwyth University (~1909–1915) and served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1929–1957).

nodes.label: Mark Allon
nodes.summary: Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Australian National University and earned his PhD at Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman (~1989–1994), later holding posts at SOAS (~1996–1998) and the University of Sydney (~2002).

nodes.label: St John's College
variants: St. John's College, University of Oxford
ケンブリッジ大学セント・ジョンズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Betty Heimann
nodes.summary: Betty Heimann worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Bonn, Strasbourg, Kiel, and Halle under Simmel, Sieg, and Hultzsch. She held posts at Kiel, Halle, Hamburg, London, Oxford, and Colombo.

nodes.label: Harold Walter Bailey
variants: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.jawiki: ハロルド・ウォルター・ベイリー
nodes.summary: Harold Walter Bailey (1899–1996) was an Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Western Australia and the University of Oxford under Frederick William Thomas, later holding posts at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (1936–1967).

nodes.label: Franz Bernhard
nodes.summary: Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and at Goethe University Frankfurt. From 1966 to 1971, he was a professor and seminar director at the University of Hamburg.

nodes.label: Ivo Fišer
nodes.summary: Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a lecturer at Charles University, attested in 1960, and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology, attested in 1970.

nodes.label: Ananda Guruge
nodes.summary: Ananda Guruge was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Ceylon (-1947) and the University of London. He was Professor of Educational Planning at NIEPA (attested 1970) and Dean Emeritus of Academic Affairs at University of the West (attested 2012).

nodes.id: I:National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration
nodes.label: National Institute of Educational Planning and Administration
Carmen Meinert
nodes.summary: Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008), Ruhr University Bochum, and Käte Hamburger Kolleg.

nodes.label: Christoph Anderl
nodes.summary: Christoph Anderl is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his MA at the University of Vienna (circa 1989–1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (circa 1997–2004) under Christoph Harbsmeier.

nodes.label: N. Venkataramanayya
nodes.summary: N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.

nodes.label: Evan Thompson
nodes.summary: Evan Thompson is a philosopher who studied at Amherst College under Robert A. F. Thurman and at the University of Toronto, also studying with Francisco Varela. His posts include York University (2002–2005), University of Toronto (2005), and UBC (2013).

nodes.label: Dan Zahavi
nodes.summary: Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his PhD at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and a habilitation at the University of Copenhagen. He became a professor at Copenhagen in 2002 and was a professor of philosophy at Oxford (2018–2021).

nodes.label: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad
nodes.summary: Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at Oxford, held research fellowships at Trinity College, Oxford and Clare Hall, Cambridge, taught at National University of Singapore, and was a professor at Lancaster University (attested 2007–2012).

nodes.summary: Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and cognitive neuroscience. He studied at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, University of Chile, and Harvard. His career included posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, École Polytechnique, and Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital.

nodes.label: Eleanor Rosch
nodes.summary: Eleanor Rosch is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned a bachelor's at Reed College and a Ph.D. at Harvard under Roger Brown. Her academic posts include Connecticut College, Brown University, and UC Berkeley from 1971.

nodes.label: Karen O'Brien-Kop
nodes.summary: Karen O'Brien-Kop is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she worked as a senior teaching fellow, before lecturing at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Daniela Bevilacqua
nodes.summary: Daniela Bevilacqua is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Paris Nanterre University
variants: University of Paris Ouest Nanterre La Defense
Laboratoire d'Ethnologie et de Sociologie Comparative, Université de Paris X, Nanterre
パリ大学ナンテール分校

nodes.label: Sravana Borkataky-Varma
nodes.summary: Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology, holding degrees from the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD). She has taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard (fellow ~2020–2022), and the University of Houston (~2022).

nodes.label: Mikel Burley
nodes.summary: Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex under Jay M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, and Brian Carr, and completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under John Peacock in 2005. He served at the University of Leeds (attested 2007–2020).

nodes.label: Philip Deslippe
nodes.summary: Philip Deslippe works in religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2020, he earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he also held a position as a teaching associate.

nodes.label: Carl W. Ernst
nodes.summary: Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Stanford (AB ~1973) and Harvard (PhD ~1981), taught at Pomona College (1981–1992), and served as professor at UNC Chapel Hill from 1992 to 2022.

nodes.label: Reichman University
variants: Muda Institute, Baruch Ivcher School of Psychology, IDC Herzliya

nodes.label: Gordon Hannington Luce
nodes.summary: Gordon Hannington Luce was a scholar of history/archaeology, Sinology, and linguistics. He was educated at Dean Close School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and served as Professor at the University of Rangoon from circa 1920 to 1964.

nodes.label: John Alexander Stewart
nodes.summary: John Alexander Stewart (1882–1948) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Aberdeen, served in the Indian Civil Service (ca. 1905–1933), and later was Reader in Burmese at SOAS, University of London.

nodes.label: Nani Gopal Majumdar
nodes.summary: A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, Nani Gopal Majumdar studied at the University of Calcutta (~1916–1920). He served as Superintendent at the Indian Museum (~1929–1938) and the Archaeological Survey of India (1931).

nodes.label: Daya Ram Sahni
nodes.summary: Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Oriental College, he trained under John Marshall. He served as curator at Lucknow Museum, worked in Jammu and Kashmir, held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, and directed archaeology in Jaipur State.

nodes.label: Sydney Frank Markham
nodes.summary: Sydney Frank Markham was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Wadham College from circa 1920 to 1923. He later served as Secretary and subsequently President of the Museums Association between 1929 and 1942.

nodes.label: Ghulam Yazdani
nodes.summary: Ghulam Yazdani (1885–1962), a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, graduated from Aligarh Muslim University (B.A. 1905) under Mohammad Ishaq and Nazir Ahmad. He held professorships at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Lahore before directing Hyderabad's Archaeological Department (~1914–1943).

nodes.label: Hirananda Sastri
nodes.summary: Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at DAV College, Oriental College, and Panjab University, he held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, and Baroda State's Department of Archaeology (1934–1942).

nodes.label: Ramaprasad Chanda
nodes.summary: Ramaprasad Chanda, who worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Scottish Church College and Dhaka College. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1917–1919) and was Superintendent of Archaeology at the Indian Museum (1921–1932).

nodes.label: Jeffrey S. Lidke
nodes.summary: Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Berry College and was attested as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia in 2003.

nodes.id: I:Lambakarna Bhatta Institute of Tantric Studies
nodes.label: Lambakarna Bhatta Institute of Tantric Studies
variants: Lambakarna Bhatta Institute of Tantric Studies

nodes.label: Georgios T. Halkias
nodes.summary: Georgios T. Halkias specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Oxford under Charles Ramble, held research posts at SOAS, Warburg, and Bochum, and became associate professor at The University of Hong Kong around 2012.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Kotyk
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at Komazawa University and a PhD from Leiden University under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University and the University of Bologna.

variants: 新加坡国立大学中文系
