nodes.label: Judith Simmer-Brown
nodes.summary: A specialist in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Simmer-Brown completed a PhD at Walden University (~1978). In 1977, she joined Naropa University, where she became Distinguished Professor Emerita.

nodes.label: Sthaneshwar Timalsina
nodes.summary: Sthaneshwar Timalsina is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University (~1993–2001), San Diego State University (~2005–2022), and Stony Brook University (~2022).

nodes.label: John Chadwick
variants: ジョン・チャドウィック
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・チャドウィック
nodes.summary: John Chadwick was a linguist and classicist who studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at the University of Oxford (~1946–1952) before serving as a lecturer and Reader in Classics at the University of Cambridge from 1952 to 1984.

nodes.label: Bridget Allchin
nodes.description: English archaeologist, specializing in South Asian archaeology
nodes.summary: Bridget Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Cape Town and earned a PhD from University College London under Frederick Zeuner. She was a fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge, and served as secretary and chairman of the Ancient India & Iran Trust.

nodes.id: I:European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art
nodes.label: European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art
variants: European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art History
European Association of South Asian Archaeologists

nodes.label: D. C. Sarasvati
nodes.summary: D. C. Sarasvati was an Indology scholar who studied under V. Raghavan. Sarasvati held an appointment at the University of Madras as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant from 1964 to 1965.

nodes.label: Seema Alavi
nodes.summary: Seema Alavi (born 1961) is an Indology and history scholar. She earned her doctorate from the University of Cambridge, taught at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and held history professorships at Jamia Millia Islamia and Ashoka University (~2020).

nodes.label: Emmie te Nijenhuis
nodes.summary: Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda. She was associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht (1964–1988) and taught at Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Alex McKay
nodes.summary: Alex McKay is a historian and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

nodes.label: Shek-wing Tam
nodes.description: Hong Kong Buddhist scholar, writer, and fortune-teller
nodes.summary: Shek-wing Tam was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Yingguang Qu, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Yui Chi Lau. He taught at Renmin University of China (~2008) and served on an advisory board at Tsinghua University.

nodes.label: Weirong Shen
nodes.summary: Weirong Shen (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held teaching posts at The University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (~2006).

nodes.label: Henry Shiu
nodes.summary: Henry Shiu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Toronto in 2006. He studied under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

nodes.label: Kapila Vatsyayan
nodes.summary: Kapila Vatsyayan was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, and held leadership roles at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (1987-2005) and India International Centre (~2005-2012).

nodes.label: David J. Kalupahana
nodes.description: Sri Lankan Buddhist scholar and philosopher (1936–2014)
nodes.summary: David J. Kalupahana (1936–2014) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. He taught at Ceylon before chairing the philosophy department at the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: N. A. Jayawickrama
nodes.summary: N. A. Jayawickrama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1978) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1978–1985).

nodes.label: Clare Carlisle
nodes.summary: Clare Carlisle (born 1977) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002) and held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and King's College London (~2011).

nodes.label: Washington and Lee University
variants: Department of Religion at Washington and Lee University

nodes.label: Edward Vernon Arnold
nodes.summary: Edward Vernon Arnold (1857–1926) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1880–1884), and served as a professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

nodes.label: Bangor University
variants: University College of North Wales in Bangor

nodes.label: Carl Darling Buck
nodes.summary: Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was an American linguist. He studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and Leipzig University (~1889–1892), and served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

nodes.label: George Foot Moore
nodes.summary: George Foot Moore was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He served as a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and as Frothingham Professor of the History of Religion at Harvard (1904–1928).

nodes.label: Pulinbihari Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Pulinbihari Chakravarti was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at The Asiatic Society, attested in 1951.

nodes.label: Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi
nodes.summary: Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi was an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including head of the Research Department as attested in 1989.

nodes.label: Donald Capps
nodes.description: American professor and author of pastoral theology (1939–2015)
nodes.summary: Donald Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1970). He held faculty posts at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).

nodes.label: Helen Hardacre
nodes.summary: Helen Hardacre specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Vanderbilt and the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith, she held posts at Princeton, Griffith University, Harvard University, and the Reischauer Institute.

nodes.label: Jim Taylor
nodes.summary: Jim Taylor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University in 1989 and served as a Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Syed Nawab Ali
nodes.description: Persian-English translator who worked as a professor in Baroda
nodes.summary: Syed Nawab Ali worked in history and archaeology. He held posts as Principal at Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, both attested in 1932.

nodes.label: Catherine Elaine Prueitt
nodes.summary: Catherine Elaine Prueitt is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Rochester and earned her PhD from Emory University in 2016 under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton.

nodes.label: Ester Bianchi
nodes.summary: Ester Bianchi specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctorates at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert. She held posts at the University of Florence and the University of Perugia.

nodes.label: Karl Debreczeny
nodes.summary: Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Wu Hung and Jennifer Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Fabienne Jagou
nodes.summary: Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1993–1999) and became maître de conférences at École Française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

nodes.label: Rob Linrothe
nodes.summary: Rob Linrothe specializes in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from the University of Chicago in 1992, he held posts at the National Palace Museum, Skidmore College (1992–2009), the Rubin Museum of Art, and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

nodes.label: Paul Nietupski
nodes.summary: Active in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Paul Nietupski earned his PhD from Columbia University and held an appointment at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Abraham Zablocki
nodes.summary: Abraham Zablocki works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).

variants: Tibetan and Himalayan Religions Group of the American Academy of Religion

nodes.label: Bal Krishen Thapar
nodes.summary: Bal Krishen Thapar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University of the Punjab, Heidelberg University, and under Mortimer Wheeler. He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and later chaired CCRT.

nodes.label: Richard King
nodes.summary: Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster University (PhD 1992). He held posts at the University of Stirling, Vanderbilt University, and the University of Glasgow.

nodes.label: Klaus Karttunen
nodes.description: Finnish ethnologist, indologist and university teacher
nodes.summary: Klaus Karttunen (born 1951) earned his degrees through PhD at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. In Indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at the University of Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.

nodes.label: Katsutoshi Ono
nodes.summary: Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist. He earned a doctorate from Kyoto University, worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture (~1931–1945) and Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and became a professor at Ryukoku University (~1965–1980).

nodes.label: Kiel University
variants: Historisches Seminar, Asiatische Geschichte, Universität Kiel

nodes.label: Rita Langer
nodes.summary: Rita Langer, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004) under Lambert Schmithausen and other mentors. She was affiliated with the University of Bristol in 2009.

nodes.label: Alexander Piatigorsky
variants: アレクサンデル・モイシェイェヴィチ・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.jawiki: アレクサンデル・ピアティゴルスキー
nodes.summary: Alexander Piatigorsky was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Moscow State University and under George de Roerich and Bidia Dandaron, later holding posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow State University, and SOAS.

nodes.label: Robert Alan Goodding
nodes.summary: Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD in 2002 from the University of Texas at Austin, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Patrick Olivelle.

St. Xavier's College, Mumbai

nodes.label: Frederick M. Smith
nodes.summary: Frederick M. Smith is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He was a student of Ludo Rocher and held a position as a professor at the University of Iowa, attested between 2006 and 2008.

nodes.label: Philip Lutgendorf
nodes.summary: Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his B.A. from the University of Chicago (~1970-1987). He joined the University of Iowa in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010-2018).

nodes.label: Albert Grünwedel
variants: アルベルト・グリュンヴェーデル
nodes.jawiki: アルベルト・グリュンヴェーデル
nodes.summary: Albert Grünwedel was a specialist in Tibetan studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Munich. He held an honorary professorship at Berlin and worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1881 to 1921.

nodes.label: Ethnological Museum of Berlin
variants: ベルリン民族学博物館

nodes.label: Ajahn Sumedho
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies teacher who earned a master's degree from the University of California, Berkeley and trained under Ajahn Chah. He served as abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).

nodes.label: Ajahn Chah
nodes.native: ชา สุภทฺโท

nodes.label: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi
nodes.summary: Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at Harvard under George David Birkhoff, he held mathematics professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962), among other posts.

nodes.id: I:Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences

variants: Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences
Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences at Stanford University

nodes.label: Hans Henrich Hock
nodes.summary: Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed graduate studies at Northwestern and Yale, studying under Warren Cowgill. He served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967, ~1982–2013).

nodes.label: Rama Nath Sharma
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Rama Nath Sharma studied at Banaras Hindu University, University of Allahabad, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and the University of Rochester. He taught at the University of Rochester (1971–1976) and was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1976–2012).

nodes.label: Satya Vrat Shastri
nodes.image: Ramashish Acharya with Padma Bhushan Satya Vrat Shastri.jpg
nodes.description: Jnanpith Award recipient in Sanskrit. Indian academic
nodes.summary: Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Charu Deva Shastri, Shukdev Jha, and Siddheshwar Varma, attending University of the Punjab, Banaras Hindu University, and Punjabi University. He served at Delhi University (1970–1995).

nodes.label: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam
nodes.summary: M. D. Balasubrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested in 1967), where he also completed his dissertation in 1969.

nodes.label: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld
nodes.summary: Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. In 1978, he became an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen.

nodes.id: I:Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine
nodes.label: Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine

Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine

nodes.label: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
nodes.summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinvijaya, he taught at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan and Gujarat University, and directed the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (~1973–2001).

nodes.label: Fabrizia Baldissera
nodes.summary: Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Federigo Enriques Department of Mathematics (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1992–2001) and the University of Florence (~2001).

nodes.label: Yun Ji
nodes.summary: Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University by 2006 and served as a librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Shanshan Jia
nodes.summary: Shanshan Jia is an Indology scholar who pursued doctoral studies in Indology at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Eun-su Cho
nodes.summary: Eun-su Cho specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini, and held posts at the University of Michigan (until 2004) and Seoul National University (2004).

nodes.label: Georges-Jean Pinault
nodes.summary: Linguist and Indologist Georges-Jean Pinault studied at ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE, learning under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Blaise Pascal University before becoming a professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 1999.

nodes.label: Jason Protass
nodes.summary: Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick. His career includes appointments as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica and visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Nathan Sivin
nodes.summary: Nathan Sivin (1931–2022) was a Sinologist and historian of science. Educated at MIT and Harvard (PhD 1966), he was a professor at MIT (1966–1977) and later Professor of Chinese Culture and History of Science at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006).

nodes.label: Joseph Needham
nodes.summary: Joseph Needham was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oundle School and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge. He held long-term posts at the University of Cambridge, Gonville and Caius College, and directed the Needham Research Institute (1976–1990).

nodes.label: J. B. Disanayaka
nodes.summary: J. B. Disanayaka (born 1937) is an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Colombo from ~1967 to 2002 and at SOAS University of London from ~1996 to 1997.

nodes.label: Sean D. Gaffney
nodes.summary: Sean D. Gaffney works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at SOAS University of London, where he completed his PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski (attested 2003) and also studied under Philip T. Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

nodes.label: Bulcsu Siklós
nodes.summary: Bulcsu Siklós is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his PhD from the University of London under supervisor Tadeusz Skorupski and teacher Charles R. Bawden. He was affiliated with SOAS University of London in 1996.

nodes.label: Yang-Gyu An
nodes.summary: Yang-Gyu An specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich, and also studied under Ven. Hojin (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Chikafumi Watanabe
nodes.summary: Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Ashok Aklujkar, Karin Preisendanz, and others.

nodes.label: Shrikant S. Bahulkar
nodes.summary: A scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies, Shrikant S. Bahulkar studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held a post at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000).

nodes.label: Catherine Ludvik
nodes.summary: Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who received her PhD from the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse. She has held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.

nodes.label: Akio Donohashi
nodes.summary: Akio Donohashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1977) and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

nodes.id: I:Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
nodes.label: Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities
variants: Forschungsstelle »Felsbilder und Inschriften am Karakorum Highway« der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften
Forschungsstelle „Felsbilder und Inschriften am Karakorum Highway“ an der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften
Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, University of Heidelberg

nodes.label: Hitoshi Obara
nodes.summary: Hitoshi Obara (1944–) works in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1963–1967) and served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart from approximately 1989 to 2015.

nodes.label: University of Cologne
variants: Indological Institute at the University of Cologne
Centre for Advanced Study of Humanities, University of Cologne

nodes.label: Robert E. Morrell
nodes.summary: Robert E. Morrell specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough, and held a post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

nodes.label: Washington University in St. Louis
variants: Washington University in St. Louis Missouri

nodes.label: James W. Heisig
nodes.jawiki: ジェームズ・ハイジック
nodes.summary: James W. Heisig is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge and served as a Permanent Research Fellow at Nanzan University across multiple periods between 1976 and 2001.

nodes.label: Barbra R. Clayton
nodes.summary: Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and she held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Katherine K. Young
nodes.summary: Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She completed an M.A. at the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. at McGill University (~1970–1978), where she also served as Professor (~1978).

nodes.label: Damien Keown
nodes.summary: Damien Keown specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from Lancaster University and a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford, later becoming Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London around 1989.

nodes.label: David P. Chandler
nodes.image: Professor David Chandler gives expert testimony on 18 July 2012 (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: David P. Chandler is a historian who studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, Yale, and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Cornell, Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

nodes.label: Sarah J. Horton
nodes.summary: Sarah J. Horton is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College, attested in 2006.

nodes.label: Gopinath Kaviraj
nodes.summary: Gopinath Kaviraj was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Maharaja's College, Jaipur, and the University of Allahabad under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani, he served as librarian, Principal, and department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Dorji Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg (~1998–2005) under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

nodes.label: Klaus-Dieter Mathes
nodes.summary: Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA under Klaus Sagaster, a PhD at Marburg under Michael Hahn, and a habilitation at Hamburg, later serving as director of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and professor at Vienna.

nodes.label: Melvyn C. Goldstein
nodes.summary: Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington (PhD ~1961–1968), and served as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

nodes.id: I:Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School
nodes.label: Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School
Jay M. Bernstein
nodes.summary: Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (1971–1975). He held academic posts at the University of Essex (circa 1975–1996), Vanderbilt University (circa 1996–2001), and The New School (circa 2001).

nodes.label: The New School
variants: The New School for Social Research, New York
The New School for Social Research

nodes.label: Osmund Bopearachchi
nodes.summary: Osmund Bopearachchi specializes in archaeology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya, the CNRS, and the Sorbonne under Paul Bernard and Jean-Marie Dentzer. He was an emeritus director at the CNRS (1989) and adjunct professor at UC Berkeley (~2014).

nodes.label: Deborah Carlson
nodes.summary: Deborah Carlson is a scholar in history and archaeology who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).

nodes.label: Paul Bernard
nodes.summary: Paul Bernard was an archaeologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne, he directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1965–1980) and held chairs at the CNRS and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Doris Meth Srinivasan
nodes.summary: Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. After earning a BA at Hunter College and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania, she held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington, George Mason, and the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Axel Michaels
nodes.summary: Axel Michaels works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg, under Laxmi Nath Shrestha, and at Kiel University. He served at the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel, University of Bern, and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Hans Hartog
nodes.summary: Hans Hartog was an Indology scholar who studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, Munich, and Marburg, where he completed his PhD under Friedrich Heiler. He was also taught by Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, and others.

nodes.label: Friedrich Heiler
nodes.summary: Friedrich Heiler worked in religious studies, completing his doctorate at the University of Munich (~1912–1917). He lectured at Munich (1918), became a religious studies scholar at Marburg (1920), and directed the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

nodes.label: Walther Wüst
nodes.description: Rector of the University of Munich and SS member (1901-1993)
nodes.summary: Walther Wüst was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1920–1923). He served as dean at Munich (1935–1945), department head at the Ahnenerbe (1936), and president of the Deutsche Akademie (1943).

nodes.label: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer
nodes.image: Bundesarchiv Bild 183-2004-0413-501, Prof. Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.jpg
nodes.summary: Jakob Wilhelm Hauer, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at the Basel Mission Seminary, University of Oxford, and University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held professorial posts at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

nodes.label: Kurt Huber
nodes.description: German folk song researcher, professor at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU) in Munich, member of the White Rose (1893-1943)
nodes.summary: Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Munich (~1913–1920). He spent his academic career at the University of Munich, where he became an associate professor in 1926 and professor in 1938.

nodes.label: Erich Rudolf Jaensch
nodes.summary: A scholar of philosophy, Jaensch completed his PhD at Göttingen and Habilitation at Strasbourg. He served as professor of philosophy at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and ordinary professor at the University of Marburg (1913).

nodes.label: Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen
nodes.summary: Philosopher Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen studied and completed his Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1934), the University of Munich (1936–1941), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

nodes.label: Wolfgang Schultz
nodes.description: German philosopher, historian and art historian (1881-1936)
nodes.summary: Philosopher Wolfgang Schultz earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (1899–1904). He served as an administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and was Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

nodes.label: Ferdinand Sommer
nodes.summary: Ferdinand Sommer was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He held professorships at the universities of Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

nodes.label: Giovanni Vacca
nodes.summary: Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence. He taught at the University of Florence (1910) and held appointments at Sapienza University of Rome from 1911 to 1948.

nodes.id: I:Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center
nodes.label: Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center
S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar
nodes.summary: S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at the University of Madras, he lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History.

nodes.label: John Kieschnick
nodes.summary: John Kieschnick is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history. He held an academic post at the University of Bristol (~2005–2011) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University in ~2011.

nodes.label: Hellmuth Hecker
nodes.summary: Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1946–1948) and under Paul Debes. From approximately 1953 to 1988, he served as a referent at the Forschungsstelle für Völkerrecht und Ausländisches Öffentliches Recht.

nodes.label: Rudrapatna Shamasastry
nodes.summary: Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist educated at the University of Madras, Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, Oriental University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College (1912–1918) and Curator of Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

nodes.label: F. B. J. Kuiper
nodes.summary: F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Utrecht and Leiden under Willem Caland, C. C. Uhlenbeck, and Nicolaas van Wijk, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1939–1972).

nodes.label: Daniel Dubuisson
nodes.summary: Daniel Dubuisson works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the CNRS around 1980 and at the University of Lille (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Jonathan Z. Smith
variants: ジョナサン・Z・スミス
nodes.summary: Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College, Yale University, and Yale Divinity School. He held positions at Dartmouth College, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago, where he served as Dean of the College (1977–1982).

nodes.label: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya
nodes.summary: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held a position at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

nodes.label: Meinrad Scheller
nodes.summary: Meinrad Scheller was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Paris and the University of Zurich under Manu Leumann, Ernst Risch, and Julius Pokorny. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).

nodes.label: Gregory Max Seton
nodes.summary: Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford, supervised by Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

nodes.label: Martin Joachim Kümmel
nodes.summary: Martin Joachim Kümmel is a linguist and Indologist who completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Freiburg, studying under Eva Tichy and Helmut Rix. He served at the University of Freiburg (1999–2008) and became chairholder at Jena in 2013.

nodes.label: Helmut Rix
nodes.summary: Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen (Habilitation ~1959). He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau, the University of Regensburg, and the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

nodes.label: Jinzhang Peng
nodes.summary: Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He served as deputy director in the Department of History at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and as a Researcher (Professor) at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).

nodes.label: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng
nodes.summary: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. at McMaster University under James A. Benn and became an Assistant Professor at Fo Guang University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Fo Guang University
variants: 佛光人文社會學院宗教學系

nodes.label: Peter Moran
nodes.summary: Peter Moran works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and earned a PhD from the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, also training under traditional Tibetan teachers including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Thomas Watters
nodes.description: British diplomat in China and Korea, sinologist
nodes.summary: Watters, a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earned a B.A. studying at Queen's University Belfast and Queen's University of Ireland from 1857 to 1861.

nodes.label: Willem van der Molen
nodes.summary: Willem van der Molen (b. 1952) is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1983) and the University of Indonesia.

nodes.label: Muhammad Ashraf Khan
nodes.summary: Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He has served as Deputy Director of Taxila Museum, Director of the Department of Archaeology and Museums in Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University.

nodes.label: Zarawar Khan
nodes.summary: Zarawar Khan specializes in archaeology and Buddhist studies, having earned an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar. He served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019-2022).

nodes.label: Satoshi Naiki
nodes.summary: Satoshi Naiki specializes in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Naiki earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he served as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

nodes.label: Jessie Pons
nodes.summary: Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011 and was attested as a Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.

nodes.label: Max Walleser
nodes.summary: Max Walleser, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nürnberg. He founded the Institut für Mahāyāna-Buddhismus and taught at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936).

nodes.label: Institut für Mahāyāna-Buddhismus
variants: society for the study of Mahāyāna

nodes.label: Michael Comans
nodes.summary: Michael Comans is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, and was a faculty member at the University of Sydney (~1988–2002).

nodes.label: Swami Dayananda Saraswati
nodes.description: Hindu monk and founder of Arsha Vidya Gurukulam (1930-2015)
nodes.summary: Swami Dayananda Saraswati was an Indologist and philosopher of religion. He studied at Bangalore Sanskrit College and under teachers including Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Swami Pranavananda, and Swami Tarananda Giri.

nodes.label: Rahul Peter Das
nodes.description: German professor of South Asian studies (born 1954)
nodes.summary: Rahul Peter Das is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, earning his D. Phil and Habilitation from Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg, Bonn, Groningen, and Marburg before becoming Professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

nodes.label: Nagin J. Shah
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Nagin J. Shah succeeded Dalsukh D. Malvania and served as Acting Director at the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

nodes.label: Ernest John Henry Mackay
nodes.summary: Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities for the Government of Mandatory Palestine from 1919 to 1922.

nodes.label: Rakhal Das Banerji
nodes.summary: Rakhal Das Banerji worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, later serving as an Archaeological Survey of India officer (1911–1926) and professor at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).

nodes.label: Stephen Wootton Bushell
nodes.summary: Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) worked in sinology and archaeology. He studied at the University of London, earning an MD (~1866–1868), and held posts as house surgeon at Guy's Hospital (1866) and resident medical officer at Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

nodes.label: Alexander Rogers
nodes.summary: Alexander Rogers worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the East India Company College from circa 1843 to 1845 and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1845 to 1879.

nodes.label: Henry Beveridge
nodes.description: British linguist and Indian Civil Service officer
nodes.summary: Henry Beveridge, an Indologist and historian, was educated at the University of Glasgow and Queen's University Belfast. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1857 to 1893 and was president of The Asiatic Society from 1890 to 1891.

nodes.label: Edgar H. Sturtevant
variants: エドガー・H・スターティヴァント
エドガー・ハワード・スターティヴァント
nodes.jawiki: エドガー・ハワード・スターティヴァント
nodes.summary: Edgar H. Sturtevant (1875–1952) was a linguist who completed his education at Illinois College and Indiana University. He held major academic appointments at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).

nodes.label: University of Western Australia
variants: 西オーストラリア大学

nodes.label: Peterhouse
variants: Peterhouse College of the University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Klaus Ludwig Janert
nodes.description: born:1922|died:1994|; Janert, Klaus Ludwig, 1922-1994; Janert, Klaus L.
nodes.summary: Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and Goethe University Frankfurt, earning his doctorate under Paul Thieme. He served as an assistant at the University of Göttingen before holding a full professorship at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

nodes.label: Christophe Vielle
nodes.summary: Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who has served as a professor of Sanskrit at UCLouvain, where his posts are attested in 2009 and 2013.

nodes.label: Robert Deliège
nodes.summary: Robert Deliège (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1980–1983) and held posts at the University of Kerala and UCLouvain, where he became a professor around 1989.

nodes.label: Jacques Scheuer
nodes.summary: Jacques Scheuer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UCLouvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, working under Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts at Centre Sèvres and served as professor at UCLouvain (~1979–2007).

nodes.label: Utz Podzeit
nodes.image: Venia Legendi 1997- Dr. Utz Podzeit mit Mechthild.jpg
nodes.summary: Utz Podzeit (1942–2022) was an Austrian Indologist who completed his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna. He served as a university lecturer at Vienna's Indology institute from 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

nodes.label: Roderick M. Chisholm
nodes.summary: Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown University and Harvard University (PhD, ~1938–1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation, Brown University (~1947–1999), and the University of Graz, and served as president of the Metaphysical Society of America.

nodes.label: Philip L. Quinn
nodes.summary: Philip L. Quinn was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. Educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh, he served on the faculty at Brown University (~1976-1985) and held the John A. O'Brien Professorship at Notre Dame from 1985.

nodes.label: Ernest Sosa
nodes.summary: Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He served as a professor at Brown University starting in 1964 and at Rutgers University from 1998 to 2006.

nodes.label: Augustus William Heyde
nodes.description: German missionary to Tibetans in Northern India; b. Wilhelm Heide, Feb. 16, 1825; later changed surname to Heyde; d. Aug. 27, 1907

nodes.label: Eduard Röer
nodes.summary: Eduard Röer worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Königsberg, Jena, and under Herbart and Bopp. He held a postdoctorate at Berlin (1833) and worked for the East India Company, the Asiatic Society, and Bibliotheca Indica.

nodes.label: Karunesh Shukla
nodes.summary: Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation (attested 1991). He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Eduard Müller
nodes.summary: Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed an inaugural dissertation at Leipzig University (~1871-1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern from circa 1886 to 1908.

nodes.label: Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff
nodes.jawiki: ウルリヒ・フォン・ヴィラモーヴィッツ＝メレンドルフ
nodes.summary: Linguist and historian Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff studied at Bonn and Berlin under Johannes Schmidt, Otto Jahn, and Moriz Haupt. He held professorships at the universities of Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin.

nodes.label: David Ludden
nodes.summary: Historian and Indologist David Ludden studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at the University of Virginia (1979–1980), University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and New York University (from 2007).

nodes.label: Yigal Bronner
nodes.summary: Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1994–1999). He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2007).

nodes.label: James B. Apple
nodes.summary: James B. Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne, alongside numerous other teachers.

nodes.label: Henepola Gunaratana
nodes.summary: Henepola Gunaratana is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied in Sri Lanka and earned a PhD at American University. He served at the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur, Washington Buddhist Vihara, American University, and Georgetown University.

nodes.label: Glenn H. Mullin
nodes.image: Visit of Telo Tulku to Roerich House, U.B. (3861963599).jpg
nodes.summary: Glenn H. Mullin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, and Geshe Rabten, and founded The Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.

nodes.label: Chogye Trichen
nodes.summary: Chogye Trichen (1920–2007) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Gyatso. He served as the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery from circa 1932 to 2007.

nodes.label: Luciano Petech
nodes.summary: Luciano Petech worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Sinology, having studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He taught at the University of Allahabad, held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984), and served as IATS president (c. 1979–1989).

nodes.label: Sojun Mel Weitsman
variants: ソウジュン・メル・ウェイツマン

nodes.label: Reb Anderson
nodes.summary: Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He succeeded Baker and served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from circa 1986 to 1995.

nodes.label: Elena De Rossi Filibeck
nodes.summary: Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian History at Sapienza University of Rome under Luciano Petech (~1966–1971). She held posts at the University of Bonn and Sapienza University of Rome as Associate Professor from 1980.

nodes.label: Stefan Mario Maul
nodes.summary: Stefan Mario Maul is a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Göttingen and Free University of Berlin. Since 1995 he has been Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University, also leading research at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Søren Sørensen
nodes.summary: Søren Sørensen was an Indologist who held a post at the Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and later served at the University of Copenhagen from around 1887 to 1902.

nodes.label: Vilhelm Thomsen
variants: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
ヴィルヘルム・ルズヴィ・ペーター・トムセン
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・トムセン
nodes.summary: Vilhelm Thomsen was a Danish scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned his PhD from the University of Copenhagen (1859–1869). He held several posts there, including Professor (1887–1913), and served as President of the Royal Danish Academy in 1909.

nodes.label: Karl Verner
variants: カール・アドルフ・ヴェルナー
nodes.summary: Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen under August Leskien, and held posts as librarian at the University of Halle (~1876–1883) and lecturer in Slavic studies at Copenhagen (1882).

nodes.label: Rosina Pastore
nodes.summary: Rosina Pastore is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisors Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She also served as an assistant and PhD candidate at Lausanne.

nodes.label: Marianne Winder
nodes.summary: Marianne Winder studied at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove. A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she served at the Wellcome Institute as Assistant Librarian (~1963–1978), Curator (1970), and Consultant (1978).

nodes.label: Nigel Allan
nodes.summary: Nigel Allan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine, succeeding Marianne Winder (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Charles Edmund Godakumbura
nodes.summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist and historian who earned multiple degrees at the University of London. He taught at University College, Colombo and SOAS, and served as Commissioner of Archaeology for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956-1967).

nodes.label: Rudolf Geiger
nodes.summary: Rudolf Geiger studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from 1912 to 1914. He later held an academic post at the University of Munich from around 1937 to 1962.

nodes.label: Union Theological Seminary
variants: Union Theological Seminary in New York City
Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York
Union Theological Seminary in New York
Union Theological Seminary, New York City

nodes.id: I:Hartford International University for Religion and Peace
nodes.label: Hartford International University for Religion and Peace
variants: Kennedy School of Missions in Hartford
Kennedy School of Missions of Hartford Seminary Foundation

nodes.label: Anne MacDonald
nodes.summary: Anne MacDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida. She held posts at the University of Vienna (attested 2008) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Bhagwan Dash
nodes.summary: Bhagwan Dash worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (PhD, ~1973–1978), and worked as a cataloguer for the Library of Congress.

nodes.label: Vaibhav Singh
nodes.summary: Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017. He held a post at the University of Reading, attested in 2018.

nodes.label: Fiona Ross
nodes.description: British type designer, academic and linguist
nodes.summary: Fiona Ross (born 1954) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1978–1988) and held posts at Tiro Typeworks and the University of Reading (~2003).

nodes.label: Himanshu Prabha Ray
nodes.summary: Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) works in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Panjab University, JNU, and Cambridge, she was associate professor at JNU (~1986–2012) and served as Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

nodes.label: Kuvempu University
variants: Centre for the Study of Local Cultures, Kuvempu University

nodes.label: Geoff Childs
nodes.summary: Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who completed his PhD at Indiana University, where he studied under Tsetan Chonjore. He held positions at the Australian National University and Washington University in St. Louis.

nodes.label: Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute
variants: 財団法人西蔵大蔵経研究会

nodes.label: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé
nodes.summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928, later serving there as a lecturer in Chinese (1946) and professor (1956–1975).

nodes.label: David N. Keightley
nodes.summary: David N. Keightley was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, where his posts are attested in 1985 and 1999.

nodes.label: Robert H. Brower
nodes.description: Professor of far east language and literature (1923–1988)
nodes.summary: Robert H. Brower (1923–1988) was a Japanologist who earned degrees at Harvard (~1941–1944) and Michigan (~1945–1947). He taught at Minnesota (1951–1954) and Stanford (1954–1966), before chairing Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

nodes.label: Arthur F. Wright
nodes.summary: Arthur F. Wright (1913–1976) was a scholar of Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard (under John King Fairbank), and held professorships at Stanford (1958) and Yale (1959, 1961).

nodes.label: University of Missouri
variants: University of the State of Missouri

nodes.label: Steven Lukes
nodes.jawiki: スティーヴン・ルークス
nodes.summary: Steven Lukes is a philosopher and sociologist who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Balliol College (1966–1987), European University Institute, University of Florence, University of Siena, LSE, and New York University (~2001–2021).

nodes.summary: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana is an Indologist who studied at Bharathiar University and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts at the Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama.

Robert E. Svoboda
nodes.summary: Robert E. Svoboda (born 1953) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under Vimalananda (~1975–1983), later holding adjunct posts at Bastyr University and The Ayurvedic Institute (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Soonil Hwang
nodes.summary: Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo, completed a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and holds a post at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Fawad Khan
nodes.summary: Fawad Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an archaeology Master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, later serving as Assistant Curator at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums.

nodes.label: Kirby Flower Smith
nodes.description: American classical philologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Kirby Flower Smith (1862–1918) studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve, Minton Warren, and Maurice Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and Director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).

nodes.label: Bhikkhu Anālayo
nodes.description: German Buddhist monk, scholar, and meditation teacher (born 1962)
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peradeniya and Marburg. He held posts at the University of Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Wataru S. Ryose
nodes.summary: Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

nodes.label: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye
variants: Kong sprul Blo gros mtha’ yas
ジャムグン・コントゥル・ロドゥ・タイェ
nodes.jawiki: ジャムグン・コントゥル・ロドゥ・タイェ
nodes.summary: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Thegchog Dorje, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa, both of whom he also taught.

nodes.label: Sukumar Sen
nodes.image: Sukumar Sen linguist 2020 cover of India cr.jpg
nodes.summary: Sukumar Sen (1900–1992) was an Indian linguist and Indologist. Educated at Burdwan Raj College, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta University under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Taraporewala, he became lecturer (1930) and Khaira Professor (1954) at Calcutta University.

nodes.label: David Kopf
nodes.summary: David Kopf (1930–2023) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1959 to 1964. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1999.

nodes.label: Willard Van Orman Quine
variants: ウィラード・クワイン
ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン

nodes.jawiki: ウィラード・ヴァン・オーマン・クワイン
nodes.summary: Willard Van Orman Quine (1908–2000) was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at Oberlin College and Harvard University, he served as an assistant professor at Harvard (1940–1978) and held visiting posts at Wesleyan and Oxford.

nodes.label: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri
nodes.summary: P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bishop Heber College, the Institute of Advanced Study in Education, Saidapet, and the University of Madras, holding posts at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University.

nodes.label: Charles Cutler Torrey
nodes.summary: Charles Cutler Torrey worked in religious studies and history/archaeology, studying under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892-1900), served as professor at Yale University (1900-1932), and founded the American Schools of Oriental Research.

nodes.label: Alexander W. Macdonald
nodes.summary: Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme from circa 1956 to 1975 and served as a professor at Paris Nanterre University from circa 1975 to 1991.

nodes.label: Rasmus Rask
variants: ラスムス・クリスチャン・ラスク
nodes.summary: Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a Danish linguist, Indologist, and Central Asian scholar educated at Odense Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen, where he later held posts as librarian and professor of literary history and Eastern languages.

nodes.label: Stella Kramrisch
nodes.summary: Stella Kramrisch (1896–1993) was an art historian and Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna. She taught at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati University, and served as Professor of South Asian Art at the University of Pennsylvania.

nodes.label: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati
nodes.summary: Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

nodes.label: H. G. Narahari
nodes.summary: H. G. Narahari specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing degrees at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1944, he held posts at the Adyar Library and the University of Madras.

nodes.label: Charles Philip Brown
nodes.summary: Charles Philip Brown was an Indologist and linguist educated at East India Company College. After serving in the Indian Civil Service from 1817 to 1854, he became Professor of Telugu at the University of London from circa 1865 to 1879.

nodes.label: Daniel Clarke Waugh
nodes.summary: Daniel Clarke Waugh works in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from Yale University and Harvard University before taking up a post at the University of Washington in 1972.

nodes.label: Katia Buffetrille
nodes.summary: Katia Buffetrille specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Paris Nanterre University (~1986–1996) under Alexander W. Macdonald, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1998) and CRCAO.

nodes.label: Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.image: Shunryu Suzuki at Zen Mountain Center (cropped).png
nodes.summary: Shunryu Suzuki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji. He served as abbot of Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Soko-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

nodes.label: Richard Baker
variants: ゼンテツ・リチャード・ベーカー
nodes.summary: Richard Baker is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and trained under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center, serving as abbot (1971–1984), and later founded Dharma Sangha.

nodes.label: Huston Smith
nodes.summary: Huston Smith (1919–2016) was a scholar of religion and philosophy who earned his BA at Central Methodist and PhD at the University of Chicago. He taught at Washington University, MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1983–1999).

nodes.label: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi
nodes.summary: Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and Nanjing University. He held posts at the University of Colombo (~2005) and as visiting lecturer at other institutions.

nodes.description: Indian judge, writer, and scholar in Sanskrit
nodes.summary: Srisa Chandra Vasu (1861–1918) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Rang Mahal School and Government College University, Lahore. He served as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1883) and founded the Panini Office in 1891.

nodes.label: Johanna Narten
nodes.description: Professor of Indo-European and Indo-Iranian Linguistics (1930-2019)
nodes.summary: Johanna Narten (1930–2019) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. She studied under Ernst Zinn at Saarland University and completed her PhD under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, where she later worked as an assistant (1973–1977).

nodes.label: Jadunath Sarkar
nodes.summary: A historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta, Jadunath Sarkar taught English at Ripon, Vidyasagar, and Ravenshaw colleges. He also served at Patna College (1899–1926) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

nodes.label: George V. Bobrinskoy
nodes.summary: George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Lutheran Theological Seminary at Philadelphia and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (1951–1967).

nodes.label: Ananda K. Coomaraswamy
nodes.summary: Ananda K. Coomaraswamy was an Indology, history, and philosophy scholar who studied at University College London and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon (~1903-1906) and served as curator and research fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1917, 1933).

nodes.label: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
variants: Museum of Fine Arts in Boston

nodes.label: Peter Masefield
nodes.summary: Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986), and taught Nicolas Revire.

nodes.label: Karel Werner
nodes.summary: Karel Werner was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University and under Robert Konečný, Jaroslav Průšek, and Vincenc Lesný at Palacký University. He taught at Palacký (~1949-1964), Durham (1969-1990), and Masaryk University (1993-1998).

nodes.label: Ninian Smart
nodes.summary: Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Glasgow, SOAS, Oxford, and Yale. His career included professorships at the University of Birmingham, Lancaster University (1967–1982), and UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

nodes.label: Denis Sinor
nodes.summary: Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Paul Pelliot (~1939–1945) and at Cambridge (~1948). He held posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University (Director 1962–1986; Series Editor ~1960–2000).

nodes.label: Griffith University
variants: グリフィス大学現代アジア研究所

nodes.label: Herbert Franke
nodes.summary: Herbert Franke was a sinologist and historian. He studied under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer and attended Bonn, Humboldt University, the Seminar for Oriental Languages, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, Cambridge, Washington, Munich, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: S. N. Balagangadhara
nodes.summary: S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and completed his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch (1991), where he served as director (~1991–2017).

nodes.label: Kazu Uehara
nodes.summary: Kazu Uehara was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1948–1992). He served as a full-time lecturer at the University of Miyazaki (~1957–1965) and later became professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1965–1995).

nodes.label: Yasuro Abe
nodes.summary: Yasuro Abe works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako University and Otani University. He held positions at Osaka University, Otemae University, Nagoya University, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Masahiro Asada
nodes.summary: Masahiro Asada is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University and served there as an assistant professor (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Qingzhi Zhu
nodes.summary: Qingzhi Zhu works in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Zhu served as a professor at Peking University (attested 2004) and at the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Jinchuan Wan
nodes.summary: Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts as professor (教授) at both National Central University and Fo Guang University, attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Christoph Harbsmeier
nodes.description: German professor of Chinese linguistics and syntax
nodes.summary: Christoph Harbsmeier is a sinologist and linguist who studied at Merton College, Oxford, and Copenhagen. He taught at Universiti Sains Malaysia (1973–1976) before becoming a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980 and an advisory professor at several Chinese universities.

nodes.label: Shu-Fen Chen
nodes.summary: A scholar in linguistics and Indology, Shu-Fen Chen studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien, completing doctoral research under Hans Henrich Hock. She served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Ryan Richard Overbey
nodes.summary: Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brown University (AB, 2001) and Harvard University (PhD, 2010), later holding posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013-2015), and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Todd T. Lewis
nodes.summary: Todd T. Lewis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under mentors Ainslie T. Embree, Morton Klass, Theodore Riccardi Jr., and Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He held posts at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 1996–2017).

nodes.label: Lothar Ledderose
nodes.summary: A scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies, Lothar Ledderose studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Tokyo, Harvard, and Cologne. He served as professor at Heidelberg University (1976–2010) and was president of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

nodes.label: Graduate Theological Union
variants: Graduate Theological Union in Berkeley, California

nodes.label: Wai-lun Tam
nodes.summary: Wai-lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. He became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

nodes.label: David Faure
nodes.summary: David Faure is a historian and sinologist who studied at The University of Hong Kong and Princeton University. He taught at Indiana University, St Antony's College (1990–2006), and became a director at The Chinese University of Hong Kong around 2006.

nodes.label: Michel Strickmann
nodes.summary: Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the EPHE and Paris Diderot University under supervisors including Maxime Kaltenmark, Léon Vandermeersch, and Kristofer Schipper, and held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Bordeaux.

nodes.label: Dodrupchen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous masters, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (~1944–1959) and Kunzang Pelden, and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and others.

nodes.label: Qinni Liu
nodes.summary: Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Jules Bloch
nodes.summary: A linguist and Indologist, Bloch studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet, earning a doctorate from the University of Paris. He held chairs at the École des langues orientales (1921–1937) and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

nodes.label: Alf Sommerfelt
nodes.summary: Alf Sommerfelt was a scholar in linguistics who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as a professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

nodes.label: Olivier Lacombe
nodes.summary: Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris, where he held a post (~1959–1970) before joining Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

nodes.label: Institut Français de Francfort
variants: French Insitute at Frankfurt am Main

nodes.label: Tu Weiming
nodes.summary: Tu Weiming is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies who earned his MA and PhD from Harvard University. He held faculty posts at Berkeley and Harvard (1981–2010), directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008), and became chair professor at Peking University (~2010).

nodes.label: Urs App
nodes.description: Swiss historian of Ideas, Religion, and Philosophy
nodes.summary: Urs App (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied under Richard DeMartino, Yoshitaka Iriya, and Seizan Yanagida, earning a Ph.D. from Temple University, and was associate director at Hanazono University's International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism.

nodes.summary: András Róna-Tas is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1950–1955) under Gyula Ortutay and Lajos Ligeti. His main academic posts included Eötvös Loránd University (1956) and the University of Szeged (1968–2002).

nodes.label: Anam Thubten Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche. He served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Carl Olson
nodes.summary: Carl Olson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College, attested between 2005 and 2015.

nodes.label: Tai-shing Wut
nodes.summary: Tai-shing Wut is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Ming-Wood Liu.

nodes.label: Sangharakshita
nodes.description: Founder of the Friends of the Western Buddhist Order (1925–2018)
nodes.summary: Sangharakshita (1925–2018) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and trained under Jagdish Kashyap, Jianmin Chen, Dhardo Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

nodes.label: Wilt L. Idema
nodes.summary: Sinologist Wilt L. Idema earned his degrees at Leiden University, completing his doctorate under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (~1968–1974). He served as professor at Leiden (1976–1999) and later became Professor of Chinese Literature at Harvard University in 2000.

nodes.label: David Schaberg
nodes.summary: David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford and Harvard. He joined the University of California, Los Angeles in 1996, later serving as Dean of Humanities (2012) and Senior Dean of the College (2020).

nodes.label: Shuming Liang
nodes.summary: Shuming Liang was a philosopher, Buddhist studies scholar, and Indologist. Educated at Shuntian Middle School, he joined Peking University's philosophy department in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

nodes.label: Nicolas Revire
nodes.summary: Nicolas Revire works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University, under doctoral supervisors Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h
nodes.summary: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was an art historian and Indologist who studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988. He served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from approximately 1989 to 2008.

シラパコーン大学考古学部
シラパコーン大学大学院

nodes.label: Thich Thien Nghiem
nodes.summary: Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under the doctoral supervision of Shalini Singhal, attested in 2012.

nodes.label: K. T. S. Sarao
nodes.summary: K. T. S. Sarao (born 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed PhDs at the University of Delhi and Cambridge (under F. R. Allchin and K. R. Norman), becoming a Professor at Delhi in 1995.

nodes.label: David Ownby
nodes.summary: David Ownby is a scholar of sinology, history, and religious studies. He earned his BA at Vanderbilt and PhD at Harvard, taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993), and served as Professor of History at Université de Montréal (1994–2023).

nodes.label: Vincent Goossaert
nodes.summary: Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997). He worked at the CNRS (~1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

nodes.label: Zhe Ji
nodes.summary: Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned a PhD in sociology from EHESS in 2007. Ji served as Associate Professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (attested 2011-2017).

nodes.label: Benjamin A. Elman
