nodes.jawiki: ベンジャミン・エルマン
nodes.summary: Sinologist and historian Benjamin A. Elman completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He taught at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program in 2002.

nodes.label: William M. Bodiford
variants: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・ボディフォード
nodes.summary: William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale (Ph.D. under Stanley Weinstein) and became a professor at UCLA circa 1992 after teaching at Davidson and Iowa.

nodes.label: Mark Juergensmeyer
nodes.summary: Mark Juergensmeyer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Illinois and UC Berkeley (PhD ~1965–1974), holding major posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College (~2020).

nodes.label: Nanyang Technological University
variants: Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies, Singapore
Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies (IDSS), Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore

nodes.label: Friederike Assandri
nodes.summary: Friederike Assandri works in sinology and religious studies. She studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and pursued doctoral studies at Heidelberg University, where she later held a post attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Tufts University
variants: Tufts University School of Veterinary Medicine

nodes.label: Karen Nelson Villanueva
nodes.summary: Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013) and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.

nodes.label: Stefan Larsson
nodes.summary: Stefan Larsson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm. He was later a postdoctoral fellow at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Shayne Clarke
nodes.summary: Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, earned an MA at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, and completed a PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, later becoming an associate professor at McMaster University.

nodes.label: Sonya S. Lee
nodes.summary: Sonya S. Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung. She taught at Swarthmore College and held posts at Stanford University and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Wu Hung
nodes.summary: Wu Hung is an art historian and Sinologist who studied at CAFA and Harvard. He taught at Harvard before joining the University of Chicago in 1994 as Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History.

nodes.label: Jerome Silbergeld
nodes.summary: Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He earned his degrees from Stanford and the University of Oregon, later holding posts at the University of Washington (circa 1975–2001) and Princeton University (circa 2001–2018).

nodes.label: William L. Ames
nodes.summary: William L. Ames works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned an M.S. from Caltech and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as a librarian at John F. Kennedy University.

nodes.id: I:University of North Carolina at Charlotte
nodes.label: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
variants: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

nodes.label: Richard A. Hutch
nodes.summary: Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

nodes.label: Southern Illinois University Carbondale
variants: Morris Library, Southern Illinois University at Carbondale

nodes.label: University of California, San Diego
variants: University of California at San Diego

nodes.label: William R. LaFleur
variants: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.jawiki: ウィリアム・R・ラフルーア
nodes.summary: William R. LaFleur specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago (Ph.D.), he held faculty posts at Princeton (~1971–1978), UCLA (~1978–1990), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

nodes.label: Sibraj Chetry
nodes.summary: Sibraj Chetry works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah. He was attested as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College in 2012.

nodes.label: Huiwen Zhuang
nodes.summary: Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher
nodes.summary: Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an Indologist and historian who earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1977–1984) and served there as an Assistant Professor from approximately 1980 to 2021.

nodes.label: Aaron P. Proffitt
nodes.summary: Aaron P. Proffitt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his master's at the University of Colorado and his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan, becoming an assistant professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (~2015).

nodes.label: Valdo H. Viglielmo
variants: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルド・ヴィリエルモ
nodes.summary: Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Harvard, Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Gakushuin. He taught at Harvard, several Tokyo universities, and Princeton, before serving as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1965–2002).

nodes.label: Dan Smyer Yü
nodes.summary: Dan Smyer Yü specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of California, Davis, and served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

nodes.label: University of California, Davis
variants: カリフォルニア大学デービス校

nodes.label: David L. McMahan
nodes.summary: David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies. He taught at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the University of Vermont, and served as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013) at Franklin & Marshall College.

nodes.label: Hugh Gray
nodes.summary: Hugh Gray (1916–2002) was a scholar in Indology who studied at Battersea Grammar School. He served as a lecturer at SOAS and the University of London from circa 1964 to 1982.

nodes.label: Drolma
nodes.summary: Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Hanna Havnevik
variants: ハンナ・ハヴネヴィク

nodes.label: J. Thomas Rimer
nodes.summary: J. Thomas Rimer (born 1933) is a Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Princeton University (1954) and Columbia University (1968, 1971). He held positions at Washington University in St. Louis, UCLA, the University of Maryland (~1986–1991), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1991–2013).

nodes.label: Lori Meeks
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies, Lori Meeks earned degrees at Columbia and Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. Following a postdoctoral fellowship at Stanford, she joined the University of Southern California in 2005 as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies.

nodes.label: Masayuki Taira
nodes.summary: Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1980) and held posts at Osaka University (~1994–2012), Kansai University, and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2012).

nodes.label: Shunsho Manabe
nodes.summary: Shunsho Manabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Tohoku University (~1960–1964). He taught Lori Meeks and held positions at Hosen Gakuen College (~1974–1999) and Shikoku University (~2007–2017).

nodes.label: Shenpen Hookham
nodes.summary: Shenpen Hookham works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Michael M. Broido, as well as under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Hildegard Diemberger
nodes.summary: Hildegard Diemberger (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology. She conducted research supervised by Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, and has taught Michela Clemente, Lobsang Yongdan, and Adrian Zenz.

nodes.label: Tsewang Gyurme
nodes.summary: Tsewang Gyurme works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He has served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Wilfred Cantwell Smith
variants: ウィルフレッド・キャントウェル・スミス
nodes.summary: Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton (PhD). He held posts at Forman Christian College, McGill University, Dalhousie University, Harvard University (1964–1973; 1978–1985), and Trinity College, Toronto.

nodes.label: Lama Kunga Rinpoche
nodes.description: Buddhist Lama of the Sakya school
nodes.summary: Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ngor Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959. In 1973, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center.

nodes.label: Brian Cutillo
nodes.summary: Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from around 1963 to 1967 and was a student of Ngawang Wangyal.

nodes.label: Kemu Jin
nodes.summary: Kemu Jin was an Indologist, Sinologist, and linguist. He served on the faculty at Visva-Bharati University from 1941 to 1945 and became a Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University in 1948.

nodes.label: Fabio Rambelli
variants: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.jawiki: ファビオ・ランベッリ
nodes.summary: Fabio Rambelli works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Venice, Naples, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and has held posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (around 2009).

nodes.label: Eric Reinders
nodes.summary: A scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Reinders studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

nodes.label: Allan G. Grapard
nodes.summary: Specializing in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Grapard earned his Ph.D. from INALCO. He served as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at the University of California (~1985–2012) and Professor Emeritus at UCSB.

nodes.label: Gregory P. A. Levine
nodes.summary: Gregory P. A. Levine is a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist visual culture who studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University. He became an Associate Professor of History of Art at UC Berkeley around 1997.

nodes.label: Lin Heng
nodes.summary: Lin Heng is a scholar of Indology who studied at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi, earning an MA (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Roger T. Ames
nodes.summary: Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at UBC, NTU, CUHK, and SOAS under D. C. Lau (PhD, 1975–1978). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016) and Peking University (~2016).

nodes.label: Steve Odin
nodes.summary: Steve Odin works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He completed graduate studies and a postdoc at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, and became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi in 1982.

nodes.label: Graham Parkes
nodes.summary: Graham Parkes is a philosopher and Japanologist who earned his Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. He served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi and later held multiple professorial and administrative chairs at University College Cork.

nodes.label: Jason M. Wirth
nodes.image: Jason Martin Wirth (born 1963) in the video 'Everybody's Climate 2025 – Jason Wirth on Humanity in the Anthropocene'.png
nodes.summary: Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki. He held the Theiline Pigott McCone Chair in Humanities at Seattle University from 2014 to 2016.

nodes.label: Graham Priest
variants: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.jawiki: グレアム・プリースト
nodes.summary: Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge and earned his PhD under John Lane Bell at LSE. He held major posts at Melbourne, St Andrews, and the Graduate Center, CUNY.

nodes.label: Jan Westerhoff
nodes.summary: Jan Westerhoff (b. 1976) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and from SOAS. Around 2013, he became Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford and Fellow at Lady Margaret Hall.

nodes.label: Lili Zheng
nodes.summary: Lili Zheng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Uma Chakravarti
nodes.summary: Uma Chakravarti works in history, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, Miranda House, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti, and was an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

nodes.label: D. Devahuti
nodes.description: D. Devahuti, 1929-1988; taught at universities of Malaya, Queensland, and Delhi

nodes.label: Ron Garry
nodes.summary: Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche as a traditional teacher and under Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Stuart Ray Sarbacker
nodes.summary: Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under the doctoral supervision of David M. Knipe.

nodes.label: B. Alan Wallace
nodes.description: American author, translator, teacher, researcher, interpreter, and Buddhist practitioner
nodes.summary: B. Alan Wallace works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst, Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt, and under several Tibetan teachers. He taught at Rabten Choeling, UC Santa Barbara, and founded the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

nodes.label: Berthe Jansen
nodes.description: Assistant Professor of Tibetan Studies at Leiden University
nodes.summary: Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk at Leiden. She held posts at Heidelberg University and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Vincent Breugem
nodes.summary: Vincent Breugem works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (MA by 1996, PhD by 2012), under Lucia Dolce, and at Taisho, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities, later serving as a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Tulku Thondup
nodes.summary: Tulku Thondup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

nodes.label: David E. Cooper
nodes.summary: David E. Cooper is a philosopher educated at Highgate School and St Edmund Hall. He held teaching posts at the University of Oxford, served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and was a visiting professor at Peking University in 2022.

nodes.label: Purushottama Bilimoria
nodes.summary: Purushottama Bilimoria specializes in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, earning a PhD at La Trobe under Shivesh Thakur. He held posts at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, and visiting professorships at Columbia and Stony Brook.

nodes.label: Simon P. James
nodes.summary: Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He taught Colette Sciberras and has held posts at Durham University, including philosophy tutor (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).

nodes.label: University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point
variants: University of Wisconsin at Stevens Point

nodes.label: Latika Lahiri
nodes.summary: Latika Lahiri was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji from 1956 to 1958. She held an academic post at the University of Delhi from around 1969 to 1988.

nodes.label: Tan Chung
nodes.summary: Tan Chung specializes in history, archaeology, and Sinology, earning a PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He held positions at the National Defence Academy, University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, the Institute of Chinese Studies, and Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

nodes.label: Michael Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

nodes.label: Sonam Chhoki
nodes.summary: Sonam Chhoki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D at SOAS University of London. She has held a post as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

nodes.label: Thierry Mathou
nodes.summary: Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

nodes.label: Françoise Pommaret
variants: フランソワーズ・ポマレ
nodes.summary: Françoise Pommaret (born 1954) specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at Sorbonne University, INALCO, and the University of Paris. Her career includes posts at INALCO, the Royal University of Bhutan (~2008), and CNRS (2002, ~2004).

nodes.label: Karma Ura
nodes.summary: Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.

nodes.label: Ronald E. Purser
nodes.summary: Ronald E. Purser is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1991–1997) and San Francisco State University (~1997) as Professor of Management.

nodes.label: San Francisco State University
variants: School of Business der San Francisco State University
サンフランシスコ州立大学

nodes.label: David R. Loy
nodes.summary: David R. Loy is a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Carleton, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore. He held posts at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

nodes.label: Pamela D. Winfield
nodes.summary: Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Temple University in 2001 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

nodes.label: Paula Arai
nodes.summary: Paula Arai specializes in Buddhist, religious, and Japanese studies. She studied at Kalamazoo College, Waseda, and Harvard (PhD 1993). She held posts at Vanderbilt (1994–2002), Louisiana State University (2007), and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

nodes.label: Patricia Fister
nodes.jawiki: パトリシア・フィスター
nodes.summary: Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas (~1978–1983), where she served as assistant professor of art history (~1983–1990), and later was professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2007–2019).

nodes.label: Michaela Mross
nodes.summary: Michaela Mross works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and earned her PhD from the University of Munich (2014), later holding positions at UC Berkeley and Stanford University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Diane E. Riggs
nodes.summary: Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford, and later held posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Daniel Timothy Aitken
nodes.summary: Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jay L. Garfield and studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: University of Tasmania
variants: Centre for Applied Philosophy and Ethics

nodes.label: Chanju Mun
nodes.summary: Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD attested 2002). Mun's teachers and supervisors included Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, John D. Dunne, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.

nodes.label: Yifa
nodes.description: Taiwanese Buddhist nun, scholar and writer
nodes.summary: Yifa (born 1959) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. She served as department head and dean at University of the West (~1996–2004) and founded Woodenfish Foundation.

nodes.label: Reginald A. Ray
nodes.summary: Reginald A. Ray is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa. Ray taught at the University of Colorado (attested 2001–2002) and served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).

nodes.label: Dainin Katagiri
nodes.summary: Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who trained under Eko Hashimoto and Daicho Hayashi at Eihei-ji and studied at Komazawa University. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission and as interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Hanh
variants: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.jawiki: ティク・ナット・ハン
nodes.summary: Thich Nhat Hanh was a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Thanh Quý Chân Thật, at Báo Quốc Buddhist Academy, Saigon University, Princeton, and Columbia, later teaching at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh, and Cornell.

nodes.label: Shodo Harada
nodes.summary: Shodo Harada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies figure who trained at Shofukuji under Mumon Yamada (~1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.

nodes.label: John Daido Loori
nodes.image: Daido Roshi in the Buddha Hall.jpeg
nodes.summary: John Daido Loori worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Rutgers University and under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi. He held a post at Naropa University in 1974 and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009).

nodes.label: Richard Sorabji
nodes.summary: Richard Sorabji is a philosopher and Indologist educated at Pembroke College, Oxford. He held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1962–1970), King's College London (circa 1970–2000), and Gresham College (circa 2000–2006).

nodes.label: Dagfinn Føllesdal
variants: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
ダグフィン・フォレスダール
nodes.jawiki: ダグフィン・フェレスダール
nodes.summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and completed his PhD at Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine. He taught at Harvard, Stanford University (1968–2011), and the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Jiang Wu
nodes.summary: Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at Nankai University and earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello, later serving as professor at the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Yonsei University
variants: Institute of East and West Studies at Yonsei University

nodes.label: Thierry Meynard
nodes.summary: Thierry Meynard is a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou, later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies.

nodes.id: I:The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
nodes.label: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies
variants: The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Scott Pacey
nodes.summary: Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing his doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011, he held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Ken McLeod
nodes.summary: Ken McLeod is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the University of British Columbia and trained under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche and the 16th Karmapa. He was resident teacher at Kagyu Dongak Chuling (circa 1985–1990).

nodes.label: Kalu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Osel Ling under teachers including Lama Norbu Tondrup. He served as Vajra Master at Palpung (~1940–1955) and Abbot at Changchub Choeling (1957).

nodes.label: Tomy Augustine
nodes.summary: Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed a master's at the University of Madras under C. S. Sundaram and earned a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal, later holding a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Michela Clemente
nodes.summary: Michela Clemente works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015), and held a post as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny
nodes.description: Polish bibliologist, paper historian, conservator of monuments.
nodes.summary: Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń. She held an affiliation at Cornell University (attested 2009) and a post at the University of Warsaw (2015).

nodes.label: Field Museum of Natural History
variants: フィールド自然史博物館

nodes.label: Thomas Cleary
nodes.summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy, Cleary studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earning a Ph.D. at Harvard University and a JD at the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jonathan Christopher Cleary
nodes.summary: Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed his doctoral work at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1976–1984). He held an instructor post at Wesleyan University from around 1984 to 1986.

nodes.label: Kazuaki Tanahashi
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Tanahashi is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977–1984) and is a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

nodes.label: Mary C. Wright
nodes.summary: Mary C. Wright was a sinologist and historian educated at Vassar College, Radcliffe College (PhD), and Harvard. She held positions at the Hoover Institution (1946–1959), Stanford University (from 1947), and Yale University (1959–1964 as associate, 1964 as full professor).

nodes.label: Torkel Brekke
nodes.summary: Torkel Brekke (born 1970), specializing in Indology and religious studies, earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo and a doctorate at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He has held posts at PRIO, the University of Oslo, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

nodes.label: Kenryu T. Tsuji
nodes.summary: Kenryu T. Tsuji (1919–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

nodes.id: I:National Museum Institute of History of Art, Conservation and Museology
nodes.label: National Museum Institute of History of Art, Conservation and Museology
Alka Patel
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Patel completed her bachelor's degree at Mount Holyoke College and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1993–2000). She became an associate professor at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

nodes.label: University of California, Irvine
variants: University of California, Irvine Seminar in Experimental Critical Theory
カリフォルニア大学アーバイン校

nodes.label: Edward S. Casey
nodes.summary: Edward S. Casey (1939–) is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Northwestern (Ph.D.), and the Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur. He taught at UCSB and Yale before serving as faculty and dean at Stony Brook University (~1978).

nodes.label: Rebecca Redwood French
nodes.summary: Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a J.D. from the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. from Yale, mentored by scholars including Robert A. F. Thurman. She held posts at the University of Colorado and University at Buffalo.

nodes.label: Rafal Stepien
nodes.summary: Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure. He was an Academic Visitor at Wadham College (2012–2013) and an Exchange Scholar at Harvard University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Chün-fang Yü
nodes.summary: Chün-fang Yü (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1965–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen, later holding professorial posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001).

nodes.label: École Normale Supérieure
variants: Husserl Archives at the École normale supérieure (ENS/CNRS)

nodes.label: University of Sussex
variants: University of Sussex's School of African & Asian Studies

nodes.label: Philippe Turenne
nodes.summary: Philippe Turenne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, having also studied under Richard P. Hayes and several traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Peter Schwieger
nodes.summary: Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and completed his doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Bonn. He held positions at the Göttingen Academy (1978), Humboldt University (2001), and Bonn (2001).

nodes.label: Dieter Schuh
nodes.summary: Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at Cologne and Bonn, earning his PhD and Habilitation at Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978-2007) and founded and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Christian Wittern
nodes.summary: Christian Wittern is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008), where he was a professor, and at Hanazono University (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Eliot Deutsch
nodes.summary: Eliot Deutsch was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Harvard, and Columbia (Ph.D. 1956–1960). He held posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi (1967–2006).

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Thittila
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Thittila (1896–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1933–1934). He was a librarian at Adyar Library and The Buddhist Society (~1938) and taught at the University of Rangoon (1952).

nodes.label: Reiho Masunaga
nodes.summary: Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya from circa 1925 to 1931 and served as a teacher at Komazawa University from circa 1930 to 1970.

nodes.label: Kamala Tiyavanich
nodes.summary: Kamala Tiyavanich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there in 1993–1994.

nodes.label: David K. Wyatt
variants: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.jawiki: デビッド・K・ワイアット
nodes.summary: David K. Wyatt (1937–2006) was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He taught at SOAS and Michigan, chaired the history department at Cornell (1969–2002), and served as president of the Association for Asian Studies.

nodes.label: Richard Polenberg
nodes.summary: Richard Polenberg was an American history scholar educated at Brooklyn College and Columbia University (PhD 1964). He served as a professor at Cornell University from 1966 to 2011 and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University.

nodes.label: Trung Huynh
nodes.summary: Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Darui Long (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Lama Jampa Thaye
nodes.summary: Lama Jampa Thaye is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester, studied with traditional teachers including Karma Thinley Rinpoche, and joined the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

nodes.label: Imre Galambos
nodes.description: Scholar of medieval Chinese and Tangut manuscripts
nodes.summary: Imre Galambos works in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd, Nankai, and UC Berkeley. His posts include the British Library, UC Santa Barbara, Zhejiang University, and the University of Cambridge.

nodes.label: Joseph Margolis
variants: ジョセフ・ザルマン・マーゴリス
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・マーゴリス
nodes.summary: Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who earned an M.A. from Columbia University (~1947–1950). He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University from 1991.

nodes.label: Sandra A. Wawrytko
nodes.summary: Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at San Diego State University, attested as Professor in 1999 and as Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.

nodes.label: Megan Bryson
nodes.summary: Megan Bryson, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at Stanford University and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Rachelle M. Scott
nodes.summary: Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her doctoral dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay. She held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

nodes.id: I:Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
nodes.label: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Asiatic Arts
variants: Ferenc Hopp Museum of Eastern Asiatic Art

nodes.id: I:Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
variants: Oriental Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences
Oriental Collection, Hungarian Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Géza Bethlenfalvy
nodes.summary: Working in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, Bethlenfalvy studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under Lajos Ligeti. He held positions at the University of Delhi, Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Zsóka Gelle
nodes.description: Hungarian Tibetologist, translator, writer, filmmaker and guide
nodes.summary: Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Vienna. She has held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College, the University of Vienna (2011-2014), and ELTE (2014-2016).

nodes.label: Benjamin Bogin
nodes.summary: Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, studying under Janet Gyatso, Gareth Sparham, and doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr.

nodes.label: Tomoko Masuzawa
nodes.summary: Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University (MA ~1977–1979), and UC Santa Barbara (PhD ~1979–1985). She held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and the University of Michigan (1999; ~2001–2020).

nodes.label: James Robson
nodes.image: James Robson (academic) on Filled with Meaning.png
nodes.summary: James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Stanford. He taught at Williams College and the University of Michigan, and has held professorships and directorships at Harvard University, including the Harvard-Yenching Institute (2024).

nodes.label: John J. Holder
nodes.summary: John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies and studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and posts at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

nodes.label: Eric Huntington
nodes.summary: Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

nodes.label: Dina Bangdel
nodes.summary: Dina Bangdel was a scholar of history, art history, and Buddhist and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University from circa 1999 to 2002 and at Virginia Commonwealth University from circa 2002 to 2017.

nodes.label: Virginia Commonwealth University
variants: Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine

nodes.label: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
variants: ジャムヤン・キェンツェ・ワンポ
nodes.summary: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a prominent figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Minling Trichen Gyurme Sangye Kunga, Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, and Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye.

nodes.label: Peter Alan Roberts
nodes.summary: Peter Alan Roberts specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under Michael Aris.

nodes.label: Somphong Santacitto
nodes.summary: Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under MA supervisor Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Watchara Ngamchitcharoen
nodes.native: วัชระ งามจิตรเจริญ

nodes.label: Prayudh Payutto
nodes.native: ประยุทธ์ ปยุตฺโต
nodes.image: ป.อ. ปยุตฺโต.jpg
nodes.description: Thai Buddhist monk, abbot of Wat Nyanavesakavan
nodes.summary: Prayudh Payutto (born 1938) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He earned his bachelor's degree and served as associate dean (c. 1964–1973) at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, and was named Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.

nodes.id: I:Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale
nodes.label: Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale
variants: Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale
Research Centre for East Asian Civilizations (CRCAO)
CRCAO (Centre de recherches sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale; UMR 8155)

nodes.label: Brian D. Ruppert
nodes.summary: Brian D. Ruppert works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He served at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (c. 1999–2018) before becoming a Japanese Studies professor and chair at Bates College around 2018.

nodes.label: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani
nodes.summary: Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani works in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Perry Link.

nodes.label: Perry Link
nodes.summary: Perry Link (born 1944) works in Sinology and linguistics. After earning a B.A. from Harvard University (~1962–1966), he held posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and the University of California, Riverside (~2008).

nodes.label: James Ishmael Ford
nodes.summary: James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied at Sonoma State University and Pacific School of Religion, training under Sojun Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant.

nodes.label: Jiyu-Kennett
nodes.summary: Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji. She was head priest at Unpuku-ji (~1968–1969) and founded Shasta Abbey in 1969, serving as abbess until 1996.

nodes.label: Jonathan C. Gold
nodes.summary: Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

nodes.label: Michael Eido Luetchford
nodes.summary: Michael Eido Luetchford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a degree in Electronic Engineering at the University of Bradford (~1964–1967) and studied traditionally under Gudō Wafu Nishijima (~1973–2007).

nodes.label: Gudō Wafu Nishijima
nodes.summary: Gudō Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who studied law at the University of Tokyo and under Kodo Sawaki and Renpō Niwa. He founded Dogen Sangha International and lectured at the University of Tokyo and the Eastern Institute.

nodes.label: Anna Balikci-Denjongpa
nodes.summary: Anna Balikci-Denjongpa, a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies, completed her PhD at SOAS under Lionel Caplan and studied under Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became research coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson
nodes.summary: Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.

nodes.label: Southern Methodist University
variants: Perkins School of Theology, Southern Methodist University
Perkins School of Theology at the Southern Methodist University
Perkins School of Theology at Southern Methodist University

nodes.label: Elizabeth Anne Morrison
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Anne Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her doctoral studies under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, and held teaching posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Chögyam Trungpa
variants: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
チョギャム トゥルンパ
チューギャム・ドゥンパ
nodes.image: Trungpa from Khenpo gangshar2 cropped image.jpg
nodes.jawiki: チョギャム・トゥルンパ
nodes.summary: Chögyam Trungpa (1939–1987) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and teacher. He studied at Oxford (1963) and under teachers including Khenpo Gangshar. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1967), Naropa University (1973), Shambhala Training, and Gampo Abbey.

nodes.label: Aruna Haldar
nodes.summary: Aruna Haldar worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose, and served as a teacher at Patna University.

nodes.label: Girindrasekhar Bose
nodes.summary: Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) was an Indian scholar of psychology and philosophy. He studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, where he served as Professor of Experimental Psychology (1917–1949). He also founded the Indian Psychoanalytic Society.

nodes.label: Joachim Gentz
nodes.summary: Joachim Gentz is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Perry Schmidt-Leukel
nodes.summary: Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Munich (~1976–1996), he held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

nodes.label: Philip Clart
nodes.description: German Sinologist, Professor of Chinese Studies at Leipzig University, Germany
nodes.summary: Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from approximately 1990 to 1996 and was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at Leipzig University around 2008.

nodes.label: Michael Stanley-Baker
nodes.summary: Specializing in sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, Michael Stanley-Baker earned an MA at Indiana University under Stephen R. Bokenkamp (attested 2006). His posts include appointments at NTU, Leipzig University, MPIWG, and the University of Pittsburgh.

nodes.label: Harold Stewart
nodes.summary: Harold Stewart (1916–1995) worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was educated at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

nodes.label: David Tracy
nodes.summary: David Tracy (1939–2025) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. After lecturing at the Catholic University of America, he was a longtime professor of Catholic studies at the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

nodes.label: Peter Schwabland
nodes.summary: Peter Schwabland is a Tibetologist who earned his MA at the University of Washington under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Michael L. Walter
nodes.summary: Michael L. Walter was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He held posts as a research fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute and as a special languages cataloger at Indiana University.

nodes.label: Akimichi Eda
nodes.summary: Akimichi Eda is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.

nodes.label: Lita Peipina
nodes.summary: Lita Peipina is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and Jens Braarvig, completing an MA at the University of Oslo, attested in 2008.

nodes.label: Stephen Prothero
nodes.summary: Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. from Yale University (~1978–1982) and his M.A. and Ph.D. from Harvard University (~1984–1990) under William R. Hutchison. Around 1996, he joined Boston University, where he became Professor Emeritus.

nodes.label: Duncan Ryūken Williams
nodes.summary: Duncan Ryūken Williams works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Reed College and earned a PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.

nodes.label: Kenneth K. Tanaka
nodes.summary: Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at CSU, Stanford, IBS, Eastern Institute, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at IBS, UC Berkeley, Musashino University, and chaired the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.

nodes.label: Kosho Uchiyama
nodes.summary: Kosho Uchiyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a master's in Western philosophy from Waseda University and studied under Kodo Sawaki. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (1937–1939) and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).

nodes.label: Kodo Sawaki
nodes.summary: Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Takada Junior College, Senju-ji, and Hōryūji Kangakuin, studying under Sotan Oka and others. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji (~1949–1965).

nodes.label: Sotan Oka
nodes.summary: Sotan Oka (1860–1921) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served at Komazawa University as dean/professor (1899) and president (1918), and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

nodes.label: Ian Kishizawa
nodes.summary: Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani.

nodes.label: See Mui Yian
nodes.summary: See Mui Yian is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Warren Lee Todd
nodes.summary: Warren Lee Todd is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Alison Denton Jones
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Jones studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, as well as Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

nodes.label: Martin King Whyte
nodes.summary: Martin King Whyte is a sociologist and sinologist educated at Cornell and Harvard (doctorate, 1971). His career includes faculty posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard University from 2000.

nodes.label: Allan H. Barr
nodes.summary: Specializing in Sinology, Barr received his doctorate from the University of Oxford in 1983 and served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Margaret Dornish
nodes.summary: Margaret Dornish is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California. She served as an Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Daniela Berti
nodes.summary: Daniela Berti is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Siena. She held a fellowship at the Centre d'Etudes Himalayennes (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Centre d'Etudes Himalayennes
variants: Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya, Paris

nodes.label: Gilles Tarabout
nodes.summary: Gilles Tarabout works in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Madeleine Biardeau. As of 2004, his positions included senior fellow at CNRS, member of EHESS, and exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.

nodes.id: I:Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
nodes.label: Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme
variants: Maison des Sciences de l'Homme, Paris

nodes.label: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, among others. He held teaching posts at Lhasa Mentsikhang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

nodes.label: Akio Tatsuguchi
nodes.summary: Akio Tatsuguchi (Myōsei Tatsuguchi) is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Diane E. Riggs and Jeff Wilson. He served as a professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Robert Charles Zaehner
nodes.image: Internationaal Theologisch Congres toekomst van de religie, religie van de toeko, Bestanddeelnr 925-4729.jpg
nodes.description: British spy and academic on Eastern religions (1913–1974)
nodes.summary: Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) studied at Christ Church, Oxford, and under Harold Walter Bailey at Cambridge. A scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Iranian studies, he served as Oxford's Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and All Souls fellow (1952–1974).

nodes.label: James A. Benn
nodes.summary: James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS under Timothy H. Barrett, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. His appointments include Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

nodes.label: Kyoko Tokuno
nodes.summary: Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.

nodes.label: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje
variants: ドゥジョム・ジグドラル・イェシェ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who founded the International Nyingma Society. He studied under Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught students including Matthew T. Kapstein.

nodes.label: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley
nodes.summary: Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teacher F. E. L. Priestley, and held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Julia Ching
nodes.summary: A scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religion, Ching earned her doctorate from Australian National University (~1968–1971). After teaching at Columbia and Yale, she became a professor of religion, philosophy, and East Asian studies at the University of Toronto (1978).

nodes.label: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby
nodes.summary: Willard Gurdon Oxtoby (1933–2003) was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. His career included teaching posts at McGill, Yale, and Trinity College, Toronto, before becoming founding director at Toronto.

nodes.label: Jacob Holubeck
nodes.summary: Jacob Holubeck is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Eric Stephen Goodell
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar, Goodell studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, completing an MA and studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Georgetown University
variants: School of Foreign Service, Georgetown University

nodes.label: Kristin Johnston Largen
nodes.summary: Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

nodes.label: Brandon Dotson
nodes.summary: Brandon Dotson is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at SOAS (c. 2005–2010) and the University of Munich (c. 2010–2019).

nodes.label: Marcus Bingenheimer
nodes.summary: Marcus Bingenheimer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his doctoral studies under Norbert Klaes at the University of Würzburg, later holding positions at the Dharma Drum Institute (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).

nodes.label: Jongmyung Kim
nodes.summary: Jongmyung Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies who studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

nodes.label: Central Academy of Fine Arts
variants: Central Academy of Fine Arts in Beijing

nodes.label: Eugene Y. Wang
nodes.summary: Eugene Y. Wang works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield (~1992–1997), and held posts at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) and Harvard University (~1997).

nodes.label: Kristofer Schipper
nodes.summary: Kristofer Schipper was a sinologist who studied in Paris. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, École Pratique des Hautes Études, CNRS, Collège de France, and Leiden University, and later taught at Fuzhou University and Minnan Normal University.

nodes.label: Erik Haarh
nodes.summary: Erik Haarh was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed a doctorate at the University of Copenhagen. He worked at the Royal Danish Library (1956, 1962) and served as a department head and theology professor at Aarhus University (1969; 1983–1993).

nodes.label: Helen Baroni
nodes.summary: Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt. In 1993, she took up a post at the University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Shou-chien Shih
nodes.summary: A specialist in history, archaeology, and Sinology, Shou-chien Shih served as a professor at National Taiwan University from approximately 1990 to 2003. He was also the director of the National Palace Museum from around 2004 to 2006.

nodes.label: Brian J. Nichols
nodes.summary: Brian J. Nichols is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his PhD at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Anne C. Klein, attested in 2011.

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Program for Chinese language studies at Tsinghua University
Inter-University Board of Chinese Language Studies

nodes.label: Tansen Sen
nodes.summary: Tansen Sen specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Peking University under Yinzeng Geng and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later holding a post at Baruch College (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Takeshi Umehara
nodes.summary: Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan, Kyoto City University of Arts, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995), and the Institute of Technologists.

nodes.label: Kennard Lipman
nodes.summary: Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Herbert V. Günther and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

variants: sDe dge Ku se gSer ljongs bshad grwa

nodes.label: Drakgyab Lodrö
variants: mKhan Rinpoche Brag gyab Blos gros

nodes.label: Sarah Aoife Richardson
nodes.summary: Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of Tibetology, art history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD in 2016 at the University of Toronto under the supervision of Jennifer Purtle.

nodes.label: Julia F. Andrews
nodes.summary: A scholar of sinology and art history, Andrews studied at Brown, Harvard, and UC Berkeley. She joined the faculty at Ohio State University around 1987.

nodes.label: Frank J. Hoffman
nodes.summary: Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.

nodes.label: Trent Walker
nodes.summary: Trent Walker is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

nodes.label: Tina Rasmussen
nodes.summary: Tina Rasmussen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed an MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer.

nodes.label: Pa-Auk Sayadaw
nodes.native: ဖားအောက်ဆရာတော်

nodes.label: Jan Chozen Bays
variants: ジャン・澄禅・ベイズ
nodes.summary: Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner. She studied at Swarthmore College, UC San Diego, and under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She served as a teacher in Oregon and abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery.

nodes.label: Taizan Maezumi
nodes.summary: Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, San Francisco State University, and under Baian Hakujun Kuroda, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, and Koryu Osaka. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission and founded the Kuroda Institute.

マサチューセッツ大学医学部

マサチューセッツ大学医学大学院

nodes.label: Neal Donner
nodes.summary: Neal Donner works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

nodes.label: Wenjie Qin
nodes.summary: Wenjie Qin specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming as well as Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: Bing Chen
nodes.summary: Bing Chen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Sichuan University from circa 1987 to 2015 and held a post at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (attested 1993).

nodes.label: Yun-hua Jan
nodes.summary: Yun-hua Jan (1923–2018) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Tan Yun-shan, served as a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953, and was a Professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

nodes.label: Stephanie Roemer
nodes.summary: Stephanie Roemer is a Tibetologist who completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

nodes.label: Eberhard Sandschneider
nodes.summary: Eberhard Sandschneider (born 1955) is a Sinologist who studied at Saarland University. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations as Otto-Wolff-Direktor (2003–2016).

nodes.label: German Council on Foreign Relations
variants: Forschungsinstitut der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Auswärtige Politik

nodes.label: Naoki Nabeshima
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Naoki Nabeshima served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University, where he also founded the Open Research Center for Humanities, Science and Religion (attested 2004).

nodes.id: I:Open Research Center for Humanities, Science and Religion, Ryukoku University
nodes.label: Open Research Center for Humanities, Science and Religion, Ryukoku University
variants: Ryūkoku's Open Research Center for Humanities, Science and Religion

nodes.label: David Matsumoto
nodes.summary: David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, with his posts there attested in 2004 and 2013.

nodes.label: Jing-shen Tao
nodes.summary: Jing-shen Tao is a historian and Sinologist educated at National Taiwan University and Indiana University (Ph.D. ~1965–1969). He was a Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000) and Correspondence Research Fellow at Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: Christian Coseru
nodes.description: American philosopher and scholar of Buddhist philosophy
nodes.summary: Christian Coseru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Bucharest and his PhD at the Australian National University (~1999–2003). In ~2006, he became Associate Professor at the College of Charleston.

nodes.label: C. W. Huntington, Jr.
nodes.summary: C. W. Huntington, Jr. (1949–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~2000–2020).

nodes.label: Kevin Buckelew
nodes.summary: Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, with doctoral supervision from Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.

nodes.label: Valeria Gazizova
nodes.summary: Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in tibetology and religious studies who completed her Master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Loden Sherab Dagyab
nodes.summary: Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and under Tenzin Gyatso, Trijang Rinpoche, and Ling Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966) and served at the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Pema Tsering
nodes.summary: Pema Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Shenga, taught Ruth Gamble, and held an attested post at the University of Bonn in 1996.

nodes.label: Martin Brauen
nodes.summary: Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi, earned a doctoral degree at the University of Zurich, and served at the Ethnographic Museum at Zurich (1975) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

nodes.label: Günter Grönbold
nodes.summary: Günter Grönbold specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Head of the South Asia Department at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1974 to 2008.

nodes.label: Michael Jay Sweet
nodes.summary: Michael Jay Sweet worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Richard Hugh Robinson, and traditional teachers, and later served as a clinical assistant professor of psychiatry there.

nodes.label: John Ross Carter
nodes.summary: John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith. He served as a professor at Colgate University's Chapel House from ~1972 to 2006.

nodes.label: Amita Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Amita Chatterjee is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.

nodes.label: Catholic University of America
variants: The Catholic University of America (Washington, DC)

nodes.label: Knut A. Jacobsen
nodes.summary: Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara. He was appointed professor in the history of religions at the University of Bergen in 1996.

nodes.label: Thomas P. Kasulis
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, Kasulis held posts at Ashland University (circa 1980–1991) and Ohio State University, where he was a professor from circa 1991 to 2018.

nodes.label: John M. Koller
nodes.summary: John M. Koller is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles Alexander Moore. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, attested in 1988 and 1999.

nodes.label: Daya Krishna
nodes.summary: Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

nodes.id: I:Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
nodes.label: Institute of Philosophy, Russian Academy of Sciences
variants: Institute of Philosophy, Academy of Sciences USSR

nodes.label: Michiko Yusa
nodes.summary: Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her PhD under Raimon Panikkar at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1976–1983) and was a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).

nodes.label: Diego Loukota
nodes.summary: Diego Loukota specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's degree from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

nodes.label: Ruixuan Chen
nodes.summary: Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, Paul Harrison, and others, earning a PhD from Leiden University (attested 2018), and holds a post at Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: Susan Andrews
nodes.summary: Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, also studying with Bernard Faure, D. Max Moerman, Michael Como, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Michael Como
nodes.summary: Michael Como is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, and Kuo-liang Wang. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Karma Thinley Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He served as abbot at Young Lamas Home School (~1963–1968) and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling (~1973).

nodes.label: Gendun Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Gendun Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master who founded Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, Dhagpo Kundreul Ling, and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling. From circa 1977 to 1997, he served as the abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling.

nodes.label: Bokar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1965–1989). He held a post at Bokar Monastery from circa 1984 until 2004.

nodes.label: Michael M. Broido
nodes.summary: Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge from ca. 1963 to 1967 and later held a post at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Geshe Tashi Tsering
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Tashi Tsering studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries, as well as under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He taught at Kopan Monastery (~1990–1992) and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

nodes.label: Qiwen Xiao
nodes.summary: Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda served as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research and as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011).

nodes.id: I:Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies
variants: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute for Asian Studies

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Saksena
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy and Indology, Shri Krishna Saksena held appointments as a professor at the University of Lucknow and at the University of Hawaiʻi, both attested in 2016.

nodes.label: East-West Center
variants: ハワイ東西センター文化・コミュニケーション研究所

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Malhotra
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1969) and founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

nodes.label: Shobhana Chelliah
nodes.summary: Shobhana Chelliah (born 1961) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1984–1990) and held a post at the University of North Texas (~1998).

nodes.label: Gregory Forgues
nodes.summary: Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, alongside receiving traditional Buddhist training.

nodes.label: Chanmyay Sayadaw U Janakabhivamsa
nodes.native: ဉာဏကာဘိဝံသ

Research Institute for Linguistics of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Pema Bhum
nodes.summary: Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University, and as Director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

nodes.label: Morton Klass
nodes.summary: Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his doctoral degree at Columbia University. He later taught at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Margaret Mead
variants: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.jawiki: マーガレット・ミード
nodes.summary: Margaret Mead studied at Barnard College and Columbia University under Franz Boas. Her major career posts included roles at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia University (1954–1978), Fordham University (1968–1970), and The New School (circa 1954–1978).

nodes.label: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ヤーコプ・マリア・デ・ホロート
nodes.summary: Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854–1921) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, later serving as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

nodes.label: Xiaoting Wei
nodes.summary: Xiaoting Wei works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under supervisor Kathy Ku Cheng Mei, attested in 2004.

nodes.label: Jinshi Fan
nodes.summary: Jinshi Fan works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Su Bai (~1958–1963). She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014) and has held a post at Lanzhou University as professor and doctoral supervisor.

nodes.label: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan
nodes.summary: Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teacher and guide Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

nodes.label: Bhajagovinda Ghosh
nodes.summary: Bhajagovinda Ghosh was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and an Editorial Board Member of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Martin Collcutt
nodes.jawiki: マーティン・コルカット
nodes.summary: Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fitzwilliam College, the University of Cambridge, and Harvard (Ph.D.). He taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo before serving at Princeton University from 1975 to 2015.

nodes.label: Andrew Quintman
nodes.summary: Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Masaharu Imai
nodes.summary: Masaharu Imai is a Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology scholar who earned his doctorate from Tokyo University of Education. He held appointments at Ibaraki University and the University of Tsukuba, along with numerous international visiting professorships.

nodes.label: Juhn Y. Ahn
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Ahn earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. He served as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Bstan 'dzin zla grags chos kyi rgyal mtshan
Lobsang Yongdan
nodes.summary: Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge by 2014 under Hildegard Diemberger, later holding postdoctoral posts at MPIWG and the University of Bonn.
