Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Berlin

nodes.label: Fernando Jose Benetti
nodes.summary: Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nalanda University and completed doctoral work supervised by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

nodes.label: William H. Nienhauser, Jr.
nodes.summary: William H. Nienhauser, Jr. (b. 1943) is a Sinologist educated at Indiana University and Bonn, studying under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He served as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, holding the Halls-Bascom chair from 1995.

nodes.label: Kristina Myrvold
nodes.summary: Kristina Myrvold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She was a doctoral candidate and editor at Lund University (attested 2005, 2008) and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Olle Qvarnström
nodes.summary: Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen, and under Tord Olsson; he held a post at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

nodes.label: Gurinder Singh Mann
nodes.summary: Gurinder Singh Mann is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Kent, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught English at Baring Union Christian College, religion at Columbia, and held a Sikh Studies chair at UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: University of Bergen
variants: Department of Social Anthropology, University of Bergen

nodes.label: Anne Hardgrove
nodes.summary: Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1993–1999), and held an editorial board post at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

nodes.id: I:University of Texas at San Antonio
nodes.label: University of Texas at San Antonio
variants: University of Texas at San Antonio

nodes.label: Paul Copp
nodes.summary: Paul Copp specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and earned his Ph.D. at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser (attested 2005), later holding posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Ch'ing-mao Cheng
nodes.summary: Ch'ing-mao Cheng (1933–2025) was a sinologist and japanologist who earned degrees from National Taiwan University and Princeton. He held posts at UC Berkeley, UMass Amherst as Chair of Asian Languages and Literatures, and founded National Dong Hwa University.

nodes.label: Donald E. Gjertson
nodes.summary: Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1969–1975) under Akira Takeda and John Ching-yu Wang, and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2010).

nodes.label: Stephen Batchelor
nodes.summary: Stephen Batchelor is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied under Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim. He led Sharpham College from approximately 1992 to 1999 and joined the core faculty of Bodhi College around 2015.

nodes.label: Royall Tyler
nodes.summary: Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology. He studied at Harvard University and Columbia University under Donald Keene. He held teaching posts at Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, and Ohio State, headed the Japan Centre at ANU (1990–2000), and visited Harvard (2001–2002).

nodes.label: Huai-Chin Nan
nodes.summary: Huai-Chin Nan worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the ROC Military Academy, the University of Nanking, and under Huanxian Yuan, later serving as professor at Chinese Culture University (~1963–1975), National Chengchi University, and Fu Jen Catholic University.

nodes.label: Chinese Culture University
variants: College of Chinese Culture Graduate School in Taipei
Institute of Chinese Culture in Taipei
中国文化大学印度研究所

nodes.label: Huynh Kim Lan
nodes.summary: Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where thesis advisers included Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Gareth Fisher
nodes.summary: Gareth Fisher is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed a Ph.D. at the University of Virginia in 2006 and held a post as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

nodes.label: Tel Aviv University
variants: Institute for Advanced Study at Tel Aviv University

nodes.label: Nirupam Chakma
nodes.summary: Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College around 2015, studying under MA supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

nodes.label: Tilak Kariyawasam
nodes.summary: Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Fa Qing
nodes.summary: Fa Qing is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, Ronald Neufeldt, Eliezer Segal, Wayne O. McCready, Xiaojie Yang, and K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Ki-yong Rhi
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

nodes.label: Martin Willson
nodes.summary: Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His education included training under traditional teachers Lama Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

nodes.label: Michael Weiers
nodes.summary: Michael Weiers was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965). He served as professor at Bonn (1972–2003) and honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University (~1996).

nodes.label: Geshe Jampa Tegchok
nodes.summary: Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1992) and as resident teacher at the Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).

nodes.label: Daniel L. Overmyer
nodes.description: Scholar of the history of Chinese popular religions
nodes.summary: Daniel L. Overmyer worked in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Westmar, Garrett-Evangelical, and the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn, Mircea Eliade, and Joseph M. Kitagawa. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (circa 1973–2001).

nodes.label: Dieter B. Kapp
nodes.summary: Dieter B. Kapp specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing his doctorate under Hermann Berger at Heidelberg University. He taught at Heidelberg, held guest professorships in Munich and Berlin, and served as Director of Indology and Tamilistics at Cologne (1990-2006).

nodes.label: Peter James Gilks
nodes.summary: Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University (attested 2010) under John Powers, and studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang as well as with several traditional Tibetan teachers.

nodes.label: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués
nodes.summary: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge in 2016 under Eivind Kahrs, and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design in 2019.

nodes.label: Di Luo
nodes.summary: Di Luo is a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by James Steele for an MA and by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge for a PhD, Luo studied at the University of Southern California (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Bettine Birge
nodes.summary: Bettine Birge is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Wm. Theodore de Bary and Masaaki Sugiyama, earning her Ph.D. from Columbia University, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

nodes.label: Richard von Glahn
nodes.summary: Richard von Glahn is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and served as a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

nodes.label: Tsinghua University
variants: Institute of Guoxue Studies, Tsinghua School

nodes.label: Jeff Watt
nodes.summary: Specializing in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, Jeff Watt studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

nodes.label: Miranda Shaw
nodes.summary: Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi, Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

nodes.label: Justin Shimeld
nodes.summary: Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jeff Malpas
nodes.summary: Philosopher Jeff Malpas earned a BA at the University of Auckland and a PhD at the Australian National University. His career included posts at Murdoch University, the University of New England, and the University of Tasmania, where he became Emeritus Distinguished Professor.

nodes.label: Sonam Thakchoe
nodes.summary: Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) under mentors Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, later taking a post there around 2005.

nodes.label: Barry Kerzin
nodes.image: Barry Kerzin, American Professor of Medicine and Buddhist monk.gif
nodes.summary: Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley and the Keck School of Medicine of USC, and he held posts at the University of Washington, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and The University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Shili Xiong
nodes.summary: Shili Xiong was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the China Institute of Inner Learning under Jian Ouyang in 1920. He held posts at Boone University, Zhejiang University, and as a lecturer at Peking University (1923–1955).

nodes.label: Zongsan Mou
nodes.summary: Zongsan Mou was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University (1927-1933) under Shili Xiong. He taught across several universities before holding major posts at CUHK (~1968-1974) and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1974-1995).

nodes.label: Philip Whalen
nodes.summary: Philip Whalen was active in Buddhist and religious studies. A Reed College graduate who studied under Richard Baker, he served as a visiting poet at Naropa University (~1974), head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984), and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

nodes.label: Karen L. Brock
nodes.summary: Karen L. Brock is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from Princeton University. She served as an assistant professor at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1988) and at the University of Michigan (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Oleg Grabar
nodes.summary: Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (PhD ~1955), and held professorships at Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).

nodes.label: Jörg Heimbel
nodes.summary: Jörg Heimbel is a Tibetologist who studied at Tibet University and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He became a Tibetan lecturer at the University of Hamburg (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Elizabeth English
nodes.summary: Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999 under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson, also studying with Harunaga Isaacson.

nodes.label: Sung Bae Park
nodes.summary: Sung Bae Park (born 1933) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctorate under Lewis Lancaster. He served as an assistant professor at Dongguk University and joined the faculty at Stony Brook University in 1977.

nodes.label: David A. Dilworth
nodes.summary: David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo, and held a post at Stony Brook University around 1970.

nodes.label: Antonio T. de Nicolás
nodes.summary: Antonio T. de Nicolás was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD from Fordham University and served on the faculty at Stony Brook University from circa 1969 to 2000.

nodes.label: Alfred Bloom
variants: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.jawiki: アルフレッド・ブルーム
nodes.summary: Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. After doctoral studies at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held faculty posts at the University of Oregon, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: University at Albany, SUNY
variants: State University of New York at Albany
University at Albany (State University of New York)
University at Albany, State University of New York

nodes.label: Ruben L. F. Habito
nodes.summary: Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikidō Takasaki. He held posts at Sophia, Ryukoku, and Southern Methodist University (1989).

nodes.label: Yutai Ikeda
nodes.summary: Yutai Ikeda (1934–2025) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a position at Otani University and served at Doho University from circa 1972 to 2005, where he became Emeritus Professor.

nodes.label: Chiken Kato
nodes.summary: Chiken Kato (1943–2017) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a professor at Tokyo Polytechnic University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Kenshi Kusano
nodes.summary: Kenshi Kusano specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1980 and served there as a professor from circa 1998 to 2018.

nodes.label: Shunsho Terakawa
nodes.summary: Shunsho Terakawa studied at the University of Tokyo and specialized in Buddhist studies. He later served as an Emeritus Professor at Otani University (~1994–2000).

nodes.label: Michael Jerryson
nodes.summary: Michael Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his undergraduate education at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1994–1998). He taught religious studies at Eckerd College (ca. 2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (ca. 2012–2021).

nodes.label: Daniel W. Kent
nodes.summary: Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia. In 2010, he held instructor posts at the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.

nodes.label: Brian Daizen Victoria
variants: ブライアン・アンドレー・ヴィクトリア
nodes.jawiki: ブライアン・ヴィクトリア
nodes.summary: Brian Daizen Victoria is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history who completed degrees at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple universities. He held academic positions at the University of Auckland, Antioch University (2005–2013), and the University of Adelaide (c. 2003–2015).

nodes.label: Nebraska Wesleyan University
variants: ネブラスカ・ウェズリアン大学

nodes.label: Baruch College
variants: Baruch College, City University of New York

nodes.label: Franz-Karl Ehrhard
nodes.summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard (born 1953) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1998) under Lambert Schmithausen, served at the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993), and was a professor at the University of Munich (2003–2019).

nodes.label: Navina Lamminger
nodes.summary: Navina Lamminger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Munich, where she studied under Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Orna Almogi
nodes.summary: Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and under supervisors David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts with the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and the University of Hamburg (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Stacey Van Vleet
nodes.summary: Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earned degrees from the University of Colorado and Columbia University (PhD), and held an attested post at Columbia in 2013.

nodes.label: Geoffrey Barstow
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Barstow is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and earned degrees from Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia, later becoming an assistant professor at Oregon State University.

nodes.label: Yutaka Yoshida
nodes.summary: Yutaka Yoshida (born 1954) specializes in history/archaeology, Japanology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education, the University of Tokyo, and Hitotsubashi University, later holding posts at Hitotsubashi and Kyoto University.

nodes.label: James Burnell Robinson
nodes.summary: James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and became an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa around 1975.

nodes.label: Cuong T. Mai
nodes.summary: Cuong T. Mai specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from Indiana University under John R. McRae, later serving as an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Reiko Ohnuma
nodes.summary: Reiko Ohnuma works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. attested 1997) under Luis O. Gómez and Padmanabh S. Jaini. She held positions at UT Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

nodes.label: Gereon Kopf
nodes.summary: Gereon Kopf specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Temple University, conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan universities, and served at Luther College and The University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: John C. Maraldo
nodes.summary: John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who served at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.

nodes.label: Seijun Ishii
nodes.summary: Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1977 to 1981 and later served as a professor there around 2000.

nodes.label: Tairyu Tsunoda
nodes.summary: Tairyu Tsunoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and became a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Ruth W. Dunnell
nodes.summary: Ruth W. Dunnell works in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987-1988), and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.

nodes.label: ETH Zurich
variants: Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich (ETHZ)
Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zürich
Swiss Federal Institute of Technology at Zurich

nodes.id: I:Purchase College, State University of New York
nodes.label: Purchase College, State University of New York
variants: Purchase College, State University of New York

nodes.label: Stephen G. Covell
nodes.description: professor of world religions and cultures
nodes.summary: Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone. He held a post at Western Michigan University starting around 2003.

nodes.label: Wendi L. Adamek
nodes.summary: Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (-1998) and held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (associate professor, attested 2018).

nodes.label: Sadajiro Sugiura
nodes.summary: Sadajiro Sugiura (1871–1947) was a philosophy and Indology scholar who studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University.

nodes.label: Bo Jiang
nodes.summary: Bo Jiang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Soochow University
variants: School of Foreign Languages, Soochow University

nodes.label: Mary Evelyn Tucker
nodes.summary: Mary Evelyn Tucker is a scholar of religion, sinology, and Japanology who earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University. She held professorships at Bucknell University (~1989–2006) and Yale University (~2006), and faculty posts at UC Berkeley and Harvard.

nodes.label: Zhiru Shi
nodes.summary: Zhiru Shi is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, having also studied under Donald Harper, Beth Harrison, and Alan E. Bernstein, and served at Pomona College (attested 2007-2014).

nodes.label: Masao Yamaguchi
nodes.summary: Masao Yamaguchi was a scholar of religious studies and other fields. He studied at Tokyo Metropolitan University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1965–1989), University of Shizuoka (1994), and Sapporo University (1997–1999).

nodes.label: Ryoshun Okubo
nodes.summary: Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University (~1974–1985), where he served as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism (~2003–2024), and was attested as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai in 2007.

nodes.label: Phanindra Nath Bose
nodes.description: Bengali historian, writer and professor at Santiniketan

nodes.label: Shashibhusan Dasgupta
nodes.description: Scholar in philosophy, languages and literature, particularly Bengali literature, literary critic, author, theologian
nodes.summary: Shashibhusan Dasgupta worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, where he earned an MA and PhD and served as a lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

nodes.label: Dung Ngoc Duong
nodes.summary: Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD at Boston University under the doctoral supervision of Malcolm David Eckel (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Dudjom Rinpoche
nodes.image: Dudjom Rinpoche with Prince Paljor Namgyal and Maharani Kunzang Dechen Tshomo Namgyal.jpg
nodes.summary: Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jampal Delek Nyima, Min Ling Orgyen Namdrol Gyatso, and Pé Kö Lama Könchok Rabten, and taught numerous students.

nodes.label: Christine Mollier
nodes.summary: Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. She served as a CNRS researcher (1989–1995) and Research Director (attested 2014), and as Numata Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Jacques Giès
nodes.summary: A specialist in sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, Jacques Giès studied at the Académie de la Grande Chaumière, ENSBA, and Paris-Sorbonne under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne and École du Louvre, and served as president of Musée Guimet (2008–2011).

nodes.label: Kōun Yamada
variants: Yamada Koun Zenshin (山田 耕雲, Yamada Kōun)
nodes.summary: Kōun Yamada (1907–1989) was a Buddhist and religious studies master. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he trained under Yasutani and Harada, founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai in 1953, and became the second head of Sanbo Zen in 1970.

nodes.label: Yaroslav Komarovski
nodes.summary: Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes and the University of Virginia, later holding a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Dzongsar Institute
variants: Dzongsar Institute for Advanced Studies of Buddhist Philosophy and Research in Bir, India
Dzongsar Institute of Advanced Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: McDougal
nodes.summary: McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

nodes.label: Kumbum Monastery
variants: クンブム・チャンパーリン寺

nodes.label: Dhivan Thomas Jones
nodes.summary: Dhivan Thomas Jones works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He served as an associate lecturer at Open University (attested 2017) and held a post at the University of Chester (2019).

nodes.label: Shan Shan Zhao
nodes.summary: Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with teachers Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
variants: International Research Consortium of "Fate, Freedom, and Prognostication in East Asia and Europe"
Internationalen Kolleg für Geisteswissenschaftliche Forschung der Universität Erlangen

nodes.label: St Edmund's College
variants: St. Edmunds College, University of Cambridge

nodes.label: Margaret Gouin
nodes.summary: Margaret Gouin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under the doctoral supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Thinh Canh Quang
nodes.summary: Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of the West, where he studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge, supervised by Kottegoda Warnasuriya.

nodes.label: Noa Ronkin
nodes.summary: Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) in 2003 under Richard Gombrich, having also studied under Shlomo Biderman. She has been a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

nodes.label: Patricia Buckley Ebrey
nodes.summary: Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and sinologist educated at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Washington, where she was Professor Emerita of History (1997–2020).

nodes.label: Kate Wharton
nodes.summary: Kate Wharton works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London by 2008 and held an attested post at Birkbeck, University of London, in 2010.

nodes.label: Peter Fenner
nodes.summary: Peter Fenner specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and held a post at Deakin University.

nodes.label: Lindsay G. McCune
nodes.summary: Lindsay G. McCune works in the fields of Tibetology and religious studies. McCune studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas, as attested in 2007, as well as under teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.

nodes.label: Nancy Lin
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Nancy Lin pursued graduate studies at Columbia University and earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, studying under teachers including Bryan J. Cuevas and Michael Hahn.

nodes.label: Hermann Kulke
nodes.summary: Kulke, an Indologist and historian, studied at Freiburg under Hermann Goetz, Madras, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

nodes.label: Werner Sundermann
nodes.summary: Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

nodes.label: Yanling Chen
nodes.summary: Yanling Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi, with Hsing Yun as a traditional teacher (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Agehananda Bharati
nodes.summary: Agehananda Bharati specialized in religious studies and Indology, studying at the University of Vienna. He held teaching posts at several institutions in India and Japan before serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

nodes.label: Ron Leifer
nodes.summary: Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught at Rumtek Monastery (1959, 1967) and served as abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).

nodes.label: Tessa J. Bartholomeusz
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Bartholomeusz studied at the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia (PhD 1991). She taught religious studies at Indiana University Indianapolis (~1991–2001) and Florida State University (1993).

nodes.label: Indiana University Indianapolis
variants: Indiana University Herron School of Art and Design

nodes.label: Krishnanath Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under teachers including Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

nodes.label: Ramaranjan Mukherji
nodes.summary: Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji earned degrees at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as Head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (1956) and later vice chancellor of the University of Burdwan (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati University (~1975–1987).

nodes.label: James Matthew Baskind
nodes.summary: James Matthew Baskind is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa
nodes.summary: Katsuhiro Yoshizawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1969) and served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1999).

nodes.label: Tsuneki Nishiwaki
nodes.summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1971). He held positions at Doshisha University (~1973–1993) and served as professor at Kyoto University (~1993–2007).

nodes.label: Anthony Cerulli
nodes.summary: Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago from 2001 to 2007 and was appointed Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Madison circa 2014.

nodes.label: Chinese Academy of Sciences
variants: 中国科学院哲学社会科学部
中国科学院哲学研究所
中国科学院世界宗教研究所

nodes.label: Pierce Salguero
nodes.description: professor of Asian history and religious studies
nodes.summary: Pierce Salguero is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia and a PhD from Johns Hopkins University (~2010), becoming professor of Asian History and Health Humanities at Penn State Abington (~2010).

nodes.label: Christoph Kleine
nodes.description: German japanologist and religious studies scholar
nodes.summary: Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bukkyo University and the University of Marburg, he held posts at Marburg and Munich before being appointed professor of religious history at Leipzig University in 2008.

nodes.label: Mervin Viggo Hanson
nodes.summary: Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980), where he was supervised by Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.

nodes.label: Kendall R. Marchman
nodes.summary: Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and earned his PhD from the University of Florida in 2015.

nodes.label: Si Ti La
nodes.summary: Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma. They also studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala, U Sajjanasara, and Sayadaw U Sasana.

nodes.label: Osvald Sirén
nodes.summary: Osvald Sirén was an art historian and sinologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Helsinki. He held a professorship at Stockholm University (1908–1923), worked as a conservator at Musée Guimet (1924–1925), and served as keeper at the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

nodes.label: Erik-Jan Zürcher
nodes.summary: Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian who earned his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), the University of Amsterdam (1993–1997), Leiden University (from 1997), and the International Institute of Social History (1990–1999, 2008–2012).

nodes.label: Sōkō Morinaga
nodes.summary: Sōkō Morinaga (1925–1995) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Toyama High School and Daitoku-ji under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto. He served as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and head priest at Daiju-in (~1963–1995).

nodes.label: City College of New York
variants: College of the City of New York
City College in New York City

nodes.label: Ngawang Wangyal
nodes.summary: Ngawang Wangyal (1901–1983) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a geshe degree at Drepung Monastery, studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, founded the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center and the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, and taught at Columbia University (~1962–1970).

nodes.label: Joseph Loizzo
nodes.summary: Joseph Loizzo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman. He served as a visiting scholar at Columbia University and founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science
variants: Nalanda Institute for Meditation and Healing

nodes.label: Trijang Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trijang Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo. He served as a teacher at Ganden Shartse Monastery and taught students including Tenzin Gyatso.

nodes.label: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima
variants: Sde gzhung Rin po che, Kun dga' bstan pa'i nyi ma
デシュン・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Buddhist scholars - Dezhung Rinpoche III seated on a stool, Chris Wilkinson, student seated at the feet of his lama, wearing Buddhist robes, malas, likely Seattle, Washington, USA (16134833232) (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including Gaton Ngawang Lekpa and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse. He was a research project participant at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.

nodes.label: Gaton Ngawang Lekpa
nodes.summary: Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

nodes.label: Culadasa
nodes.summary: Culadasa (1944–2021) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu, taught Matthew Immergut, and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Matthew Immergut
nodes.summary: Matthew Immergut is a scholar of religious studies and sociology who studied under Culadasa. Attested in 2011, he served as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

nodes.label: Namgyal Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Namgyal Rinpoche studied at the University of Michigan, Jarvis Baptist Seminary, and under teachers including Sayadaw U Thila Wunta and the 16th Karmapa. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

nodes.label: Sun-Ah Choi
nodes.summary: Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago, where she studied under Juhyung Rhi, Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

nodes.label: Robert S. Nelson
nodes.summary: A historian and archaeologist, Nelson studied at Rice University and New York University. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) before taking a post at Yale University circa 2005.

nodes.label: Jaś Elsner
nodes.summary: Jaś Elsner is a scholar of archaeology, art history, and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, London, and Harvard, his career includes fellowships at Cambridge and posts at the Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, and the University of Oxford as professor.

nodes.label: Aden Kumler
nodes.summary: Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at Chicago, Toronto, Harvard (PhD), and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (2007–2020) before becoming professor at the University of Basel in 2020.

nodes.label: Tainan National University of the Arts
Carl Gustav Jung
nodes.jawiki: カール・グスタフ・ユング
nodes.summary: Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) studied medicine at the University of Basel (1895–1900). A scholar of psychology and religious studies, he held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1914), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

nodes.label: Erwin Rousselle
nodes.summary: Erwin Rousselle worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich, Heidelberg, Freiburg, Berlin, Darmstadt, and Frankfurt under teachers including Max Walleser. He held posts at Peking University, Yenching University, Tsinghua University, Frankfurt, and the China-Institut Frankfurt.

nodes.label: Richard Wilhelm
nodes.summary: Sinologist Richard Wilhelm was educated at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and the University of Tübingen (~1891–1895). He served as a guest professor at Peking University in 1923 and held the chair of Sinology at Goethe University Frankfurt starting in 1924, founding the institution in 1925.

nodes.label: Joseph Campbell
variants: ジョーゼフ・キャンベル
nodes.image: Joseph Campbell at Feathered Pipe Ranch, Montana (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョーゼフ・キャンベル
nodes.summary: Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar educated at Canterbury School, Dartmouth College, Columbia University, and the universities of Paris and Munich. He taught at Canterbury School (1933) and was a faculty member at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.

nodes.label: David L. Gosling
nodes.summary: David L. Gosling is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge, in 1992 and had an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

Academy of Social Science of Shanghai

variants: Académie des Sciences Sociales de Chengdu

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Achard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the CNRS.

nodes.label: Ramin Etesami
nodes.summary: Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College around 2015, where he was supervised by Geshe Lozang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.

nodes.label: Richard J. Davidson
nodes.image: Rajesh Kasturirangan at Mind and Life.jpg
nodes.summary: Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University and Harvard University. He held academic positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as a psychology professor there from 2001 to 2017.

nodes.label: Benjamin Brose
nodes.description: American cultural historian of religion in China
nodes.summary: Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. Around 2009 to 2016, he served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Erik J. Hammerstrom
nodes.summary: Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University and served as an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Michelle C. Wang
nodes.summary: Michelle C. Wang specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her doctorate under Eugene Y. Wang (~2002–2008) and was appointed assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University around 2012.

nodes.label: Randy J. LaPolla
nodes.summary: Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as a professor at City University of Hong Kong and held a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai.

nodes.label: Tak Pui Sze
nodes.summary: Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen.

nodes.label: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh
nodes.summary: Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall.

nodes.label: Brigitte Marschall
nodes.summary: Brigitte Marschall earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she later held a post as professor (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Guo Jun
nodes.summary: Guo Jun works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, under Sheng Yen, Song Nian, and Qinyin, and served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).

nodes.label: George Lakoff
nodes.native: ジョージ・P・レイコフ
variants: ジョージ・P・レイコフ
nodes.summary: George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and Indiana University. He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969), was a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016), and founded the Rockridge Institute in 2003.

nodes.label: Mark Johnson
nodes.jawiki: マーク・ジョンソン (哲学者)

nodes.label: Glenn Wallis
nodes.summary: Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

nodes.label: Alexander Berzin
nodes.summary: Alexander Berzin is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He co-founded the translation bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and serves on advisory boards in Germany and Thailand.

nodes.label: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Ganden Monastery. He held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery and taught Tenzin Gyatso, Alexander Berzin, and Thubten Chodron.

International Organizing Committee for the UN Day of Vesak

nodes.label: Akira Takeda
nodes.summary: Akira Takeda was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1959) under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1959–1968), the University of Tokyo (assistant 1961, professor 1965–1991), and Meikai University.

nodes.id: I:School of Youth for Social Service
nodes.label: School of Youth for Social Service
variants: School of Youth for Social Service

nodes.label: Charles Taliaferro
nodes.summary: Charles Taliaferro is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University, later serving as a professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2022).

nodes.label: Charlene E. Makley
nodes.summary: Charlene E. Makley is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (1999) under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She serves as associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

nodes.label: Roy Rappaport
nodes.summary: Roy Rappaport (1926–1997) was a religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and past president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

nodes.label: Marco Walther
nodes.summary: Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich (attested 2017) under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and also studied under Khenpo Dondrup Namgyal.

nodes.label: Jamie Hubbard
nodes.summary: Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. In 2016, he was attested as an endowed professor at Smith College.

nodes.label: Becket Institute
variants: Becket Institute, St Hugh's College, Oxford
Becket Institute at St. Hugh's College, Oxford
Becket Institute, St. Hugh's College, Oxford

nodes.label: Takayasu Higuchi
nodes.summary: Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) studied at Kyoto University and worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1968–1983) and directed the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Sen-oku Hakuko Kan, and the Institute of Silk Road Studies.

nodes.label: P. R. Srinivasan
nodes.description: Indian epigraphist, archaeologist and art historian

nodes.label: John Woodroffe
nodes.summary: John Woodroffe was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888). He served as a judge at the Calcutta High Court, Tagore Law Professor at the University of Calcutta, and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford.

nodes.label: Eishoji Zen Center
variants: Eishoji Zen training and practice facility

nodes.label: Bingtao Ma
nodes.summary: Bingtao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from Peking University in 2008 and completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Cécile Ducher
nodes.summary: Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she subsequently held an appointment as a research fellow.

nodes.label: Nicholas Justin Allen
nodes.summary: Nicholas Justin Allen worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Oxford, including under doctoral supervisor Rodney Needham, and at SOAS. He lectured at Durham (1972–1976) and Oxford (from 1976), later serving as Reader at Wolfson College.

nodes.label: Charles Taylor
nodes.jawiki: チャールズ・マーグレイヴ・テイラー
nodes.summary: Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University, and Balliol College, Oxford. His career includes posts at McGill University (~1961–1998), the Université de Montréal (~1962–1971), and Northwestern University (~2002–2014).

nodes.label: Zhiru Ng
nodes.summary: Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello.

nodes.label: Michel Clasquin-Johnson
nodes.description: Professor of Religious Studies at the University of South Africa
nodes.summary: Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his studies and doctoral thesis at the University of South Africa (~1991–1999), where he also held an academic post beginning in 1990.

nodes.label: Bryan W. Van Norden
nodes.summary: Bryan W. Van Norden is a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Stanford University from ~1985 to 1991. Around 1996, he became a professor at Vassar College in Philosophy and Chinese & Japanese.

nodes.label: Chi-wah Chan
nodes.summary: Chi-wah Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, earning a Ph.D. at UCLA in 1993, and served as a teaching assistant at CUHK.

nodes.label: Barend Jan Terwiel
nodes.summary: Barend Jan Terwiel works in history/archaeology and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University, and held posts at the ANU, the University of Munich, the University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.

nodes.label: Patrice Ladwig
nodes.summary: Patrice Ladwig works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Münster, the University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, later holding posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
variants: Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology
Max Planck Institute of Social Anthropology

nodes.label: Ingmar Heise
nodes.summary: Ingmar Heise works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University (completed by 2005) and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

nodes.label: G. C. Nayak
nodes.summary: G. C. Nayak was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study from circa 1992 to 1994 and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 1996.

nodes.label: Peter D. Hershock
nodes.summary: Peter D. Hershock (born 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and under Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim, later directing the Asian Studies Development Program at the East-West Center (attested 2007–2013).

nodes.label: Stephen J. Laumakis
nodes.summary: Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Aquinas Scholars Honors Program at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2013).

nodes.label: British Academy
variants: British Academy Committee for Southeast Asian Studies

nodes.label: Christopher Ives
nodes.summary: Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (circa 1989–2000) and later became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College.

nodes.label: Sharon J. Roe
nodes.summary: Sharon J. Roe is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Yozo Taniyama
nodes.summary: Yozo Taniyama is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1991-1996). He held posts at Tohoku University (~2011), St. Thomas University, Japan (~2008-2010), International Buddhist University, and Sophia University.

nodes.label: Dickwela Piyananda
nodes.summary: Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Catholic University of America, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Siegfried A. Schulz.

nodes.label: Christian Bernert
nodes.summary: Christian Bernert is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he completed his Magister degree under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Hugh J. Silverman
nodes.summary: Hugh J. Silverman (1945–2013) was a philosopher who earned his doctorate at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He became a professor at Stony Brook University in 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

nodes.label: Heeraman Tiwari
nodes.summary: Heeraman Tiwari (b. 1961), an Indology and philosophy scholar, studied at Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He has held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1996), Heidelberg (2011–2012), and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014–2015).

nodes.label: Lang Chen
nodes.summary: Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed a PhD at Yale University, where she was supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Matthew B. Orsborn
nodes.summary: Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, alongside traditional studies under Hsing Yun and Huishang.

nodes.label: Richard Barron
nodes.summary: Richard Barron works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

nodes.label: Sogyal Rinpoche
variants: ソギャル・リンポチェ
nodes.description: Tibetan Dzogchen lama of the Nyingma tradition
nodes.summary: Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at the University of Delhi, Cambridge, and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse. He founded Rigpa in 1975.

nodes.label: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje
nodes.summary: Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Kathok and Nyoshul monasteries and under teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

nodes.label: Tuyet Tam Thi Pham
nodes.summary: Tuyet Tam Thi Pham is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where she studied under Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

nodes.label: Phra Brahmapundit
nodes.native: พระพรหมบัณฑิต
nodes.summary: Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997-2018), Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996), and President of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004).

nodes.label: Hansa Dhammahaso
nodes.summary: Hansa Dhammahaso works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, he was attested as Director at the International Buddhist Studies College and as director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Erica Baffelli
nodes.description: professor of Japanese studies in the UK
nodes.summary: Specializing in Japanology and religious studies, Baffelli studied under Massimo Raveri (~2002–2006). She held academic posts at the University of Otago (~2009–2013) and the University of Manchester (~2013, 2018).

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for Human Development
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for Human Development
variants: Max Planck Institute for Human Development

nodes.label: Lara Braitstein
nodes.summary: Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes.

nodes.label: Markus Viehbeck
nodes.summary: Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (-2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and held positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) and Heidelberg University.

nodes.label: David R. Kinsley
nodes.summary: David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago. He held a faculty post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

nodes.label: Liang Cai
nodes.summary: Liang Cai works in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held an attested post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas in 2014.

nodes.label: Kenneth Doo Young Lee
nodes.summary: Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University, attested in 2007.

nodes.label: D. Phillip Stanley
nodes.summary: D. Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano at the University of Virginia and served as an associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (born 1965), working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under Dilgo Khyentse and others. He directed the Nitartha Institute and served at Kamalashila Institute.

nodes.label: W. F. Jayasuriya
nodes.summary: W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963) and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

nodes.label: Sister Vajirā
nodes.summary: Sister Vajirā (1928–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Paul Debes and traditional teacher Narada Maha Thera (1955).

nodes.label: Victoria Sujata
nodes.summary: Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

nodes.label: Beata Grant
nodes.summary: Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. at Stanford University, she held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and served as Associate Professor at Washington University in St. Louis.

nodes.label: Weiru Guan
nodes.summary: Weiru Guan is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Sayadaw U Silananda
nodes.summary: Sayadaw U Silananda (1927–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw U Pannavanta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at University College, Colombo. He served as abbot at multiple monasteries, Spiritual Director of the Theravada Buddhist Society of America (1979–2005), and ITBMU Chancellor (1999).

nodes.label: Mahasi Sayadaw
nodes.native: မဟာစည်ဆရာတော်
nodes.summary: Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Mingun Jetawun Sayadaw U Narada, among others. He was Abbot at Mawlamyine Monastery (1941) and resident teacher/meditation instructor at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha from 1947.

nodes.label: Atithokdayone Pali University
variants: Atithokdāyone Pali University in Shwegu Taik Monastery

nodes.label: V. Venkatachalam
nodes.summary: V. Venkatachalam (1925–2002) was an Indologist educated at Madras and Nagpur universities. He directed the Scindia Oriental Research Institute and the Bhogilal Leherchand Institute of Indology, served as vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and chaired the ICPR.

nodes.label: Edo Shonin
nodes.summary: Edo Shonin works in Buddhist studies and psychology. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.label: William Van Gordon
nodes.summary: William Van Gordon is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Attested in 2015, he worked as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

nodes.id: I:Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
nodes.label: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research
variants: Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research

nodes.label: Nirbhay N. Singh
nodes.summary: Nirbhay N. Singh works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University.

nodes.label: Mark D. Griffiths
nodes.summary: Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford and the University of Exeter (PhD 1987–1990). He lectured at the Workers' Educational Association and the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) before serving at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

nodes.label: Charles Gabriel Seligman
nodes.summary: Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. Working in history and archaeology, he held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

nodes.label: James C. Dobbins
nodes.summary: James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies, japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Yale University in 1984 and served as the Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College.

nodes.label: Francis H. Cook
nodes.summary: Francis H. Cook (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1991) and chaired the Numata Center in 1999.

nodes.label: Taitetsu Unno
nodes.summary: Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo (~1951–1968) and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).

nodes.label: Joshua Cutler
nodes.summary: Joshua Cutler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ngawang Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Anna Sawerthal
nodes.summary: Anna Sawerthal is a scholar in Tibetology. She earned an MA at the University of Vienna, supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and completed her PhD at Heidelberg University under doctoral supervisors Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer.

nodes.label: Lauran Hartley
nodes.summary: Lauran Hartley is a scholar of Tibetology. She has held positions as an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University, visiting assistant professor at Indiana University, teacher at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and consultant and editor at Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Ann Appleby Hazlewood
nodes.summary: Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Master of Arts degree at the Australian National University (attested 1983) under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.

nodes.label: Nika Jovic
nodes.summary: Nika Jovic is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Magistra der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Géza Bethlenfalvy.

nodes.label: Conor Roddy
nodes.summary: Conor Roddy is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Kathleen M. Higgins (attested 2011), also studying under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

nodes.label: Kathleen M. Higgins
nodes.summary: Kathleen M. Higgins is a philosopher. She was a resident scholar at the Bellagio Center in 1993, a visiting fellow at the Australian National University in 1997, and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2012).

nodes.label: John W. Pettit
nodes.summary: John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, did doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Ashok Gangadean, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

nodes.label: Haverford College
variants: Margaret Gest Center for the Cross-Cultural Study of Religion at Haverford

nodes.label: Ashok Gangadean
nodes.summary: Ashok Gangadean is a philosopher who completed his PhD at Brandeis University. In 1981, he was appointed Margaret Gest Professor of Global Philosophy at Haverford College, and he founded the Global Dialogue Institute.

nodes.label: Lal Mani Joshi
nodes.summary: Lal Mani Joshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under Govind Chandra Pande, later holding posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, Haverford, Amherst, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Drubwang Shakya Shri, and later taught John W. Pettit.

nodes.label: New College of Florida
variants: New College of the University of South Florida

nodes.label: Rongdao Lai
nodes.summary: Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at McGill University (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisors G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

nodes.label: Robin D. S. Yates
nodes.summary: Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar in sinology and archaeology who completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980). Around 1990, he was appointed to a James McGill Professorship at McGill University.

nodes.label: Zhenhua
nodes.summary: Zhenhua was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist Institute in 1947 and under Yin Shun in 1952. Zhenhua served as a manager at the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Robert Baker Aitken
nodes.summary: Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, UC Berkeley, Ryutaku-ji, and under numerous Zen teachers. He held posts at Besant Hill School, East-West Center, and University of Hawaiʻi.

nodes.label: Bruno Dagens
nodes.summary: Bruno Dagens, a scholar of archaeology and Indology, studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, UCLouvain, the French Institute of Pondicherry, KU Leuven (~1977–1986), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).

nodes.label: Constance Powell Chin
nodes.summary: Constance Powell Chin works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She earned a Master's degree at San Jose State University by 2012 and studied under Christian Luczanits.

nodes.label: Benjamin Wood
nodes.summary: Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett, and studied under Shayne Clarke, Thupten Champa, and traditional teacher Khenpo Kunga Sherab.

nodes.label: Donald Keene
nodes.summary: Donald Keene (1922–2019) was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University (~1938–1951) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard University (~1946–1947). He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

nodes.label: Kathleen M. Erndl
nodes.summary: Kathleen M. Erndl specialized in Indology and religious studies. She held academic posts at DePauw University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

nodes.label: D. Dennis Hudson
nodes.summary: D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. From approximately 1970 to 2004, he taught at Smith College as a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies.

nodes.label: Dominique-Sila Khan
nodes.summary: Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University from circa 1990 to 1993. She was attested as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies in 2000.

nodes.label: June McDaniel
nodes.summary: June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

nodes.label: Yu-Chen Tsui
nodes.summary: Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's study at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü. Tsui also studied under doctoral supervisor Natasha Heller (attested 2018) and traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Dermott Walsh
nodes.summary: Dermott Walsh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a BA at Trinity College Dublin (-2003), an MA at Leiden University (-2009), and a PhD at UCLA (-2018) under the supervision of William M. Bodiford.

nodes.label: C. D. Sebastian
nodes.summary: C. D. Sebastian is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and indology who earned his PhD from Banaras Hindu University. Having studied with Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, and Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, he became Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Gavin D'Costa
nodes.summary: Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies. After studying at the universities of Birmingham and Cambridge, he taught at the West London Institute of Higher Education and held the post of Professor of Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol from 1993.

nodes.label: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee
nodes.summary: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti, earning his BA, MA, and PhD. He was a professor and department head at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and Banaras Hindu University (1963–1985).

nodes.label: Dennis A. Johnson
nodes.summary: Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Hiroko Kawanami
nodes.summary: Hiroko Kawanami works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott, and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

nodes.label: Alfred Gell
nodes.summary: Gell studied at Cambridge under Edmund Leach and completed his Ph.D. at the LSE. He lectured at the University of Sussex (~1972–1974), Australian National University (1974), and London School of Economics (1979), becoming a British Academy Fellow.

nodes.label: John Okell
nodes.summary: John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London from 1959 to 1999.

nodes.label: Sunhee Kim
nodes.summary: Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the doctoral supervision of Phillip Zarrilli.

nodes.label: Phillip Zarrilli
nodes.summary: Phillip Zarrilli was a scholar in Indology and theatre. He served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1979 to 2003 and subsequently held a post at the University of Exeter from approximately 2003 to 2020.

nodes.label: Nancy McCagney
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, Nancy McCagney studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and Ninian Smart. She held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

nodes.label: Jeong-Eun Kim
nodes.summary: Jeong-Eun Kim specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London in 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

nodes.label: Giovanni Verardi
nodes.summary: Giovanni Verardi (born 1947) works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities. His career includes posts at Ca' Foscari (1972–1987), Bologna (1981–1987), and a professorship at Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Aoyagi
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Aoyagi is a linguist who studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1993–1998). He served as a professor at Nanzan University (~2007).

nodes.label: Antonio Terrone
nodes.summary: Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as a scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

nodes.label: Alak Zenkar Rinpoche Thupten Nyima
variants: A lags gzan dkar rin po che thub bstan nyi ma

nodes.label: Sarah H. Jacoby
nodes.summary: Sarah H. Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Yale University (~1995–1999) and the University of Virginia (~2000–2007). She has held academic posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

nodes.label: Royal University of Bhutan
variants: Institute of Language and Cultural Studies, Royal University of Bhutan
Institute of Language and Cultural Studies, Semtokha
College of Language and Culture Studies (CLCS), Royal University of Bhutan

nodes.label: Somboon Watana
nodes.summary: Somboon Watana works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Panjab University in 1999, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.

nodes.label: Bhuvan Chandel
nodes.summary: Bhuvan Chandel is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She served as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1999–2004) and held a professorship at Panjab University (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Tulku Sherdor
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tulku Sherdor studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia. He studied under Jeffrey Hopkins and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Yuko Matsuda
nodes.summary: Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Natalie Gummer
nodes.summary: Natalie Gummer works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested at Harvard University in 2001, she became a professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

nodes.id: I:Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture
nodes.label: Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture
variants: Thomas Burke Memorial Washington State Museum, University of Washington

nodes.label: Wolfram Eberhard
nodes.summary: Wolfram Eberhard worked in Sinology and history. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Seminar for Oriental Languages, taught in China and at Ankara University (1937–1948), and served as Professor of Sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).

nodes.label: Barbara Gerke
nodes.summary: Barbara Gerke is a Tibetologist who earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held research posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (2011–2015), CSDS, and the University of Oxford (attested 2017).

nodes.id: I:Centre for the Study of Developing Societies
nodes.label: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies
variants: Centre for the Study of Developing Societies

nodes.label: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt
nodes.summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Erlangen-Nürnberg, Bonn, and Marburg, she served as a visiting professor at the University of Vienna (~2005) and as Privatdozentin at the University of Marburg (2009).

nodes.label: Huidi Zeng
nodes.summary: Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Yi-hsun Huang
nodes.summary: Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Huang earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner and later taught Huidi Zeng.

variants: Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions
Institute for Advanced Studies in World Religions
Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions, New York

nodes.label: Alexander Kabanoff
nodes.summary: Alexander Kabanoff was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Phra Medhidhammaporn
nodes.native: พระเมธีธรรมาภรณ์
nodes.summary: Phra Medhidhammaporn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi by 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

nodes.label: David Azzopardi
nodes.summary: David Azzopardi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied for his PhD at SOAS University of London under the doctoral supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

nodes.label: János Szerb
nodes.summary: János Szerb was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University, he held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (around 1985–1988).

nodes.label: Kurt Tropper
nodes.summary: Kurt Tropper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, later holding posts as a Vertragsassistent at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ñāṇavīra Thera studied at Magdalene College and under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1950). He previously served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

nodes.label: Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa
