Pælæne Siri Vajiranana Maha Nayaka Thera

nodes.label: Heng Sure
nodes.summary: Heng Sure is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua, he has taught at the Graduate Theological Union, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and Bond University.

nodes.label: Edmond Yee
nodes.summary: Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculty at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from circa 1986 to 2008.

nodes.label: Hsuan Hua
nodes.summary: Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies and religious studies master who studied under Chang Chih and Hsu Yun. He founded the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, Buddhist Text Translation Society, and served as Abbot of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas (~1976–1995).

nodes.label: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan
nodes.summary: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.

nodes.label: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle
nodes.summary: Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed doctoral research under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994). He held an academic post at the University of Sydney.

nodes.label: Ministry of Education
variants: 文部省芸術局古文書課

nodes.label: Chien-hsing Ho
nodes.summary: Chien-hsing Ho is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held positions as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Charles B. Jones
nodes.summary: Charles B. Jones is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and served as Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

nodes.label: Technical University of Berlin
variants: ベルリンのシャルロッテンブルク工科大学

nodes.label: David Sneath
nodes.summary: David Sneath works in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge, held a British Academy Postdoctoral Research Fellowship at the University of Oxford, and served as a Director at Cambridge from 2000 to 2009.

nodes.label: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology
variants: Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: Michael Wenger
nodes.summary: Michael Wenger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at The New School and studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984–2012) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

nodes.label: Ralph Abraham
nodes.summary: Ralph Abraham worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, and the University of California, Santa Cruz, where he became professor in 1980.

nodes.label: Sisir Roy
nodes.summary: Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He held a professorship at the Indian Statistical Institute and a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, both attested in 2009.

nodes.label: National Institute of Advanced Studies
variants: National Institute of Advanced Studies, Bangalore

nodes.label: Ajahn Brahm
nodes.summary: Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He studied at the University of Cambridge and trained under Boonman Poonsuwan and Ajahn Chah. He has served as the abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery since ~1983.

nodes.label: Boonman Poonsuwan
nodes.native: บุญมั่น พูนสุวรรณ

nodes.label: Terese Tse Bartholomew
nodes.summary: Active in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology, Bartholomew earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She held posts at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, including Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art (attested 2001–2003).

nodes.label: International Association of Shin Buddhist Studies

nodes.label: Ryan Anningson
nodes.summary: Ryan Anningson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and completed his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Amy Heller
nodes.summary: Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. from the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She has held posts at the CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS University of London, and INALCO.

nodes.label: Mireille Helffer
nodes.summary: Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) was a Tibetologist and researcher. She served as Chargé de Recherche at the CNRS from circa 1967 to 1993 and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

nodes.label: Nawang Tsering Shakspo
nodes.summary: Nawang Tsering Shakspo (born 1952) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).

variants: Gomang College of the Gelugpa Drepung monastic university
Gomang College of Drepung Monastic University

nodes.label: Chien Y. Hsu
nodes.summary: Chien Y. Hsu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua and under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple.

nodes.label: Joseph D. Markowski
nodes.summary: Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Peter Kornicki
nodes.summary: Peter Kornicki works in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford and Tokyo, he taught at the University of Tasmania and Kyoto University before serving at the University of Cambridge (~1985–2017) and Robinson College.

nodes.label: Rosemary Radford Ruether
nodes.summary: Rosemary Radford Ruether (1936–2022) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

nodes.label: E. W. Adikaram
nodes.summary: E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he was principal at Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

nodes.label: Arthur Philip McKeown
nodes.summary: Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Diana L. Eck, Parimal G. Patil, and Palri Sangye.

nodes.label: Nathan W. Hill
nodes.summary: Nathan W. Hill (born 1979), a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, studied at Harvard University. He was a reader at SOAS University of London (~2008–2019) and became the Sam Lam Professor in Chinese Studies at Trinity College Dublin in 2021.

nodes.label: Cameron David Warner
nodes.summary: Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Harvard University, studying under Yudru Tsomu. He has held academic posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.

nodes.label: Polly Young-Eisendrath
nodes.summary: Polly Young-Eisendrath is a psychologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis (PhD ~1980). In 1994, she was appointed clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Moriya Okano
nodes.summary: Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has been affiliated with Musashino University and served as director of the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies.

nodes.id: I:Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies
nodes.label: Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies
variants: Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies

nodes.label: Yasuo Deguchi
nodes.summary: Yasuo Deguchi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having completed his doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1991–1996). He held academic posts at Nagoya Institute of Technology, Kyoto University (2002–2025), and ZEN University (2025), and founded the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy.

nodes.label: Constance Kassor
nodes.summary: Constance Kassor works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned a BA from Smith College and a PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, also studying with Jay L. Garfield and Ngawang Jorden, and joined Smith's faculty.

nodes.label: Karin Meyers
nodes.summary: Karin Meyers works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and held a post at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eyal Aviv
nodes.summary: Eyal Aviv specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

nodes.label: Annette Baier
nodes.summary: Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1947–1952) and earned a PhD from Somerville College, Oxford (1952). She held faculty posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

nodes.label: Wilfrid Sellars
variants: ウィルフリド・ストーカー・セラーズ
nodes.jawiki: ウィルフリド・セラーズ
nodes.summary: Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale (1958–1963), and held a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

nodes.label: Zuicho Tachibana
nodes.summary: Zuicho Tachibana was a researcher in history/archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kōzui Ōtani (~1903) and Edward Denison Ross (~1910-1912).

nodes.label: Ines Konczak-Nagel
nodes.summary: Ines Konczak-Nagel is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University (2012) and as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums.

nodes.label: Angela Falco Howard
nodes.summary: Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed her doctorate at New York University under Alexander C. Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and served as a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Giuseppe Vignato
nodes.summary: Giuseppe Vignato works in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held an affiliation there attested in 2017.

nodes.label: Su Bai
nodes.summary: Su Bai (1922–2018) was a Chinese archaeologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under teachers including Yongtong Tang and Rong Geng, and served as a professor at Peking University from 1948 to 2004.

nodes.label: Shichang Ma
nodes.summary: Shichang Ma was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He served as a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in Peking University's Archaeology Department beginning in 1982.

nodes.label: Max Oidtmann
nodes.summary: Max Oidtmann specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Tibetology, having studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott. He held posts at Georgetown University in Qatar (2013–2021), Georgetown University (~2014–2020), and the University of Munich (~2020).

nodes.label: Gustav Haloun
nodes.summary: A sinologist, Gustav Haloun studied at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Charles University. He held positions at Halle, Göttingen (1931–1938), and served as Chair of Chinese Language and History at the University of Cambridge (1938–1951).

nodes.label: Jotika Khur-Yearn
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Jotika Khur-Yearn earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Rangama Chandawimala
nodes.summary: Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied traditionally under Attaragama Gnanawimala. He earned a PhD from The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin and co-supervisor Kakkapalliye Anuruddha Thera.

nodes.label: Gregory Price Grieve
nodes.summary: Gregory Price Grieve is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

nodes.label: Michael S. Drummond
nodes.summary: Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Michel Bitbol
nodes.summary: Michel Bitbol is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Paris Diderot University (completed 1985) and under Pierre Mills. He held positions at CNRS (~1990), IHPST (~1990–2009), and École Normale Supérieure (~2010).

nodes.label: Sharpham College
variants: Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry
Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry

nodes.label: Owen Flanagan
nodes.summary: Owen Flanagan is a philosopher working in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Archbishop Stepinac High School, Fordham University, and Boston University, and became a Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

nodes.label: Andrew Olendzki
nodes.summary: Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Insight Meditation Society
variants: Insight Meditation Society in Barre, Massachusetts

nodes.label: Fazun
nodes.summary: Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and under Taixu and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and held leadership roles at the Buddhist Academy of China.

nodes.label: Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute
variants: Institut d'études du bouddhisme sino-tibétain (Hanzang jiaoli yuan)
Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (Hanzang Jiaoliyuan 漢藏教理院)

nodes.label: Tzung-Kuen Wen
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Tzung-Kuen Wen earned a PhD at the University of Queensland under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He also studied under Yang-zhu Xu, Nandasiri Sayadaw, and Sayadaw U Pandita, and lectured at Fuyan Buddhist Institute.

nodes.label: Robert Anthony Orsi
nodes.summary: Robert Anthony Orsi is a religious studies and history scholar who studied at Trinity College and Yale University. He held posts at Fordham, Indiana University, Harvard (2001–2007), Northwestern University (~2007), and the University of Notre Dame (2020–2021).

nodes.label: Clara Sue Kidwell
nodes.description: Native American academic scholar, historian, feminist
nodes.summary: Clara Sue Kidwell (1941–2025) studied at the University of Oklahoma (PhD ~1970). A historian, she held posts at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), Oklahoma (1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

nodes.label: Karen McCarthy Brown
nodes.summary: Karen McCarthy Brown (1942-2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She held a post at Temple (~1971-1976) and served as professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976-2009).

nodes.label: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri
nodes.summary: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nalanda College, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Toronto. He founded and served as president of the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: Christopher Hatchell
nodes.summary: Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under the mentorship of David Germano.

nodes.label: Jason Matthew McCombs
nodes.summary: Jason Matthew McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen, where he was attested as a lecturer in 2014.

nodes.label: Lobsang Tenpa
nodes.summary: Lobsang Tenpa is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Tenpa earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

nodes.label: Jigmeth Junu
nodes.summary: Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under Yongdong Shi, while also studying under traditional teacher Huixian (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Miri Albahari
nodes.summary: Miri Albahari is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at UNSW and the University of Western Australia.

nodes.label: University of New South Wales
variants: The University of New South Wales

nodes.label: Martin Heidegger
variants: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.jawiki: マルティン・ハイデッガー
nodes.summary: Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1928–1958) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

nodes.label: Christian Haskett
nodes.summary: Christian Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), advised by Robert A. F. Thurman and Michael Chamberlain, and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Graeme MacQueen
nodes.summary: Graeme MacQueen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as a lecturer at McMaster University from circa 1977 to 2003.

nodes.label: Linda Jean LaMacchia
nodes.summary: Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).

nodes.label: China Institute of Inner Learning
variants: China Institute of Inner Learning (支那內學院)

nodes.label: Michael R. Sheehy
nodes.summary: Michael R. Sheehy specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2007) under Steven D. Goodman and held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia.

nodes.label: Qingying Chen
nodes.summary: Qingying Chen was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Qinghai Nationalities University, Qinghai Normal University, and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He held posts at Delingha High School, Qinghai Academy of Social Sciences, and China Tibetology Research Center.

nodes.label: Anagarika Govinda
nodes.image: Lama Govinda in an internment camp during World War II.jpg
nodes.summary: Anagarika Govinda worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, earning a doctorate at the University of Freiburg and studying under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Tomo Geshe Rinpoche. He taught at Visva-Bharati (1931-1935) and Patna University (1935-1936), and served as Ācārya of Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933-1985).

nodes.label: Adeu Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Adeu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Drukpa Choegon Rinpoche, and he later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Zen Mountain Monastery
variants: Zen Mountain Monastery at Mt. Tremper

nodes.label: Hegoda Khemananda
nodes.summary: Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal of Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director of Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

nodes.label: Dewei Zhang
nodes.summary: Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Paul Crowe
nodes.summary: Paul Crowe is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and held a professorship at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

nodes.label: King Pong Chiu
nodes.summary: King Pong Chiu specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under doctoral supervisor Jacqueline Suthren Hirst, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Ilkka Pyysiäinen
nodes.description: Finnish cognitive science of religion scholar
nodes.summary: Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied under René Gothóni and earned a PhD at the University of Helsinki. He served as an Academy Research Fellow at Helsinki and a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Hiram W. Woodward
nodes.summary: Hiram W. Woodward is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Harvard and Yale, taught at the University of Michigan (1972–1982) and University of Vermont (~1982–1986), and was curator of Asian Art at Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

nodes.label: ISEAS–Yusof Ishak Institute
variants: Institute of Southeast Asian Studies, Singapore

nodes.label: Andrew B. Irvine
nodes.summary: Andrew B. Irvine is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from Boston University. He held an attested post as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College in 2009.

nodes.label: Brooke Schedneck
nodes.summary: Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

nodes.label: Jacques Leider
nodes.summary: A historian and Buddhist studies scholar, Jacques Leider studied at INALCO, Paris-Sorbonne, and the University of Luxembourg, completing his PhD under Denise Bernot and also studying under Pierre L. Lamant. He taught at Chulalongkorn University and joined EFEO in 2001.

nodes.label: William Edward Soothill
nodes.summary: William Edward Soothill (1861–1935) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London, he served as President of Shanxi University in 1911 and became Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

nodes.label: Lewis Hodous
nodes.summary: Lewis Hodous (1872–1949) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Case Western Reserve University, Hartford International University, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served at Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1917) and Hartford International University (1917–1945).

nodes.label: Adrian Zenz
nodes.summary: Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He later held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

nodes.label: Xiuzhi Zeng
nodes.summary: Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ramon N. Prats
nodes.summary: Ramon N. Prats is a Tibetologist. He was affiliated with Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources in 1999 and Pompeu Fabra University in 2017.

nodes.label: Pompeu Fabra University
variants: Department of Humanities of the University Pompeu Fabra

nodes.label: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy
nodes.summary: Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, EPHE, and Harvard under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts at Laval University, including teaching anthropology around 2004.

nodes.label: Tibet Arts Research Institute
variants: Tibetan Arts Research Bureau (Bod ljongs sgyu rtsal zhib 'jug khang)

nodes.label: James Whitehill
nodes.summary: James Whitehill is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000) and founded the Columbia Zen Center.

nodes.label: David Bubna-Litic
nodes.summary: David Bubna-Litic is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who completed his PhD at Western Sydney University (attested 2000). He served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney.

nodes.label: University of Technology Sydney
variants: School of Management in the University of Technology, Sydney

nodes.label: Susan Naquin
nodes.summary: Susan Naquin is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at Stanford and Yale, she served on the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1988) and Princeton University (1993–2013).

nodes.label: Jiyu Ren
nodes.summary: Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) studied at Peking University under Lin He and Yongtong Tang. A scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhism, he taught at Peking University (1942–1964) and directed the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and Chinese Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Xiaoling Wu
nodes.summary: Xiaoling Wu was a sinologist and Indologist. He was a research scholar and lecturer at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), taught at Peking University (~1946–1949), and served as a professor at Academia Sinica (~1950–1977) and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).

nodes.label: Marion L. Matics
nodes.summary: Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

nodes.label: Horace L. Friess
nodes.summary: Horace L. Friess was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg University, later serving at Johns Hopkins University and holding the Buttenwieser Professorship of Human Relations at Columbia (1962–1966).

nodes.label: Soto Zen Buddhism International Center
variants: Soto Zen Education Center of North America

nodes.label: Susan L. Beningson
nodes.summary: Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Wayne Bass
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Wayne Bass studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and earned his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen. A scholar in Buddhist studies, he has held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego.

nodes.label: William P. Chu
nodes.summary: William P. Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his MA at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2006 and conducted doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.id: I:International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
variants: International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies
IITB GmbH (International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies GmbH)

nodes.label: Dhirendra Sharma
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under teachers David Friedman and Surendra Sharma.

nodes.label: John R. B. Campbell
nodes.summary: John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, while also studying under several traditional and academic teachers.

nodes.label: H. V. Nagaraja Rao
nodes.summary: H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He has held positions at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Geshe Karma Sonam
nodes.summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Karma Sonam held posts at Gyume Tantric Monastery (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

nodes.label: Lang Eun Ra
nodes.summary: Lang Eun Ra is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies at Temple University under the supervision of Charles Wei-hsun Fu.

nodes.label: Norbert Max Samuelson
nodes.description: Scholar and professor of Jewish philosophy
nodes.summary: Norbert Max Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned degrees from Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He held major professorships at Temple University and Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Leonard Swidler
nodes.summary: Leonard Swidler (1929–2026) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from St. Norbert College, Marquette University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Tübingen. He was Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).

nodes.label: Alan Gerard Wagner
nodes.summary: Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under Parimal G. Patil, and also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

nodes.label: Iselin Frydenlund
nodes.summary: Iselin Frydenlund works in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she is attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo and a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo.

nodes.label: Bruce M. Knauft
nodes.summary: Bruce M. Knauft studied at the University of Michigan (~1976–1983). He has served as Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology at Emory University (~1985).

nodes.label: Richard Taupier
nodes.summary: Richard Taupier works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MS and a doctorate from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he served as Associate Director of Research Development, and was a visiting lecturer at Smith College.

nodes.label: Martin Lehnert
nodes.summary: Martin Lehnert works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg and was attested in 2016 as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich.

nodes.label: James Mark Shields
nodes.summary: James Mark Shields is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

nodes.id: I:Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg
nodes.label: Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg
variants: Foundation for Buddhist Studies in Hamburg

nodes.label: Kim Gutschow
nodes.summary: In Tibetology and religious studies, she earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.

nodes.label: Geshe Ngawang Nyima
nodes.summary: Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, and Trijang Rinpoche. He served at Leiden University (1960) and as abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

nodes.label: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Bonn (~1969–1970), the University of Toronto (~1971–1972), and Brown University (~1974–1975).

nodes.label: Jenkuan Shih
nodes.summary: Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the doctoral supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

nodes.label: Mark Csikszentmihalyi
nodes.summary: Mark Csikszentmihalyi works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He held a post as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2004) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley in ~2005.

nodes.label: Giuliana Martini
nodes.summary: Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.

nodes.label: Keith Dowman
nodes.description: Dzogchen teacher, translator of Tibetan Buddhist texts
nodes.summary: Keith Dowman is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under numerous traditional teachers, including Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Kangyur Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

nodes.label: David Ralph Quinter
nodes.summary: David Ralph Quinter works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed an MA at Colorado and a PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Alberta (attested 2019).

nodes.id: I:Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
nodes.label: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies
variants: Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies in Yokohama
Inter-University Center for Advanced Language Study
Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies

nodes.label: Kenji Matsuo
nodes.summary: Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1981 and served at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.

nodes.label: Sonja Arntzen
nodes.summary: Sonja Arntzen (born 1945) is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1970–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied with Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

nodes.label: Shuichi Kato
nodes.summary: Shuichi Kato was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of British Columbia, Sophia University, and Free University of Berlin, and directed the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.

nodes.label: Qichao Liang
nodes.summary: Qichao Liang worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology, studying at Xuehai Tang, National Tsing Hua University, and under Youwei Kang. He held posts at the Current Affairs Academy, Translation Bureau, Tsinghua University, Nankai University, and the National Library of China.

nodes.label: Youwei Kang
nodes.summary: Youwei Kang worked in philosophy, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He founded the Wanmu Caotang in 1890, taught there from ~1891 to 1898, and taught Qichao Liang.

nodes.label: Cameron Bailey
nodes.summary: Cameron Bailey works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University, Florida State University, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), where his supervisors and teachers included Bryan J. Cuevas, Richard F. Nance, and Ulrike Roesler.

nodes.label: Lucia Galli
nodes.summary: Lucia Galli works in Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford, where she also held an academic post.

nodes.label: Rory Lindsay
nodes.summary: Rory Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and earned his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp alongside numerous other teachers.

nodes.label: Donald K. Swearer
nodes.summary: Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and Harvard University (2004–2010), where he was a Distinguished Visiting Fellow at the Center for the Study of World Religions.

nodes.label: Amanda K. Goodman
nodes.summary: Amanda K. Goodman is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, under Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr. She holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

nodes.id: I:Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
variants: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
Hong Kong University of Science & Technology

nodes.label: Mamoru Tonami
nodes.summary: Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, later serving there as assistant (1965), associate professor (1975), and professor (1984, 1993, 1996–2001).

nodes.label: Jeffery D. Long
nodes.summary: Working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, Jeffery D. Long studied at the University of Notre Dame and earned an MA and PhD from the University of Chicago Divinity School. In 2000, he joined Elizabethtown College as Associate Professor.

nodes.label: Angela Sumegi
nodes.summary: Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa under Nalini Devdas. In 2008, she was attested as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities.

nodes.id: I:Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre
nodes.label: Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre
variants: Hongyi and Feng Zikai Research Centre

nodes.label: Lucia Dolce
nodes.summary: Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She served at SOAS University of London as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Grace S. Fong
nodes.summary: Grace S. Fong is a Sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She served as Professor at Smith College before becoming associate professor and chair of East Asian Studies at McGill University around 1992.

nodes.label: Ching-mei Shyu
nodes.summary: Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and completed her PhD in 2008 at Cornell University under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

nodes.label: Ellison Banks Findly
nodes.summary: Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. Her academic appointments include Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was associate professor of religion and Asian studies (attested 1989).

nodes.label: Kazuo Okabe
nodes.summary: Kazuo Okabe was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1958) and the University of Tokyo (~1958–1966). He served as an associate professor and professor at Komazawa University from 1973 until 2006.

nodes.label: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara
nodes.native: สมเด็จพระญาณสังวร
variants: Somdet Phra Sangharaja Chao Krommaluang Vajirañāṇasaṃvara
nodes.jawiki: ワシラガーナサンバラ
nodes.summary: Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Swami Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. In Buddhist and religious studies, he served as Director at Mahamakut Buddhist University, meditation teacher at Kasetsart University, and abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara.

nodes.label: Hanung Kim
nodes.summary: Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a PhD from Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

nodes.label: Ruth Gamble
nodes.summary: Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger Jackson, and David Templeman. She has held posts at the Australian National University and the University of Munich (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Petra Maurer
nodes.summary: Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has been affiliated with the Bavarian Academy of Sciences, the University of Munich, and the International Consortium for Research in the Humanities.

nodes.label: Cuilan Liu
nodes.summary: Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held positions as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Emanuela Garatti
nodes.summary: Emanuela Garatti is a scholar of Tibetology who has held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Satya Narayan Goenka
variants: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ
nodes.image: The Kalyanmitra Satyanarayan Goenka who brought Vipassana Meditation technique to India after 2500 years is seen with his wife while speaking at a talk on "Values in Education - Good Governance through Vipassana Meditation" in.jpg
nodes.jawiki: サティア・ナラヤン・ゴエンカ
nodes.summary: Satya Narayan Goenka (1924–2013) was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under U Ba Khin from circa 1955 to 1971 and founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

nodes.label: Phramonchai Saitanaporn
nodes.summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Jeff Wilson
nodes.summary: Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under mentors Taitetsu Unno and Akio Tatsuguchi.

nodes.label: Shuman Chen
nodes.summary: Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Northwestern University in 2014 under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, having also studied under Weijue Shi.

nodes.label: Brook Ziporyn
nodes.summary: Brook Ziporyn, a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religion, studied at the University of Chicago and earned his PhD from the University of Michigan. He taught at Northwestern University (~2003–2012), the National University of Singapore (~2012–2013), and the University of Chicago (~2013).

nodes.label: Sarah E. Fraser
nodes.summary: Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University. She held appointments at Northwestern University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

nodes.label: Anne Ruth Hansen
nodes.summary: Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Charles Hallisey. She held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Thomas Nathan Patton
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Patton earned his PhD at Cornell University under Anne M. Blackburn. He held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Anne M. Blackburn
nodes.summary: Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who pursued graduate studies at the University of Chicago (~1989–1996). She served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001–2005).

nodes.label: Hoseok Leigh
nodes.summary: Hoseok Leigh worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Carol S. Anderson
nodes.summary: Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago and studied under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

nodes.label: Catherine Bell
nodes.summary: Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Chicago Divinity School under Joseph M. Kitagawa. She served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

nodes.label: Xiangguang Zhou
nodes.summary: Xiangguang Zhou worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied under Swami Sivananda Saraswati and served as Professor of Chinese at the University of Allahabad, Lecturer in History at Delhi, and Chancellor at Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

nodes.id: I:Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
nodes.label: Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration
Kin Cheung
nodes.summary: Kin Cheung works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo, attested in 2017.

nodes.label: James Blumenthal
nodes.summary: James Blumenthal studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College in Buddhist studies and philosophy.

nodes.label: Kosen Imakita
nodes.summary: Kosen Imakita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Daisetsu Jōen, Gisan Zenkai, Togai Fujisawa, and Kyokuso Hirose at Shokoku-ji and Sōgen-ji. He served as abbot at Eikō-ji and Engaku-ji, and as Doctrinal Instructor in the Ministry of Religion.

nodes.label: Beatrice Erskine Lane
variants: ベアトリス・アースキン・レイン・スズキ
nodes.jawiki: ベアトリス・レイン・スズキ
nodes.summary: Beatrice Erskine Lane worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana, earned a master's at Columbia University, and was appointed professor at Otani University in 1921.

nodes.label: Josiah Royce
nodes.summary: Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins (PhD 1878). He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

nodes.label: George Santayana
variants: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・サンタヤーナ
nodes.summary: George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Harvard, Humboldt University of Berlin, and King's College, Cambridge, earning his PhD under William James. He served on the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.

nodes.label: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche
variants: ティンレー・ノルブ・リンポチェ
nodes.image: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche wearing a white shirt, red zen, pink curtain in background.jpg
nodes.summary: Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje), and later founded the White Lotus School.

nodes.label: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche (1930–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Shyé Chen Kong Trul Pema Drimé.

nodes.label: Thubten Chodron
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Chodron studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan, and Dorje Pamo. She held posts at Istituto Lama Tzong Khapa, Amitabha Buddhist Centre, and Dharma Friendship Foundation, and founded Sravasti Abbey in 2003, serving as its abbess.

nodes.label: Daniel R. Tuzzeo
nodes.summary: Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his thesis at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

nodes.label: George A. Keyworth
nodes.summary: George A. Keyworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., Ronald Egan, Shuizhao Wang, and William F. Powell. He held posts at Colorado (2001) and Saskatchewan (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Ronald Egan
nodes.summary: Ronald Egan is a sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University. He held posts at Harvard (~1978–1987), Wellesley College (~1987–1991), UC Santa Barbara as Professor of Chinese Literature (~1991–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

nodes.label: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen
nodes.summary: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD from Leiden University by 1991, where he was also attested as a research fellow in 1996.

nodes.label: Stephen H. West
nodes.summary: Stephen H. West is a sinologist who studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (Ph.D. 1968–1972). He served as executive director of the IUP and held professorships in Chinese at UC Berkeley (~1986–2004) and Arizona State University (~2004).

nodes.label: Namio Egami
nodes.summary: A scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Namio Egami studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1967) and directed the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).

nodes.label: Ulrike Roesler
nodes.summary: Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg, and became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford.

nodes.label: Nalini Devdas
nodes.summary: A scholar of religious studies and Indology, Nalini Devdas earned her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr, having also studied under Steven Collins and others. She was affiliated with Carleton University (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Paul David Devanandan
nodes.summary: Paul David Devanandan was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Presidency College and Yale University (doctorate ~1928–1931), he served as professor at United Theological College (1932–1949) and director of the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).

nodes.label: Tsultrim Gyatso
nodes.summary: Tsultrim Gyatso was active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

nodes.label: Hozen Seki
nodes.summary: Hozen Seki was a figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Ganden Monastery
variants: Shartse College of Ganden Monastic University
Shartse College of Ganden monastic university
Shartse Norling College of Gaden Monastery

nodes.label: Bhuwan Lal Joshi
nodes.summary: Bhuwan Lal Joshi (1930–1977) was an Indology scholar who studied at Patna University. He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1967) and served as a professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1970–1977).

nodes.label: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov
nodes.summary: Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy around 1920 to 1928. From around 1928 to 1937, he served at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

nodes.label: Jørn Borup
nodes.summary: Jørn Borup (1966–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, later serving there as Associate Professor (~2008–2023).

nodes.label: Ian Reader
nodes.summary: Ian Reader is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Leeds (~1979–1983). He held posts at Stirling (~1989–1999) and Lancaster (~2003–2008), and taught Jørn Borup.

nodes.label: Michaela Haas
nodes.summary: Michaela Haas is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger. She also studied under Jigme Namgyel and Rechungpa.

nodes.label: Jigme Namgyel
variants: ‘Jigs med rNam rgyal ‘Dzi sgar Kong sprul

nodes.label: Rudolf Kaschewsky
nodes.summary: Rudolf Kaschewsky specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, where he later served as Akademischer Rat from 1974 to 2004. He also taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt.

nodes.label: Andreas Doctor
nodes.summary: Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura. He also studied under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche, Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche, and Phakchok Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche
nodes.description: tibetan teacher and religious ritual master
nodes.summary: Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen (~2003–2020).

nodes.label: Phakchok Rinpoche
nodes.description: Vajra Master of Ka-Nying Shedrup Ling monastery
nodes.summary: Phakchok Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute and studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

nodes.label: Ngodup Tsering
nodes.image: Ngodup Tsering, Geshe Lhakdor and Geshe Lobsang Monlam.jpg

nodes.label: Susan Niditch
nodes.summary: Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served on the faculty in the religion department at Amherst College from around 1978 to 2020.

nodes.label: Tenzin L. Mullin
nodes.summary: Tenzin L. Mullin is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at the University of Otago, supervised by Erica Baffelli and Elizabeth Guthrie.

nodes.label: Will Sweetman
nodes.description: professor of religion in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Will Sweetman is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1989–1992) and Lancaster University (~1993–1996), and held a post at the University of Otago around 2004.

nodes.label: Dongchu
nodes.summary: Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Academy (~1929–1933) and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He was abbot of Dinghui Temple (~1945–1949) and held posts at Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute and Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Craig Preston
nodes.summary: Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Paul
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Paul is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist. Her doctoral supervisor was Gudrun Bühnemann, and she also studied under teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

nodes.label: Philadelphia Museum of Art
variants: フィラデルフィア美術館

nodes.label: David Jones
nodes.summary: David Jones is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi. He served as a philosophy professor in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

nodes.id: I:Center for the Development of Asian Studies
nodes.label: Center for the Development of Asian Studies
variants: Center for the Development of Asian Studies

nodes.label: Maxime Kaltenmark
nodes.summary: Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He directed the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and University of Paris (~1957–1979).

nodes.label: Léon Vandermeersch
nodes.summary: Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) was a Sinology and philosophy scholar. Educated at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot, he held posts at Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, the Maison Franco-Japonaise, and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient.

nodes.label: Wen-ling Jane
nodes.summary: Wen-ling Jane specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Geshe Lozang Jamspal.

nodes.label: Roy Tzohar
nodes.summary: Roy Tzohar (born 1973) works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2005) and completed his PhD at Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb (~2005–2011), later joining Tel Aviv University (~2011).

nodes.label: Kammie Takahashi
nodes.description: academic, college faculty, Associate Professor of Religion Studies
nodes.summary: Kammie Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano and Paul Groner, holding a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.

nodes.label: Sabine Löhr
nodes.summary: Sabine Löhr is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, where she was supervised by Lambert Schmithausen and worked as a graduate assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft).

nodes.label: Robert Barnett
nodes.summary: Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1976). He served as an adjunct professor at Columbia University (~1999–2018), directed Tibet University's summer program (2000–2006), and held posts at SOAS and King's College London.

nodes.label: Halle Elizabeth O'Neal
nodes.summary: Halle Elizabeth O'Neal is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Kansas under doctoral supervisor Sherry Fowler (attested 2011).

nodes.label: David W. Tien
nodes.summary: David W. Tien is a scholar in sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, earning a PhD at Michigan under James Robson and also studying under Robert H. Sharf.

nodes.label: Jim Rheingans
nodes.summary: Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hamburg and completed his PhD at the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University, supervised by David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery.

nodes.id: I:University of the West of England
nodes.label: University of the West of England
variants: University of the West of England, Bristol
University of the West of England

nodes.label: Stephen Suen
nodes.summary: Stephen Suen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Mark T. Unno
nodes.summary: Mark T. Unno is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University (~1987–1994) and held posts at Brown University (~1994–1996) and the University of Oregon (~2000).

nodes.id: I:Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies
nodes.label: Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies
variants: Institute of Mongolian, Tibetan, and Buddhist Studies at the Buryat Scientific Center of the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences
Institute for Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies
Institut des Études mongoles, bouddhistes et tibétaines
Buryat-Mongolian Research Institute of Culture in Ulan-Ude

nodes.label: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir
nodes.summary: Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and also studied under Lama Byambaa.

nodes.label: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska
nodes.summary: Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and held an attested post at the University of Warsaw in 2008.

nodes.label: Moscow State University
variants: Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies
Institute of Asian and African Studies

nodes.label: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz
nodes.summary: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Attested in 2018, he earned his MA at Florida State University under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas.

nodes.label: Yu Yan Pang
nodes.summary: Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. Pang earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

nodes.label: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza
nodes.summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University from 1988.

nodes.label: Ngawang Jorden
nodes.summary: Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.

nodes.label: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee
nodes.description: Indian historian, numismatist, epigraphist and iconographist
nodes.summary: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta and completed his doctorate at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was the Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).

nodes.label: Sulak Sivaraksa
nodes.native: สุลักษณ์ ศิวรักษ์
nodes.summary: Sulak Sivaraksa (born 1933) is an activist and scholar of Buddhist studies and history. Educated at Lampeter and SSRC, he served as an editor, held visiting posts at Berkeley, Harvard, Lampeter, Toronto, and Cornell, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists.

nodes.label: Subhadradis Diskul
nodes.native: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล
variants: モムチャオ＝スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.image: สุภัทรดิศ ดิศกุล.jpg
nodes.jawiki: スパトラディット・ディッサクン
nodes.summary: Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a scholar of history and archaeology. Educated at Chulalongkorn, the École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL, he held posts at the Bangkok National Museum, Silpakorn University, SEAMEO SPAFA, and the Siam Society.

nodes.label: Dave Tomlinson
nodes.summary: Dave Tomlinson is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold (attested 2019), studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.

nodes.label: Sven Wittemann
nodes.summary: Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa.

nodes.label: Juichiro Tanabe
nodes.summary: Tanabe studied philosophy and other subjects, undertaking PhD studies at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studying under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

nodes.label: Bong Seok Joo
nodes.summary: Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under the doctoral supervision of Stephen F. Teiser.

nodes.label: Jeffrey Stout
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Stout studied at Brown University and earned his PhD at Princeton University. A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

nodes.label: Jann Ronis
nodes.summary: Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor David Germano and teacher Jeffrey Hopkins, and was attested in an academic post there in 2007.

nodes.label: Faren
nodes.summary: Faren works in Buddhist and religious studies. Faren earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Wenbiao Mai
nodes.summary: Wenbiao Mai works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and Peking University (PhD), and served as a visiting assistant professor at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Zhonghui Cui
nodes.summary: Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at SOAS University of London and a PhD at The University of Hong Kong, where she later served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Christopher D. Emms
nodes.summary: Christopher D. Emms is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued his doctoral studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.

nodes.label: Jampa Samten
nodes.summary: Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Director (attested 1991) and later Professor (attested 2015) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Gin Ling Liu
nodes.summary: Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin, also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

nodes.label: Kim Knott
nodes.summary: In religious studies and Indology, she held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1984–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

nodes.label: Eleanor Nesbitt
nodes.summary: Eleanor Nesbitt is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1969–1972) and the University of Oxford (~1972–1973), and later served as emerita professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989).

nodes.label: John Berthrong
nodes.summary: John Berthrong worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed his graduate studies under Alfonso Verdu and held an appointment at Boston University from around 1989 to 2013.

nodes.label: Defense Language Institute
variants: アメリカ陸軍の語学学校

nodes.label: Jang-Kil Chun
nodes.summary: Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His studies were conducted under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

nodes.label: Alexander Rödel
nodes.summary: Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, where he studied under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

nodes.label: University of Rhode Island
variants: ロードアイランド大学

nodes.label: Yongtong Tang
nodes.summary: Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, he held professorships at Southeast, National Central, and Peking Universities, later serving as Peking University's vice-president.

nodes.label: UNESCO
variants: International Commission for a History of the Scientific and Cultural Development of Mankind

nodes.label: Hsueh-li Cheng
nodes.summary: Hsueh-li Cheng is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Ohio University (~1972–1973) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo (~1973–2010).

nodes.label: Troy Organ
nodes.summary: Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa. He held academic posts at Chatham University, Parsons College, the University of Akron, and Ohio University.

nodes.label: Aristotle C. Dy
nodes.summary: Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

nodes.label: University of Tehran
variants: Faculty of Political and Social Sciences in Tehran

nodes.label: Kristin Scheible
nodes.summary: Kristin Scheible is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. She has held posts at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College.

nodes.label: Matthew Steven Mitchell
nodes.summary: Matthew Steven Mitchell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center, the University of Hawaiʻi (MA), and Duke University (PhD), his mentors included Richard M. Jaffe, Helen Baroni, and Michel Mohr.

nodes.label: Richard M. Jaffe
nodes.summary: Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at North Carolina State University from circa 1995 to 2000 and at Duke University around 2000.

nodes.label: Chong Go
nodes.summary: Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Dongguk University and under the traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Bongkil Chung
nodes.summary: Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and served as a professor of philosophy at Florida International University (1991–1992, attested 2012).

nodes.label: Woosung Huh
nodes.summary: Woosung Huh is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Patrick R. Uhlmann
nodes.summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was a Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles (attested 2012), where he studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Woncheol Yun
nodes.summary: Woncheol Yun is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jin Y. Park
nodes.summary: Jin Y. Park specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and has been a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Pema Chödrön
nodes.summary: Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at Sarah Lawrence and UC Berkeley. She studied under Chime Tulku Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Chögyam Trungpa, serving as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center (~1979–1984) and abbess and director at Gampo Abbey.

nodes.label: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen, and served as professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

nodes.label: Geo Widengren
variants: ゲオ・ヴィデングレン
nodes.summary: Geo Widengren was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. Educated at Stockholm and Uppsala universities under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, he was Professor of the History of Religions at Uppsala University (1940–1973) and president of the IAHR.

nodes.label: Benoît Vermander
nodes.summary: Benoît Vermander specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres, and served as Academic Director at the Taipei Ricci Institute before joining Fudan University in 2009.

nodes.label: Taipei Ricci Institute
variants: Taipei Ricci Institute for Chinese Studies

nodes.label: Chiko Corona
nodes.summary: Chiko Corona is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Mikaël Bauer
nodes.summary: Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Adi Da
nodes.summary: Adi Da worked in religious studies and philosophy. He completed his studies at Columbia University (~1957–1961) and Stanford University (~1961–1963).

nodes.label: Toshiichi Endo
nodes.summary: Toshiichi Endo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (-1995), and held a professorship at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Hyon Gak Sunim
nodes.summary: Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), and Harvard University (~1989–1992), and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

nodes.label: Walther Heissig
variants: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
nodes.jawiki: ワルター・ハイシッヒ
nodes.summary: Walther Heissig worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as religious studies. He studied at Vienna, Humboldt University, Göttingen, and Bonn, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Heidi Fjeld
nodes.summary: Heidi Fjeld (b. 1970) is a Tibetology scholar. She earned her doctorate under the supervision of Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006), where she subsequently held a postdoctoral fellowship (~2007–2010).

nodes.label: Ben Jiao
nodes.summary: Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Alexander O. Hsu
nodes.description: researcher of Global Affairs and religious studies scholar (field of Buddhism)
nodes.summary: Alexander O. Hsu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago Divinity School under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching post at North Dakota State University.

nodes.label: Anthony C. Yu
nodes.description: American scholar of literature and religion (1938-2015)
nodes.summary: Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, where he served as a professor from circa 1968 to 2005.

nodes.label: Smithsonian Institution
variants: Bureau of Ethnicity of the Smithsonian Institution

nodes.label: Joan Jiko Halifax
nodes.image: Joan Halifax and the Dalai Lama.jpg
nodes.description: American Zen Buddhist roshi, anthropologist, ecologist, and civil rights activist
nodes.summary: Joan Jiko Halifax (b. 1942) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Newcomb, Tulane, and Union Institute (PhD), she held posts at Columbia, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Miami, and later founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.

nodes.label: Ajahn Sucitto
nodes.summary: Ajahn Sucitto is a Buddhist studies figure who earned a degree from the University of Warwick. He studied under Ajahn Sumedho beginning in 1977 and served as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

nodes.label: Franz Aubrey Metcalf
nodes.summary: Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

nodes.label: California State University, Los Angeles
variants: California State University at Los Angeles

nodes.label: Paul David Numrich
nodes.summary: Paul David Numrich is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Michigan in 1992 and held posts at the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Ann Gleig
nodes.summary: Ann Gleig is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy degree at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

nodes.label: Geshe Losang Chödar
nodes.summary: Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics, both attested in 2010.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Everding
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1978–1985) and his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1993–1999). He was a Privatdozent at Hamburg (1999) and a researcher at Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1991–2018).

nodes.label: Shri Krishna Sharma
nodes.summary: A scholar in Indology and linguistics, Shri Krishna Sharma founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva. He also taught the scholar Dieter Schuh.

nodes.label: John B. Cobb Jr.
nodes.summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago and founded the Center for Process Studies. In 1989, he held professorships at Claremont Graduate University and Claremont School of Theology.

nodes.label: Joseph Prabhu
nodes.summary: Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under Bernard Williams. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007), and held visiting professorships at UCSB, United Theological College, and Bossey.

nodes.label: Ecumenical Institute of Bossey
variants: Ecumenical Institute of the World Council of Churches

nodes.label: Sakyong Mipham
variants: サキョン・ミパム・リンポチェ
サワン・ウーセル・ランジュン・ムクポ
nodes.summary: Sakyong Mipham works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under Chögyam Trungpa, Dilgo Khyentse, and Penor Rinpoche. He succeeded Chögyam Trungpa and served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

nodes.label: Dilgo Khyentse
variants: ディルゴ・キェンツェ
Dil mgo Mkhyen brtse Rin po che, Rab gsal zla ba
nodes.description: Buddhist Vajrayana master, scholar, poet, and teacher (1910–1991)
nodes.summary: Dilgo Khyentse was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap Pema Namgyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and later taught numerous prominent Buddhist teachers and scholars.

nodes.label: Penor Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Palyul Monastery under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Dilgo Khyentse, Jampel Gyepai Dorje, and Karma Tekchok Nyingpo. In 1978, he founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

nodes.label: Shinobu Arai Apple
nodes.summary: Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003), teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi (2000), and academic adviser Robert Bickner.

nodes.label: Robert Warren Clark
nodes.summary: Clark works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao and doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang.

nodes.label: Daniel A. Getz
