nodes.summary: Daniel A. Getz specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and later served as an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Kelsey Alise Seymour
nodes.summary: Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018) and was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science.

nodes.label: Sue Hamilton
nodes.summary: Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil from the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and was affiliated with King's College London (attested 2001–2003).

nodes.label: Tsukasa Mizushima
nodes.summary: Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, from the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

nodes.label: Ankur Barua
nodes.summary: Ankur Barua, active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and The University of Hong Kong. He held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Dorothy C. Wong
nodes.summary: Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She is a faculty member at the University of Virginia and was attested in 2009 as a visiting Professor of Buddhist Art at the Centre of Buddhist Studies, University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Randall Studstill
nodes.summary: Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral work under the supervision of Richard K. Payne.

nodes.label: Chisan Kohō
nodes.summary: Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyōdō Kōshūin, and founded Tsurumi University in 1966. He held posts at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Soji-ji (circa 1957–1967).

nodes.label: Maurine Stuart
nodes.summary: Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Manitoba and trained under Nadia Boulanger, Soen Nakagawa, Eido Tai Shimano, and Yasutani. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

nodes.label: Eido Tai Shimano
nodes.summary: Eido Tai Shimano (1932–2018) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa, and attended the University of Hawaiʻi. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and held posts at New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

nodes.label: Prabhasa Dharma Cheney
nodes.summary: Prabhasa Dharma Cheney (1931–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kyozan Joshu Sasaki in 1967 and Seikō Hirata.

nodes.label: Kyozan Joshu Sasaki
nodes.summary: Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (1907–2014) was a Buddhist studies figure who trained at Zuiryo-ji and Myoshin-ji. He served as abbot of Yotoku-in and Shojuan, founded Mount Baldy Zen Center, and was its abbot from ~1971 to 2012.

nodes.label: Seikō Hirata
nodes.summary: Seikō Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He held a post at Hanazono University from circa 1965 to 1994.

nodes.label: Yong Hua
nodes.summary: Yong Hua is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Hua completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Hyoung Seok Ham
nodes.summary: Hyoung Seok Ham is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under Madhav M. Deshpande, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and others.

nodes.label: Charles H. Long
nodes.description: African-American cultural historian and religious studies scholar (1926–2020)
nodes.summary: Charles H. Long was a religious studies scholar who earned his BD and PhD at the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara.

nodes.label: 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje studied under Kalu Rinpoche, the 1st Beru Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Kobun Chino Otogawa
nodes.summary: Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and taught at Naropa University in 2001.

nodes.label: Ritsumeikan University
variants: 立命館大学総合心理学部
立命館大学国際関係学部

nodes.label: Erik Braun
nodes.summary: Erik Braun is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun.

nodes.label: Anagarika Munindra
nodes.summary: Anagarika Munindra was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied under Satya Narayan Goenka and disciple of Mahasi Sayadaw (1957-1966). He served as superintendent at the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.

nodes.label: Zuigan Goto
nodes.summary: Zuigan Goto was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Sōkatsu Shaku (~1900-1914) and attended the Second Higher School and the University of Tokyo (1903-1906). He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

nodes.label: Dominic Sur
nodes.summary: Dominic Sur works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia—under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer—as well as under Khenpo Lama Chönam. He was attested at Utah State University in 2017.

nodes.label: Ravi M. Gupta
nodes.description: Vaishnava religious scholar, author and editor
nodes.summary: Ravi M. Gupta is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. He taught at Florida, Centre College, and William & Mary before becoming Charles Redd Chair at Utah State University.

nodes.label: Prasarn Lao-areun
nodes.summary: Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD at the University of Mysore (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Mabel Haynes Bode
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Bode earned her PhD at the University of Bern under Edouard Müller-Hess and studied widely across Europe. She later lectured at University College London (1909, 1911–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

nodes.label: Shrivatsa Goswami
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Shrivatsa Goswami studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught philosophy and religion. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University and held a post at the Vrindaban Research Institute (attested 1994).

nodes.label: Trevor Leggett
nodes.summary: Trevor Leggett worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Yukio Tani, Hari Prasad Shastri, and Arthur Waley. He headed the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lectured for The Buddhist Society.

nodes.label: John Riley Perks
nodes.summary: John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

nodes.label: Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang
nodes.summary: Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Villages, and the University of Glasgow, later serving as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Villages and teaching Tibetan at the University of Oxford from 2001.

nodes.label: Tibetan Children's Villages
variants: Central Tibetan Children's Village (TCV) school in Dharamsala

nodes.label: Jack Laughlin
nodes.summary: Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999. He subsequently held an academic appointment at the University of Sudbury.

nodes.label: Singhathon Narasabho
nodes.summary: Singhathon Narasabho works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti (attested 1971).

nodes.label: Takeo Hibino
nodes.summary: Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University. He worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities and the university itself (1948–1977), later becoming a professor at Otemon Gakuin University and professor and president at Otemae University.

nodes.label: Abigail I. MacBain
nodes.summary: Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA from McMaster University, where her teachers included Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald.

nodes.label: Flavio A. Geisshuesler
nodes.summary: Flavio A. Geisshuesler works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Lausanne, Bern, and Virginia, where he completed a PhD under David Germano, and held a postdoctoral research position at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2019.

nodes.label: Farzand Ali Durrani
nodes.summary: Farzand Ali Durrani was a historian and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Peshawar, University of the Punjab, and University of London, he served as a professor at the University of Peshawar (~1960–1993).

nodes.label: Yu-min Lee
nodes.summary: Yu-min Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Lee studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington, taught Pei-jung Wu, and served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Yaping Dou
nodes.summary: Yaping Dou is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Steffen Döll
nodes.summary: Steffen Döll is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned his MA and doctorate at the University of Munich. After serving as an assistant at Munich, he became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

nodes.label: Stefania Travagnin
nodes.image: Stefania Travagnin in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor of religion in Asia at the University of Groningen from approximately 2013 to 2020 before joining SOAS University of London.

nodes.label: Koen Wellens
nodes.summary: Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne.

nodes.label: Yu-guang Liu
nodes.summary: Yu-guang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Samten, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).

nodes.label: James H. Austin
nodes.summary: James H. Austin is a neurologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori, Kyozan Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at the University of Oregon, University of Colorado, and University of Idaho.

nodes.label: Carmen Blacker
variants: カーメン・ブラッカー
nodes.jawiki: カーメン・ブラッカー
nodes.summary: Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at SOAS, Somerville College, Oxford, Keio University, and under Shigeru Gorai. She served as a lecturer at the University of Cambridge and president of The Folklore Society (1982–1984).

nodes.label: Shigeru Gorai
nodes.summary: Shigeru Gorai was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held posts at Koyasan University, Otani University, Ryukoku University, and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore.

nodes.label: Vladimir Tikhonov
nodes.image: Prof. Vladimir Tikhonov (Pak Noja) San-Peterbur Khanon-214.jpg
nodes.summary: Vladimir Tikhonov is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Moscow State University. After lecturing at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000), he was appointed Associate Professor (2000) and then Professor (2006) at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Dharma Drum Mountain
variants: International Affairs Office of Dharma Drum Mountain
International Cultural and Educational Foundation of Dharma Drum Mountain

nodes.label: Hyejeong Choi
nodes.summary: Hyejeong Choi works in Buddhist studies and archaeology. Supervised by John C. Huntington and taught by Byung-Hyun Choi and others, she completed a PhD at Ohio State University (attested 2015) and was a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

nodes.label: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara
variants: Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture

nodes.label: Karl Brunnhölzl
nodes.summary: Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

nodes.label: Tenga Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery under Tai Situ Rinpoche, served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1980), and founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

nodes.label: Ringu Tulku
nodes.summary: Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who founded Bodhicharya. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, learning under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse, the 16th Karmapa, and Tubten Tsondru.

nodes.id: I:Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
nodes.label: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
variants: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity
Max-Planck-Institut zur Erforschung multireligiöser und multiethnischer Gesellschaften

nodes.label: Peter van der Veer
nodes.summary: Peter van der Veer is a religious studies and Indology scholar educated at Groningen and Utrecht. He held professorships at Amsterdam, Utrecht, and Pennsylvania, and served as Director at the Max Planck Institute (~2008–2021).

nodes.label: Polish Academy of Sciences
variants: Committee on Oriental Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences

nodes.label: John M. Rosenfield
variants: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド3世
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マックス・ローゼンフィールド
nodes.summary: John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland and served as Harvard's Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of East Asian Art from 1965 to 1991.

nodes.label: Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā
nodes.summary: Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, having also studied under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and N. A. Jayawickrama.

nodes.label: Sumanapala Galmangoda
nodes.summary: Sumanapala Galmangoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya and Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007, 2012).

nodes.label: Ross Bolleter
nodes.summary: Ross Bolleter (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley (~1964–1967). He served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia until 2023.

nodes.label: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit
nodes.summary: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit (1939–1999) worked in religious, Iranian and Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and doctoral supervisor Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded at the University of Bonn, serving as Direktor from 1972.

nodes.label: Jared Rhoton
nodes.summary: Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Columbia University by 1985 under the supervision of Alex Wayman and also studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

nodes.label: Richard D. McBride II
nodes.summary: Richard D. McBride II is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UCLA under mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University.

nodes.label: Seiichi Mizuno
nodes.summary: Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, later working at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (1938, 1961) and as university professor (1949–1968).

nodes.label: Toshio Nagahiro
nodes.summary: Toshio Nagahiro (1905–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there and at its Institute for Research in Humanities (1929–1969), later becoming president of Kyoto Tachibana University (1978–1986).

nodes.label: Lucy Annette Jones
nodes.summary: Lucy Annette Jones works in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under Anne C. Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, and she also studied under Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Edith Wyschogrod
nodes.summary: Edith Wyschogrod (1930–2009) was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies who completed her BA at Hunter College and her PhD at Columbia University. From 1992 to 2002, she was a professor at Rice University.

nodes.label: Helena Michie
nodes.summary: Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from 1979 to 1984. She held an academic post at Rice University around 1990.

nodes.label: John Vincent Bellezza
nodes.summary: John Vincent Bellezza is a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology who studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences as attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Konchok Gyatso
nodes.summary: Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Sherab Gyatso and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

nodes.id: I:MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society
nodes.label: MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society
variants: Lutheran School of Theology in Oslo
MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society

nodes.label: Paul W. Kroll
nodes.summary: Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1976). He served at the University of Colorado as Associate Professor of Chinese and department chair (~1979) and later as a Faculty Fellow (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Anna M. Shields
nodes.image: Anna M. Shields (born 1966) at the Center for Chinese Studies Annual Lim Lecture.png
nodes.summary: Anna M. Shields is a scholar in the field of sinology. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and at Princeton University (~2015).

nodes.label: Douglas Allen
nodes.summary: Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt. He taught at Southern Illinois and Central Connecticut State before joining the University of Maine, becoming Professor Emeritus in 2020.

nodes.id: I:Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality
nodes.label: Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality
variants: Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality at SUNY Oneonta

nodes.label: Gary Snyder
variants: ゲイリー・スナイダー
ゲーリー・スナイダー
nodes.jawiki: ゲーリー・スナイダー
nodes.summary: Gary Snyder is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, later serving as a professor at the University of California, Davis from 1986 to 2002.

nodes.label: Enamul Haque
nodes.summary: Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Dhaka and Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and held leadership roles at the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art and ICOM.

nodes.label: Matthew King
nodes.summary: Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett in 2014, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.

nodes.label: Natalie Rothman
nodes.summary: Natalie Rothman (born 1976) is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan (1999–2006). She joined the University of Toronto in 2006.

nodes.label: Marylin M. Rhie
nodes.summary: Marylin M. Rhie was a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She served as a professor at Smith College from circa 1974 to 2013.

nodes.label: Pramod Chandra
nodes.summary: Pramod Chandra (1930–2016) was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Georgetown and Mumbai. He served at the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, University of Chicago, and Harvard University as George P. Bickford Professor (1980–2004).

nodes.label: Richard Foltz
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・フォルツ
nodes.summary: Richard Foltz is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, religious, and historical studies who earned degrees from the University of Utah and Harvard University. He taught at several institutions before becoming Founding Director at Concordia University (~2006–2026).

nodes.label: Louise Child
nodes.summary: Louise Child is a religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Leeds and studied under Ringu Tulku. She held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

nodes.label: Tyler Dewar
nodes.summary: Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and under traditional teachers Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche and Acharya Tashi Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Mettanando Bhikkhu
nodes.summary: Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

nodes.label: Franz Xaver Erhard
nodes.summary: Franz Xaver Erhard is a scholar in Tibetology. He completed master's studies at the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin, and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Noa Gal
nodes.summary: Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy degree at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

nodes.id: I:Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
nodes.label: Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
variants: Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore
Buddhist and Pali College in Singapore

nodes.label: T. Y. Lee
nodes.summary: T. Y. Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mangala Vihara and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Andrew P. Tuck
nodes.summary: Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, John Pemberton, D. Dennis Hudson, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Alan Sponberg, and Richard Rorty.

nodes.label: Huaiyu Chen
nodes.summary: Huaiyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong and studied under Stephen F. Teiser, becoming assistant professor of Chinese religions at Arizona State University (~2007).

nodes.label: Sally McAra
nodes.summary: Sally McAra works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she studied under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

nodes.label: Karen Nero
nodes.description: professor of education in New Zealand
nodes.summary: Karen Nero held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (~2000-2008) and the University of Otago.

nodes.label: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung
nodes.summary: Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD from The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and studied under Toshiichi Endo.

nodes.label: Nikolai Solmsdorf
nodes.summary: Nikolai Solmsdorf specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard and held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Martin Lowenthal
nodes.summary: Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of Buddhist studies who trained under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

nodes.label: Signe Howell
nodes.summary: Signe Howell studied at SOAS University of London (~1974–1977) and the University of Oxford (~1977–1980), working in religious studies and other fields. She became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989 and taught Heidi Fjeld.

nodes.label: René Gothóni
nodes.summary: René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1970 to 1982, later held a post there from circa 1977 to 2014, and taught Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

nodes.label: Michael Pye
nodes.summary: Michael Pye is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and the University of Leeds (Ph.D., ca. 1972–1976), he held academic posts at Leeds, Lancaster, and as professor of religious studies at the University of Marburg.

nodes.label: Hung-Yi Yang
nodes.summary: Hung-Yi Yang is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon.

nodes.label: Penghao Sun
nodes.summary: Penghao Sun specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Leonard van der Kuijp as doctoral supervisor, Qingying Chen (2009–2011), Weirong Shen, Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Peter K. Bol, Jay Jasanoff, James Robson, Ryuichi Abe, and Jie Li.

nodes.id: I:Society for the Study of Japanese Religions
nodes.label: Society for the Study of Japanese Religions
variants: Society for the Study of Japanese Religions

nodes.label: Alva Noë
nodes.summary: Alva Noë is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford and Harvard University. He held faculty posts at the University of California, Santa Cruz (circa 1996–2003), University of California, Berkeley (circa 2003), and the City University of New York (circa 2010–2011).

nodes.label: Kuntala Bhattacharya
nodes.summary: Kuntala Bhattacharya specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA supervised by Prabal Kumar Sen and a PhD at Jadavpur University supervised by Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, holding a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Prabal Kumar Sen
nodes.summary: Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who taught Kuntala Bhattacharya. He has held posts at the University of Calcutta as a professor (attested 2009) and at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.

nodes.label: Yoshinori Takeuchi
nodes.description: Japanese historian of religion and philosopher (1913-2002)
nodes.summary: Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe, later serving there as professor (1959–1976) before teaching at Aichi Gakuin University (1976–1988).

nodes.label: Shu-chen Chen
nodes.summary: Shu-chen Chen worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and worked there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

nodes.label: Willy Vande Walle
nodes.jawiki: ウィリー・ヴァンドゥワラ

nodes.label: Youlan Feng
nodes.summary: Youlan Feng worked in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Peking University and Columbia University, among other institutions, and held posts at Tsinghua University (~1928-1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946-1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1946-1947).

nodes.label: Sohanwela Pemarathana
nodes.summary: Sohanwela Pemarathana is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore (attested 2004).

nodes.label: Joy Cecile Brennan
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Brennan completed a PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

nodes.label: Paul Mendes-Flohr
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies, philosophy, and history, Paul Mendes-Flohr studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

nodes.label: Zhiyi Yang
nodes.summary: Zhiyi Yang is a sinologist who studied at Peking University, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern). Her posts include assistant researcher at Erlangen-Nürnberg and an affiliation at Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Kazuharu Mizuno
nodes.summary: Kazuharu Mizuno is a scholar in geography and archaeology. He earned a BA at Nagoya University (~1978–1982), a master's at Hokkaido University (~1982–1985), and a DSc at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1985–1990), later becoming a professor at Kyoto University (~2009).

nodes.label: Guge Tsering Gyalpo
variants: Gu ge Tshe ring rgyal po

nodes.label: Martha Nussbaum
variants: マーサ・クレイヴン・ヌスバウム
nodes.summary: Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at Wellesley College, NYU (B.A.), Harvard (M.A.), and under Bernard Williams. She held positions at Harvard, Oxford, Brown, UNU-WIDER, and became Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

nodes.label: Yasuo Yuasa
nodes.summary: Yasuo Yuasa specialized in philosophy and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

nodes.label: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
variants: American School of Classical Studies at Athens
School of Classical Studies at Athens

nodes.label: Inyoung Chung
nodes.summary: Inyoung Chung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2008), where the doctoral supervisor was Paul Groner.

nodes.label: Seunghak Koh
nodes.summary: Seunghak Koh specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2011 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later serving as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

nodes.label: James Legge
nodes.summary: James Legge was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1831–1835), and Highbury College (~1836–1839). He was appointed professor at the University of Oxford in 1876.

nodes.label: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Palpung Sherabling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He became abbot of Palpung Sherabling Monastery around 1994.

nodes.label: Lars Fogelin
nodes.summary: Lars Fogelin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli and held positions at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

nodes.label: Wenjie Duan
nodes.summary: Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) worked in Buddhist studies and archaeology, studying at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts. He held several leadership roles at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946, serving as director in 1991.

nodes.label: Helen Wang
nodes.summary: Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.

nodes.label: David A. Hall
nodes.summary: David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his doctorate from the University of California, Berkeley in 1990 and studied under Shoshin Ichishima in 1976. He held posts at Taisho University and Montgomery College.

nodes.label: Guy G. Stroumsa
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Guy G. Stroumsa studied at Paris, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, EPHE, and Harvard. He held positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 1978 to 2009 and served as professor at Oxford (2009–2013).

nodes.label: John Daishin Buksbazen
nodes.summary: John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and under Taizan Maezumi, Bernie Glassman, and Wendy Egyoku Nakao (attested 2002).

nodes.label: Bernie Glassman
nodes.summary: Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist studies. He earned degrees at Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn and UCLA, and studied under traditional teachers Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.

nodes.label: Zen Center of Los Angeles
variants: Buddha Essence Temple, the Zen Center of Los Angeles

nodes.label: Soiku Shigematsu
nodes.summary: Soiku Shigematsu (1943–) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. In Buddhist studies and literature, he held professorships at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Tuyet
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Tuyet specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at Punjabi University under Inder Mohan Singh (attested 2012) and also studied under traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Punjabi University
variants: Guru Gobind Singh Department of Religious Studies, Punjabi University, Patiala

nodes.label: Wei Lin
nodes.summary: Wei Lin, a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies, studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Her career includes posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum and Transylvania University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Dagmar Schwerk
nodes.summary: Dagmar Schwerk works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at the University of Hamburg from approximately 2012 to 2017 under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk.

nodes.label: Eva Wilden
nodes.summary: Eva Wilden is an Indologist who earned her degrees and habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1986–2003). She held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and the University of Hamburg (2017).

nodes.label: Julie Gifford
nodes.summary: Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds. She held an academic post at Miami University.

nodes.label: Scott A. Mitchell
nodes.summary: Scott A. Mitchell is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Marybeth White
nodes.summary: Marybeth White is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned an honors degree at York University and pursued doctoral studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Hiroshi Araki
nodes.summary: Hiroshi Araki specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD, at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at Osaka University and as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

nodes.label: Tao Jiang
nodes.summary: Tao Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo and was an associate professor of religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Margarita Kleibel
nodes.summary: Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under her master's supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2010) and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

nodes.label: Siu-tong Kwan
nodes.summary: Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, and also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.

nodes.label: Marc-Henri Deroche
nodes.summary: Marc-Henri Deroche specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He pursued doctoral studies supervised by Matthew T. Kapstein, and studied under Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

nodes.label: Heather Stoddard
nodes.summary: Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London and was supervised by Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, also studying under D. C. Lau and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

nodes.label: In-gun Kang
nodes.summary: In-gun Kang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Kang completed an STL at Santa Clara, an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and a doctorate at Heythrop College under Michael Barnes.

nodes.label: Aloysius Pieris
nodes.summary: Aloysius Pieris was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Bernard de Give, at Sacred Heart College, University of London, and Pontifical Theological Faculty of Southern Italy, earning doctorates from Sri Lanka and Tilburg. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre.

Jesuit School of Theology at Santa Clara University

nodes.label: Jungmin Ha
nodes.summary: Jungmin Ha is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed a master's at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University (attested 2016) under the supervision of Stanley Abe.

nodes.label: Stanley Abe
nodes.summary: Stanley Abe works in the fields of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.

nodes.label: Wei-Cheng Lin
nodes.summary: Wei-Cheng Lin works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, when he took up a post at the University of Chicago.

nodes.label: Rafał Jan Felbur
nodes.summary: Rafał Jan Felbur is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued his doctoral studies at Stanford University under Paul Harrison, also studying under John R. McRae and Luis O. Gómez.

nodes.label: Vincent Lefèvre
nodes.summary: Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle under Bruno Dagens. He has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

nodes.label: Jean-François Jarrige
nodes.summary: Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the École du Louvre and the University of Paris. He served as director (1986–2004) and president (circa 1986–2008) of the Musée Guimet.

nodes.label: Namita Das
nodes.summary: Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Namita Das completed a PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

nodes.label: Alexander C. Soper
nodes.image: Milo Cleveland Beach presenting Freer Medal to Alexander C. Soper.jpg
nodes.summary: Alexander C. Soper was a scholar of archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hamilton College and Princeton University before holding long-term faculty appointments at Bryn Mawr College and New York University.

variants: The Institute of Ismaili Studies, London

nodes.label: Kang-yuan Sung
nodes.summary: Kang-yuan Sung specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Calgary (attested 1999) under MA supervisor Anthony W. Barber and teacher Leslie S. Kawamura.

nodes.label: Edwin F. Bryant
nodes.summary: Edwin F. Bryant (1957–) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1991–1997). He taught at Harvard University (~1998–2003) and served as Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).

nodes.label: Koenraad Elst
nodes.summary: Koenraad Elst is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned an MA at KU Leuven and studied at Banaras Hindu University between ~1988 and 1992.

nodes.label: Braj Basi Lal
nodes.summary: Braj Basi Lal was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad and trained under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

nodes.label: Diane A. Lichtenstein
nodes.summary: Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

nodes.label: Jim G. Shaffer
nodes.summary: Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Arizona State University (B.A., ~1961–1965) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D., ~1966–1972). He served as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University from ~1972 to 2010.

nodes.label: Chris Clark
nodes.summary: Chris Clark is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon by 2015, where he later served as an honorary associate (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Amod Jayant Lele
nodes.summary: Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

nodes.label: Michele Martin
nodes.summary: Michele Martin (born 1942) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

nodes.label: Trevor Ling

nodes.label: Yijie Tang
nodes.summary: Yijie Tang (1927–2014) worked in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1947–1951), he served there as a professor (~1956–2014), held a post at Stanford (~1990–1991), and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

nodes.label: Andrew William Kennedy
nodes.summary: Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

nodes.label: Philip A. Mellor
nodes.summary: Philip A. Mellor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989 and served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of Humanities at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Chie Ikeya
nodes.summary: Chie Ikeya is a historian and archaeologist who studied under David K. Wyatt, earning a Ph.D. from Cornell University in 2006.

nodes.label: Jan Peter F. Hintelmann
nodes.summary: Jan Peter F. Hintelmann specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper and also studied under traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

nodes.label: Marianne Pieper
nodes.summary: Marianne Pieper studied at the University of Hamburg and completed her Habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held posts at the University of Kassel (1994–1996) and the University of Hamburg (1990–1994; professor of sociology 1996–2015).

nodes.label: Eviatar Shulman
nodes.summary: Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1999–2008), where he later held posts in 2009 and served as department chairman around 2011.

nodes.label: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul
nodes.summary: Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Huishan Lin
nodes.summary: Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kuo-wei Liu, also studying under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.

nodes.label: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah
nodes.summary: Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard under Bryce Ryan. He taught at Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and was Rabb Professor of Anthropology at Harvard (1976–2001).

nodes.label: Peter J. Wilson
nodes.summary: Peter J. Wilson (1933–2005) earned his PhD at Yale University (~1957–1961). He taught at Yale (~1961–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1965–1970), Bennington College, and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).

nodes.label: Linda Penkower
nodes.summary: Linda Penkower specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1993 and served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).

nodes.label: Don A. Pittman
nodes.summary: Don A. Pittman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago. He was attested as a faculty member at Texas Christian University in 2001.

nodes.label: Chun-min Yen
nodes.summary: Chun-min Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello (attested 2004), having also studied under Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.

nodes.label: Stephen A. Murphy
nodes.summary: Stephen A. Murphy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who completed his MA at SOAS University of London and conducted doctoral research under the supervision of Elizabeth Howard Moore.

nodes.label: East China Normal University
variants: Center for China Studies Abroad at East China Normal University

nodes.label: Colin Leslie Dean
nodes.summary: Colin Leslie Dean studied philosophy and religious studies under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (both attested 2002).

nodes.label: Martina Draszczyk
nodes.summary: Martina Draszczyk is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Lambert Schmithausen and completed her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), where she also held an academic post.

nodes.label: Dragana Majhen
nodes.summary: Dragana Majhen specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Shang Shung Institute
variants: International Shang-Shung Institute for Tibetan Studies

nodes.label: Takami Inoue
nodes.summary: Takami Inoue works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

nodes.label: Imre Hamar
nodes.summary: Imre Hamar is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a Professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and a visiting professor at Otani University.

nodes.label: Mónika Kiss
nodes.summary: Mónika Kiss works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. A PhD student in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University, she studied under advisor Masanori Yamaji as well as Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

nodes.label: G. V. Aston
nodes.summary: G. V. Aston is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Aston earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy at the University of Canterbury between 1986 and 2004, studying under doctoral supervisor Jack Copeland and teacher Paul Harrison.

nodes.label: Jack Copeland
nodes.description: New Zealand (British born) philosopher, logician and historian of science
nodes.summary: Jack Copeland (born 1950) is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1975–1979). He held positions at the University of Portsmouth and the University of Canterbury, joining the latter in 1985.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Hoa
nodes.summary: Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Hoa completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Nam-lin Hur
nodes.summary: A scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history, Nam-lin Hur studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University (PhD) under Helen Hardacre. He held posts at Harvard University and the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Pori Park
nodes.summary: Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. She has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

nodes.label: Cornelis Jan Kuiken
nodes.summary: Cornelis Jan Kuiken works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under MA supervisor Jaap den Hollander and earned his PhD at the University of Groningen by 2002 under doctoral supervisors Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

nodes.label: Jan N. Bremmer
nodes.summary: Jan N. Bremmer (b. 1944) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, taught at Utrecht University (1974–1990), and held the Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Groningen (1990–2009).

nodes.label: Colette Sciberras
nodes.summary: Colette Sciberras is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and with traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Winston Kyan
nodes.summary: Winston Kyan is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Wu Hung (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas
variants: Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas, Rome
Angelicum, Pontifical University of the Dominican Order

nodes.label: Jay Holt Valentine
nodes.summary: Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD at Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

nodes.label: Walter Nowick
nodes.summary: Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies figure who attended the Juilliard School and studied under Zuigan Goto from 1950 to 1965. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

nodes.label: Nicole Vandier-Nicolas
nodes.summary: Nicole Vandier-Nicolas worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. She taught at the École du Louvre (~1966) and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO/École des langues orientales from ~1966 to 1977.

nodes.label: D. C. Lau
nodes.summary: D. C. Lau was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied under Xu Dishan at The University of Hong Kong and later attended the University of Glasgow. He held appointments at SOAS, University College London, the University of London, and CUHK.

nodes.label: Jeannine Auboyer
nodes.summary: Jeannine Auboyer was an Indologist and art historian educated at EPHE and the École du Louvre under Joseph Hackin, Paul Pelliot, and others. She was chief curator at Musée Guimet (1965–1980) and held a chair at École du Louvre.

nodes.label: Mauli Chand Prasad
nodes.summary: Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. He served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

nodes.label: Daniel Amadé Scheidegger
nodes.summary: Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

nodes.label: Mark Teeuwen
nodes.summary: Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD (~1989–1996) at Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University (1994–1999), and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

nodes.label: Martino Dibeltulo
nodes.summary: Martino Dibeltulo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2015) under the doctoral supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentorship of Ester Bianchi.

nodes.label: Gary Urton
nodes.summary: Gary Urton is an archaeologist and historian who studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) and held an endowed professorship at Harvard University (2012–2020).

nodes.label: Hongyue Guo
nodes.summary: Hongyue Guo is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo studied under teacher Xubang Qi and completed a PhD at Indiana University under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp, attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Yawen Yang
nodes.summary: Yawen Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Yang earned an MA from Fo Guang University, studying under supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Cynthia Col
nodes.summary: Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

nodes.label: Yongshan He
nodes.summary: Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

nodes.label: Brad Warner
nodes.summary: Brad Warner is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Kent State University and under Tim McCarthy, Gudō Wafu Nishijima, and Gyomay Kubose. He became head of Dogen Sangha International in 2007 and founded Dogen Sangha Los Angeles in 2012.

nodes.label: Joseph Marino
nodes.summary: Joseph Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017), where he studied under Collett Cox and doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon.

nodes.label: Christian Lee Novetzke
nodes.summary: Christian Lee Novetzke (born 1969) works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard, and Columbia University. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) before becoming a professor at the University of Washington in 2007.

nodes.label: John Crook
nodes.summary: John Crook was a scholar in tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe. He founded the Western Chan Fellowship and taught at the University of Bristol in 1977.

variants: Groupe de Recherches et d'Etudes sur le Zen of the Universite Bouddhique Europeene

nodes.label: Chöje Akong Tulku Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Chöje Akong Tulku Rinpoche (1939–2013) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he later served as abbot (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Liu Zaifu
nodes.summary: Liu Zaifu (1941–2026) was a scholar in Sinology and philosophy. After studying at Xiamen University (~1959–1963), he worked at CASS (1963, 1985–1989), and held posts at Chicago, Colorado, Stockholm, City University of Hong Kong, and HKUST.

nodes.label: Junko Minamoto
nodes.summary: Junko Minamoto works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University (around 1976–1980) and held a research post at Kansai University.

nodes.label: Baatr Kitinov
nodes.summary: Baatr Kitinov is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. in World History from Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor in the Department of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

nodes.label: Peoples' Friendship University of Russia
variants: Peoples' Friendship at University of Russia in Moscow

nodes.label: Uranchimeg Tsultem
nodes.summary: Uranchimeg Tsultem, a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and art history, earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. She held positions at the Mongolian State University of Arts and Culture, National University of Mongolia, and Indiana University Indianapolis.

nodes.label: Hürelbaatar Ujeed
nodes.summary: Hürelbaatar Ujeed works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge and serves as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

nodes.label: Uranchimeg B. Ujeed
nodes.summary: Uranchimeg B. Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

variants: Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in Bylakuppe, Mysore

nodes.label: Alicia Turner
nodes.summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Turner earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisors Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, also studying with Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

nodes.label: Northern Illinois University
variants: Center for Burma Studies, Northern Illinois University

nodes.label: Yoel Hoffmann
nodes.summary: Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University, and Kyoto University (PhD), and served as a professor of philosophy, Buddhism, and Japanese poetry at the University of Haifa (~1978–2003).

nodes.label: 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge
nodes.summary: 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche (1973), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

nodes.label: Ajahn Amaro
nodes.summary: Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College, London, and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in ~2010.

nodes.label: Hank Glassman
nodes.summary: Hank Glassman is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held faculty posts at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

nodes.label: Ryan Matthew Jacobson
nodes.summary: Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, D. Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Tenpa Gyaltsen, L. S. Summer, and three traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Sarah Harding
nodes.summary: Sarah Harding is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who trained under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpon Lama Tenpa. She held teaching posts at Naropa University (~1992–2018) and a fellowship at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000).

nodes.label: Amelia Hall
nodes.summary: Amelia Hall is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford. In 2019, she was attested as Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at Naropa University and online faculty at Central Michigan University.

nodes.label: Lama Tsultrim Allione
nodes.summary: Lama Tsultrim Allione is a scholar and practitioner in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a master's degree at Antioch University, studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and the 16th Karmapa, and founded Tara Mandala in 1993.

nodes.label: Elijah Sacvan Ary
nodes.summary: Elijah Sacvan Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University (~2001–2007) under supervisors Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp, as well as Charles Hallisey and Geshe Karma Sonam.

nodes.label: St Bartholomew's Hospital Medical College
variants: St Bartholomew's Medical School, London University

nodes.label: Cynthea J. Bogel
nodes.summary: Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburo Mizuno and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Keizaburo Mizuno
nodes.summary: Keizaburo Mizuno is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He worked at Tokyo National Museum, Tokyo University of the Arts, Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art, and the Hanzomon Museum.

nodes.label: Katharina Sabernig
nodes.summary: Katharina Sabernig works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Vienna by 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.

nodes.label: Medical University of Vienna
variants: Center for Public Health, Medical University of Vienna

nodes.label: Claudia Weber
nodes.summary: Claudia Weber is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

nodes.label: Gregor Ahn
nodes.summary: Gregor Ahn is a religious studies scholar who studied at Bonn and Copenhagen under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. He taught at Münster and Tartu before serving as Professor of Comparative Religion at Heidelberg University from 1996 to 2025.

nodes.label: Michael Hookham
nodes.summary: Michael Hookham works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa (1965) and Dilgo Khyentse, and he founded the Longchen Foundation.

nodes.label: Fred Pfeil
nodes.summary: Fred Pfeil (1949–2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned degrees from Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973), and taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (~1985–2005).

nodes.label: Karen Cheatham
nodes.summary: Karen Cheatham is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree from the Graduate Theological Union and a doctoral degree from the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Amber D. Carpenter
nodes.summary: Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte, among others. Her career includes posts at the University of York, Einstein Forum, and an associate professorship at Yale-NUS College.

nodes.label: Rachael Wiseman
nodes.summary: Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York. She was appointed as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool around 2014.

nodes.label: Bronwyn Finnigan
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Bronwyn Finnigan studied at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, completing doctoral research under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop. She held posts at Auckland (~2008–2014), Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

nodes.label: Christopher Kelley
nodes.summary: Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University, where he co-founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. He has taught at Columbia, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

nodes.label: Heidi I. Köppl
nodes.summary: Heidi I. Köppl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

nodes.label: Eugen Pander
nodes.summary: Eugen Pander was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1873–1876) and served at Tongwen Guan in 1881 as a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German.

nodes.label: Qiang Ning
nodes.summary: Qiang Ning is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who earned a doctorate under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. Ning taught at Yale, San Diego State, and the University of Michigan, and held a research post at Dunhuang Academy.

nodes.label: Shuhong Chang
nodes.summary: Shuhong Chang was a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist. He studied in France and China, taught at Zhejiang University and the National Beiping Art School, and held leadership roles at the Dunhuang Academy from 1942, becoming honorary director.

nodes.label: Ives Waldo
nodes.summary: Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988.
