nodes.label: Starr King School for the Ministry
variants: Starr King School for the Ministry

nodes.label: Masaaki Sugiyama
nodes.summary: Masaaki Sugiyama was a historian and scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University (circa 1970–1978) and taught at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1983 to 1992.

nodes.label: Sukhlal Sanghvi
nodes.description: Jain Scholar and Philosopher from India
nodes.summary: Sukhlal Sanghvi (1880–1978) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Balakrishna Mishra. He served as professor of Indian philosophy at Gujarat Vidyapith and held the Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University from 1934 to 1944.

nodes.label: Brandon J. Harwood
nodes.summary: Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Louisville under advisor Patrick Arthur Pranke, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Patrick Arthur Pranke
nodes.summary: Patrick Arthur Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis O. Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.

nodes.label: Andree Dominique Messent
nodes.summary: Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.

nodes.label: Tan Poh Beng
nodes.summary: Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under supervisors Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, also studying under Sumanasiri and Shengshou.

nodes.label: Ayya Khema
nodes.summary: Ayya Khema was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Matara Sri Ñāṇarāma. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma and Sakyadhita, and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.

nodes.label: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh
nodes.native: ฉัตรสุมาลย์ กบิลสิงห์
nodes.summary: Chatsumarn Kabilsingh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities, and served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University (~1973–2000).

nodes.label: Thích Thiện Châu
nodes.summary: Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He pursued his education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1967–1971) and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1970–1977), where he completed his doctoral dissertation.

nodes.label: Tulana Research Centre
variants: Tulana-Forschungszentrum (Tulana Research Center for Encounter and Dialogue)
Tulana Research Centre for Encounter and Dialogue

nodes.label: Elizabeth J. Harris
nodes.summary: Elizabeth J. Harris is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate (~1988–1993) from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and Kelaniya under Ananda Guruge and Y. Karunadasa, later working at Birmingham (~2014).

nodes.label: Hla Pe
nodes.summary: Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon, UCL, and SOAS. At SOAS University of London, he taught Burmese language and culture beginning in 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.

nodes.label: Gisela Emma Full
nodes.summary: Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she held research fellow positions at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

nodes.label: European University Viadrina
variants: フランクフルト（オーダー）大学

nodes.label: Samueli Institute
variants: Samueli-Institute of Brain, Mind and Healing

nodes.label: Mingyu Fu
nodes.summary: Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Rob Nairn
nodes.summary: Rob Nairn was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied law and criminology at the University of Zimbabwe, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, and the University of London. He held posts as senior lecturer at the University of Zimbabwe and professor at the University of Cape Town.

nodes.id: I:Buddhist Association of the United States
nodes.label: Buddhist Association of the United States
variants: Buddhist Association of the United States

nodes.label: Joey Hung
nodes.summary: Joey Hung (b. 1991) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. Hung has held an academic post at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

nodes.label: Vidya Dehejia
nodes.summary: Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's College, Newnham College, and the University of Cambridge. She served as chief curator at the Smithsonian Institution and as a professor of Indian art at Columbia University.

nodes.label: American Museum of Natural History
variants: アメリカ自然史博物館

nodes.label: James Miller
nodes.summary: James Miller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Cambridge (1997) and a PhD from Boston University (2000). He was attested as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast in 2014.

nodes.label: Emily T. Yeh
nodes.summary: Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993, 1995) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She joined the faculty of the University of Colorado around 2003.

nodes.label: John Grim
nodes.summary: John Grim is a religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Fordham University under Thomas Berry. He held a professorship at Bucknell University (attested 2005) and served as Senior Lecturer and Research Scholar at Yale University.

nodes.label: Surendra Man Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Tribhuvan University under the supervision of Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervision of Ranjana Bajracharya.

nodes.label: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya
nodes.summary: Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

nodes.label: Yungfen Ma
nodes.summary: Yungfen Ma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Jeffrey K. Riegel
nodes.summary: Jeffrey K. Riegel is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley from 1979 to 2007, and subsequently held a post at the University of Sydney from 2007 to 2017.

nodes.label: Paul Debes
nodes.summary: Paul Debes was a German scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), co-founded and served on the board of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), and founded the Deutsche Buddhistische Union (1955).

nodes.label: Hari Shankar Prasad
nodes.summary: Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, as well as under Ramakant Tripathi and doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong.

nodes.label: Mark A. Nathan
nodes.summary: Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD from UCLA (2010) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and has held posts at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (all attested 2010).

nodes.label: Leopold Pospisil
nodes.summary: Leopold Pospisil (1923–2021) earned degrees from Charles University, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and curator of anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956–1993).

nodes.label: Harold C. Conklin
nodes.summary: Harold C. Conklin (1926–2016) worked in linguistics and anthropology. He studied at UC Berkeley and Yale University, later teaching at Columbia University (1955) and serving as professor at Yale (1962–1996) and curator at the Peabody Museum (1974–1996).

nodes.label: Mirjan Damaška
nodes.summary: Mirjan Damaška (born 1931) studied at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD 1960). He held posts at Zagreb, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale Law School.

nodes.label: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak
nodes.jawiki: ヤン・ユリウス・ローデウェイク・ドイフェンダック
nodes.summary: Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a sinologist who studied at Leiden, the Sorbonne, and Humboldt University under Jan Jakob Maria de Groot and others. He served as professor of Chinese language and literature at Leiden University from 1930 to 1954.

nodes.label: Hitoshi Miyake
nodes.summary: Hitoshi Miyake (1933–) is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1951–1955) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1962), later serving as a professor at Keio University (~1972–1999) and Kokugakuin University (~1999–2004).

nodes.label: Helena Blankleder
nodes.summary: Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, as attested in 1999.

nodes.label: Marek Zemánek
nodes.summary: Marek Zemánek works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and completed his dissertation at Charles University under the supervision of Radek Chlup.

nodes.label: Thich Nhat Tu
nodes.image: TT. Thích Nhật Từ phát biểu trong lễ bế mạc Đại lễ Vesak 2014.JPG

nodes.label: Tan Yun-shan
nodes.summary: Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After studying at institutions including Hunan First Normal University and under Taixu, he co-founded Visva-Bharati University, serving as Professor of Chinese Studies there (~1937–1968).

nodes.label: Kshitimohan Sen
variants: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.jawiki: クシティモハン・セン
nodes.summary: Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy after earning an M.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He served in the Chamba State Education Department (~1904–1908) and held long-term posts at Visva-Bharati University, serving as Adhyaksha from 1953 to 1954.

nodes.label: Paul Kingsbury
nodes.summary: Paul Kingsbury, active in linguistics and Indology, completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

nodes.label: John Stevens
nodes.description: Buddhist priest, teacher of Buddhist studies and aikido teacher

nodes.label: Hui-tzu Lu
nodes.summary: Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Jing-shen Tao and with traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi (attested 2003).

nodes.label: Piotr Klafkowski
nodes.summary: Piotr Klafkowski was a Polish scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski and received instruction from Lozang Jamspal, Geleg Gyatso, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Jerzy Bańczerowski
nodes.summary: Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań. He later served there as head of the Department of General and Comparative Linguistics (1969) and as professor from 1977 to 1991.

nodes.label: Adelheid Mette
nodes.summary: Adelheid Mette was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held professorships at the University of Munich before serving as Indology chair at the University of Münster (1988–2000).

nodes.label: Olav Hackstein
nodes.summary: Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Pennsylvania, Freiburg (Dr. phil. 1993), and Halle-Wittenberg (Habilitation 1999), later becoming full professor at the University of Munich in 2008.

nodes.label: Linda Learman
nodes.summary: Linda Learman works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She was a doctoral student of Robert P. Weller and had postdoctoral mentorship under Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).

nodes.label: University of Nebraska at Omaha
variants: ネブラスカ大学オマハ校

nodes.label: Hajime Tanabe
nodes.summary: Hajime Tanabe worked in philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and later under Kitaro Nishida, Heinrich Rickert, and Martin Heidegger. His main academic posts were at Tohoku University (1913) and Kyoto University (1919–1945).

nodes.label: Cuma Ozkan
nodes.summary: Cuma Ozkan works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Stephan Marcus Salzberg
nodes.summary: Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

nodes.id: I:Institute for the Study of American Religion
nodes.label: Institute for the Study of American Religion
variants: Institute for the Study of American Religion

nodes.label: Edmund Leach
nodes.summary: Edmund Leach worked in religious studies and related fields. Educated at Cambridge and the London School of Economics, he lectured at LSE (~1947-1953) and served as Professor at Cambridge (1953-1978), Provost of King's College (1966-1979), and RAI President (1971-1975).

nodes.label: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt
nodes.summary: Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University (attested 1990).

nodes.label: Yanfei Zhou
nodes.summary: Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. She earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

nodes.label: Yiliang Zhou
nodes.summary: Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, Harvard University, and under Yinke Chen (~1935–1939). From ~1952 to 2001, he served as a professor at Peking University.

nodes.label: Yinke Chen
nodes.summary: Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, Sinologist, and linguist. Educated abroad, including at Berlin, Harvard, and under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Heinrich Lüders, he held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.

nodes.label: Eberhard Fischer
nodes.image: The President, Smt. Pratibha Devisingh Patil presenting the Padma Shri Award to Dr. Eberhard Fischer, at an Investiture Ceremony-II, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, in New Delhi on April 04, 2012.jpg
nodes.summary: Eberhard Fischer (born 1941) is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned his PhD at the University of Basel. He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and later as president of the Rietberg-Gesellschaft.

nodes.label: Université libre de Bruxelles
variants: Center for Study of South and Southeast Asia at the University of Brussels

nodes.label: Chack-fan Lee
nodes.summary: Chack-fan Lee (born 1945) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at The University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1969–1972), later serving as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at HKU (1994–2015).

nodes.label: Tso Sze-bong
nodes.summary: Tso Sze-bong is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982) under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

nodes.label: Loukram Ibempishak Devi
nodes.summary: Loukram Ibempishak Devi specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma (attested 1999) and also studied under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

nodes.label: Kazuhiro Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Yamamoto works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Silpakorn University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya.

nodes.label: Chirapat Prapandvidya
nodes.summary: Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is an Indology scholar who founded Silpakorn University, served as its director, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

nodes.label: Phra Sigambhirayan
nodes.summary: Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BLA from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an MA from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. He served as an associate professor at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2013.

nodes.label: Riika J. Virtanen
nodes.summary: Tibetologist Riika J. Virtanen pursued doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu K. Riikonen, and also studied under teacher Sangye Tandar Naga.

nodes.label: Hannu K. Riikonen
nodes.summary: Hannu K. Riikonen studied at the University of Helsinki from 1967 to 1978. He later served there as a professor from approximately 1999 to 2014.

nodes.label: Sandra Hochwarter
nodes.summary: Sandra Hochwarter works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Anne MacDonald and completed her master's thesis under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Thanissaro Bhikkhu
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Thanissaro Bhikkhu studied at Oberlin College (~1967–1971) and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1972–1986). He co-founded Metta Forest Monastery, serving as its abbot beginning in 1993.

nodes.label: August Johan Bernet Kempers
nodes.image: Installatie nieuwe directeur van het Rijksmuseum voor Volkenkunde Het Nederland, Bestanddeelnr 909-2587.jpg
nodes.summary: August Johan Bernet Kempers specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Leiden University. He served as director of Dinas Purbakala (1947–1953) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum and the University of Amsterdam.

nodes.label: Jan Fontein
nodes.summary: Jan Fontein (1927–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin, served as a curator at the Rijksmuseum, and was curator of Asiatic art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

nodes.label: Theodoor van Erp
nodes.image: Portret van Dr Th. van Erp, luitenant der genie en restaurator van de Borobudur, RP-F-2013-61-1.jpg

nodes.label: Madhu Khanna
nodes.summary: Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She held posts attested in 2012 at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

nodes.label: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Suk Fun Ng
nodes.summary: Suk Fun Ng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, having also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Sarat Sarma
nodes.summary: Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Manipur University, studying under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jan Dolensky
nodes.summary: Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Ming Mei
nodes.summary: Ming Mei works in Sinology and history and archaeology. She earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin, and also studied at SOAS University of London under Andrey Terentyev.

nodes.label: Andrey Terentyev
nodes.summary: Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970–1975) and worked at the Museum of the History of Religion from ~1977 to 1998.

nodes.label: Wulstan Fletcher
nodes.summary: Wulstan Fletcher is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).

nodes.label: Pei-jung Wu
nodes.summary: Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from National Taiwan University and completed her PhD at UCLA in 2002 under Donald F. McCallum, also studying under Hironobu Kohara, Shou-chien Shih, and Yu-min Lee.

nodes.label: Ng-Fung Yuen
nodes.summary: Ng-Fung Yuen specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Yuen earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tsoknyi Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Adeu Rinpoche. He founded the Pundarika Foundation and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

nodes.label: Ling Ji
nodes.summary: Ling Ji is a scholar in Sinology who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore, attested in 2014, under the supervision of Chi Xiao and Yuet Keung Lo.

nodes.label: Thomas Berry
nodes.summary: Thomas Berry was a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Indology. He studied at the Catholic University of America (~1944–1948) and held posts at the City University of New York and Fordham University (~1966–1979).

nodes.label: Notto R. Thelle
nodes.summary: Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions and held a post at the University of Oslo from 1986 to 2011.

nodes.id: I:NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
nodes.label: NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
variants: National Christian Council (NCC) Center for the Study of Japanese Religions
NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in Kyōto

nodes.label: Kiattisak Ponampon
nodes.summary: In Buddhist studies, he earned his MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and also studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, John Kieschnick, Barend J. ter Haar, and Seishi Karashima (2013).

nodes.label: Somchai Thanavuddho
nodes.native: สมชาย ฐานวุฑฺโฒ

nodes.label: Ann Grodzins Gold
nodes.summary: Ann Grodzins Gold is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed her B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1971–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).

nodes.label: Mumon Yamada
variants: Mumon Yamada (山田 無文, Yamada Mumon)
nodes.summary: Mumon Yamada was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofukuji, president of Hanazono University from 1949 to 1978, and director of the Institute for Zen Studies.

nodes.id: I:First Zen Institute of America in Japan
nodes.label: First Zen Institute of America in Japan
variants: First Zen Institute of America in Kyoto

nodes.label: Gianpaolo Vetturini
nodes.summary: Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

nodes.label: Keir Strickland
nodes.summary: Keir Strickland works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Durham University under Robin Coningham and studied at the University of the Highlands and Islands, later working at the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University.

nodes.label: Zeng Yang
nodes.summary: Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Tsering Shakya
nodes.summary: Tsering Shakya is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS University of London, where he was a research fellow (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and held a research chair at the University of British Columbia.

nodes.label: Kang-nam Oh
nodes.summary: Kang-nam Oh works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yun-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

nodes.label: Hsu-feng Lee
nodes.summary: Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin. Lee completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Filippo Marsili
nodes.summary: Filippo Marsili is a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley, under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, and Arcangela Santoro, and later held a post at Saint Louis University.

nodes.label: Jane Bunnag
nodes.summary: Jane Bunnag is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of London by 1969, where she studied under the supervision of E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

nodes.label: E. Michael Mendelson
nodes.description: American poet, essayist, anthropologist, and translator (1928–2024)
nodes.summary: E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his education at the University of Cambridge (King's College), the University of Paris (~1951–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).

nodes.label: Barbara E. Ward
nodes.summary: Barbara E. Ward was a Sinologist and anthropologist. She studied at Newnham College, University of London, and the LSE. She held posts at the University of London, Cambridge, CUHK (1978–1982), and headed the International Institute for Environment and Development (1973).

nodes.label: David M. DiValerio
nodes.summary: David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the School for International Training and the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2015.

nodes.label: Hubert Decleer
nodes.summary: Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Regent Hotel and Technical School, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte (1975). He later held academic directorship and advisory roles at the School for International Training.

nodes.label: Maria Heim
nodes.summary: Maria Heim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Reed College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey. She served as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

nodes.label: Lloyd W. Pflueger
nodes.summary: Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University, attested in 2015.

nodes.label: Kshanika Saha
nodes.summary: Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Calcutta (attested 1966) under the instruction of Nalinaksha Dutt.

nodes.label: Michael Baxandall
variants: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.jawiki: マイケル・バクサンドール
nodes.summary: Michael Baxandall was an art historian who studied at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held appointments at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute of Art, Cornell University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

nodes.label: Jean-Pierre Drège
nodes.summary: Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yves Hervouet and at INALCO. He served as president of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1998 to 2004.

nodes.id: I:Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition
nodes.label: Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition
variants: Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition

nodes.label: Mohammad Ashraf Dar
nodes.summary: Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology and history scholar. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.

nodes.label: Nyingcha Duoji
nodes.summary: Nyingcha Duoji works in Tibetology. He studied at Boston University and completed a PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.

nodes.label: Stephen Fuchs
nodes.summary: Stephen Fuchs (1908–2000) was an Indologist and anthropologist who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned a PhD from the University of Vienna. He lectured at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and founded the Anthropos Institute and the Institute of Indian Culture.

nodes.label: Ronald Neufeldt
nodes.summary: Ronald Neufeldt (born 1941) is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a long-term post at the University of Calgary (~1977–2006), where he served as Associate Professor in the Religious Studies Department around 1977.

nodes.label: Fumio Tamamuro
nodes.summary: Fumio Tamamuro specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University from circa 1954 to 1964 and subsequently held a post there from circa 1966 to 2006.

nodes.label: Yuan Ren
nodes.summary: Yuan Ren is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

nodes.label: Doris Unterthurner
nodes.summary: Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

nodes.label: Manfred Taube
nodes.summary: Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Friedrich Weller at Leipzig University (1949–1953), where he was appointed Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.

nodes.label: Diane L. Howard
nodes.summary: Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 1982, she was attested as a graduate student at McMaster University, where she studied under supervisor Graeme MacQueen.

nodes.label: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso
nodes.summary: Lama Yeshe Gyamtso works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Lama Norlha.

nodes.label: Douglas Fairchild Ober
nodes.summary: Douglas Fairchild Ober specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Harjot Oberoi
nodes.summary: Harjot Oberoi specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, taking up the chair for Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia in ~1987.

nodes.label: Ter Ellingson
nodes.description: American ethnomusicologist and professor of music
nodes.summary: A scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, Ter Ellingson studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979). He held a post at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

nodes.label: Alnis Dickson
nodes.summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dickson earned an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

nodes.label: Ösel Tendzin
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies practitioner Ösel Tendzin studied at Fordham University and under Swami Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He was executive vice president at Vajradhatu (1973) and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

nodes.label: Chamnong Adivadhanasit
nodes.summary: Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and other fields. He earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University, where he later served as a part-time instructor (attested 2012), and was a professor at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Lê Mạnh Thát
nodes.summary: Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He studied at Saigon University and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University from circa 1974 to 1975.

nodes.label: Pataraporn Sirikanchana
nodes.summary: Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and held a professorship at Thammasat University.

nodes.label: Holmes Welch
nodes.summary: Holmes Welch (1924–1981) worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1940–1957) under Francis Woodman Cleaves, and later served as a lecturer at both Harvard University and Yale University.

nodes.label: Nobumi Iyanaga
nodes.summary: Nobumi Iyanaga (born 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held positions at the University of Tokyo and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient's Tokyo Centre (2008–2014).

nodes.label: Phillip E. Bloom
nodes.summary: Phillip E. Bloom works in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. Attested in 2013, he completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

nodes.label: John Corrigan
nodes.summary: John Corrigan is a historian of religion who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at the University of Virginia, Harvard, and Arizona State, before joining Florida State University around 2001 as Distinguished Professor.

nodes.label: Françoise Robin
nodes.summary: Françoise Robin (born 1968) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She studied at INALCO and under Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). Her career includes leadership roles at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and INALCO (2011, 2013–2014).

nodes.label: Maurice Wiles
nodes.summary: Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar educated at Christ's College and Ridley Hall. He held posts at Ridley Hall, University of Ibadan, Clare College, and King's College London, before serving as Oxford's Regius Professor of Divinity (1970–1991).

nodes.label: Iso Kern
nodes.summary: Iso Kern is a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at UCLouvain, KU Leuven, Heidelberg, and National Taiwan University. He held positions at KU Leuven, Heidelberg University, and the universities of Zurich, Fribourg, and Bern.

nodes.label: David Fiordalis
nodes.summary: David Fiordalis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, later chairing religious studies at Linfield University.

nodes.label: Margaret J. Pearson
nodes.summary: Margaret J. Pearson is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She pursued her PhD at the University of Washington, studying under Hellmut Wilhelm and Burton Watson, and served as a Visiting Fellow at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1997.

nodes.label: Burton Watson
nodes.summary: Burton Watson (1925–2017) worked in sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and Columbia University under L. Carrington Goodrich, Chi-chen Wang, and Wm. Theodore de Bary, later holding posts at Columbia and Stanford University.

nodes.label: Victor Forte
nodes.summary: Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. He served as Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College, attested in 2007.

nodes.label: Robert Magliola
nodes.summary: A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Magliola earned his Ph.D. at Princeton. He held professorships at Purdue, Assumption University, and National Taiwan University, along with positions at Tamkang University and Columbia University.

nodes.label: Nile Green
nodes.summary: Nile Green is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~2005–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~2008).

nodes.label: Rinzin Thargyal
nodes.summary: Rinzin Thargyal was a Tibetology scholar who completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.

nodes.label: Fredrik Barth
nodes.summary: Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) was an anthropologist who studied at the University of Chicago and University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

nodes.label: John Buescher
nodes.summary: John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia by 1982. He was attested as Director at the Voice of America in 2001.

nodes.label: James Duerlinger
nodes.summary: James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of Iowa (~1971–2012).

nodes.label: Marshall Sahlins
nodes.jawiki: マーシャル・サーリンズ
nodes.summary: Marshall Sahlins was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), later holding faculty posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (1973).

nodes.label: Jinping Liao
nodes.summary: Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

nodes.label: Gary D. DeAngelis
nodes.summary: Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar, he served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at the College of the Holy Cross.

nodes.label: George Rupp
nodes.summary: George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies who was educated at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He served as president or faculty member at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).

nodes.label: Thomas Borchert
nodes.summary: Thomas Borchert works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Chicago, studying under teachers including Bruce Lincoln and Martin Riesebrodt, and became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont.

nodes.label: Anna Brown
nodes.summary: Anna Brown, active in religious studies, was attested in 2017 as a Zen student of Robert Kennedy. In 2017, she was attested as chair of political science and director of the social justice program at Saint Peter's University.

nodes.label: Robert Kennedy
nodes.description: American Jesuit priest, psychoanalyst and Zen rōshi

nodes.label: Hsiao-Lan Hu
nodes.summary: Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Temple University. Hu served as an associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Richard Sylvan
nodes.summary: Richard Sylvan was a philosopher who studied at Victoria University of Wellington (~1953–1958) and Princeton University (~1959–1963). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1963–1964) and the Australian National University, where he became a fellow in 1971.

nodes.label: Mei Ching Hsuan
nodes.summary: Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology, having completed a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and teacher Dieter Schuh.

nodes.label: Richard Rorty
variants: リチャード・マッケイ・ローティ
リチャード・ローティ
nodes.jawiki: リチャード・ローティ
nodes.summary: Richard Rorty was a philosopher educated at the University of Chicago and Yale University. He held professorships at Wellesley College, Princeton University (ca. 1962–1982), the University of Virginia (1982–1998), and Stanford University starting in 1998.

nodes.label: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse and founded the organization Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

nodes.label: Matthieu Ricard
nodes.summary: Matthieu Ricard (b. 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a doctorate at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob, studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Kangyur Rinpoche, and served as a board member of the Mind and Life Institute.

nodes.label: Meei-Hwa Chern
nodes.summary: Meei-Hwa Chern works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under John Raines (attested 2000) and served as a visiting researcher at Academia Sinica.

nodes.label: John Raines
nodes.image: John Curtis Raines (1933–2017) speaking at Temple University on October 11, 2014.png
nodes.summary: John Raines was a religious studies scholar who studied at Carleton College and Union Theological Seminary. He held an academic post at Temple University from ~1965 to 2011.

nodes.label: Karolinska Institute
variants: Department of Histology at the Karolinska Institute

nodes.id: I:National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
nodes.label: National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery
variants: National Hospital for the Paralysed and Epileptic

nodes.id: I:Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels
nodes.label: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels
variants: Research Institute for Brain and Blood Vessels

nodes.id: I:National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
nodes.label: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
variants: National Institute of Neurology and Psychiatry

nodes.label: Levi McLaughlin
nodes.summary: Levi McLaughlin works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Susumu Shimazono and earned his PhD at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. He was appointed associate professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

nodes.label: Takashi Nakao
nodes.summary: Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. Educated at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education, he held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College, Rissho University (emeritus professor, 1979–2002), and the Society of Japanese Historical Documents.

nodes.label: Axel Klein
nodes.summary: Axel Klein is a scholar of Japanology. He studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994), where he was a wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (1998–2007), later holding posts at the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011) and the University of Duisburg-Essen (2012).

nodes.label: Natasha Reichle
nodes.summary: Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, where she was supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams.

nodes.label: Amin Sweeney
nodes.summary: Amin Sweeney was a linguistics scholar who completed a doctorate at the University of London. He taught at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (1970–1977) and chaired South and Southeast Asian Studies at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1998.

nodes.label: Luboš Bělka
nodes.summary: Luboš Bělka works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from circa 1978 to 1983 and held a post there around 1993.

nodes.label: Masaryk University
variants: Institute for the Study of Religions at Masaryk University of Brno

nodes.label: Diana Lange
nodes.summary: Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet, and Humboldt Universities, with a habilitation from EPHE, she held research posts across Germany before becoming Professor of Central Asian History and Cultures at Humboldt in 2025.

nodes.label: Solomon George FitzHerbert
nodes.summary: Solomon George FitzHerbert is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford, where he was a Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies, and held a research post at the CNRS (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Kathleen McDonald
nodes.summary: Kathleen McDonald works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Lama Thubten Yeshe (~1974–1984), Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974), and Tenzin Gyatso, Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche (all attested 2010).

nodes.label: Adam Pearcey
nodes.summary: Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

nodes.label: Trulshik Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Trulshik Rinpoche was a Buddhist and Tibetology scholar. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and his students included Tenzin Gyatso, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Raimon Panikkar
nodes.summary: Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned doctorates from Complutense University and Pontifical Lateran University, and he held faculty positions at Complutense (1946–1953), Harvard (1966–1971), and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978).

nodes.label: Victor B. Lieberman
nodes.summary: Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned his BA at Yale University and his PhD at SOAS University of London. In 1984, he was appointed Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

nodes.label: Christopher Jon Jensen
nodes.summary: Christopher Jon Jensen is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, where he completed his PhD in 2018 under the supervision of James A. Benn.

nodes.label: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse
nodes.summary: Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse (born 1961) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under Dilgo Khyentse, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, the 16th Karmapa, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

nodes.label: Kathrin Holz
nodes.summary: Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

nodes.label: Eva K. Neumaier
nodes.summary: Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 2006, she was attested as a professor emeritus at the University of Alberta and Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Shri Singha Shedra
variants: Shri Singha Shedra at Dzogchen Monastery

nodes.label: Hammalawa Saddhatissa
nodes.image: Most Venerable Hammalawa Saddhatissa Maha Thera (1914–1990).jpg
nodes.summary: Hammalawa Saddhatissa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Maha Bodhi College, Banaras Hindu University, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990).

nodes.label: Dongmei Fang
nodes.summary: Dongmei Fang (1899–1977) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, under John Dewey, and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1921–1923), later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

nodes.label: Zhengyan
nodes.summary: Zhengyan is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who became a disciple of Yin Shun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.

nodes.label: Shenghai Li
nodes.summary: Shenghai Li specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Li earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., having also studied with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Ram Shankar Tripathi, and several Geshes.

nodes.label: Bradley L. Herling
nodes.summary: Bradley L. Herling is a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held an attested post at Marymount Manhattan College in 2008.

nodes.label: Sumi Lee
nodes.summary: Sumi Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and a PhD at UCLA (attested 2014) under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

nodes.label: Christmas Humphreys
nodes.summary: Christmas Humphreys (1901–1983) was an English scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as President of The Buddhist Society from circa 1924 to 1983 and taught Alan Watts.

nodes.label: Alan Watts
nodes.image: Alan Watts UVM 15 June 1958 Hon. D.D (cropped).jpg
nodes.summary: Alan Watts worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, studying under Christmas Humphreys, D. T. Suzuki, and Sokei-an Sasaki, among others. He was an Episcopal chaplain at Northwestern (1944–1950) and taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957).

nodes.label: Michael von Brück
nodes.description: German Protestant theologian and pastor, religious scientist and author, and Zen and yoga teacher
nodes.summary: Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed his Promotion at the University of Rostock (1968–1973). He held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Mehlman
nodes.summary: Working in French literature and philosophy, Jeffrey Mehlman held positions at Cornell, Yale, and Johns Hopkins. Around 1983, he became University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University.

nodes.label: Stephanie Kaza
nodes.summary: Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Oberlin College, Stanford University, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry. She served as a professor at the University of Vermont from 1991 to 2015.

nodes.label: Nguyen Thi Xinh
nodes.summary: Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She pursued her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).

nodes.label: Kathleen D. Morrison
nodes.summary: Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, later holding posts at Northwestern University (~1993–1995) and the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

nodes.label: Joseph Walser
nodes.summary: Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.

nodes.label: Khenpo Dazer
nodes.summary: Khenpo Dazer specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and held teaching posts at Shri Singha Shedra and Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

nodes.label: Hisao Kanaseki
nodes.summary: Hisao Kanaseki studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1941). He was a professor at Kobe University (~1961–1967), professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1967–1982), and professor at Komazawa University (~1982–1993).

nodes.label: King Chung Lo
nodes.summary: King Chung Lo specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Leipzig University under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.

nodes.label: Jinling He
nodes.summary: Jinling He specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.

nodes.label: Karma Sonam Palmo
nodes.summary: Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She completed Shastri and Acharya degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned a PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

nodes.label: Yui Suzuki
nodes.summary: Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Jeffrey Schoening
nodes.summary: Jeffrey Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he was supervised by Collett Cox and advised by Sanghasen Singh.

nodes.label: Chönyi Drolma
nodes.summary: Chönyi Drolma is a practitioner and scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Her education included studying under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

nodes.label: Tsering Gyaltsen
nodes.summary: Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

nodes.label: Mark Owen
nodes.summary: Mark Owen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

nodes.label: Elizabeth Stuart
nodes.summary: Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and was appointed director at the University of Winchester in 2021.

nodes.label: Jürgen Renn
nodes.description: German physicist, historian of science and university professor
nodes.summary: Jürgen Renn (born 1956) works in philosophy and history and archaeology. Educated at FU Berlin, Sapienza, and TU Berlin (PhD ~1987), he held posts at Boston University, became Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994), and joined MPI Geoanthropology (2022).

nodes.label: Yulian Zeng
nodes.summary: Yulian Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Graham E. Clarke
nodes.summary: Graham E. Clarke was a Tibetologist who held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Gelek
nodes.summary: Gelek is a Tibetology scholar who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center, attested in 1998. He has also held appointments as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and as a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

nodes.label: Angela Manderscheid
nodes.summary: Angela Manderscheid works in Tibetology and related fields. She has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

nodes.label: Rong Ma
nodes.summary: Rong Ma (born 1950) is a Tibetology and sociology scholar who earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University and served as Director of Peking University's Institute of Sociology and Anthropology (attested 1998).

nodes.label: Ronald D. Schwartz
nodes.summary: Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Hong Kong.

nodes.label: Klaus-Josef Notz
nodes.summary: Klaus-Josef Notz was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a theology diploma at Benediktbeuern, obtained a doctorate in theology at the University of Munich, and later served there as a lecturer in 1996.

nodes.id: I:Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München
nodes.label: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München
variants: Gesellschaft für europäisch-asiatische Kulturbeziehungen in München

nodes.label: Chüan-ying Yen
nodes.summary: Chüan-ying Yen specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University (attested 1986), where she studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

nodes.label: Chu-tsing Li
nodes.summary: Chu-tsing Li (1920–2014) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa, teaching at Nanking (1943–1947), Iowa (~1955–1966), and the University of Kansas (from 1966).

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Saunders
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. From circa 1921 to 1935, he served at the Pacific School of Religion and the University of California.

nodes.label: Takamaro Shigaraki
nodes.summary: Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Ryukoku University. He served as professor and president (1989–1995) at Ryukoku University, and was chairman and board director of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.

nodes.label: Ontario Tech University
variants: University of Ontario Institute of Technology

nodes.label: Vienna University of Economics and Business
variants: Institut für Wirtschafts- und Sozialgeschichte, Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien

nodes.label: Kuno Lorenz
nodes.summary: Kuno Lorenz (born 1932) is a philosopher who completed his PhD at Kiel University and habilitation at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

nodes.label: Claus Oetke
nodes.summary: Claus Oetke was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg, Kiel, and Vienna, and led the Department of Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014).

nodes.id: I:International Consortium for Research in the Humanities
nodes.label: International Consortium for Research in the Humanities
Rolf Scheuermann
nodes.summary: Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Chödrag Tenphel.

nodes.label: Edward H. Schafer
nodes.summary: Edward H. Schafer (1913–1991) was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi, and Harvard. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Sōen Shaku
nodes.summary: Sōen Shaku (1860–1919) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Keio University and under teachers including Kosen Imakita, whom he succeeded. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).

nodes.label: Paul Carus
nodes.summary: Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen (~1874–1876), taught at Kriegsschule Dresden (~1876–1881), and worked at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

nodes.label: Thomas B. Ellis
nodes.summary: Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Appalachian State University.

nodes.label: Jos Gommans
nodes.summary: Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. After a fellowship at the Dutch Research Council, he became an associate professor at Leiden University in 1993.

nodes.label: Dirk H. A. Kolff
nodes.summary: Dirk H. A. Kolff (born 1938) is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA and doctorate at Leiden University. He served at Leiden as a lecturer in 1967 and held the Chair of Indian History from 1971 to 2003.

nodes.label: Delhi School of Economics
variants: Delhi School of Economics, University of Delhi

nodes.label: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph
nodes.summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a scholar of Indology who studied at Sarah Lawrence, Harvard, and Radcliffe. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), was a professor at the University of Chicago (1964), and presided over the APSA (2003–2004).

nodes.id: I:Institute of Fine Arts, Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan
nodes.label: Institute of Fine Arts, Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan
variants: Fine Arts Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan
Fine Arts Institute, Academy of Sciences, Uzbekistan

nodes.label: Eiki Hoshino
nodes.summary: Eiki Hoshino (1943–) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He later served there as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (~1980–2013).

nodes.label: Phanit Jetjiravat
nodes.summary: Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he was advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

nodes.label: Prayoon Dhammacitto
nodes.native: พระธรรมโกศาจารย์

nodes.label: Yuri Mikhailovich Parfionovich
nodes.summary: Yuri Mikhailovich Parfionovich (1921–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology who studied under George de Roerich and traditional teacher Bidia Dandaron.

nodes.label: Francis N. J.
nodes.summary: Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a master's degree in ancient history and pursued doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier at the University of Calicut (attested 2002).

nodes.label: M. R. Raghava Varier
nodes.summary: M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Calicut, Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and was a professor at the University of Calicut (~1976–1996).

nodes.label: Rajan Gurukkal
nodes.summary: Rajan Gurukkal is a historian educated at Calicut University and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and held posts at JNU, Humboldt University, EHESS, and IISc.

nodes.label: Harold Scheub
nodes.summary: Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD). After posts at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was Evjue-Bascom Professor of Humanities Emeritus at Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2008).

nodes.label: Thomas J. Mazanec
nodes.summary: A scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies, Mazanec studied at Calvin University and the University of Colorado, completing doctoral work under supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser, and doctoral advisor Wang Ping.

nodes.label: Jeff Dolven
nodes.summary: Jeff Dolven studied at Oxford and earned his PhD in English from Yale. He held posts at Brandeis, the Harvard Society of Fellows, and Trinity College, Cambridge, and became professor of English at Princeton in 1999.

nodes.label: Joshua T. Katz
nodes.summary: Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD 1998). He served as Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute in 2022.

nodes.label: Nalini Bhushan
nodes.description: Andrew W. Mellon Professor in the Humanities at Smith College

nodes.label: Will B. Miller
nodes.summary: Will B. Miller is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Janet Gyatso, and he also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.

nodes.label: Wilburn Hansen
nodes.summary: Wilburn Hansen works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a master's program at the University of Colorado and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

nodes.label: Yu-kwan Ng
nodes.summary: Yu-kwan Ng studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD at McMaster University. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ng held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~2001-2016).

nodes.label: Bruce Charles Williams
nodes.summary: Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

nodes.label: Sodo Yokoyama
nodes.summary: Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957) and trained under teachers Kodo Sawaki and Eko Hashimoto.

nodes.label: Elena France Hanson
nodes.summary: Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey.

nodes.label: Katherine Anne Narraway
nodes.summary: Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she studied under MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

nodes.label: Cheryl A. Crowley
nodes.summary: Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar of Japanology. She studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

nodes.label: Roland Wenzlhuemer
nodes.summary: Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Salzburg and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Heidelberg, the University of Basel, and became Professor of Modern History at the University of Munich in 2017.

nodes.label: Dawa Tsering
nodes.summary: Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and held a post at Tibet University.

nodes.label: Dörte Kamarid
nodes.summary: Dörte Kamarid is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

nodes.label: Bhikkhu U Dhammissara
nodes.summary: Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he studied under MA supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Asen Balikci
nodes.summary: Asen Balikci earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1956. He worked at the Canadian Museum of History (1954), National Museum of Canada (~1957–1968), and was Professor of Ethnology at the Université de Montréal (1963–1993).

nodes.label: Bo-Kwang Han
nodes.summary: Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).

nodes.label: Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology
variants: Norwegian Institute for Palaeography and Historical Philology
