nodes.label: Regent Hotel and Technical School in Ostend
variants: Regent Hotel and Technical School in Ostend

nodes.label: Anne Nishimura Morse
nodes.summary: Anne Nishimura Morse is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology who earned her PhD at Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield. She held posts at Smith College (1988–1989) and as a visiting scholar at the Tokyo, Nara, and Kyoto national research institutes and museums.

nodes.label: Taka Yanagisawa
nodes.summary: Taka Yanagisawa (1926–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Japan Women's University and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.

nodes.label: Yutaka Hirata
nodes.summary: Yutaka Hirata (1931–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He obtained a doctorate from Kyushu University (-1996) and held positions at the Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.

nodes.label: Bunsaku Kurata
nodes.description: born:1918|died:1983|; 倉田, 文作, 1918-1983; Kurata, Bunsaku, 1918-....; 倉田, 文作; Kurata, Bunsaku
nodes.summary: Bunsaku Kurata (1918–1983) studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda University. Active in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he served at the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for Protection of Cultural Properties, and became Director of Nara National Museum in 1975.

nodes.label: Seiji Nemoto
nodes.summary: Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and was a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2001–2015).

nodes.label: Martin T. Adam
nodes.summary: Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

nodes.label: Michael P. Berman
nodes.summary: Michael P. Berman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2012.

nodes.label: Bernard Williams
nodes.jawiki: バーナード・ウィリアムズ (哲学者)
nodes.summary: Bernard Williams (1929–2003) was a philosopher who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at University College London from around 1959 to 1964 and at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1988 to 2003.

nodes.label: Bruno Galasek
nodes.summary: Bruno Galasek, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Julia A. B. Hegewald
nodes.summary: Specializing in Indology and architectural history, Hegewald completed a BA and PhD at SOAS, an MA at Oxford, and a habilitation at RWTH Aachen. In 2010, she became a professor at the University of Bonn.

nodes.label: Palmo Kyi
nodes.summary: Palmo Kyi is a Tibetologist who studied under Hanna Havnevik, Rinzin Thargyal, and supervisor Per Kværne.

nodes.label: Hiroo Sato
nodes.summary: Hiroo Sato specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1977), held a post at Morioka College (~1984–1987), and served as a professor at Tohoku University (~1997–2019).

nodes.label: Hsiu-hui Ji
nodes.summary: Hsiu-hui Ji specializes in Buddhist studies. Ji earned a master's degree at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

nodes.label: David Patt
nodes.summary: David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, completing his PhD under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa, attested in 1993.

nodes.label: Ngan-che Chan
nodes.summary: Ngan-che Chan works in Buddhist studies. Chan completed a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2007) and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

nodes.label: Geshe Lhakdor
nodes.summary: Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held posts at Tibet House (1986–1989), the University of British Columbia (2002), and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 2005.

nodes.label: Tenzin
nodes.summary: Tenzin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Philosophy degree at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik.

nodes.label: Meiping Li
nodes.summary: Meiping Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

nodes.label: Tao Jin
nodes.summary: Tao Jin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD in 2008 from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under the supervision of Alexander L. Mayer.

nodes.label: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck
nodes.summary: Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augsburg and the University of Munich, and held posts at Munich (1978–1988), the Munich School of Politics (1989–1991), and the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

nodes.id: I:Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt
nodes.label: Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt
Carlo Jamelle Harris
nodes.summary: Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA in philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

nodes.label: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto
nodes.summary: Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano.

nodes.label: Taryo Makita
nodes.summary: Taryo Makita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1936–1939). He held faculty posts at Kyoto University, Gifu University of Education, and Saitama Institute of Technology, where he served as president.

nodes.label: Richard P. Boyle
nodes.summary: Richard P. Boyle pursued graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was later affiliated with the University of New Mexico.

nodes.label: Tenshin Tanouye
nodes.summary: Tenshin Tanouye was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Sogen Omori and went on to found Chozen-ji.

nodes.label: Sogen Omori
nodes.summary: Sogen Omori (1904–1994) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy after studying at Nihon University and under traditional teachers including Seisetsu Seki. He served as a professor and president of Hanazono University (1978–1982).

nodes.label: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach
nodes.summary: Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

nodes.label: Johannes Beltz
nodes.summary: Johannes Beltz specializes in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies by 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under the supervision of Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst.

nodes.label: Esben Andreasen
nodes.summary: Esben Andreasen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

nodes.label: Daniel Borengasser
nodes.summary: Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley, attested in 2014.

nodes.label: Akiko Walley
nodes.summary: Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009). She held a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

nodes.label: Sonam Tsering
nodes.summary: Sonam Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his doctoral studies under Gray Tuttle and also studied under teachers including Namgyel Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Lobsang Trinley.

nodes.label: Günter Blamberger
nodes.description: German specialist in literature, university teacher and writer
nodes.summary: Günter Blamberger worked at the University of Kassel (~1993–1995) and held the Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne from circa 1995 to 2018.

nodes.label: Sudhir Kakar
nodes.summary: Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Trained at Gujarat, Mannheim, the Sigmund-Freud-Institut, and Vienna, he held posts at IIM Ahmedabad, IIT Delhi, and INSEAD, along with numerous international visiting professorships and fellowships.

nodes.label: Naman P. Ahuja
nodes.summary: Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, Naman P. Ahuja earned a doctorate from SOAS University of London. He was appointed Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

nodes.label: Jens Schlieter
nodes.summary: Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Josef Simon, later serving as professor at the University of Bern (circa 2009).

nodes.label: Yeshi Dhonden
nodes.summary: Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) was a specialist in Tibetology. He studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961, he founded Men-Tsee-Khang, serving as its director from 1961 to 1966.

nodes.label: Chi Chen Ho
nodes.summary: Chi Chen Ho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, earned a Ph.D. at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and served as a teaching assistant there.

nodes.label: K. Venkata Ramanan
nodes.summary: K. Venkata Ramanan was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Doctor of Letters at Visva-Bharati University, researched at Peking University (1947–1949) under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, and later taught at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Satyendra Nath Bose
variants: サティエンドラ・ナート・ボース
nodes.jawiki: サティエンドラ・ボース
nodes.summary: Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at Dhaka University (1921–1945), Calcutta University (1916; physics professor 1945–1956), and was Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

nodes.label: Walter Liebenthal
nodes.summary: Walter Liebenthal was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his doctorate at Breslau. He taught at Peking University, held research and visiting positions at Visva-Bharati, and was an honorary professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Tübingen.

nodes.label: Norman Fischer
nodes.description: American Soto Zen roshi, poet and Buddhist author practicing in the lineage of Shunryu Suzuki
nodes.summary: Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Colgate University, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, and trained under Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. He founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

nodes.label: Kichinosuke Ito
nodes.summary: In philosophy, he studied at First Higher School, University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), and University of Freiburg (1920). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918, 1923, 1926, 1930–1945), Hokkaido University (1947, 1950–1951), and Chuo University (1951–1958).

nodes.label: Anna Madelyn Hennessey
nodes.summary: Anna Madelyn Hennessey specializes in sinology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2011) under the doctoral supervision of William F. Powell.

nodes.label: Huynh Thi Ha Vy
nodes.summary: Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.

nodes.label: Douglas Gildow
nodes.summary: Douglas Gildow specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University (attested 2016), studying under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser and supervisor Qi Zhou.

nodes.label: Ülo Valk
nodes.summary: Ülo Valk, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1981–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu (~1995) and edited Numen (~2004–2013).

nodes.label: David Gonsalez
nodes.summary: David Gonsalez is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under teachers including Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra
nodes.summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery and trained under teachers including Yeshe Päldrup, Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen.

nodes.label: Dietmar Rothermund
nodes.summary: Dietmar Rothermund was a scholar of Indology and South Asian history who earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He held a visiting fellowship at ANU (1963) and was Chair of South Asian History at Heidelberg University (1968-2001).

nodes.label: Lama Palden Drolma
nodes.summary: Lama Palden Drolma is a specialist in Buddhist and religious studies who was trained by traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Tai Situ Rinpoche, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

nodes.label: Amar Singh
nodes.summary: Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teachers Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, and Alasdair Urquhart.

nodes.label: Alasdair Urquhart
nodes.summary: Alasdair Urquhart is a philosopher who completed his MA at the University of Edinburgh and his Ph.D. at the University of Pittsburgh. He taught at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and became an emeritus professor at the University of Toronto.

nodes.label: Tianshu Zhu
nodes.summary: Tianshu Zhu specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Educated at Northwest University (MA) and Ohio State University (PhD under John C. Huntington), Zhu has held posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Korea University, and Ohio State University.

nodes.label: Jacob N. Kinnard
nodes.summary: Jacob N. Kinnard (born 1968) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held positions as Assistant Professor of Religion at William & Mary and as a faculty member at the Iliff School of Theology.

nodes.label: Bryce Ryan
nodes.summary: Bryce Ryan was an indologist who held academic posts at Cornell University and the University of Ceylon, where he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

nodes.label: Nguyen Van Thuong
nodes.summary: Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where K. T. S. Sarao served as his MA supervisor.

nodes.label: Xinru Liu
nodes.summary: Xinru Liu specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher (~1980–1985), was a professor at CASS (1993), and became professor emeritus at The College of New Jersey (~1999).

nodes.label: Lawrence William Nelson
nodes.summary: Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at institutions including Butler University, Indiana University, and New York University, completing a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012).

Bryan D. Lowe
nodes.summary: Bryan D. Lowe, a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religion, studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone. He held an academic post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

nodes.label: Andrew Watsky
nodes.summary: Andrew Watsky is a specialist in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1986–1994). He held a post at Vassar College from ~1994 to 2008.

nodes.label: Towao Sakaehara
nodes.summary: Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He held posts at Otemon Gakuin University and Osaka City University, and later served as director of the Osaka Museum of History from 2014 to 2020.

nodes.label: Ben Joffe
nodes.summary: Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

nodes.label: Saba Mahmood
nodes.description: American anthropologist, Professor, University of California, Berkeley
nodes.summary: Saba Mahmood (1961–2018) was a religious studies and anthropology scholar who studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University. She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (from 2004).

nodes.label: Winnifred Fallers Sullivan
nodes.summary: Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan earned her BA at Cornell, followed by a JD and PhD from the University of Chicago. Her faculty posts include Washington and Lee University, the University of Chicago, and the University at Buffalo.

nodes.label: Martin Riesebrodt
nodes.summary: Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Humboldt University, Heidelberg (Promotion), and Munich (Habilitation). He held posts at Munich, the University of Chicago (1990–2011), and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).

nodes.label: Mark I. Wallace
nodes.description: author, minister, and theologian who teaches in the department of religion at Swarthmore College
nodes.summary: Mark I. Wallace works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (~1982–1986) and held posts at Merrimack College, Georgia State University, and Swarthmore College (~1989).

nodes.label: Joanne Punzo Waghorne
nodes.summary: Joanne Punzo Waghorne is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago (~1970–1976). She held posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

nodes.label: Takahiko Kameyama
nodes.summary: Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2015, he held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

nodes.label: Wes Borton
nodes.summary: Wes Borton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University, where he was taught by Derek F. Maher, and later studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

nodes.label: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer
nodes.summary: Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and also studied under postdoctoral mentor Xiuping Hong.

variants: Medical School of University of Chile Santiago
Biología del Conocer (Biology of Knowing) research center

nodes.label: Yangdon Dhondup
nodes.summary: Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London between approximately 2000 and 2004 under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.

nodes.label: Christopher Byrne
nodes.summary: Christopher Byrne is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), studying under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.

nodes.label: Alexander James O'Neill
nodes.summary: Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has pursued PhD studies at the University of Toronto and held a research fellowship at Taisho University.

nodes.label: St Antony's College
variants: Asian Studies Centre, St Antony's College, Oxford

nodes.label: Kenneth J. Guest
nodes.summary: Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, under Aloysius Pieris, and earned his PhD at the CUNY Graduate Center. He held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.
