variants: The Institut d'Histoire et Philosophie des sciences et des Techniques

nodes.label: Vishwanath Prasad Varma
nodes.summary: Vishwanath Prasad Varma is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, Kali Kinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach.

nodes.label: Dhirendra Mohan Datta
nodes.summary: Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1920–1936) and held academic posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).

nodes.label: Joachim Wach
nodes.summary: Joachim Wach (1898–1955) studied at Leipzig, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. A religious studies and philosophy scholar, he taught at Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and chaired the History of Religions at the University of Chicago Divinity School (1945–1955).

nodes.label: Don Handelman
nodes.summary: Don Handelman (born 1939) is a scholar in anthropology and religious studies who studied at McGill, Pittsburgh, and Manchester. He served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1972 to 2008.

nodes.label: Charles Malamoud
nodes.description: French historian of religion and orientalist
nodes.summary: Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held posts at the University of Lyon (c. 1957-1972) and as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1979-1998).

nodes.label: Laren Hogen Bays
nodes.summary: Laren Hogen Bays is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who studied under Shodo Harada. In 2002, he founded the Great Vow Zen Monastery, where he serves as co-abbot.

nodes.label: Mikio Otsuki
nodes.summary: Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. In 2007, he is attested as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University.

nodes.label: M. M. McCabe
nodes.summary: M. M. McCabe (born 1948) is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She held positions at Murray Edwards College, King's College London, University College London, and Newnham College.

nodes.label: Verity Harte
nodes.summary: Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held research fellowships at St Edmund's College and St Hilda's College, lectured at King's College London, and became Professor of Philosophy and Classics at Yale University in 2006.

nodes.label: Raimond Gaita
nodes.summary: Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

nodes.label: Jonathan Lear
nodes.summary: Jonathan Lear is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University, and the Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held posts at Yale, Cambridge, and the University of Chicago, serving as John U. Nef Distinguished Service Professor (2014–2022).

nodes.label: Susan Neiman
nodes.description: American philosopher, essayist and cultural commentator (born 1955)
nodes.summary: Susan Neiman is a philosopher educated at Harvard and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and has served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000–2026).

nodes.label: Jonathan Glover
nodes.summary: Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a fellow and tutor in philosophy at New College, Oxford (c. 1967–1996) and held a post at King's College London (c. 1996–2013).

nodes.label: L. Carrington Goodrich
nodes.summary: L. Carrington Goodrich (1894–1986) was a Sinologist who studied at Chefoo School and Williams College (~1913–1917). He served as the Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University from ~1945 to 1961.

nodes.label: Songeun Choe
nodes.summary: Songeun Choe is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Michael W. Meister
nodes.summary: Michael W. Meister is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Harvard (BA 1960–1964, MA 1968–1971, PhD 1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania. He became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania around 1976.

nodes.label: Melissa R. Kerin
nodes.summary: Melissa R. Kerin works in art history and archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and held a professorship at Washington and Lee University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Manfred B. Steger
nodes.summary: Manfred B. Steger works in religious studies, philosophy, and political science. After studying at the University of Hawaiʻi and Rutgers University, he taught at Illinois State (1996–2005), RMIT University (2005–2011), and the University of Hawaiʻi (2011–2016).

nodes.label: Keenan W. Cox
nodes.summary: Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

nodes.label: Brian Bocking
nodes.summary: Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the instruction of Michael Pye.

nodes.label: André Couture
nodes.summary: André Couture is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965–1971), EPHE (~1971–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977). He held an academic post at Laval University starting around ~1979.

nodes.label: Xianda
nodes.summary: Xianda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at The University of Hong Kong, studying under K. L. Dhammajoti and Toshiichi Endo (attested 2016).

nodes.label: Seung-yeon Lee
nodes.summary: Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Lee Sang-hae and has held posts at the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties and Sungkyunkwan University.

nodes.label: College of Art, Delhi
variants: College of Art in New Delhi

nodes.label: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart
nodes.summary: Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

nodes.label: Yukihiko Asayama
nodes.summary: Yukihiko Asayama (1931–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

nodes.label: Balliol College, Oxford
variants: ベリオール・カレッジ
オックスフォード大学ベリオール・カレッジ

nodes.label: Toshihiko Izutsu
nodes.description: Japanese author of many books on Islam and other religions (1914–1993)
nodes.summary: Toshihiko Izutsu (1914–1993) worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. A Keio University graduate, he held long-term posts at Keio (1937–1981), McGill University (1961; 1969–1975), and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

nodes.label: Tadashi Inoue
nodes.summary: Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) worked in archaeology and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Tokyo. His career included roles at Kyoto National Museum, director of Iida City Museum (1988–2006), and professorships at Nara, Bukkyo, and Kyoto Arts universities.

nodes.id: I:K. J. Somaiya Centre for Buddhist Studies
nodes.label: K. J. Somaiya Centre for Buddhist Studies
Sally Mellick Cutler
nodes.summary: Sally Mellick Cutler works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1993) and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).

nodes.label: György Hazai
nodes.description: Hungarian orientalist, turkologist, university professor, academic (1932–2016)
nodes.summary: György Hazai worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1950–1954) and held a post at the Institut für Orientforschung from circa 1963 to 1982.

nodes.label: Institut für Orientforschung
variants: ベルリン・アカデミー東洋学研究所

nodes.label: Hamamatsu University
variants: 常葉学園浜松大学経営情報学部

nodes.label: Kenpon Hokkeshu Research Institute
variants: 顕本法華宗教学研究所

nodes.id: I:Ministry of Education, Science and Culture
nodes.label: Ministry of Education, Science and Culture
Kansei Tamura
nodes.summary: Kansei Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).

nodes.label: Katsuji Fujioka
nodes.summary: Katsuji Fujioka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and Leipzig University (1901–1905). He served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.

nodes.label: Leonard Bloomfield
variants: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.jawiki: レナード・ブルームフィールド
nodes.summary: Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood (1908–1909). He held professorial posts at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale (1940–1949).

nodes.label: Kaigen Noritake
nodes.summary: Kaigen Noritake is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He held an academic post as assistant professor (助教授) at Rissho University (attested 2007).

nodes.label: Daito Shimaji
nodes.summary: Daito Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Ryukoku and Toyo universities, he taught Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1923, and taught at Toyo, Komazawa, and Rissho universities in the 1920s.

nodes.label: Amalia Pezzali
nodes.summary: Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under T. R. V. Murti and Michel Hulin.

nodes.label: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff
nodes.summary: Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a linguist and historian. After studies in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he held posts at the École française d'Athènes, the University of Groningen (1903; 1908–1916), and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

nodes.label: Fumio Masutani
nodes.summary: Fumio Masutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, later serving as professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and president of Tsuru University.

nodes.label: Kumataro Kawada
nodes.summary: Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied and earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).

nodes.label: Daegu University
variants: 大邱大学校日語日文学科

nodes.label: Hoseong Kim
nodes.summary: Hoseong Kim is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo and served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).

nodes.id: I:Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism Propagation Department
nodes.label: Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism Propagation Department
Kazuhiro Kawasaki
nodes.summary: Kazuhiro Kawasaki focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral coursework at Koyasan University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 2005.

nodes.label: Chandima
nodes.summary: Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Jogendra Singh
nodes.summary: Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, where he studied under Uma Shankar Vyas.

nodes.label: Hartmut Scharfe
nodes.summary: Hartmut Scharfe (1932–2020) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and served on the faculty at the University of California, Los Angeles.

nodes.label: Daijo Tokiwa
nodes.summary: Daijo Tokiwa was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University.

nodes.label: Yuishin Ito
nodes.summary: Yuishin Ito (1931–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He served as associate professor at Bukkyo University (1961–1997) and president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (1997).

nodes.label: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn
nodes.summary: Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen (1770–1774). He held professorships in oriental languages at Jena (1775) and philosophy at Göttingen (1788).

nodes.label: Keiki Yabuki
nodes.summary: Keiki Yabuki worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Jōdo Shū Tōhoku Shikō, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. His career included posts at Shukyo University (circa 1913–1926), University of Tokyo, and Taisho University (circa 1926–1939).

nodes.label: Shigeru Matsumoto
nodes.summary: Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957) and Harvard University (~1961–1967). He held posts at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1971–1994) and Tenri University (~1994–2004).

nodes.id: I:Center for the Study of World Religions
nodes.label: Center for the Study of World Religions
variants: ハーバード大学世界宗教学研究所
Harvard University Center for the Study of World Religions
Harvard’s Center for the Study of World Religions
ハーバード大学の世界宗教研究所

nodes.label: Unshō Shaku
nodes.summary: Unshō Shaku (1827–1909) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded both the Juzen-kai in 1884 and the Kairitsu Gakkō.

nodes.label: Kōzen Shaku
nodes.summary: Kōzen Shaku (1849–1924) was an Indology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Senmyō. He was head priest at Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded Shakuson Shofukai (1893).

nodes.label: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
variants: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・ヴィルヘルム・フリードリヒ・ヘーゲル
nodes.summary: Philosopher Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel studied at Tübingen, the Tübinger Stift, and Jena under Schelling. He held academic posts at Jena (~1801–1807), Heidelberg (~1816–1818), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1818–1831).

nodes.label: Bernhard Kölver
nodes.summary: Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (chair, 1974–1993), and Leipzig University (chair, 1993–2001).

nodes.label: Tübingen University Library
variants: テュービンゲン大学図書館

nodes.label: Georges Dumézil
variants: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.jawiki: ジョルジュ・デュメジル
nodes.summary: Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss. He held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, and the EPHE, before holding a chair at the Collège de France.

nodes.label: Claude Lévi-Strauss
variants: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.jawiki: クロード・レヴィ＝ストロース
nodes.summary: Claude Lévi-Strauss studied philosophy and other fields, attending Paris Law Faculty and studying under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo, EPHE, EHESS, and the Collège de France (chair of Anthropologie sociale, 1959–1982).

nodes.label: Antoine Meillet
variants: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.jawiki: アントワーヌ・メイエ
nodes.summary: Antoine Meillet worked in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Darmesteter, Lévi, and Saussure in Paris, later holding professorships at the EPHE, INALCO (1902–1906), and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

nodes.label: Émile Benveniste
variants: エミール・バンヴニスト
エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.jawiki: エミール・バンヴェニスト
nodes.summary: Linguist, Iranian, and Indology scholar Émile Benveniste studied at EPHE and Paris under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes. He held posts as directeur d’études at EPHE (1927–1969) and Chair of Comparative Grammar at Collège de France (1937–1969).

nodes.label: Theodore Dwight Woolsey
nodes.description: American jurist; president of Yale University (1801–1889)
nodes.summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Hopkins School, Yale, and Princeton. He later served as president of Yale University (1831–1871) and president of the American Oriental Society (~1861–1870).

nodes.label: Sures Chandra Banerji
nodes.description: born:1917-08-04|died:2000|; Sureśa Candra Bandyopādhyāya 1917-; Banerji, Sures Chandra; Banerji, Sures Chandra 1917-2000

nodes.label: Toru Takahashi
nodes.summary: Toru Takahashi (1878–1967) worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo, his academic career included professorships at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

nodes.id: I:Academic Association of Koreanology in Japan
nodes.label: Academic Association of Koreanology in Japan
Tsutomu Kubo
nodes.summary: Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He served on the faculties of the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (professor 1940–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).

nodes.label: Ernest Renan
variants: ジョゼフ・エルネスト・ルナン
nodes.summary: Ernest Renan was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Eugène Burnouf and Etienne Marc Quatremère. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France as Hebrew professor (1861) and director (1883).

nodes.label: Gyoei Fukuda
nodes.summary: Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He held posts at Taisho University as president (~1926–1944), the University of Tokyo as professor (1928), and Toyo University as a lecturer.

nodes.label: Tendai Daigakurin
variants: 天台宗西部大学専修院

nodes.label: Victor Henry
nodes.summary: Victor Henry was a French linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Douai, the University of Lille, and the École Centrale de Lille, and in 1888 became professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris.

nodes.label: Auguste Barth
nodes.summary: Auguste Barth was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned his licence at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at Collège de Saverne (1860–1870) and was a member of the Institut de France.

nodes.label: Jean Deloche
nodes.summary: Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian. He directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966) and served as a researcher and associate member at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, as well as an associate member at the French Institute of Pondicherry.

nodes.label: Anna Seidel
nodes.summary: Anna Seidel (1938–1991) was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at the universities of Munich and Hamburg and under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf A. Stein. She joined the EFEO in 1969 and worked at the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1970–1991).

nodes.label: Götz von Selle
nodes.summary: A historian of Central Asia, von Selle studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. ~1918–1920). He held library posts in Göttingen and Berlin, and was a professor and library director at the University of Königsberg (~1936–1944).

nodes.label: John Borthwick Gilchrist
variants: ジョン・ボースウィック・ギルクリスト
nodes.image: John Borthwick Gilchrist, cropped from UCL portrait by Blanconi.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・ギルクリスト
nodes.summary: John Borthwick Gilchrist was a linguist and Indologist educated at Edinburgh's Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh. He served at Fort William College, the East India Company College, and University College London.

nodes.label: Claudius Buchanan
nodes.summary: Claudius Buchanan, a scholar in Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Glasgow and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795). In 1801, he served as Vice-Provost at Fort William College.

nodes.label: Bruno Petzold
variants: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.jawiki: ブルーノ・ペツォルト
nodes.summary: Bruno Petzold, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied at Leipzig University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Daito Shimaji and Hikoshiro Hoshino. In Japan, he taught at First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.

nodes.label: Seiichiro Ono
nodes.summary: Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) studied at First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, Daito Shimaji, Kanae Tada, and Jokan Chikazumi. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922; 1938–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

nodes.label: Haya Akegarasu
nodes.summary: Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and attended Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954) and Shinshu Otani-ha (1951–1952).

nodes.label: Edwin Arnold
variants: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.jawiki: エドウィン・アーノルド
nodes.summary: Edwin Arnold (1832–1904) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology educated at King's College London and Oxford. He served as Principal of Deccan College (1856), fellow at the University of Mumbai, and guest lecturer at Keio University.

nodes.label: Siddharth College
variants: シッダールタ女子大学

nodes.label: Ryoshin Nakao
nodes.summary: Ryoshin Nakao (1952-) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Komazawa University (~1971-1980), Nakao worked at the Research Institute of Soto Studies (~1980-1990) and became a professor at Hanazono University (~1996).

nodes.label: Poerbatjaraka
nodes.summary: Poerbatjaraka was an Indonesian scholar of linguistics, Indology, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under N. J. Krom and served as a professor at Gadjah Mada, University of Indonesia, and Udayana University, which he founded.

nodes.label: Herman Kellgren
nodes.summary: Herman Kellgren worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux, and held a post at the University of Helsinki from around 1849 to 1856.

nodes.label: Surendranath Sen
nodes.summary: Surendranath Sen (1890–1962) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1917–1939) and the University of Delhi (~1950–1953).

nodes.label: David Brown
variants: デイヴィッド・ブラウン
nodes.summary: David Brown (1762–1812) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Joseph Milner and at Magdalene College, Cambridge. He founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society and served as Provost at Fort William College in 1800.

nodes.label: Magdalene College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学のモードリン・カレッジ

nodes.label: William Kirkpatrick
variants: ウィリアム・カークパトリック
nodes.description: British army officer in the East India Company and diplomat (1754 or 1756-1812)

nodes.label: Francis Gladwin
variants: フランシス・グラッドウィン
nodes.description: British scholar of the Persian language
nodes.summary: Francis Gladwin (1745–1812) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1806).

nodes.label: William S.-Y. Wang
nodes.summary: William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and sinologist who studied at Columbia and Michigan. He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley (1966–1994), City University of Hong Kong (1996–2004), and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2004–2016).

nodes.label: Albert Thumb
nodes.image: Professor Albert Thumb 18.05.1865 bis 14.08.1915 Sohn von Ida Schanzenbach und Albert Alois Thump.jpg
nodes.summary: Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his Habilitation at Freiburg. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (1891–1901), University of Marburg (1901), and University of Strasbourg (1909).

nodes.label: Genro Gito
nodes.summary: Genro Gito was an 18th-century Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku. He served as the first seat (dai-ichiza) at Myōshin-ji.

nodes.label: Hakuin Ekaku
nodes.summary: Hakuin Ekaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711). He also taught Suiō Genro.

nodes.label: Julius Klaproth
nodes.jawiki: ユリウス・ハインリヒ・クラプロート

nodes.label: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland
nodes.summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and served as professor of law at Presidency University.

nodes.id: I:Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
nodes.label: Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters
variants: ノルウェー科学文学アカデミー

nodes.label: Richard Bowring
nodes.summary: Richard Bowring is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees, including a Litt.D, at the University of Cambridge. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, and Cambridge, serving as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

nodes.label: Muzaffar Alam
nodes.description: historian at the University of Chicago
nodes.summary: Muzaffar Alam is a historian and scholar of Indology and Central Asian studies. After degrees at Jamia Millia Islamia, AMU, and JNU (doctorate), he taught at JNU (~1973–2001) before becoming a professor at the University of Chicago around 2001.

nodes.label: Benkyo Shiio
nodes.summary: Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at several universities, headed Taisho University (1926) and Tokai Gakuen Women's College (1963), and directed the Sanko institutions.

nodes.label: Sanko Library
variants: 三康文化研究所附属三康図書館

nodes.label: Karl Ferdinand Johansson
nodes.summary: Karl Ferdinand Johansson (1860-1926) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala University in 1880 and later served there as University Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology of Indo-European Languages from approximately 1893 to 1925.

nodes.id: I:W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research
nodes.label: W. F. Albright Institute of Archaeological Research
variants: American School of Oriental Research in Jerusalem
オルブライト考古学研究所

nodes.label: Louis H. Gray
nodes.summary: Louis H. Gray worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Princeton and Columbia, he held posts at Princeton University (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (1921).

nodes.id: I:Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH
nodes.label: Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH
variants: Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH Research
Centre for Bhutan Studies and Gross National Happiness Research
Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH Studies

nodes.label: Sangay Dorji
nodes.summary: Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tengtho Goenpa and the Institute of Language and Culture Studies. He has served as a teacher at Simtokha Dzong and as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission.

nodes.id: I:Institute of Language and Culture Studies
nodes.label: Institute of Language and Culture Studies
Ugyen Pelgen
nodes.summary: Ugyen Pelgen works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

nodes.label: John A. Ardussi
nodes.summary: John A. Ardussi is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied for his MA under Turrell V. Wylie, earned his PhD at the Australian National University (attested 1977), and served as a research team member at CNRS.

nodes.label: Phuntsok Tashi
nodes.summary: Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

nodes.label: George van Driem
variants: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.jawiki: ジョージ・ヴァン・ドリーム
nodes.summary: Linguist and Tibetologist George van Driem studied at the University of Virginia, Radboud University Nijmegen, and Leiden University. He held posts at Leiden University, served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022), and worked at IIT Guwahati.

nodes.label: Lungten Dubgyur
nodes.summary: Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar in Tibetology. He completed a graduate degree at Sherubtse College, an LL.B at Government Law College, Mumbai, and an LL.M at the University of Edinburgh.

nodes.label: Kees W. Bolle
nodes.summary: Kees W. Bolle was a religious studies and history scholar who studied at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He lectured at Brown University and served as Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA (~1969–1991).

nodes.label: Thinley Dorji Bhutia
nodes.summary: Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

nodes.label: Henry Rawlinson
variants: ヘンリー・ローリンソン
nodes.image: Rawlinson, Sir Henry Creswick, par Arthur J.Melhuish, BNF Gallica.jpg
nodes.jawiki: ヘンリー・ローリンソン (初代準男爵)
nodes.summary: Henry Rawlinson was a linguist, historian, and Iranian studies scholar educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University. He served with the East India Company (ca. 1827–1856), the Foreign Office (ca. 1859–1860), and held leadership roles at the RGS and RAS.

nodes.label: Georg von der Gabelentz
variants: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
ハンス・ゲオルク・コーノン・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.jawiki: ゲオルク・フォン・デア・ガーベレンツ
nodes.summary: Georg von der Gabelentz worked in Sinology and linguistics, studying at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. He served as professor of East Asian languages at Leipzig (1878–1889) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1889), joining the Prussian Academy of Sciences in 1889.

nodes.label: Alexander Cunningham
variants: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.jawiki: アレキサンダー・カニンガム
nodes.description: British army engineer and amateur archaeologist (1814-1893)
nodes.summary: Alexander Cunningham was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Christ's Hospital and Addiscombe Military Seminary, studying under James Prinsep. He founded and led the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director and later director-general.

nodes.label: Robert Hyde Colebrooke
nodes.description: British infantry officer and surveyor in India (1762–1808)
nodes.summary: Working in history and archaeology, Colebrooke was a member of The Asiatic Society (1785–1802) and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1794 to 1808.

nodes.label: John Herbert Harington
nodes.description: British administrator in India and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and as honorary professor at Fort William College (~1801–1819).

nodes.label: Amaranatha Jha
nodes.summary: Amaranatha Jha was an Indologist educated at Muir Central College. He served as Professor of English at Muir Central College, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (circa 1938–1946), and Vice-Chancellor of Banaras Hindu University (circa 1947–1948).

nodes.label: Charles Elliott
nodes.summary: Charles Elliott was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the East India Company from around 1795 to 1827 and was Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1836 to 1856.

nodes.label: Klaus Butzenberger
nodes.summary: Klaus Butzenberger (born 1964) studied at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm and habilitated at the Free University of Berlin. Active in Indology and philosophy, he succeeded Heinrich von Stietencron as chairholder at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

nodes.label: George Thomas Staunton
nodes.summary: George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797–1800). He served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1823 to 1859.

nodes.label: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder
nodes.summary: Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

nodes.label: William Matthew Flinders Petrie
nodes.jawiki: フリンダーズ・ピートリー

nodes.label: British School at Athens
variants: British School of Archaeology in Athens

nodes.label: James Irving Manatt
nodes.summary: James Irving Manatt worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and held posts at Denison College, Marietta College, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, and Brown University (~1892–1915).

nodes.label: James Hadley
nodes.summary: James Hadley was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Fairfield Academy and Yale College under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, later serving as professor of Greek at Yale University (1845–1872) and leading member of the American Oriental Society.

nodes.label: Royal Holloway, University of London
variants: Royal Holloway College der University of London

nodes.label: Gordon Johnson
nodes.summary: Gordon Johnson is a historian of Indology who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. He held fellowships at Trinity and Selwyn College, served as President of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Deputy Vice-Chancellor of Cambridge (1974–2010), and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

nodes.label: Kurfürst-Ruprecht-Gymnasium Neustadt
variants: Gymnasium at Neustadt an der Haardt

nodes.label: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe
nodes.summary: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indologist, historian, and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Geiger at Erlangen (~1894–1897). He served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1928) and worked at the University of London (~1917–1930).

nodes.label: Charles Barbier de Meynard
nodes.image: Barbier de Meynard, Charles Adrien Casimir, par Eugène Pirou, BNF Gallica.jpg
nodes.jawiki: シャルル・バルビエ・ド・メナール
nodes.summary: Charles Barbier de Meynard worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Jules Mohl, he held posts at École des langues orientales, Institut de France, and Collège de France.

nodes.label: Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar
nodes.summary: A scholar of Indology, Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College in 1884. He subsequently held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

nodes.label: Rewata Dhamma
nodes.summary: Rewata Dhamma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and earned a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

nodes.label: Narada Maha Thera
nodes.image: Portrait Of Most Venerable Narada Maha Thera (1898-1983).jpg
nodes.summary: Narada Maha Thera (1898–1983) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo, and by Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa. He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple from circa 1955 to 1983.

nodes.label: C. R. Krishnamacharlu
nodes.summary: C. R. Krishnamacharlu (b. 1888) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and indology who completed his studies at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College.

nodes.label: James Gibbs
nodes.summary: James Gibbs was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1876–1881).

nodes.label: Oliver Codrington
nodes.summary: Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was active in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

nodes.label: Dermot Killingley
nodes.summary: Dermot Killingley (born 1935) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS. His academic career included posts at the University of Malaya (1961–1968), Newcastle University (1970–2005), and the University of Vienna (2008).

nodes.label: Institute of Economic Growth
variants: Institute of Economic Growth (University of Delhi)

nodes.label: Vasudha Narayanan
nodes.summary: Vasudha Narayanan is a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at the University of Madras, University of Mumbai, and Harvard University. She became Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida and served as president of the American Academy of Religion.

nodes.label: Sumathi Ramaswamy
nodes.summary: Sumathi Ramaswamy (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist. She studied at Delhi University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania, and held academic positions at the University of Pennsylvania (1993–1999) and the University of Michigan (1999–2007).

nodes.label: Declan Quigley
nodes.summary: Declan Quigley works in Indology and religious studies. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.label: Gauri Viswanathan
nodes.summary: Gauri Viswanathan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University, taught English at the University of Delhi (~1973–1975), and became a professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia University (~1989).

nodes.label: Henry Herbert Dodwell
nodes.summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell was a historian and Indologist educated at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions in Asia at SOAS (1922–1946).

nodes.label: Suzanne Karpelès
nodes.summary: Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Suzanne Karpelès studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at the EFEO (1922–1941) and was first curator of the National Library of Cambodia (1925).

nodes.label: Henry Sullivan Jarrett
nodes.summary: Henry Sullivan Jarrett worked in history and archaeology. He served as Secretary and Member on the Board of Examiners at Fort William from around 1870 to 1892, succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

nodes.label: Heinrich Blochmann
nodes.summary: Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer at Leipzig, Karl Benedikt Hase in Paris, and at Calcutta. He held posts at Fort William, Doveton, and Aliah University.

nodes.label: Ian James Coghlan
nodes.summary: Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004 and held a research fellow post at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).

nodes.label: Holly Gayley
nodes.summary: Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies in Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado around 2008.

nodes.label: Heinz Mode
nodes.description: German art historian, orientalist and indologist (1913-1992)
nodes.summary: Heinz Mode was an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Berlin, under Malalasekera and Fischer, and at Basel. He served as professor of Oriental archaeology at the University of Halle from 1948 to 1978.

nodes.id: I:Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR
nodes.label: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR
variants: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Buddhistische Forschungen in der DDR

nodes.label: Otto Fischer
nodes.description: German art historian, director of Kunstmuseum Basel (1886–1948)
nodes.summary: Otto Fischer was an art historian who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920), head of the Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and associate professor of art history at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

nodes.label: Willem Bollée
nodes.summary: Willem Bollée (1927–2020) was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University and the University of Hamburg. He served as assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and later as lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University (~1977–1993).

nodes.label: William Frederic Sinclair
nodes.summary: William Frederic Sinclair (d. 1900) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He was educated at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered a post with the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

nodes.id: I:Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
nodes.label: Oriental Translation Fund of Great Britain and Ireland
Austen Henry Layard
nodes.image: Henry Austen Layard Fratelli Vianelli BNF Gallica.jpg
nodes.jawiki: オースティン・ヘンリー・レヤード

nodes.label: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall
nodes.jawiki: ジョセフ・フォン・ハンマー・プルグスタル
nodes.summary: Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).

nodes.label: Dilli Raman Regmi
nodes.summary: Dilli Raman Regmi was a scholar of history and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D.Litt. from Patna University (circa 1939-1961), and taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

nodes.label: William Rainey Harper
nodes.summary: William Rainey Harper was a linguist who studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He served as professor at Yale (1886) and became the founding president and department head at the University of Chicago (1891–1906).

nodes.label: Daniel Coit Gilman
nodes.summary: Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution for Science (1902–1904).

nodes.label: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh
nodes.summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

nodes.label: John Jorgensen
nodes.summary: John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University, worked as a researcher at the Australian National University, and served as Senior Research Associate at La Trobe University (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Thomas Jülch
nodes.summary: Jülch is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, University of Hull, Heidelberg University, and University of Munich (PhD), later working as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).

nodes.label: Klaus Pinte
nodes.summary: Klaus Pinte works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served there as a teaching assistant in 2006.

nodes.id: I:Singapore University of Technology and Design
nodes.label: Singapore University of Technology and Design
variants: Singapore University of Technology and Design

nodes.label: Thomas Roebuck
nodes.summary: A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Roebuck studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He was a member of The Asiatic Society (circa 1810–1819) and assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811.

nodes.id: I:Keio Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies
nodes.label: Keio Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies
variants: Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies (慶應大學言語文化研究所)
Keio Institute of Cultural & Linguistic Studies

nodes.label: Jacob Samuel Speyer
nodes.summary: Jacob Samuel Speyer (1849–1913) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University (~1867–1872). He held posts at Amsterdam (1877–1889), Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden (1903–1913).

nodes.label: Lionel Obadia
nodes.summary: Lionel Obadia (born 1969) is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology in 1997, he held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lyon 2.

nodes.label: Richard Hughes Seager
nodes.summary: Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1987). In ~1994, he became Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College.

nodes.label: Michelle Spuler
nodes.summary: Michelle Spuler (born 1971) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1997–2001) and taught at Victoria University of Wellington and Colorado College.

nodes.label: William Muir
nodes.summary: William Muir was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kilmarnock Academy, Haileybury (~1835–1837), and the University of Edinburgh. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh (~1885–1903).

nodes.label: Robert Maclagan
nodes.description: British Army officer and military engineer (1820–94)
nodes.summary: Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Maclagan studied at Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

nodes.label: Erberto Lo Bue
nodes.description: Italian indologist, tibetologist, translator and university teacher
nodes.summary: Lo Bue specialized in Tibetology and earned his Ph.D. at SOAS University of London (~1975–1981). He was a lecturer in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (~1983–2002) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

nodes.label: Corpus Christi College, Cambridge
variants: Corpus Christi College der Universität Cambridge
ケンブリッジ大学コーパス・クリスティ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Edward Delavan Perry
nodes.summary: Edward Delavan Perry (1854–1938) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his A.B. at Columbia University (~1871–1875) and Dr. phil. at the University of Tübingen (~1877–1879), later serving as Jay Professor at Columbia University (1891–1931).

nodes.label: Nathaniel Wallich
nodes.jawiki: ナサニエル・ウォーリッチ
nodes.description: surgeon and botanist of Danish origin who worked in India (1786-1854)
nodes.summary: Nathaniel Wallich (1786–1854) studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as Superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from circa 1817 to 1846.

nodes.label: Jean-Luc Chevillard
nodes.summary: Jean-Luc Chevillard is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Culioli. He worked as a researcher at the CNRS from circa 1990 to 2021.

nodes.label: Theodorus Willem Juynboll
nodes.summary: Theodorus Willem Juynboll was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Leiden University from around 1884 to 1893 and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.

nodes.label: Nicolaas Johannes Krom
nodes.summary: Nicolaas Johannes Krom worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1913–1916) and held academic posts at Leiden University in 1919 and from 1925 to 1945.

nodes.label: Cornelis Christiaan Berg
nodes.summary: Cornelis Christiaan Berg (1900–1990) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1919–1927). He held posts at Leiden University (1929–1971) and the University of Amsterdam (1950–1967), and taught Jan Gonda.

nodes.label: Rajendralal Mitra
nodes.summary: Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Medical College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He directed the Wards' Institution (1856–1881) and served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and later president (1885) of The Asiatic Society.

nodes.label: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton
nodes.jawiki: フランシス・ブキャナン＝ハミルトン
nodes.summary: Francis Buchanan-Hamilton (1762–1829) studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he served in the Bengal Medical Service and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

nodes.label: Mona Schrempf
nodes.summary: Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin (2001) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University (attested 2006).

nodes.label: Jogindra Nath Samaddar
nodes.summary: Jogindra Nath Samaddar worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, and Bangabasi College. He held lectureships at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, and Patna College (1912), becoming University Reader at Patna University in 1923.

nodes.label: Winfred Robert Martin
nodes.summary: Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

nodes.label: Daniel John Gogerly
nodes.summary: Daniel John Gogerly was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press (circa 1818–1834), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society in 1838, and served as an officer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (circa 1845–1862).

nodes.label: Graves Chamney Haughton
nodes.summary: Graves Chamney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist educated at Fort William College. He co-founded the Royal Asiatic Society, served as its secretary, and was Professor at the East India Company College from 1819 to 1827.

nodes.label: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study
variants: Netherlands Institute for Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences

nodes.label: James Mackintosh
nodes.image: Sir James Mackintosh by Sir Thomas Lawrence.jpg
nodes.summary: James Mackintosh was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh, he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served as its president (~1804–1811).

nodes.label: J. M. E. McTaggart
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・マクタガート
nodes.summary: J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who was educated at Clifton College (~1882–1885). He subsequently held an academic appointment at the University of Cambridge from ~1897 to 1923, where he taught Surendranath Dasgupta.

nodes.label: Parul Dave-Mukherji
nodes.summary: Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford (1988–1991) under Alexis Sanderson and became a professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

nodes.label: Kazuaki Komine
nodes.summary: Kazuaki Komine is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from Waseda University. He held positions at Tokushima University and the National Institute of Japanese Literature before becoming professor at Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

nodes.label: Hermann Sauppe
nodes.summary: A scholar in linguistics and other fields, Sauppe studied at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann. He served as chief librarian and professor in Zurich, director at Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium, and professor at the University of Göttingen from 1855.

nodes.label: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner
nodes.summary: Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at King's College London and Heidelberg University, he taught at King's College, served as Principal of Government College Lahore, and was Registrar at the University of the Punjab.

nodes.label: Addiscombe Military Seminary
variants: Hon. East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
Honourable East India Company's Military Seminary, Addiscombe
アディスコム軍事神学校

nodes.label: Henry George Keene
nodes.description: English employee of the East India Company and Persian scholar
nodes.summary: Henry George Keene was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar educated at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge. After serving in the East India Company (ca. 1798–1811), he became Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (1824–1834).

nodes.label: William Price
nodes.summary: William Price was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College from circa 1813 to 1830.

nodes.label: David Ruddell
nodes.summary: David Ruddell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

nodes.label: John Shakespear
nodes.summary: John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied under John Richardson. He held professorships of oriental languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).

nodes.label: Emil Rödiger
variants: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.jawiki: エミル・レーディガー
nodes.summary: Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a linguist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at Halle (associate in 1830, full 1835–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1860).

nodes.label: Alfred Master
nodes.description: Master, Alfred (1883-1978) Lecturer in Indian Philology

nodes.label: William Erskine
nodes.summary: William Erskine (1773–1852) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1787 to 1792.

nodes.label: John Caspar Leyden
nodes.summary: John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1790 to 1797. In 1808, he served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

nodes.label: James Atkinson
nodes.description: English surgeon, artist and Persian scholar (1780–1852)
nodes.summary: Educated at the University of Edinburgh, James Atkinson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as Indology. He held posts at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.

nodes.label: Dayong
nodes.summary: Dayong (1893–1929) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Bai Puren, and Dpal ldan bstan 'dzin snyan grags. He taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1923) and founded the Tibetan Studies College.

nodes.label: Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo
variants: Pha bong kha pa dbe chen snying po

nodes.label: Buddhist Academy of China
variants: Institute of Buddhist Studies of Beijing

nodes.label: Eberhard Schrader
nodes.summary: Eberhard Schrader (1836–1908) was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held professorial posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, Jena, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

nodes.label: George Uglow Pope
nodes.summary: George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist. He founded and led Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School, taught at St Peter's School, and later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (circa 1884–1908).

nodes.label: John Thompson Platts
variants: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.jawiki: ジョン・トンプソン・プラッツ
nodes.summary: John Thompson Platts was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford. He served at Saugor High School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and became Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford in 1880.

nodes.id: P:Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
nodes.label: Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
nodes.enwiki: Richard Fleming St Andrew St John

nodes.label: Finnian M. M. Gerety
nodes.summary: Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from Harvard University in 2015. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Yale (2017–2018) and a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).

nodes.label: Andrea R. Jain
nodes.summary: Andrea R. Jain is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned her PhD from Rice University (2004-2010). She joined Indiana University in 2010, rising to associate professor (2016) and full professor (2021).

nodes.label: Kwangsoo Park
nodes.summary: Kwangsoo Park works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Iowa (MA) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD), and is attested as a professor at Wonkwang University in 2020.

nodes.label: Samani Pratibha Pragya
nodes.summary: Samani Pratibha Pragya specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she was attested as a research assistant in 2020.

nodes.label: Edward Clive Bayley
nodes.summary: Edward Clive Bayley (1821–1884) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and East India Company College (~1840–1842). In 1842, he took up a post with the Indian Civil Service.

nodes.label: Henry Miers Elliot
nodes.summary: Henry Miers Elliot, an Indologist and historian, was educated at Winchester College. He served as a civil servant with the East India Company from ca. 1826 to 1853.

nodes.label: Justus Olshausen
variants: ユストゥス・オルスハウゼン
nodes.summary: Justus Olshausen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kiel University, Paris, and Berlin, learning under Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at Kiel University, the University of Königsberg, and the Prussian Ministry.

nodes.label: Carl Paul Caspari
nodes.summary: Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig University under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Humboldt University of Berlin. In 1847 he became Lektor and in 1857 professor at the University of Oslo.

nodes.label: Hokkaido University of Education
variants: 北海道教育大学岩見沢分校
北海道教育大学函館分校

nodes.label: Tetsuo Otani
nodes.summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Otani studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He served as professor and president of Komazawa University (2002–2006) and later held presidencies at Tsuru University (2013–2016) and Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

nodes.label: Asahikawa University Junior College
variants: 旭川大学女子短期大学部

nodes.label: Doranne Jacobson
nodes.summary: Doranne Jacobson is an Indologist who earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University. She held a post at Columbia University as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

nodes.label: McKim Marriott
variants: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.jawiki: マッキム・マリオット
nodes.summary: McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard and the University of Chicago under Clyde Kluckhohn. He served as professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago (~1955–1998).

nodes.label: George Ritso Jervis
nodes.description: George Ritso Jervis (1794-1851) 1841 Lieut-Col George Ritso Jervis of the Engineers, Bombay Company

nodes.label: S. Sankaranarayanan
nodes.summary: S. Sankaranarayanan (1926–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

nodes.label: Chinmaya International Foundation
variants: Adi Sankara Nilayam, Chinmaya International Foundation

nodes.label: R. Thangaswami Sarma
nodes.summary: R. Thangaswami Sarma was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. He held posts at Presidency College, the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and was Honorary Professor at Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

nodes.id: I:Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre
nodes.label: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre
variants: Sri Sarada Education Society Research Centre

nodes.label: Camillo Alessio Formigatti
nodes.summary: Camillo Alessio Formigatti specializes in Indology and Tibetology. Educated at the University of Milan, he worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at Cambridge (2011–2014), taught Sanskrit at SOAS, and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Library (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Geoffrey Goble
nodes.summary: Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Virginia and a PhD at Indiana University, later serving as an assistant professor of religious studies at the University of Oklahoma.

nodes.label: Alastair Gornall
nodes.summary: Alastair Gornall works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2009–2013), he was a Research Associate at SOAS University of London (~2015) and an Assistant Professor in the Humanities at SUTD (~2016).

nodes.label: August Boeckh
nodes.summary: August Boeckh was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher, and held posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

nodes.label: Max Leopold Margolis
nodes.summary: Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University (1889–1891). He held positions at Hebrew Union College, the University of California, and Dropsie College (1909–1932).

nodes.id: I:Research Institute of Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha
nodes.label: Research Institute of Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha
variants: 浄土真宗本願寺派総合研究所

nodes.label: Jodoshu Seizan Fukakusaha Gakuin
variants: 浄土宗西山深草派学院

nodes.label: Soshuku Shibatani
nodes.summary: Soshuku Shibatani (born 1954) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Waseda University and Koyasan University. He has held positions at Sonoda Women's University, Junrei Henro Kenkyukai (2014), and Koyasan University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Yuka Otani
nodes.summary: Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She held positions as a part-time lecturer at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (attested 2015).

nodes.label: Frederik David Kan Bosch
nodes.summary: Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He led the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

nodes.id: I:Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies
nodes.label: Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies
George Cœdès
nodes.summary: George Cœdès was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and archaeology who studied under Louis Finot, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Richard Pischel. He served as Director of the EFEO (1929–1947) and held leadership roles at the National Library of Thailand.

nodes.id: I:Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
nodes.label: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi
variants: Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi

nodes.label: Scottish Naval and Military Academy
variants: Naval and Military Academy in Edinburgh
