nodes.label: Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka
variants: Ceylon Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society
Sri Lanka branch of the Royal Asiatic Society

nodes.label: Arthur Christensen
nodes.summary: Arthur Christensen (1875–1945) was a Danish scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1900) and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding Copenhagen's first chair of Orientalistics (1919–1945).

nodes.label: Friedrich Carl Andreas
nodes.jawiki: フリードリッヒ・カール・アンドレアス
nodes.summary: Friedrich Carl Andreas, a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1868–1869). He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).

nodes.label: Henrik Samuel Nyberg
variants: エンリコ・サムエリ・ニーベリ
nodes.summary: Henrik Samuel Nyberg was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at Uppsala University in 1908. He taught at Fjellstedt School (ca. 1912–1919) and served as docent and professor of Semitics at Uppsala University (ca. 1919–1956).

nodes.label: Otto Höfler
nodes.summary: Otto Höfler was an Austrian linguist and religious studies scholar who studied at Vienna under Rudolf Much, Lund, and Kiel. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and the University of Vienna (1957–1971).

nodes.label: George Shirt
nodes.summary: George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at Church Missionary Society College, Islington, from circa 1864 to 1866.

nodes.label: Jean Humbert
nodes.description: academic (1792 - 1851), member of the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino since 1832

nodes.label: Syed Ali Bilgrami
nodes.summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and the University of London. He served the Government of Hyderabad before becoming Reader in Marathi at Cambridge in 1901.

nodes.label: Sukumari Bhattacharji
nodes.summary: Sukumari Bhattacharji (1921–2014) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University, and held academic posts at Lady Brabourne College (from 1945) and Jadavpur University (1957–1986).

nodes.label: Johann Tobias Beck
nodes.summary: Johann Tobias Beck (1804–1878) worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tübingen (ca. 1822–1826), he held academic posts at the University of Basel (ca. 1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (ca. 1843–1878).

nodes.label: Gerardus van der Leeuw
variants: ヘラルドゥス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.jawiki: ゲラルダス・ファン・デル・レーウ
nodes.description: Dutch religious studies scholar and politician (1890–1950)
nodes.summary: Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

nodes.label: Edward Albert Gait
nodes.summary: Edward Albert Gait was an administrator and scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1880-1882) and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914, serving as its president from 1915 to 1920.

nodes.label: Frederick James Furnivall
nodes.summary: Frederick James Furnivall (1825–1910) was a linguist educated at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910) and taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1870).

nodes.label: Royal Masonic School for Boys
variants: Royal Masonic School for Boys at Wood Green

nodes.label: Tanzan Hara
nodes.summary: Tanzan Hara worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Shoheizaka Gakumonjo and under traditional teachers. He held posts at the Ministry of Religion, University of Tokyo, Japan Academy, and Komazawa University, and founded Bussensha.

nodes.label: Chatral Sangye Dorje
nodes.image: Tulku Sangay Yonten Gyatsho and HH ChatralSangyeDorje Rinpoche.jpg
nodes.summary: Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, Dorje Dradul, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (~1931–1941), whom he later succeeded.

nodes.label: Leedom Lefferts
nodes.summary: Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He was Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University (attested 2011) and a Research Associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

nodes.label: Louise Allison Cort
nodes.summary: Louise Allison Cort, a specialist in Japanology and archaeology, studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College. She served as ceramics curator at the Smithsonian Institution's Freer and Sackler Galleries from circa 1981 to 2020.

nodes.label: Kavita Singh
nodes.summary: Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist who earned her PhD from Panjab University (~1989–1996). She served as research editor at Marg Publications (~1999–2001) and became dean at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of Arts and Aesthetics in 2001.

nodes.label: Jules Michelet
nodes.description: French historian; popularized the historical concept of the Renaissance
nodes.summary: A historian educated at Lycée Charlemagne, Michelet served as maître de conférences at the École Normale Supérieure (from 1827), section chief at the Archives nationales (1831–1851), and professor of history at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

nodes.label: Raghu Ananthanarayanan
nodes.summary: Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained in philosophy and religious studies under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. He taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad.

nodes.label: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya
nodes.summary: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and the University of Mysore, and with Ramamohana Brahmachari. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1953–1958).

nodes.label: T. K. V. Desikachar
nodes.summary: T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1961–1989) and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

nodes.label: Manshi Kiyozawa
nodes.summary: Manshi Kiyozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa, he served as principal of Kyoto Prefectural Middle School (1888) and became the founding president of Otani University (~1901–1902).

nodes.label: Ernest Francisco Fenollosa
variants: アーネスト・フランシスコ・フェノロサ
nodes.jawiki: アーネスト・フェノロサ
nodes.summary: Ernest Francisco Fenollosa worked in philosophy, Japanology, and art history after studying at Harvard. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1878), Tokyo National Museum (1888), Tokyo University of the Arts (1887–1890), and Boston's Museum of Fine Arts (1890–1896).

nodes.label: Jinjo Middle School
variants: Jinjō Middle School 尋常中学校

nodes.label: Khenpo Gangshar
nodes.summary: Khenpo Gangshar was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Shechen Monastery under teachers including Khyentse Ozer, later serving as a senior teacher at Shechen Monastery.

nodes.label: Gembo Dorji
nodes.summary: Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed studies at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, and trained under several traditional teachers, including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

nodes.label: Norihisa Baba
nodes.summary: Norihisa Baba is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He holds a professorship at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

nodes.label: Shechen Gyaltsab
nodes.summary: Shechen Gyaltsab was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Dilgo Khyentse and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, among others.

nodes.label: Khakyab Dorje
variants: 15世カルマパ・カキャブ・ドルジェ
nodes.summary: Khakyab Dorje was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye (~1886–1899) and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1886–1892).

nodes.label: Karuna Kusalasaya
nodes.native: กรุณา กุศลาสัย
nodes.summary: Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

nodes.label: Fafang
nodes.summary: Fafang (1904–1951) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

nodes.label: Satiranjan Sen
nodes.summary: Satiranjan Sen was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied at Peking University. He was a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

nodes.label: Rongtha Damchö Gyatso
variants: Rong tha Dam chos rgya mtsho

nodes.label: Yuexia
nodes.summary: Yuexia was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.

nodes.label: Dixian
nodes.summary: Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from circa 1879 to 1882. He later served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

nodes.label: Nicholas Roerich
nodes.jawiki: ニコライ・リョーリフ
nodes.description: Russian painter, writer, archaeologist and philosopher (1874–1947)
nodes.summary: Nicholas Roerich worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts. He served as director of the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and president of Mir iskusstva.

nodes.label: Khenpo Shenga
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Önpo Tenzin Norbu, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo, among others. He taught at Shri Singha Shedra (1902) and became Dzongsar Monastery's first khenpo in 1918.

nodes.label: Xifan Xueguan
variants: School of the Tibetan Language (Xi fan xue zong guan)

nodes.id: P:Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
nodes.label: Constantin François de Chassebœuf, comte de Volney
John Lockwood Kipling
nodes.image: John Lockwood Kipling és Rudyard Kipling.jpg
nodes.summary: John Lockwood Kipling was a scholar in Indology and history who studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He held posts at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art, Lahore Museum (1875–1893), National College of Arts (1875–1893), and the Journal of Indian Art and Industry.

nodes.label: Alfonsa Ferrari
nodes.summary: Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi at Sapienza University of Rome, where she also conducted post-graduate research.

nodes.label: Jacques Bacot
nodes.image: Tchraker lama, Jacques Bacot et moines.png
nodes.summary: Jacques Bacot (1877–1965) was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot in 1908. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1919, the University of Paris, and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

nodes.label: Daoquan Yu
nodes.summary: Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University and under Jacques Bacot in the 1930s, later serving as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China (circa 1952–1992).

nodes.label: Lorna Dewaraja
nodes.summary: Lorna Dewaraja was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London, and held faculty posts at the University of Peradeniya, University of Colombo, and St Anne's College.

nodes.label: Senarat Wijayasundara
nodes.summary: Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who, in 1999, held posts as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

nodes.label: Walter Simon
variants: エルンスト・ユーリウス・ヴァルター・ジーモン
nodes.jawiki: ヴァルター・ジーモン
nodes.summary: Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke, later holding posts at Berlin, Kiel, the National Library of China, and the University of London (1938–1960).

nodes.label: Tibetan Studies College
variants: Institute of Tibetan Studies (Zangwen Xueyuan 藏文學院)

nodes.label: Wilhelm Wundt
variants: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.jawiki: ヴィルヘルム・ヴント
nodes.description: German physician, physiologist, philosopher and professor (1832–1920)
nodes.summary: Wilhelm Wundt was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Tübingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (1857), Leipzig University (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

nodes.label: Edvard Westermarck
nodes.jawiki: エドワード・ウェスターマーク
nodes.summary: Edvard Westermarck was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881-1889) and later held posts at the London School of Economics (~1907-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918-1932).

nodes.label: Dedong Wei
nodes.summary: Dedong Wei (born 1968) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China and served there as an associate professor of religious studies around 2002.

nodes.label: Claude Jacques
nodes.summary: Claude Jacques worked in Indology, history, and archaeology, studying under George Cœdès (~1958–1969). He served as director at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1965–1973) and taught epigraphy and history at the EPHE (~1970–1997).

nodes.label: Amy Paris Langenberg
nodes.image: Amy Paris Langenberg in the video 'Accomplished women Female leadership and reproductive health in the Bhikṣuņī-Vinaya'.png
nodes.summary: Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College circa 2014.

nodes.label: Benedetta Lomi
nodes.summary: Benedetta Lomi works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London, later teaching at the University of Virginia around 2014 to 2019 and holding a post at the University of Bristol around 2019.

nodes.id: I:Indiana University Uralic and Altaic Series
nodes.label: Indiana University Uralic and Altaic Series
variants: Indiana University Uralic and Altaic Series

nodes.label: Tenzin Namdak
nodes.summary: A scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Tenzin Namdak studied under sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan, Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and at Menri Monastery (1950–1953). In 1986, he founded Triten Norbutse Monastery.

nodes.id: P:sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
nodes.label: sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan
variants: sGangs ru tshul khrims rgyal mtshan

nodes.label: Marsha Weidner
nodes.summary: Marsha Weidner works in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

nodes.label: Meir Shahar
nodes.summary: Meir Shahar is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1987–1992) and became an Associate Professor of Chinese Studies at Tel Aviv University (~1994).

nodes.label: Damdin Badaraev
nodes.summary: Damdin Badaraev worked in Tibetology and linguistics, having studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

nodes.label: Filippo De Filippi
nodes.jawiki: フィリッポ・デ・フィリッピ
nodes.summary: Filippo De Filippi (1869–1938) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

nodes.label: Daehaeng
nodes.description: Korean Buddhist nun and Seon(禪) master

nodes.label: Tokiyuki Hojo
nodes.summary: Tokiyuki Hojo (1858–1929) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). During his career, he held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1894–1896), Kanazawa University (~1898–1908), and Tohoku University (~1913–1917).

nodes.label: Giovanni Gentile
variants: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.jawiki: ジョヴァンニ・ジェンティーレ
nodes.description: Italian philosopher, educator, fascist theoretician and politician (1875-1944)
nodes.summary: Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was a philosopher educated at Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the University of Pisa. He held professorships at Palermo (1906–1914), Pisa (1914–1917), and Sapienza University of Rome (1917–1944), and founded ISMEO in 1933.

nodes.label: Mipham Chokyi Lodro
nodes.summary: Mipham Chokyi Lodro was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973), and taught Trinley Thaye Dorje and Ole Nydahl.

nodes.label: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje
nodes.summary: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, Tubten Chokyi Dorje, and Karma Shedrub Chokyi Sengge.

nodes.label: Thegchog Dorje
nodes.summary: Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Thegchog Dorje studied under Pema Nyinje Wangpo and Kunzik Chokyi Nangwa. As a teacher, his prominent students included Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Chokgyur Lingpa.

nodes.label: King's College, Cambridge
variants: ケンブリッジ大学キングズコレッジ
ケンブリッジ大学キングズ・カレッジ

nodes.label: Christopher G. Framarin
nodes.summary: Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an MA in philosophy from the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from the University of New Mexico, later becoming an associate professor at the University of Calgary.

nodes.label: Emmanuel College, Toronto
variants: Emmanuel College of Victoria University in the University of Toronto

nodes.label: Tao Pan
nodes.summary: Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.

nodes.label: Nicholas Witkowski
nodes.summary: Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Stanford University by 2015 and was a research fellow at the University of Tokyo in 2017.

nodes.label: Yingguang Qu
nodes.summary: Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1904–1907) and under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Bai Puren, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche, later teaching Shek-wing Tam and Yui Chi Lau.

nodes.label: Yuanxing Guo
nodes.summary: Yuanxing Guo (1920-1982) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche, and held positions at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism and the Jinling Scriptural Press.

nodes.label: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism
variants: Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism (Zhongguo Fojiao Wenhua Yanjiusuo 中國佛教文化研究所)

nodes.label: Nianzu Huang
nodes.summary: Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) studied at Beijing Institute of Technology and trained under multiple traditional teachers. He worked in Buddhist studies, headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station, and served as a professor at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (~1953–1978).

nodes.label: Voice of America
variants: Tibetan Broadcast Service for Voice of America

nodes.label: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz
nodes.summary: René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He also studied at SOAS, LSE, and Berlin under scholars including Giuseppe Tucci, and held a post at Weltmuseum Wien (1958).

nodes.label: Pieter Hendrik Pott
nodes.summary: Pieter Hendrik Pott was a Dutch scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as curator at the National Museum of Ethnology in Leiden (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

nodes.label: Constantin Régamey
nodes.summary: Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He studied at the Universities of Warsaw and Paris under Stanisław Schayer, Jean Przyluski, Marcelle Lalou, and Józef Turczyński, later teaching at Warsaw, Fribourg, and Lausanne.

nodes.label: Lajos Ligeti
nodes.summary: Lajos Ligeti (1902–1987) worked in Inner Asian, Sinological, and Tibetan studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Paris under Pelliot and Maspero, he held the chair of Inner Asian Studies at Eötvös Loránd University from 1940.

nodes.id: P:Kun dga' chos legs rdo rje
nodes.label: Kun dga' chos legs rdo rje
Chogye Shabdrung
nodes.summary: Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 and was taught by Sonam Gyatso.

nodes.label: Hideki Yukawa
nodes.summary: Working in philosophy and other fields, Yukawa studied at Kyoto and Osaka universities. He held academic appointments at Osaka University, the University of Tokyo, Columbia University, and Kyoto University (circa 1939–1970).

nodes.id: P:Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
nodes.label: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drime Lekpe Lodro
variants: Shechen Kongtrul Pema Drimé Lekpé Lodrö
シェチェン・コントゥル

nodes.label: Rustam Sabirov
nodes.summary: Rustam Sabirov specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He received his doctorate in history from Moscow State University in 2004, where he also held a post as a senior researcher.

nodes.label: Krisztina Teleki
nodes.description: (1978–) Hungarian literary translator, linguist, orientalist, tibetologist and mongolist
nodes.summary: Krisztina Teleki is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA in Tibetan and Mongolian at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009), where she also served as a research fellow around 2010.

nodes.label: Immanuel Kant
nodes.summary: Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was a philosopher who studied at Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). He held the chair of logic and metaphysics at the University of Königsberg from 1770 and taught Johann Gottfried von Herder.

nodes.label: August Conrady
variants: アウグスト・コンラーディ
nodes.jawiki: アウグスト・コンラーディ (中国学者)
nodes.summary: August Conrady specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, earning degrees at Würzburg and Leipzig. He spent most of his academic career at Leipzig University, becoming full professor of Sinology in 1920, and held a post at Peking University (1903–1904).

nodes.label: Berthold Laufer
variants: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.image: Annual report of the Director to the Board of Trustees for the year .. (1933) (17811378703).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ベルトルト・ラウファー
nodes.summary: Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under Conrady and others. He held posts at AMNH, Columbia University, and the Field Museum of Natural History.

nodes.label: Friedrich Weller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Weller worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, earning his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at Leipzig University under August Conrady. He held Indology chairs at Leipzig (1928, 1938–1958) and was a member of the Saxon Academy (1943–1980).

nodes.label: Bruno Schindler
variants: ブルーノ・シンドラー

nodes.label: Johannes Schubert
nodes.summary: Johannes Schubert (1896–1976) was a scholar of Tibetology and sinology who studied at Leipzig University. He worked at the Leipzig University Library, held teaching posts in Tibetan and Mongolian at Leipzig University, and worked for the Ahnenerbe (ca. 1939–1945).

nodes.label: Stanisław Schayer
nodes.summary: Stanisław Schayer (1899–1941) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.

nodes.label: Jan Jaworski
nodes.summary: Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar of sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw from circa 1923 to 1928, and also studied under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

nodes.label: Ludwik Skurzak
nodes.summary: Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer and worked as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

nodes.label: Maryla Falk
nodes.description: Polish indologist and historian of religions
nodes.summary: Maryla Falk was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held an academic post at the University of Warsaw from circa 1931 to 1939 and became a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1974.

nodes.label: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz
nodes.summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1926), later holding posts there (~1928–1941), at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1953), and at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

nodes.label: Paul Ekman
nodes.summary: Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held a post at the University of California, San Francisco from circa 1960 to 2004.

nodes.label: Ajahn Maha Somchai Kusalacitto
nodes.summary: Ajahn Maha Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2003.

nodes.label: Stephen Addiss
nodes.summary: Stephen Addiss (1935–2022) was an art historian and scholar of Japanology who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He served as professor of art history at the University of Kansas and held a professorship at the University of Richmond.

nodes.label: Juan Wu
nodes.summary: Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under doctoral supervisor Max Deeg (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Laurence Austine Waddell
nodes.summary: Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a medical degree from the University of Glasgow (~1874–1878), served in the Indian Medical Service (~1879–1917), and was Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

nodes.label: Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok
nodes.summary: Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Khenchen Dazer (~1951–1957), among other traditional teachers.

nodes.label: Marian Ury
nodes.summary: Marian Ury was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in circa 1953. She served as a professor at the University of California, Davis from 1969 to 1995.

nodes.label: Eric J. Sharpe
nodes.summary: Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Sharpe studied at Manchester under Samuel George Frederick Brandon and earned a doctorate from Uppsala University. He held posts at Lancaster, Uppsala, and the University of Sydney as First Chair of Religious Studies (1977–1996).

nodes.label: Phra Rajavaramuni
nodes.summary: Phra Rajavaramuni works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, and served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

nodes.label: Tampalawela Dhammaratana
nodes.summary: Buddhist studies scholar Tampalawela Dhammaratana studied at Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études with Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

nodes.label: Liqian Liu
nodes.summary: Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1949), the State Council of the People's Republic of China translation administration department (~1952–1959), and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1959–1978).

nodes.label: West China Union University
variants: Border Area Institute of Research of the West China University

nodes.id: I:State Council of the People's Republic of China
nodes.label: State Council of the People's Republic of China
Genzao
nodes.summary: Genzao was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

nodes.label: Dzogchen Monastery
variants: monastische Kolleg Shri Singha des Dzogchen-Klosters

nodes.id: I:Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
nodes.label: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
variants: Beijing Institute of Post and Telecommunications

nodes.label: John Claude White
nodes.description: British engineer, civil servant and photographer in India (1853–1918)
nodes.summary: John Claude White was an engineer active in tibetology and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College before being appointed Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

nodes.label: Eric Teichman
nodes.summary: A scholar in Tibetology and Sinology, Teichman completed his studies at Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge between ~1903 and 1906.

nodes.label: Edward Sapir
nodes.summary: Edward Sapir (1884–1939) was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (~1910–1925) and held academic posts at the University of Chicago and Yale University.

nodes.label: Friedrich Schleiermacher
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・シュライアマハー
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and biblical scholar (1768-1834)
nodes.summary: Friedrich Schleiermacher worked in philosophy and religious studies after studying at Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1790). He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1804–1806) and a chair at the University of Berlin (~1810–1834).

nodes.label: Józef Szczepan Kowalewski
nodes.summary: Józef Szczepan Kowalewski was a scholar of Mongolian, Buddhist, and Iranian studies. He studied at Vilnius University and Kazan Federal University, later serving as professor and rector at Kazan (1833–1860) and professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.

nodes.label: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk
nodes.summary: Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Jampel Gyepai Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

nodes.label: Longlian
nodes.summary: Longlian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

nodes.label: Guankong
nodes.summary: Guankong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a teacher at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

nodes.label: D. Neil Schmid
nodes.summary: D. Neil Schmid specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair at the University of Pennsylvania, and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.

nodes.label: Rachel H. Pang
nodes.summary: Rachel H. Pang works in religious studies, Tibetology, and sinology, holding a PhD from the University of Virginia. She served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

nodes.label: Sangseraima Ujeed
nodes.summary: Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2012–2018) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

nodes.label: Mother Sayamagyi
nodes.summary: Mother Sayamagyi was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied as a disciple under U Ba Khin and later succeeded him.

nodes.label: U Ba Khin
nodes.description: Burmese civil servant and Vipassana meditation master
nodes.summary: U Ba Khin worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studying under Saya Thetgyi. He founded the International Meditation Centre and taught disciples including Satya Narayan Goenka and Mother Sayamagyi.

nodes.label: Sōkatsu Shaku
nodes.summary: Sōkatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kosen Imakita (1889) and Sōen Shaku (1893), and founded Ryōbōkai (1901, 1906) and Ningen Zen Kyodan.

nodes.label: Peter Connolly
nodes.summary: Peter Connolly works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at Lancaster University and was appointed Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

nodes.label: Lynn Thomas
nodes.summary: Lynn Thomas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees at Lancaster University and a D.Phil from the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton, attested in 1997.

nodes.label: Theodore Gabriel
nodes.summary: Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

nodes.label: Agvan Dorzhiev
variants: アグワン・ドルジェフ
nodes.jawiki: アグワン・ドルジェフ
nodes.description: Russian Buddhist monk and diplomat, envoy and Finance Minister of Tibet (1853–1938)
nodes.summary: Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang, earning the Geshe Lharampa degree. He founded Atsagat Datsan and Datsan Gunzechoinei, and his students included the 13th Dalai Lama.

nodes.label: Erik Erikson
nodes.jawiki: エリク・H・エリクソン
nodes.summary: Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. He later held academic positions at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (1951–1960), and Harvard University (circa 1960–1970).

nodes.id: I:Lille University of Science and Technology
nodes.label: Lille University of Science and Technology
Pratap Kumar Penumala
nodes.summary: Pratap Kumar Penumala is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. In 2010, he was attested as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and as a visiting professor at Colorado College.

nodes.label: St. Stephen's College
variants: St. Stephen’s College der University of Delhi

nodes.label: Eiichi Makino
nodes.summary: Eiichi Makino (1878–1970) worked in philosophy and other fields. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903), he taught there (~1903–1938) and held posts at Kyushu, Tohoku, and Chuo Universities, as well as Shiraume Gakuen Junior College.

nodes.label: Max Uhle
nodes.summary: Max Uhle was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Leipzig University (~1876–1880) under Georg von der Gabelentz.

nodes.label: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller
nodes.summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz (~1889–1893) and Karl Foy.

nodes.label: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal
nodes.summary: Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812-1894) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1842 to 1845.

nodes.label: Shenpen Nangwa
nodes.summary: Shenpen Nangwa was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Patrul Rinpoche around 1885–1887. He held a post at Dzogchen Monastery from around 1900 to 1927.

nodes.label: Patrul Rinpoche
nodes.summary: Patrul Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and philosopher. He studied under numerous masters, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1828–1842), Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje, and became a renowned teacher whose students included Shenpen Nangwa and Shechen Gyaltsab.

nodes.label: Denise Bernot
nodes.summary: Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. She studied at the École des chartes (~1942–1947) and the École des langues orientales (~1946–1950), later serving on the faculty of INALCO from ~1960 to 1989.

nodes.label: Georg Ruppelt
nodes.image: Georg Ruppelt Direktor der Gottfried-Wilhelm-Leibniz Bibliothek anläßlich der Buchvorstellung Alles über Wikipedia im Werner Kraft Vortragssaal.jpg

nodes.label: Sven Hedin
nodes.description: Swedish geographer, topographer, explorer, photographer, travel writer and illustrator (1865-1952)
nodes.summary: Sven Hedin worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his education at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the Humboldt University of Berlin, and the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

nodes.label: Staatsgalerie Stuttgart
variants: Württembergische Museum der Bildenden Künste in Stuttgart

nodes.label: James Darmesteter
nodes.jawiki: ジャーム・ダルメステテール
nodes.summary: James Darmesteter was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal (~1872–1877), later holding posts there (~1877–1894) and at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

nodes.label: Émile Durkheim
variants: エミール・デュルケーム
nodes.jawiki: エミール・デュルケーム
nodes.summary: Scholar of religion Émile Durkheim studied at ENS and Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt. He held academic posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1905), and Sorbonne University (~1902–1917), and founded L'Année Sociologique (1898).

nodes.label: Marcel Cohen
nodes.summary: Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris (~1919–1955), as well as L'Humanité (~1944–1974).

nodes.label: Lucien Tesniere
nodes.jawiki: ルシアン・テニエール
nodes.summary: Linguist Lucien Tesniere studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig University, and the École des langues orientales, also studying under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the universities of Ljubljana and Strasbourg (1924–1937) and the University of Montpellier (1937).

nodes.label: Pierre Chantraine
nodes.summary: Pierre Chantraine was a French linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between ~1920 and ~1927. He later served as a professor at the University of Paris from ~1938 to ~1969.

nodes.label: Michel Lejeune
nodes.summary: Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) under Antoine Meillet. He held academic posts at the University of Poitiers (~1933–1937), the University of Paris (~1947–1951), and the EPHE (~1951–1977).

nodes.label: Jerzy Kuryłowicz
variants: イェジ・クリウォヴィチ
nodes.jawiki: イェジ・クリウォヴィチ
nodes.summary: Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Lviv and under Antoine Meillet, later holding academic posts at the University of Lviv (circa 1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (circa 1946–1965).

nodes.label: André Martinet
nodes.jawiki: アンドレ・マルティネ
nodes.summary: André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne (~1926–1937) and under Antoine Meillet (~1930–1936). He held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938–1947), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1977).

nodes.label: Joseph Vendryes
nodes.image: Réunion des doyens des facultés dans le bureau du recteur, décembre 1940. M. Bruhat M. Gidel M. Baudouin M. Carcopino M. Maurain M. Vendryès M. Damiens (cropped).jpg
nodes.jawiki: ジョゼフ・ヴァンドリエス
nodes.summary: Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1950), École Normale Supérieure (~1904–1907), and the University of Paris (~1907–1946).

nodes.label: Alfred Ernout
nodes.summary: A linguist, Ernout held positions at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1951), University of Paris (~1927–1944), and Collège de France (1941–1951).

nodes.label: Herman Wirth
nodes.summary: Herman Wirth worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Utrecht University from around 1903 to 1906, held a post at the University of Bern from around 1909 to 1916, and founded Ahnenerbe.

nodes.label: Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku High School
variants: Kyōto Prefectural Ordinary Junior High School

nodes.label: Jacques André
nodes.summary: Jacques André (1910–1994) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris until 1948, he held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), EPHE (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

nodes.label: Raphael Kühner
nodes.summary: Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a German linguist who was educated at Ernestinum Gotha and studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1821 to 1824.

nodes.label: Peter K. Austin
nodes.summary: Peter K. Austin is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University (1975–1978). He held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 2002 to 2018.

École nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer
フランス海外領国立学校

nodes.label: Robert Göbl
nodes.summary: Robert Göbl (1919–1997) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (1947–1950) and later held an academic post there from around 1955 to 1989.

nodes.label: Karl Lachmann
nodes.summary: Karl Lachmann was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Leipzig University (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815), and later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1825–1851).

nodes.label: Tulane University
variants: H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College der Tulane University
Harriet Sophie Newcomb College at Tulane University

nodes.label: Alan Lomax
nodes.jawiki: アラン・ローマックス
nodes.summary: Alan Lomax was a scholar who pursued studies at St. Mark's School of Texas (~1929–1930), Choate Rosemary Hall (~1930–1932), Harvard University (~1932–1933), the University of Texas at Austin (~1934–1936), and Columbia University (~1939–1940).

nodes.label: Stanislav Grof
nodes.image: Крістіна і Станіслав Грофи (Christina and Stanislav Grof) (cropped).JPG
nodes.jawiki: スタニスラフ・グロフ
nodes.summary: Stanislav Grof is a religious studies scholar who studied at Charles University. He held positions at various psychiatric institutes in Prague, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and the California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).

Fachbereich Interkulturelle Studien der Donau-Universität Krems

nodes.label: Erich Schmidt
nodes.summary: Erich Schmidt worked in linguistics, having studied at the universities of Graz, Strasbourg (under Wilhelm Scherer), and Jena. He held academic posts at the universities of Würzburg (1875–1877), Vienna (circa 1880–1887), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1887–1913).

nodes.label: American Academy in Rome
variants: American School of Classical Studies in Rome
School of Classical Studies in the American Academy in Rome

nodes.label: Alfred Körte
nodes.summary: An archaeology and linguistics scholar, Körte studied at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890). He served on the faculties of Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig University (~1917–1934).

nodes.label: Friedrich Leo
nodes.summary: Friedrich Leo, a linguist, studied at Bonn under Hermann Usener (~1869–1873) and at Göttingen. He held academic posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and the University of Göttingen (1889–1914).

nodes.label: Walter Porzig
nodes.summary: Walter Porzig was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Jena (~1913–1920) and under Wilhelm Streitberg (~1920–1921). He held academic posts at Leipzig, Bern, Jena (~1936–1945), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1951–1961).

nodes.label: Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö
variants: ジャムヤン・ケンツェ・チューキ・ロドゥー
nodes.summary: Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo and studied under numerous traditional masters, including Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

nodes.id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.label: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.native: Πρίγκιπας Πέτρος της Ελλάδας και της Δανίας
variants: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.image: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark by Boucas.jpg
nodes.enwiki: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
nodes.jawiki: ペトロス・ティス・エラザス
nodes.description: anthropologist, specialising in Tibetan beliefs and customs
nodes.summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark (1908–1980) worked in Tibetology, history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics, and served in the Office of Strategic Services (c. 1944–1945).

nodes.label: Rudolf Thurneysen
nodes.summary: Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), the University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and the University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

nodes.label: Bedřich Hrozný
nodes.jawiki: ベドジフ・フロズニー
nodes.summary: Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1905–1919) and Charles University (circa 1919–1952).

nodes.id: I:Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis
nodes.label: Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis
variants: Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis

nodes.label: Friedrich Nietzsche
variants: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・ニーチェ
nodes.summary: Friedrich Nietzsche was a philosopher and linguist who studied at Bonn and Leipzig, learning under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl. He served as a faculty member at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

nodes.label: Friedrich Delitzsch
nodes.jawiki: フリードリヒ・デーリッチュ
nodes.summary: Linguist and historian Friedrich Delitzsch studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Fleischer, Brockhaus, Curtius, Windisch, and Dillmann. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1893–1899) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1899–1920).

nodes.label: Gustav Mensching
nodes.summary: Gustav Mensching worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, Göttingen, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto (~1920–1924), later holding academic posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

nodes.label: Rudolf Otto
nodes.description: German theologian, philosopher, and comparative religionist (1869–1937)
nodes.summary: Rudolf Otto worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and under Richard von Garbe, and held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).

nodes.label: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer
nodes.summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1968) and the University of Munich (~1968–1972), later holding professorships at Munich (~1981–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2013).

nodes.label: Shimin Geng
nodes.summary: Shimin Geng was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China from around 1949 to 1953 and held a post there from around 1953 to 2000.

nodes.label: Jens Peter Laut
nodes.summary: Jens Peter Laut works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Succeeding Klaus Röhrborn in 2008, he held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 2008 to 2020.

nodes.label: Franz Boas
nodes.summary: Franz Boas was a linguist and anthropologist. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, including under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University, the Smithsonian Institution, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (c. 1896–1936).

nodes.label: Otto Jahn
nodes.description: German classical philologist, archaeologist and musicologist (1813-1869)
nodes.summary: Otto Jahn was an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Kiel University (~1839–1845), the University of Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig University (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

nodes.label: Hans Küng
nodes.description: Swiss Catholic priest, theologian and author (1928-2021)
nodes.summary: Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1948–1955), and the Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), and later served on the faculty at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).

nodes.label: Clemente Merlo
nodes.summary: Clemente Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Pavia (~1898–1903) and held a post at the University of Pisa (~1910–1949).

nodes.id: I:Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires
nodes.label: Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires

nodes.label: Dipa Ma
